title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
我
國家承平日久
列聖紹統仁漸義摩禮陶樂鎔
文化彌深人才彌盛非惟庠序
之所教育其山林田野戎行
掌故亦在在彪彪而江西則
===
又其尤者也求才科目
制酌前古三年一大比之百三
十餘年名卿碩輔凡百良工
所與共天下而成
至治者胥此焉出以故有司奉
行
彝典維慎維重而務精於柬拔
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序

我國家承平日久，列聖紹統，仁漸義摩，禮陶樂鎔，文化彌深，人才彌盛。非惟庠序之所教育，其山林田野、戎行掌故，亦在在彪彪，而江西則又其尤者也。

求才科目，制酌前古，三年一大比之。百三十餘年，名卿碩輔、凡百良工，所與共天下而成至治者，胥此焉出。以故有司奉行彝典，維慎維重，而務精於柬拔
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

Our dynasty has long enjoyed peace. Successive sage emperors have continued the imperial line, nurturing the people through benevolence, refining them through righteousness, and shaping them through ritual and music. The transforming influence of culture has grown ever deeper, and men of talent have become ever more numerous. Such men are found not only among those educated in the schools: in the mountains and forests, in the fields, in military ranks, and among clerks, outstanding men are to be found everywhere. Jiangxi is particularly distinguished in this respect.

The examination system for seeking talent was established with due consideration of ancient precedents, holding a comprehensive examination once every three years. For more than a hundred and thirty years, renowned ministers, eminent chief councillors, and capable officials of every kind—those with whom the sovereign has governed the realm and achieved consummate good government—have all emerged through this system. For this reason, the responsible officials carry out its established regulations with utmost care and seriousness, striving for discernment in selecting candidates…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
以仰副
國家之求况江西多才宜加之
意尤非諸藩之可比者譬之
鄧林材固多於天下然不皆
合抱之良冀北馬固多於天
下然不皆千里之駿非精以
掄選之烏知合抱之良不遺
於鄧林千里之足不遺於冀
===
北哉弘治辛酉又維開科之
期江西藩臬重臣具故事以
裁之廵按達之鎮守廵撫預
擇考官預葺塲屋預汰士子
預戒百執事以待維時鎮守
則
punctuated:
以仰副國家之求。况江西多才，宜加之意，尤非諸藩之可比者。譬之鄧林，材固多於天下，然不皆合抱之良；冀北，馬固多於天下，然不皆千里之駿。非精以掄選之，烏知合抱之良不遺於鄧林，千里之足不遺於冀北哉？

弘治辛酉，又維開科之期。江西藩臬重臣具故事以裁之廵按，達之鎮守、廵撫，預擇考官，預葺塲屋，預汰士子，預戒百執事以待。維時鎮守則
translation_en:
…to fulfill the state's demand for talent. Moreover, Jiangxi has many talented men and deserves particular attention; in this respect, it is especially unlike the other provinces. Consider Denglin: its timber certainly surpasses that of the rest of the realm in abundance, yet not every tree is fine timber with a trunk an armspan around. Jibei certainly surpasses the rest of the realm in its abundance of horses, yet not every horse is a fine steed capable of traveling a thousand li. Unless selection is meticulous, how can one be sure that fine timber an armspan around is not left overlooked in Denglin, or a thousand-li steed in Jibei?

The xinyou year of the Hongzhi reign [1501] was again a year for holding the examination. The high officials of Jiangxi's Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions assembled the established precedents for adjudication by the Regional Inspector [?] and communicated them to the Defender and Grand Coordinator. They selected Examiners beforehand, repaired the examination compound beforehand, screened out unsuitable candidates beforehand, and instructed all personnel beforehand in preparation. At that time, the Defender was…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
御用監太監董〔讓〕巡撫則都察
院右副都御史韓〔邦問〕巡按
則監察御史周〔進隆〕何〔歆〕監
権則戸部貟外郎左〔然〕布政
按察二司左右布政使則周
〔宏〕林〔泮〕按察使則周〔南〕左右
条政則吴〔文度〕張〔冕〕副使則
===
李〔澄〕馮〔允中〕邵〔寶〕沈〔銳〕左右
条議則蔣〔浤〕黄〔皡〕王〔綸〕僉事
則萬〔祥〕沈〔元〕任〔漢〕王〔純〕而〔寶〕
以提學為職者考試官主考
則學正韓〔宗堯〕教諭黄〔秩〕分
考則學正章〔鉞〕楊〔曰宗〕教諭
張〔聰〕傅〔鼎〕潘〔援〕李〔聰〕徐〔冠〕林
punctuated:
御用監太監董〔讓〕，巡撫則都察院右副都御史韓〔邦問〕，巡按則監察御史周〔進隆〕、何〔歆〕，監権則戸部貟外郎左〔然〕。布政、按察二司，左右布政使則周〔宏〕、林〔泮〕，按察使則周〔南〕，左右条政則吴〔文度〕、張〔冕〕，副使則李〔澄〕、馮〔允中〕、邵〔寶〕、沈〔銳〕，左右条議則蔣〔浤〕、黄〔皡〕、王〔綸〕，僉事則萬〔祥〕、沈〔元〕、任〔漢〕、王〔純〕，而〔寶〕以提學為職者。

考試官，主考則學正韓〔宗堯〕、教諭黄〔秩〕；分考則學正章〔鉞〕、楊〔曰宗〕，教諭張〔聰〕、傅〔鼎〕、潘〔援〕、李〔聰〕、徐〔冠〕、林
translation_en:
… Dong Rang, Grand Eunuch of the Directorate of Imperial Accoutrements. The Grand Coordinator was Han Bangwen, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. The Regional Inspectors were Investigating Censors Zhou Jinlong and He Xin. The official overseeing [the monopoly?; transcription doubtful] was Zuo Ran, Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

In the Provincial Administration Commission and Provincial Surveillance Commission, Zhou Hong and Lin Pan were the Left and Right Provincial Administration Commissioners. Zhou Nan was Provincial Surveillance Commissioner. Wu Wendu and Zhang Mian were the Left and Right Administration Vice Commissioners [title doubtful in the transcription]. Li Cheng, Feng Yunzhong, Shao Bao, and Shen Rui were Surveillance Vice Commissioners. Jiang Hong, Huang Hao, and Wang Lun were Left and Right Administration Assistant Commissioners [title doubtful in the transcription]. Wan Xiang, Shen Yuan, Ren Han, and Wang Chun were Surveillance Assistant Commissioners. Of these, Shao Bao was charged with supervising education.

Among the Examiners, the chief examiners were Han Zongyao, an Instructor, and Huang Zhi, an Instructor. The Associate Examiners were Zhang Yue and Yang Yuezong, both Instructors, and the Instructors Zhang Cong, Fu Ding, Pan Yuan, Li Cong, Xu Guan, and Lin …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
倖
訓導孟〔鏜〕劉〔天錫〕掌卷洎
封謄諸執事則知府祝瀚朱
華并各屬知縣之良者至期
讓〔邦問〕綱維之〔歆然〕作新之
協相之〔宏南文度〕〔銳〕內而提
調監糾之〔泮晃澄浤皞綸祥元〕
漢〔純〕外而整飭防範之都指
===
揮同知何〔昇〕都指揮僉事戴
賢〔清〕李〔清〕與監巡官卒之責亦
從而衛護之其總擅監臨振
肅之柄寔惟〔進隆〕馮時自鎖
院三試大小有事者罔不精
白一心以令以承而其綜理
之周警飭之至又嚴而弗苛
punctuated: 倖，訓導孟〔鏜〕、劉〔天錫〕。掌卷洎封謄諸執事，則知府祝瀚、朱華，并各屬知縣之良者。至期，讓〔邦問〕綱維之，〔歆然〕作新之、協相之，〔宏南文度〕〔銳〕內而提調監糾之，〔泮晃澄浤皞綸祥元〕漢〔純〕外而整飭防範之。都指揮同知何〔昇〕、都指揮僉事戴賢〔清〕、李〔清〕，與監巡官卒之責，亦從而衛護之。其總擅監臨振肅之柄，寔惟〔進隆〕馮。時自鎖院三試，大小有事者，罔不精白一心，以令以承；而其綜理之周、警飭之至，又嚴而弗苛。
translation_en: …[Lin] Xing, and the assistant instructors Meng Tang and Liu Tianxi. Those charged with managing the examination scripts, sealing and transcribing them, and the other duties were the prefects Zhu Han and Zhu Hua, together with capable county magistrates from their respective jurisdictions. When the appointed time arrived, Rang and Bangwen [?] provided overall direction; Xin and Ran [?] encouraged renewed effort and assisted the work. Hong, Nan, Wendu, and Rui [?] handled arrangements, supervision, and disciplinary oversight within the examination compound, while Pan, Huang, Cheng, Hong, Hao, Lun, Xiang, Yuan, Han, and Chun [?] maintained order and precautions outside. Vice Regional Military Commissioner He Sheng and Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Dai Xianqing [?] and Li Qing, together with the officers and soldiers responsible for supervision and patrol, also provided protection. Overall authority for supervision and the enforcement of discipline rested solely with Jin, Long, and Feng [?]. From the sealing of the examination compound through the three sessions, everyone entrusted with duties, great or small, acted with complete integrity and a single purpose, whether issuing instructions or carrying them out. Their comprehensive management and utmost vigilance were strict without being harsh …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
簡而弗疏就試士子咸得竭
其底蘊舒其英華於三日之
間非復往時之驅迫猝遽而
莫能竟其長也試既卷入〔鼎〕
〔援天錫〕校易〔鉞偕〕校書〔曰宗〕
〔聰冠〕校詩〔聰〕校春秋〔鑛〕校禮
記〔宗堯秩〕則謬承推讓又從
===
而總校之凡自始校至去取
之定〔宗堯〕等數人者昕夕忘
疲誓諸
天日公無少私誠慮混玉石而迷
五色深有負今日慎重為
國家求才之意心力自謂已殫
第愚學識目力之未至耳卷
punctuated: 簡而弗疏，就試士子咸得竭其底蘊，舒其英華於三日之間，非復往時之驅迫猝遽而莫能竟其長也。試既，卷入，〔鼎〕〔援天錫〕校《易》，〔鉞偕〕校《書》，〔曰宗〕〔聰冠〕校《詩》，〔聰〕校《春秋》，〔鑛〕校《禮記》。〔宗堯秩〕則謬承推讓，又從而總校之。凡自始校至去取之定，〔宗堯〕等數人者昕夕忘疲，誓諸天日，公無少私，誠慮混玉石而迷五色，深有負今日慎重為國家求才之意。心力自謂已殫，第愚學識目力之未至耳。卷
translation_en:
…simple without being lax. All the candidates taking the examination were able, over the three days, to draw fully upon their accumulated learning and display their finest abilities. They were no longer subjected to the pressure and haste of former times, which had prevented them from giving full expression to their strengths.

Once the examination was over and the scripts submitted, Ding, Yuan, and Tianxi [?] assessed those on the Book of Changes; Yue and Xie [?], those on the Book of Documents; Yuezong, Cong, and Guan [?], those on the Book of Odes; Cong, those on the Spring and Autumn Annals; and Kuang, those on the Book of Rites. Zongyao and Zhi [?], undeservedly accorded precedence by their colleagues, then undertook the overall review.

From the initial assessment until the final decisions on acceptance and rejection, we few, Zongyao and the others, labored from dawn to dusk, heedless of fatigue. We swore before Heaven and the sun to be impartial, without the slightest private bias. We truly feared confusing jade with common stone and failing to distinguish the five colors, thereby gravely betraying the present intention to exercise care in seeking talent for the state. We believe we have exhausted our mental and physical energies; any shortcomings lie only in our limited learning, understanding, and discernment. As for the examination scripts …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
三千有奇僅拔九十有五遵
制額也既事有錄刻舉子姓名
并文字之優者
獻之以傳〔宗堯〕當序于首敢拜
手稽首而言曰猗歟休哉
國家求才之
大典也猗歟盛哉江西多才之
===
大藩也是科也郡邑士子報
試者霧滃雲集無慮萬人提
學既閱而汰其太半以進之
巡按巡按覆閱而汰其十二
以進之場屋〔宗堯〕等復柬閱
於三千卷中得九十五人以
獻之
punctuated: 三千有奇，僅拔九十有五，遵制額也。既事有錄，刻舉子姓名并文字之優者，獻之以傳。〔宗堯〕當序于首，敢拜手稽首而言曰：「猗歟休哉！國家求才之大典也！猗歟盛哉！江西多才之大藩也！是科也，郡邑士子報試者霧滃雲集，無慮萬人。提學既閱而汰其太半，以進之巡按；巡按覆閱而汰其十二，以進之場屋。〔宗堯〕等復柬閱於三千卷中，得九十五人以獻之
translation_en: …of more than three thousand examination scripts, only ninety-five were selected, in accordance with the prescribed quota. Once the proceedings were concluded, a record was compiled, printing the candidates’ names together with the finest of their writings, to be respectfully presented and circulated. I, Zongyao 〔宗堯〕, being charged with placing a preface at its head, venture to bow with hands joined and forehead to the ground and say: “Ah, how splendid! This is the state’s great ceremony for seeking talent! Ah, how flourishing! Jiangxi is a great province rich in talent! For this examination, scholars from the prefectures and counties who registered to sit gathered like mist and clouds, numbering fully ten thousand. The Education Intendant examined them and eliminated more than half, forwarding the remainder to the Regional Inspector. The Regional Inspector examined them again and eliminated two-tenths, sending the remainder on to the examination hall. We, Zongyao and the others, then reviewed and selected from among three thousand scripts, obtaining ninety-five men to present to …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
天子盖幾百人而得一人也猗歟
難哉夫
天之生才所以為
國家也
國家求才所以承
天意也有司之舉行科目又所以
心
===
國家之心也慎重不當如是歟
江西環二千餘里以為藩於
山有仁蒙有靈華有匡廬之
雄奇於水有章貢有盱汝有
番陽之洪秀於人有陶桓公
有歐陽六一有臨川有草廬
之事業烜赫有文山有疊山
punctuated:
天子，盖幾百人而得一人也。猗歟，難哉！夫天之生才，所以為國家也；國家求才，所以承天意也；有司之舉行科目，又所以心國家之心也。慎重不當如是歟？
江西環二千餘里以為藩，於山有仁蒙、有靈華、有匡廬之雄奇；於水有章貢、有盱汝、有番陽之洪秀；於人有陶桓公、有歐陽六一、有臨川、有草廬之事業烜赫，有文山、有疊山
translation_en:
…the Son of Heaven: thus only one man was selected out of every several hundred. Ah, how difficult! Heaven brings forth talent for the sake of the state; the state seeks talent in order to fulfill Heaven’s intent; and the responsible officials conduct the examinations in order to take the state’s concerns as their own. Should they not exercise such care?
Jiangxi forms a province extending more than two thousand li around its perimeter. Among its mountains are Renmeng [?], Linghua [?], and the majestic, wondrous Kuanglu; among its waters are the Zhang and Gong, the Xu and Ru, and the vast, beautiful Poyang. Among its people are Duke Huan, Tao Kan; Ouyang Liuyi; and Linchuan and Caolu, with their illustrious achievements. There are also Wenshan and Dieshan…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
有孺子有彭澤之忠節巍義
炳靈降神千古一日今九十
五人之登是錄者將来鴻勛
偉烈以彌隆我
皇明無疆之治化以爭高競爽於
前修夫豈無人藹藹王多吉
士維君子使媚于
===
天子藹藹王多吉人維君子命媚
于庶人鳳凰于飛傅天之咏
敢敬舉之併是錄以
獻
湖廣郴州儒學學正韓〔宗堯〕
謹序
punctuated:
有孺子、有彭澤之忠節巍義，炳靈降神，千古一日。今九十五人之登是錄者，將来鴻勛偉烈，以彌隆我皇明無疆之治化，以爭高競爽於前修，夫豈無人？「藹藹王多吉士，維君子使，媚于天子。藹藹王多吉人，維君子命，媚于庶人。」鳳凰于飛、傅天之咏，敢敬舉之，併是錄以獻。
湖廣郴州儒學學正韓〔宗堯〕謹序。
translation_en:
…there are the steadfast loyalty and towering righteousness [?] of Ruzi and Pengze. This radiant spiritual potency descends to inspire men; across a thousand ages, it remains as constant as a single day. Among the ninety-five men whose names now enter this record, surely there will be those whose future great achievements and splendid deeds will further magnify the boundless governance and transforming influence of our August Ming, vying in eminence and excellence with the worthies of earlier times!
“Multitudinous are the king’s worthy officers; the noble ruler employs them, and they win the favor of the Son of Heaven. Multitudinous are the king’s worthy men; the noble ruler appoints them, and they win the favor of the common people.” I venture respectfully to invoke this song of phoenixes in flight, spreading across the heavens, and present it together with this record.
Preface respectfully written by Han〔Zongyao〕, Instructor of the Confucian School of Chenzhou, Huguang.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
弘治十四年江西鄉試
監臨官
巡按江西監察御史周進隆〔紹立福建莆田縣人甲辰進士〕
提調官
江西等處承宣布政使司左布政使周宏〔懋德浙江德清縣人乙未進士〕
江西等處承宣布政使司左參政吳文度〔憲之應天府江寧縣人壬辰進士〕
監試官
江西等處提刑按察司按察使周南〔文化浙江縉雲縣人戊戌進士〕
江西等處提刑按察司副使沈銳〔文進浙江仁和縣人己丑進士〕
===
考試官
湖廣郴州儒學學正韓宗堯〔仁卿廣東番禺縣人壬子貢士〕
山東東昌府高唐州夏津縣儒學教諭黃秩〔子禮福建莆田縣人癸卯貢士〕
同考試官
湖廣沔陽州儒學學正章鉞〔君儀直隸吳縣人癸卯貢士〕
河南開封府許州儒學學正楊曰宗〔汝慶福建莆田縣人壬子貢士〕
福建延平府將樂縣儒學教諭張聰〔天與浙江仁和縣人壬子貢士〕
直隸松江府華亭縣儒學教諭傅鼎〔用養福建閩縣人己酉貢士〕
福建福州府長樂縣儒學教諭潘援〔匡善浙江景寧縣人乙卯貢士〕
punctuated:
弘治十四年江西鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按江西監察御史周進隆〔紹立，福建莆田縣人，甲辰進士〕。

提調官：
江西等處承宣布政使司左布政使周宏〔懋德，浙江德清縣人，乙未進士〕。
江西等處承宣布政使司左參政吳文度〔憲之，應天府江寧縣人，壬辰進士〕。

監試官：
江西等處提刑按察司按察使周南〔文化，浙江縉雲縣人，戊戌進士〕。

translation_en: Dou Lei 竇櫑, courtesy name Yicai, was Station Master of the Shicha Relay Station in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture. He was a native of Kuaiji County, Zhejiang, and came from service as a messenger (chengchai).

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
上好義則民莫敢不服
故君子內省不疚無惡於志
親親仁也敬長義也
易
範天之神道而四時不忒
說而巽孚乃化邦也
齊小大者存乎卦
復德之本也恒德之固也
===
書
帝光天之下至于海隅蒼生
惟天聰明惟聖時憲
成湯既受命時則有若伊尹格于皇天在
太甲時則有若保衡在太戊時則有若
伊陟臣扈格于上帝巫咸乂王家
詩
舉能其官惟爾之能
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書
上好義，則民莫敢不服。
故君子內省不疚，無惡於志。
親親，仁也；敬長，義也。

易
範天之神道，而四時不忒。
說而巽，孚乃化邦也。
齊小大者，存乎卦。
復，德之本也；恒，德之固也。

書
帝光天之下，至于海隅蒼生。
惟天聰明，惟聖時憲。
成湯既受命，時則有若伊尹，格于皇天；在太甲，時則有若保衡；在太戊，時則有若伊陟、臣扈，格于上帝；巫咸乂王家。

詩
舉能其官，惟爾之能。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
When those above cherish righteousness, none among the people dare withhold their submission.
Thus the gentleman examines himself inwardly and finds no cause for remorse, nor anything reprehensible in his intentions.
Affection for one’s kin is benevolence; respect for one’s elders is righteousness.

Book of Changes
Take Heaven’s numinous Way as a model [?], and the four seasons do not deviate.
Joyous and yielding, one transforms the realm through sincerity.
Bringing the small and the great into due order lies in the hexagrams.
Return (Fu) is the root of virtue; Constancy (Heng) is the firmness of virtue.

Book of Documents
The emperor’s radiance reached all beneath Heaven, extending to the common people at the edges of the seas.
Heaven alone is keen of hearing and clear of sight; the sage takes this as his model.
When Cheng Tang had received the Mandate, there was Yi Yin, who reached August Heaven. In the time of Tai Jia, there was the Protector and Counselor; in the time of Tai Wu, there were Yi Zhi and Chen Hu, who reached the Lord on High, while Wu Xian governed the royal household.

Book of Odes
Raise the capable to their offices [?]; this is your ability.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
游環脅驅陰剨鍪續
自古有年今適南畝或耘或耔黍稷薿薿
陟我高岡無矢我陵我陵我阿無飲我泉
我泉我池
我龍受之蹻蹻王之造
春秋
肆大眚〔莊公二十有二年〕
晉人秦人戰于河曲〔文公十有二年〕季孫行
父臧孫許叔孫僑如公孫嬰齊帥師會
===
晉郤克衛孫良夫曹公子首及齊侯戰
于鞌〔成公二年〕晉侯及楚子鄭伯戰于
鄢陵〔成公十有六年〕晉趙鞅帥師及鄭罕
達帥師戰于鐵〔哀公二年〕
宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯會晉師于棐林伐鄭
〔宣公元年〕晉人宋人衛人陳人侵鄭
〔宣公二年〕晉欒書帥師伐鄭〔成公九年〕
晉侯及楚子鄭伯戰于鄢陵〔成公十有六
年〕公會尹子單子晉侯齊侯宋公衛
punctuated:
游環脅驅，陰剨鍪續。
自古有年，今適南畝，或耘或耔，黍稷薿薿。
陟我高岡，無矢我陵。我陵我阿，無飲我泉。我泉我池。
我龍受之，蹻蹻王之造。

春秋
肆大眚〔莊公二十有二年〕。
晉人、秦人戰于河曲〔文公十有二年〕。季孫行父、臧孫許、叔孫僑如、公孫嬰齊帥師，會晉郤克、衛孫良夫、曹公子首，及齊侯戰于鞌〔成公二年〕。晉侯及楚子、鄭伯戰于鄢陵〔成公十有六年〕。晉趙鞅帥師，及鄭罕達帥師戰于鐵〔哀公二年〕。
宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯會晉師于棐林，伐鄭〔宣公元年〕。晉人、宋人、衛人、陳人侵鄭〔宣公二年〕。晉欒書帥師伐鄭〔成公九年〕。晉侯及楚子、鄭伯戰于鄢陵〔成公十有六年〕。公會尹子、單子、晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛
translation_en:
Sliding rings and flank restraints [on the chariot harness]; the remaining phrase, 陰剨鍪續, is garbled [?].
From ancient times there have been abundant harvests. Now we go to the southern fields: some weed, some bank up the soil; the millets grow luxuriantly.
Climb my high ridge, but do not deploy upon my hills [?]. My hills and my slopes—do not drink from my springs. My springs and my pools.
I receive this favor—the mighty achievements of the king.

Spring and Autumn Annals
An amnesty was proclaimed for grave offenses. 〔Twenty-second year of Duke Zhuang.〕
The men of Jin and Qin fought at Hequ. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Wen.〕 Jisun Xingfu, Zangsun Xu, Shusun Qiaoru, and Gongsun Yingqi led an army and joined Xi Ke of Jin, Sun Liangfu of Wei, and Prince Shou of Cao to fight against the Marquis of Qi at An. 〔Second year of Duke Cheng.〕 The Marquis of Jin fought against the Viscount of Chu and the Earl of Zheng at Yanling. 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Cheng.〕 Zhao Yang of Jin led an army and fought at Tie against Han Da of Zheng, who also led an army. 〔Second year of Duke Ai.〕
The Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao joined the army of Jin at Feilin and attacked Zheng. 〔First year of Duke Xuan.〕 The men of Jin, Song, Wei, and Chen invaded Zheng. 〔Second year of Duke Xuan.〕 Luan Shu of Jin led an army to attack Zheng. 〔Ninth year of Duke Cheng.〕 The Marquis of Jin fought against the Viscount of Chu and the Earl of Zheng at Yanling. 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Cheng.〕 The duke joined the Viscount of Yin, the Viscount of Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and the ruler of Wei…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
侯曹伯邾人伐鄭公會單子晉侯宋公
衛侯曹伯齊人邾人伐鄭〔俱成公十有七〕
年戍鄭虎牢楚公子貞帥師救鄭〔襄〕
公十年
公會劉子晉侯宋公蔡侯衛侯陳子鄭伯
許男曹伯莒子邾子頓子胡子滕子薛
伯杞伯小邾子齊國夏于召陵侵楚
公及諸侯盟于皐鼬〔俱定公四年〕
禮記
===
天子使其大夫爲三監監於方伯之國國
三人
禮俗刑然後樂
流而不息合同而化而樂興焉
臣下竭力盡能以立功於國君必報之以
爵禄故臣下皆務竭力盡能以立功是
以國安而君寧禮無不答言上之不虛
取於下也上必明正道以道民民道之
而有功然後取其什一故上用足而下
punctuated:
侯、曹伯、邾人伐鄭。公會單子、晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊人、邾人伐鄭〔俱成公十有七〕年。戍鄭虎牢。楚公子貞帥師救鄭〔襄〕公十年。
公會劉子、晉侯、宋公、蔡侯、衛侯、陳子、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、莒子、邾子、頓子、胡子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊國夏于召陵，侵楚。公及諸侯盟于皐鼬〔俱定公四年〕。
禮記
天子使其大夫爲三監，監於方伯之國，國三人。
禮俗刑，然後樂。
流而不息，合同而化，而樂興焉。
臣下竭力盡能，以立功於國，君必報之以爵禄。故臣下皆務竭力盡能，以立功，是以國安而君寧。禮無不答，言上之不虛取於下也。上必明正道以道民，民道之而有功，然後取其什一，故上用足而下
translation_en:
…the Marquis [of Wei], the Earl of Cao, and men of Zhu attacked Zheng. The duke met with Viscount Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, and men of Qi and Zhu to attack Zheng. 〔Both entries concern the seventeenth year of Duke Cheng.〕 They garrisoned Hulao in Zheng. Prince Zhen of Chu led an army to relieve Zheng. 〔The tenth year of Duke Xiang.〕
The duke met with Viscount Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Wei, Viscount Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Xiao Zhu, and Guo Xia of Qi at Shaoling to invade Chu. The duke and the regional lords made a covenant at Gaoyou. 〔Both entries concern the fourth year of Duke Ding.〕
Record of Rites (Liji)
The Son of Heaven appoints his grand masters as the Three Supervisors to oversee the states of the regional chiefs, three men in each state.
Only after rites and customs have taken shape does music follow.
They flow without ceasing, unite and transform; thus music arises.
When ministers expend their strength and exercise their abilities to the utmost to render service to the state, the ruler must reward them with noble rank and emoluments. Thus all ministers strive to expend their strength and exercise their abilities to the utmost to render service. Consequently, the state is secure and the ruler at peace. Ritual leaves nothing unreciprocated: this means that those above do not take from those below without giving something in return. Those above must make the correct Way clear so as to guide the people. Once the people follow it and achieve results, only then may those above take one tenth of their produce. Thus those above have enough for their needs, while those below…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
不匱也是以上下和親而不相怨也和
寧禮之用也此君臣上下之大義也
第貳場
論
人主務聰明之實
詔誥表〔内科壹道〕
擬漢詔太官勿受郡國異味詔〔建武十三年〕
擬唐加左僕射房玄齡太子少師誥〔貞觀〕
十三年
===
擬宋以歐陽脩知制誥謝表〔慶曆三年〕
判語〔五條〕
上言大臣德政
收留迷失子女
禁止師巫邪術
邊境申索軍需
同行知有謀害
第叄場
策五道
punctuated:
不匱也。是以上下和親而不相怨也。和寧，禮之用也。此君臣上下之大義也。
第貳場
論
人主務聰明之實。
詔誥表〔内科壹道〕
擬漢詔太官勿受郡國異味詔〔建武十三年〕。
擬唐加左僕射房玄齡太子少師誥〔貞觀〕十三年。
擬宋以歐陽脩知制誥謝表〔慶曆三年〕。
判語〔五條〕
上言大臣德政。
收留迷失子女。
禁止師巫邪術。
邊境申索軍需。
同行知有謀害。
第叄場
策五道。
translation_en:
…are not left in want. Thus those above and those below live in harmony and affection, without resentment toward one another. Harmony and tranquility are the effects of ritual. This is the great principle governing ruler and minister, superior and subordinate.
Second Session
Discourse
The ruler must strive for the substance of perceptiveness and understanding.
Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One topic from among these [?]〕
Compose, in the historical setting of the Han, an edict ordering the Grand Provisioner not to accept exotic delicacies from the commanderies and kingdoms. 〔Thirteenth year of Jianwu〕
Compose, in the historical setting of the Tang, a proclamation conferring on Fang Xuanling, Vice Director of the Left of the Department of State Affairs, the additional title of Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. Thirteenth year of 〔Zhenguan〕.
Compose, in the historical setting of the Song, a memorial of thanks by Ouyang Xiu for his appointment as Drafter of Proclamations. 〔Third year of Qingli〕
Legal Judgments 〔Five cases〕
Submitting statements to the throne praising the virtue and administration of high ministers.
Taking in and sheltering lost boys and girls.
Prohibiting the illicit arts of ritual masters and spirit mediums.
Requests from frontier regions for military supplies.
Knowing that a traveling companion intends to harm someone.
Third Session
Five policy questions.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
闡春秋大一統者天地之常經古今之通
義也然惟聖人在上議禮制度考文以
新天下之耳目以一天下之心志始足
以語此洪惟我
太祖高皇帝受
天明命奄有萬方
建極之初爰有
制作須示天下竊嘗仰觀其一二若
禮儀定式
===
稽古定制
洪武正韻皆制作之大端萬世臣民所當遵
守而不敢違也其品節凡例雖
命儒臣輯錄而實
淵衷所剖析是不可以不究夫議禮以辨上
下定式所載為條三十有七上下辨矣
不知始於何事終於何條而其間最切
而要者何居制度以殊等威定制所編
類皆經常之法等威殊矣不知所監者
punctuated: 闡《春秋》大一統者，天地之常經，古今之通義也。然惟聖人在上，議禮、制度、考文，以新天下之耳目，以一天下之心志，始足以語此。洪惟我太祖高皇帝受天明命，奄有萬方，建極之初，爰有制作，須示天下。竊嘗仰觀其一二，若《禮儀定式》、《稽古定制》、《洪武正韻》，皆制作之大端，萬世臣民所當遵守而不敢違也。其品節凡例，雖命儒臣輯錄，而實淵衷所剖析，是不可以不究。夫議禮以辨上下，《定式》所載為條三十有七，上下辨矣。不知始於何事，終於何條，而其間最切而要者何居？制度以殊等威，《定制》所編，類皆經常之法，等威殊矣。不知所監者
translation_en: The principle of grand unity elucidated in the Spring and Autumn Annals is the constant norm of Heaven and Earth and the universally valid principle of antiquity and the present. Yet only when a sage occupies the throne, deliberating upon rites, establishing institutions, and examining written forms, thereby renewing what all under Heaven hear and see and unifying their minds and purposes, can this truly be spoken of. We solemnly reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s illustrious mandate and possessed the myriad regions. At the beginning of his establishment of supreme rule, he instituted regulations to be made known throughout the realm. I have ventured to contemplate a few of these: the Established Forms of Ritual and Ceremony (Liyi dingshi), Established Institutions Based on the Study of Antiquity (Jigu dingzhi), and Correct Rhymes of the Hongwu Reign (Hongwu zhengyun). These are all major achievements in institutional creation, which subjects and people through all generations must observe and dare not transgress. Although Confucian officials were commanded to compile their detailed provisions and general conventions, these in fact resulted from the discerning analysis of his profound imperial mind and must therefore be thoroughly investigated. Now, deliberating upon rites serves to distinguish superiors from inferiors. The Established Forms contains thirty-seven articles, through which these distinctions are made clear. With what matter does it begin, with what article does it end, and which provisions among them are the most pressing and essential? Establishing institutions serves to differentiate ranks and their attendant dignities. The categories compiled in the Established Institutions are all enduring norms, through which these distinctions are made clear. Yet we ask what served as their model …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
何代所舉者何君而其間語及財利者
何爲又若考文以正形聲正韻一書去
沈約之謬而成經緯之交發於形聲者
亦正矣抑不知雅音取於何地註釋依
於何人併析見於何韻耶夫制未備則
化未成自我
聖祖立法品式畢具迄今百三十餘年師無異
道人無異論誠一統文明之治也不知
聖祖制作之善所以能致是者何所本歟諸士
===
子生
今之世觀
國之光鋪張揚厲之志盖素負矣幸究言之
以觀爲下不倍之意
問程子於龜山之行有吾道南矣之歎然
程子受學周子實自於南其所以相從
之故可得聞歟或謂周之於程猶范之
於張或又謂其造詣不同契悟亦異必
有見矣而朱子於學庸之序孟子之卒
punctuated:
何代，所舉者何君，而其間語及財利者何爲？又若考文以正形聲，《正韻》一書，去沈約之謬而成經緯之交，發於形聲者亦正矣。抑不知雅音取於何地，註釋依於何人，併析見於何韻耶？夫制未備則化未成。自我聖祖立法，品式畢具，迄今百三十餘年，師無異道，人無異論，誠一統文明之治也。不知聖祖制作之善，所以能致是者，何所本歟？諸士子生今之世，觀國之光，鋪張揚厲之志盖素負矣。幸究言之，以觀爲下不倍之意。

問：程子於龜山之行，有「吾道南矣」之歎。然程子受學周子，實自於南，其所以相從之故，可得聞歟？或謂周之於程，猶范之於張；或又謂其造詣不同，契悟亦異，必有見矣。而朱子於《學》《庸》之序、《孟子》之卒
translation_en:
…which dynasty was taken as the model, which ruler was cited, and why were matters of wealth and profit discussed therein? Likewise, in examining written language to rectify character forms and sounds, the Correct Rhymes (Zhengyun) eliminated Shen Yue’s errors and established the interconnections of warp and weft, thereby also correcting what is expressed in written forms and sounds. Yet from what region was its standard pronunciation drawn? Whose explanations did its annotations follow? In which rhyme categories can mergers and divisions be seen? Until institutions are complete, moral transformation cannot be accomplished. Since our Sagely Progenitor established the laws, with all ranks and prescribed forms fully provided for, more than 130 years have passed. Teachers follow no divergent Ways, and people voice no divergent doctrines: this is truly a unified and culturally enlightened order. On what foundation did the excellence of the Sagely Progenitor’s institutions rest, enabling them to achieve this? You scholars, born into the present age and beholding the glory of the realm, have surely long cherished the ambition to proclaim and extol it. Please discuss these matters thoroughly, so that we may discern your commitment to serving without disloyalty.

Question: When Guishan departed, Master Cheng exclaimed, “My Way has gone south!” Yet Master Cheng received instruction from Master Zhou, and that learning actually came from the south. May we hear why he followed Zhou as his teacher? Some say that Zhou’s relationship to Cheng was like Fan’s relationship to Zhang; others say that their attainments differed, as did their intuitive understanding. These claims must have some basis. Yet Master Zhu, in his prefaces to the Great Learning and the Doctrine of the Mean, and in the final … of the Mencius …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
章論道統之傳皆言程而不及周何也
夫周之學既授二程矣當是時廬陵有
歐陽氏南豐有曾氏豫章有黃氏臨川
有王氏盱江有李氏各學其學而不相
為謀其間知周子者抑有人焉其說安
在朱子後周程而出往来於饒信南康
之境多矣而二陸胥會議竟不合草廬
吴氏乃尊信於聞知之餘吴之為學其
於朱也程也周也果符契乎諸生論學
===
於古此其最切近者不可無說也
問齊道德一風俗上之所好民必趨焉先
王盛時無異教無異政無異尚無異情
無異心何道歟秦而降俗有薄者厚者
虛者實者浮者醇者仁厚者何施歟要
之上之化也而士夫之風軌欬動則又
有可舉者夫感二絹之遺而縣無復盜
激一布之恵而道不拾遺學古人居晉
鄙而薰德者善良負孤兒隱山陽而感
punctuated:
章，論道統之傳，皆言程而不及周，何也？夫周之學既授二程矣，當是時，廬陵有歐陽氏，南豐有曾氏，豫章有黃氏，臨川有王氏，盱江有李氏，各學其學而不相為謀。其間知周子者，抑有人焉，其說安在？朱子後周程而出，往来於饒信南康之境多矣，而二陸胥會，議竟不合。草廬吴氏乃尊信於聞知之餘。吴之為學，其於朱也、程也、周也，果符契乎？諸生論學於古，此其最切近者，不可無說也。
問：齊道德，一風俗，上之所好，民必趨焉。先王盛時，無異教，無異政，無異尚，無異情，無異心，何道歟？秦而降，俗有薄者、厚者、虛者、實者、浮者、醇者、仁厚者，何施歟？要之，上之化也，而士夫之風軌欬動，則又有可舉者。夫感二絹之遺，而縣無復盜；激一布之恵，而道不拾遺。學古人，居晉鄙，而薰德者善良；負孤兒，隱山陽，而感
translation_en:
…chapter, when discussing the transmission of the succession of the Way, he always mentions Cheng but does not mention Zhou. Why is this? Zhou’s learning had already been transmitted to the two Cheng brothers. At that time, there were Ouyang of Luling, Zeng of Nanfeng, Huang of Yuzhang, Wang of Linchuan, and Li of Xujiang. Each pursued his own learning without consulting the others. Yet among them there were some who understood Master Zhou. Where are their statements to be found? Master Zhu appeared after Zhou and Cheng and frequently traveled through Raozhou, Xinzhou, and Nankang. The two Lu brothers met with him, yet their discussions ultimately failed to produce agreement. Wu Caolu, however, came to revere and trust him through what he learned at second hand. Did Wu’s learning truly accord with that of Zhu, Cheng, and Zhou? As you candidates discuss the learning of the ancients, these are matters of the most immediate relevance; you must offer an explanation.
Question: To bring moral principles into accord and unify customs, whatever those above favor, the people will surely pursue. In the flourishing age of the former kings, there were no divergent teachings, policies, preferences, sentiments, or intentions. By what means was this achieved? From the Qin onward, customs have been mean or generous, hollow or substantial, frivolous or sincere, or benevolent and kind. What measures brought these about? In essence, these resulted from the transforming influence of those above. Yet examples can also be cited of the exemplary conduct and influence [?] of scholar-officials. Moved by a gift of two lengths of silk, a county ceased to have thieves; stirred by the kindness of a gift of one length of cloth, people left lost property untouched on the road. One who studied the ancients lived in a remote district of Jin, and those imbued with his virtue became good and upright; another carried an orphan on his back and withdrew to Shanyang, and those moved by him …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
行者脩義可指言歟江西人物稱首文
獻開先東湖有思賢之亭京師有忠烈
之廟忠肅堅始終持立之操清純來遠
近受業之多夫雖無老成人亦有典刑
所以端鄉國之習者固已久矣久則難
變也井田一也廢之然復之亦然俗一
也變華効胡然變胡効華亦然由是觀
之俗之情安於所習駭於所未見習素
善驅之惡不能入也然則士生其鄉豈
===
非其幸而道德文章素甲於天下者謂
非先正之力然歟請對
問古之爲國者四今存者學古之爲學者
四今存者誦此宋人之論也以今觀之
其存者有幾乎夫既有學矣所缺者何
政既有誦矣所遺者何事雖然今之學
非古之學也今之誦非古之誦也苟欲
復之當何致力由是二者求復其餘於
斯六者孰先孰後孰緩孰急孰難孰易
punctuated:
行者脩義，可指言歟？江西人物稱首，文獻開先。東湖有思賢之亭，京師有忠烈之廟。忠肅堅始終持立之操，清純來遠近受業之多。夫雖無老成人，亦有典刑。所以端鄉國之習者，固已久矣。久則難變也。井田一也，廢之然，復之亦然；俗一也，變華効胡然，變胡効華亦然。由是觀之，俗之情安於所習，駭於所未見。習素善，驅之惡，不能入也。然則士生其鄉，豈非其幸？而道德文章素甲於天下者，謂非先正之力然歟？請對。
問：古之爲國者四，今存者學；古之爲學者四，今存者誦。此宋人之論也。以今觀之，其存者有幾乎？夫既有學矣，所缺者何政？既有誦矣，所遺者何事？雖然，今之學非古之學也，今之誦非古之誦也。苟欲復之，當何致力？由是二者求復其餘，於斯六者，孰先孰後，孰緩孰急，孰難孰易？
translation_en:
…those whose conduct was influenced cultivated righteousness. Can you identify and discuss these examples? Jiangxi ranks foremost in distinguished people and has led the way in texts and learned worthies. At Donghu there is a Pavilion for Remembering the Worthy; in the capital there is a Shrine to the Loyal and Martyred. The figure honored as “Loyal and Reverent” steadfastly maintained his integrity from beginning to end; the “Pure and Unsullied” figure [?] attracted many students from near and far. Though the venerable elders are no more, their exemplary standards remain. The influences that have set local customs aright have thus been at work for a very long time. What has endured long is difficult to change. The well-field system illustrates the same principle: this holds for its abolition, and likewise for its restoration. Customs are no different: this holds when Chinese ways are changed to imitate those of the Hu, and likewise when Hu ways are changed to imitate Chinese ones. Viewed thus, the nature of custom is to rest content with what is familiar and recoil from what has never been seen. Where established habits are good, even if people are driven toward evil, it cannot take hold. Is it not fortunate, then, for scholars to be born in such a place? And when its moral cultivation and literary achievement have long ranked foremost under Heaven, can one say that this is not owing to the efforts of former worthies? Please respond.
Question: Of the four ancient institutions for governing a state, only schools survive today; of the four ancient practices of learning, only recitation survives today. This is an argument made by a man of the Song dynasty. Judged from the present, how much of these really survives? Given that schools already exist, which institutions of government are lacking? Given that recitation already exists, which practices have been left out? Nevertheless, today’s schools are not the schools of antiquity, and today’s recitation is not the recitation of antiquity. If we wish to restore them, where should we direct our efforts? Starting from these two surviving elements and seeking to restore the remainder, which of those six should come first and which later? Which may wait and which are urgent? Which are difficult and which easy? …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
得其意而不必更其制漢以下君臣亦
嘗有論矣不然則於時制之中亦可得
古人之意也諸生其詳著之
問帝王之於夷狄服則有一視之仁叛則
有一怒之勇制御之道自古為然惟我
聖祖之訓謂當選將練兵謹備胡戎而於諸夷
乃特列國名以致無故興兵之戒其
洪謨遠畧何獨異於帝王與昔之論者或謂
周得中策漢得下策而秦無策或謂周
===
得上策秦得中策而漢無策辨而未詳
其失孰歸其於所謂選將練兵者抑孰
為合歟今燕薊以西甘凉以東疆埸距
胡戎者皆古要害之地求古之人有居
鴈門以怯敵敵者有次細柳以靜却虜
者有屯金城以計降羌者有嚴備以盟
回紇者有紆籌以制吐蕃者有聲威震
於西夏者今復有若人乎如其未也何
法以求之何道以任之何術以御之而
punctuated:
得其意而不必更其制，漢以下君臣亦嘗有論矣。不然，則於時制之中亦可得古人之意也。諸生其詳著之。

問：帝王之於夷狄，服則有一視之仁，叛則有一怒之勇，制御之道自古為然。惟我聖祖之訓，謂當選將練兵，謹備胡戎，而於諸夷乃特列國名，以致無故興兵之戒。其洪謨遠畧，何獨異於帝王與？昔之論者或謂周得中策，漢得下策，而秦無策；或謂周得上策，秦得中策，而漢無策。辨而未詳，其失孰歸？其於所謂選將練兵者，抑孰為合歟？今燕薊以西、甘凉以東，疆埸距胡戎者，皆古要害之地。求古之人，有居鴈門以怯敵敵者，有次細柳以靜却虜者，有屯金城以計降羌者，有嚴備以盟回紇者，有紆籌以制吐蕃者，有聲威震於西夏者。今復有若人乎？如其未也，何法以求之，何道以任之，何術以御之，而
translation_en:
…to grasp their intent without necessarily changing the institutions: rulers and ministers from the Han onward have also discussed this. Otherwise, even within the institutions of the present age, one may recover the intent of the ancients. You candidates should set this out in detail.

Question: In their dealings with the Yi and Di, emperors and kings show the benevolence of treating all alike when these peoples submit, and the courage of rising in wrath when they rebel. Such has been the way of controlling them since antiquity. Yet the instructions of our Sagely Progenitor state that commanders should be selected and troops trained, and that careful defenses should be maintained against the Hu and Rong; regarding the various foreign peoples, he specifically listed their countries by name to convey his admonition against launching wars without cause. Why do his grand designs and far-reaching strategies alone differ from those of the emperors and kings?

Among earlier commentators, some held that the Zhou adopted a middling policy, the Han an inferior policy, and the Qin had no policy at all; others held that the Zhou adopted the best policy, the Qin a middling policy, and the Han had no policy at all. These arguments have not been fully clarified: to whom should error be attributed? Which accords with the injunction to select commanders and train troops?

Today, west of Yan and Ji and east of Gan and Liang, the frontier regions confronting the Hu and Rong are all places of strategic importance from antiquity. Looking for examples among men of old, there was one who held Yanmen and intimidated the enemy [the transcription repeats “enemy,” 敵, here; ?]; one who encamped at Xiliu and repelled the foe through calm discipline; one who stationed troops at Jincheng and induced the Qiang to surrender through stratagem; one who maintained stringent defenses and thereby secured an alliance with the Huihe; one who devised plans to control the Tufan; and one whose renown and might struck awe into Western Xia. Are there such men again today? If there are not yet, by what methods should they be sought, in what manner should they be employed, and by what means should they be directed, and …

translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“When those above cherish righteousness, none of the people dare fail to submit.”

Liu Jie

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: The topic is exceptionally straightforward. Most candidates here fail to make “righteousness” and “submission” correspond adequately in their essays; moreover, their language and ideas are superficial and verbose, making them tiresome to read. This paper alone makes the principle clear in a few unforced words. Compared with [?] those devoted solely to superficial ornament, it is distinctive. Select it for inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Cherishing righteousness and the people’s submission constitute stimulus and response according to kind. The author has grasped this thread. The essay uses no unnecessary words, yet its meaning runs coherently throughout. This is someone who understands the principle; the paper deserves selection.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, School Instructor: On this topic, few candidates here can develop the point about cherishing righteousness, while their treatment of submission is disjointed and fails to convey a response according to kind. Moreover, many force connections with the idea that the people submit when the upright are raised above the crooked [?], greatly departing from the topic’s original intent. An essay such as this, with clear reasoning and fluent language, deserves selection and should head this examining section’s papers.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: It dispenses with empty ornament and achieves concision and precision. It deserves selection.

Comment by Examiner Han, School Instructor: Its discussion of righteousness and submission connects the two throughout. This is precisely how the meaning should be conveyed. Include it.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
應顧慼之者何如耳然則上能慮事合其宜而
民焉有不服者乎昔夫子因樊遲問稼圃既辭
而非之矣俟其既出復言之而使聞焉意謂稼
圃小人之事不必學也所當為者不有大人之
事乎彼大人之事有所謂義焉乃心之制事之
宜也上能精在我之權度於凡所設施者惟義
是好而適莫之心不存在事之質幹於凡所
措置者惟義是尚而信果之意不留政治所在
有關民利病者處之惟公舉有以當乎人心法
===
令所存有係民休戚者施之惟正舉有以合乎
事宜夫上能好義如此吾知以下事上亦義當
然下民得於觀感者悅服之心油然以興順從
之念翕然以動供正徃役盡職分於政治之下
或遠或近敢有不從者乎所以然者非强之使
從也從乎義也畏威遠罪遵約束於法令之中
無小無大敢有不服者乎所以爾者非驅之使
服也服乎義也吁一義感於上衆心應於下如
此則大人之事自有可為者矣惡用稼圃學哉
punctuated: 應，顧慼之者何如耳。然則上能慮事合其宜，而民焉有不服者乎？昔夫子因樊遲問稼圃，既辭而非之矣，俟其既出，復言之而使聞焉。意謂稼圃，小人之事，不必學也。所當為者，不有大人之事乎？彼大人之事，有所謂義焉，乃心之制、事之宜也。上能精在我之權度，於凡所設施者惟義是好，而適莫之心不存；在事之質幹，於凡所措置者惟義是尚，而信果之意不留。政治所在，有關民利病者，處之惟公，舉有以當乎人心；法令所存，有係民休戚者，施之惟正，舉有以合乎事宜。夫上能好義如此，吾知以下事上，亦義當然。下民得於觀感者，悅服之心油然以興，順從之念翕然以動。供正徃役，盡職分於政治之下，或遠或近，敢有不從者乎？所以然者，非强之使從也，從乎義也。畏威遠罪，遵約束於法令之中，無小無大，敢有不服者乎？所以爾者，非驅之使服也，服乎義也。吁！一義感於上，衆心應於下。如此，則大人之事自有可為者矣，惡用稼圃學哉？
translation_en:
…respond depends simply on how those above regard and care for them [?]. If those above can deliberate on affairs and act appropriately, how could the people fail to submit? Formerly, when Fan Chi asked about farming and gardening, the Master declined to instruct him and condemned his request. After Fan Chi had left, he spoke further so that Fan Chi would hear of it. His meaning was that farming and gardening were the occupations of lesser men and need not be studied. Were there not the affairs of the great man that he ought to undertake? Among the affairs of the great man is what is called righteousness: the mind’s power to judge and the appropriateness of affairs.

If those above can refine their own standards of judgment, delighting solely in righteousness in everything they institute, no disposition to favor or reject things arbitrarily will remain. In attending to the essential substance of affairs [?], if they esteem righteousness alone in everything they arrange, no insistence on keeping one’s word and carrying out one’s resolve regardless of circumstances will linger. In matters of government affecting the people’s welfare or distress, they deal with them impartially, so that every action accords with the people’s hearts. In laws and ordinances affecting the people’s well-being or suffering, they act with rectitude, so that every measure suits the circumstances.

If those above can thus delight in righteousness, I know that serving one’s superiors from below will likewise be recognized as what righteousness requires. Through observing and being moved by their example, the people below will spontaneously develop a willing submission, and their desire to obey will arise in unison. Providing what is required [?] and going forth to perform service, they fulfill their proper duties under the government. Whether far or near, would any dare not comply? They do so not because they are forced to comply, but because they follow righteousness. Fearing authority and avoiding wrongdoing, they observe the restraints imposed by laws and ordinances. In matters small or great, would any dare not submit? They do so not because they are driven into submission, but because they submit to righteousness.

Ah! Righteousness alone, exerting its influence above, elicits a response in the hearts of the multitude below. Thus there are indeed affairs of the great man worth undertaking. What need is there to study farming and gardening?

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
嗟夫聖賢之學明德新民非二道也故雖勢在
匹夫之賤而所以堯舜其君民者皆其分内事
耳樊遲所師者何人所志者何道而乃以稼圃
為問何其陋哉吾夫子以大人禮義信告於既
出之後所以曉之之意至深切矣厥後問仁問
智而知大人之道其亦有得聖教之深歟
故君子内省不疚無惡於志
李文潔
同考試官教諭林　批〔潛伏之地公私誠偽之幾正〕
〔君子心學第一關此作於題旨發越精透盖究心〕
〔於此者歟〕
===
同考試官學正章　批〔作者於不疚無惡處以易〕
〔忽之率多體認不真下筆便語意重複令人可〕
〔厭此篇能以雄健之筆性理之詞發揮得出知其〕
〔志於謹獨之學久矣哉〕
考試官教諭黄　批〔說理明白〕
考試官學正韓　批〔簡明說理文字良是〕
君子自求乎心之純而自得其心之慊與謹獨
punctuated:
嗟夫！聖賢之學，明德新民，非二道也。故雖勢在匹夫之賤，而所以堯舜其君民者，皆其分内事耳。樊遲所師者何人？所志者何道？而乃以稼圃為問，何其陋哉！吾夫子以大人禮義信告於既出之後，所以曉之之意至深切矣。厥後問仁問智，而知大人之道，其亦有得聖教之深歟？

故君子内省不疚，無惡於志。
李文潔

同考試官教諭林　批〔潛伏之地，公私誠偽之幾，正〕〔君子心學第一關。此作於題旨發越精透，盖究心〕〔於此者歟？〕

同考試官學正章　批〔作者於不疚無惡處，以易〕〔忽之，率多體認不真，下筆便語意重複，令人可〕〔厭。此篇能以雄健之筆、性理之詞發揮得出，知其〕〔志於謹獨之學久矣哉！〕

考試官教諭黄　批〔說理明白。〕

考試官學正韓　批〔簡明說理，文字良是。〕

君子自求乎心之純，而自得其心之慊與？謹獨
translation_en:
Alas! In the learning of sages and worthies, illuminating virtue and renewing the people are not two separate ways. Thus, even when occupying the humble station of a common man, whatever serves to make his ruler and people like Yao and Shun falls within his own proper responsibilities. Whom did Fan Chi take as his teacher? To what Way did he aspire? Yet he asked about growing grain and vegetables—how narrow his outlook! After Fan Chi had gone out, our Master spoke of the great man's ritual propriety, righteousness, and trustworthiness; his intention to enlighten him was profoundly earnest. Later, Fan Chi asked about benevolence and wisdom and came to understand the way of the great man. Had he perhaps also attained a deep understanding of the sage's teaching?

“Thus the gentleman examines himself inwardly and finds no cause for guilt, having no evil in his intentions.”
By Li Wenjie.

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “In the hidden recesses lie the first stirrings of public-mindedness and selfishness, sincerity and falsity: precisely the first checkpoint in the gentleman's learning of the mind. This composition develops the meaning of the topic with penetrating precision. Perhaps its author has devoted close attention to this?”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Writers often treat ‘no cause for guilt’ and ‘no evil’ as easy and neglect them, generally failing to comprehend them truly. Once they begin writing, their wording and ideas become repetitive and tiresome. This essay succeeds in bringing out their meaning through vigorous writing and the language of human nature and principle. We can tell that its author has long devoted himself to the learning of vigilance in solitude!”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “The principles are explained clearly.”

Comment by Examiner Han, Instructor: “The explanation of principles is concise and clear; the writing is very sound.”

Does the gentleman himself seek purity of mind and thereby attain inward satisfaction? Vigilance in solitude …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之功也夫心有不純者欲累之也能無所累則
自慊矣君子謹獨之功一何至哉中庸卒章言
君子下學之事至此引小雅正月之詩而申之
若曰潛伏之地雖隱微而難知事理之幾則顯
著而易見君子於此豈待徵於色而後省耶幾
一動也人雖不知而已則獨知即從而省之何
者為公何者為私私間乎公心之病也必純乎
公而私不能間則吾心無所病焉抑豈待發於
聲而後察耶念一萌也人雖不見而已則獨見
===
即從而察之何者為誠何者為偽偽雜乎誠心
之疵也必純乎誠而偽不能雜則吾心無所疵
焉內省不疚如此又豈有所惡於志哉蓋志者
心之所之公而無私天之則也私或病焉未能
無愧矣今也既純乎公則所發者揆諸天則而
允協于神明之舍夫何有所愧乎誠而無偽天
之命也偽或疵焉未能無惡矣今也既純乎誠
則所發者質諸天命而信乎于虛靈之境夫何
有所惡乎君子謹獨而能自慊如此此其所以為
punctuated: 之功也。夫心有不純者，欲累之也。能無所累，則自慊矣。君子謹獨之功，一何至哉！《中庸》卒章言君子下學之事，至此引《小雅·正月》之詩而申之，若曰：潛伏之地，雖隱微而難知，事理之幾，則顯著而易見。君子於此，豈待徵於色而後省耶？幾一動也，人雖不知，而已則獨知，即從而省之：何者為公？何者為私？私間乎公，心之病也。必純乎公，而私不能間，則吾心無所病焉。抑豈待發於聲而後察耶？念一萌也，人雖不見，而已則獨見，即從而察之：何者為誠？何者為偽？偽雜乎誠，心之疵也。必純乎誠，而偽不能雜，則吾心無所疵焉。內省不疚如此，又豈有所惡於志哉？蓋志者，心之所之。公而無私，天之則也；私或病焉，未能無愧矣。今也既純乎公，則所發者揆諸天則，而允協于神明之舍，夫何有所愧乎？誠而無偽，天之命也；偽或疵焉，未能無惡矣。今也既純乎誠，則所發者質諸天命，而信乎于虛靈之境，夫何有所惡乎？君子謹獨而能自慊如此，此其所以為
translation_en: …is the achievement of vigilance in solitude. When the heart is impure, it is because desires burden it. If it can be free of such burdens, it will be content within itself. How consummate is the gentleman’s achievement through vigilance in solitude! The final chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean discusses the gentleman’s learning in ordinary affairs. At this point it quotes the poem “The First Month” from the Lesser Odes to elaborate its meaning, as if to say: although what lies concealed is obscure and difficult to know, the incipient stirrings of the principles governing affairs are manifest and easy to perceive. Must the gentleman wait until these show in his countenance before examining himself? As soon as a stirring occurs, though others do not know it, he alone knows it, and immediately examines it: which is impartial, and which is selfish? Selfishness intruding upon impartiality is a sickness of the heart. Only when impartiality is pure and selfishness cannot intrude will my heart be free of sickness. Or must he wait until a thought finds expression in sound before scrutinizing it? As soon as a thought arises, though others do not see it, he alone sees it, and immediately scrutinizes it: which is sincere, and which is false? Falsehood mingling with sincerity is a blemish of the heart. Only when sincerity is pure and falsehood cannot mingle with it will my heart be free of blemish. When inward examination thus reveals no cause for remorse, how could there be anything objectionable in one’s intentions? For intention is the direction in which the heart moves. To be impartial and without selfishness is Heaven’s rule. If selfishness afflicts the heart, one cannot yet be free of shame. Now that impartiality is pure, whatever issues from the heart accords with Heaven’s rule when measured against it, and truly harmonizes with the abode of spiritual intelligence. What cause for shame could there be? To be sincere and without falsehood is Heaven’s mandate. If falsehood blemishes the heart, one cannot yet be free of anything objectionable. Now that sincerity is pure, whatever issues from the heart proves true when tested against Heaven’s mandate, within the heart’s empty and numinously aware realm. What could there be to find objectionable? Such is the gentleman’s ability to attain inner contentment through vigilance in solitude. This is why his learning constitutes…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
為己之學而有不可及也歟大抵君子為己之
學莫要於省察尤莫要於存養聖賢相傳心法
實在於斯子思於首章既揭以示人而此復推
言之其曰不動而敬不言而信即首章所謂戒
慎恐懼也若内省之説所以申謹獨者則尤切
矣蓋必如是而後可以馴致乎不賞民勸不怒
民威篤恭而天下平之效焉中和位育之化豈
外於一心也哉故君子志於學者當自立心始
親親仁也敬長義也
葉釗
同考試官訓導劉　批　連日閲卷類多以愛親敬
長盡於孝弟之節者言之不知出於童幼自然之
性而此篇詞理明暢發出孟子之意親切是可
與論性學矣
同考試官教諭潘　批　雖不掉弄文法而意義自
足深得本領文字體
同考試官教諭傅　批　孟子七篇仁義惟此章從
人良知良能説来最為精切此卷辭純縝而理亦
punctuated:
為己之學而有不可及也歟？大抵君子為己之學，莫要於省察，尤莫要於存養。聖賢相傳心法，實在於斯。子思於首章既揭以示人，而此復推言之。其曰「不動而敬，不言而信」，即首章所謂戒慎恐懼也。若内省之説，所以申謹獨者，則尤切矣。蓋必如是，而後可以馴致乎不賞民勸、不怒民威、篤恭而天下平之效焉。中和位育之化，豈外於一心也哉？故君子志於學者，當自立心始。

親親仁也，敬長義也。
葉釗

同考試官訓導劉批：連日閲卷，類多以愛親敬長盡於孝弟之節者言之，不知出於童幼自然之性。而此篇詞理明暢，發出孟子之意親切，是可與論性學矣。

同考試官教諭潘批：雖不掉弄文法，而意義自足，深得本領文字體。

同考試官教諭傅批：孟子七篇仁義，惟此章從人良知良能説来，最為精切。此卷辭純縝，而理亦
translation_en:
…learning for one’s own sake, in which he cannot be equaled? In general, for the gentleman’s learning for his own sake, nothing is more essential than self-examination—and still more essential is preserving and nurturing the mind. Here indeed lies the method of cultivating the mind transmitted by the sages and worthies. Zisi already set it forth for others in the opening chapter, and here he elaborates upon it again. The words “reverent without acting, trustworthy without speaking” refer precisely to the caution, vigilance, fear, and apprehension spoken of in the opening chapter. As for the discussion of inward examination, it is especially pertinent in elaborating upon watchfulness over oneself when alone. Only through this can one gradually achieve the effects whereby the people are encouraged without rewards, stand in awe without displays of anger, and all under Heaven is brought to peace through earnest reverence. Could the transforming power of equilibrium and harmony, through which Heaven and Earth take their proper places and all things are nurtured, lie outside this single mind? Thus, the gentleman who aspires to learning must begin by establishing his mind.

“To love one’s parents is benevolence; to respect one’s elders is righteousness.”
Ye Zhao

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor: In reviewing papers over the past several days, I have found that most discuss loving parents and respecting elders as matters exhausted by the observances of filial piety and fraternal deference. They fail to recognize that these arise from the spontaneous nature of young children. This essay, however, is clear and fluent in both expression and reasoning, and brings out Mencius’s meaning aptly and closely. Its author is someone with whom one can discuss the study of human nature.

Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor: Although the author does not make a display of literary technique, the meaning is fully expressed. He has deeply grasped the essentials of the essay form [?].

Comment by Associate Examiner Fu, Instructor: Of the discussions of benevolence and righteousness in the seven books of Mencius, this chapter alone explains them through people’s innate knowledge and innate capacity, making it especially precise and pertinent. This paper’s language is pure and closely wrought, and its reasoning is also…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
精緻一結尤得孟子之心其殆有道者歟
考試官教諭黄　批〔得旨〕
考試官學正韓　批〔發明仁義之旨殆盡〕
大賢指良心之所發者為本心之所具者盖愛
親敬長發於良心者然也則夫仁義之具於本
心者豈有外於是哉昔孟子之意盖謂立人之
道曰仁與義仁義之心不為人皆有乎彼子之
於親分於一體故人當夫幼也無不知愛其親
欣慕之意藹然於孩抱之間眷戀之情油然於
===
提攜之頃此果何為而然哉人有此心即具此
仁仁主於愛而愛莫切於愛親惟帝降衷自有
不能已者借曰非仁則有待於習矣然則親親
不謂之仁而何哉弟之於兄出於一氣故人及
其長也無不知敬其兄一飲食歟而推讓之不
忽一起居歟而順遜之有序此又何為而然哉
人有此心即有此義義主於敬而敬莫先於敬
兄惟民秉彝自有不容遏者借曰非義則有事
於脩矣然則敬長不謂之義而何哉吁親親為
punctuated:
精緻，一結尤得孟子之心，其殆有道者歟！
考試官教諭黄批〔得旨〕
考試官學正韓批〔發明仁義之旨殆盡〕
大賢指良心之所發者為本心之所具者。盖愛親敬長，發於良心者然也，則夫仁義之具於本心者，豈有外於是哉？昔孟子之意，盖謂立人之道曰仁與義，仁義之心，不為人皆有乎？彼子之於親，分於一體，故人當夫幼也，無不知愛其親。欣慕之意，藹然於孩抱之間；眷戀之情，油然於提攜之頃。此果何為而然哉？人有此心，即具此仁。仁主於愛，而愛莫切於愛親。惟帝降衷，自有不能已者。借曰非仁，則有待於習矣。然則親親，不謂之仁而何哉？弟之於兄，出於一氣，故人及其長也，無不知敬其兄。一飲食歟，而推讓之不忽；一起居歟，而順遜之有序。此又何為而然哉？人有此心，即有此義。義主於敬，而敬莫先於敬兄。惟民秉彝，自有不容遏者。借曰非義，則有事於脩矣。然則敬長，不謂之義而何哉？吁！親親為
translation_en:
…is refined and precise. The conclusion especially captures Mencius’s intent. Surely its author is one who possesses the Way!
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔Captures the essential meaning.〕
Examiner Han, School Director, comments: 〔Elucidates the meaning of benevolence and righteousness almost completely.〕
The great worthy identifies what issues from the good heart as what is inherently present in the original heart. For loving one’s parents and respecting one’s elders are indeed expressions of the good heart. How, then, could the benevolence and righteousness inherent in the original heart lie outside these? Mencius’s intention was, in substance, to say: the Way that establishes humanity consists of benevolence and righteousness. Does not everyone possess a heart of benevolence and righteousness? A child and its parents have divided from a single body. Thus, when people are young, none fail to know to love their parents. Joyful affection flourishes while they are babes in arms; fond attachment wells up as they are led by the hand. Why, indeed, is this so? Possessing this heart, a person already possesses this benevolence. Benevolence centers on love, and no love is more intimate than love for one’s parents. The Lord on High has bestowed this moral nature, and it naturally contains impulses that cannot cease. Suppose this were not benevolence: then benevolence would have to await practice. What, then, should loving one’s parents be called, if not benevolence?
A younger brother and his elder brother arise from the same vital force. Thus, as people grow older, none fail to know to respect their elder brothers. At every meal they yield precedence without neglect; in every daily activity they defer in due order. Why, again, is this so? Possessing this heart, a person already possesses this righteousness. Righteousness centers on respect, and no respect takes precedence over respect for one’s elder brother. The people hold fast to their constant moral nature, and it naturally contains impulses that cannot be suppressed. Suppose this were not righteousness: then righteousness would require cultivation. What, then, should respecting one’s elders be called, if not righteousness? Ah! Loving one’s parents constitutes…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
仁仁出於天下之同愛敬長為義義出於天下
之同敬仁義之在人如此而可以不求乎雖然
孟子七篇無非性善仁義之說或以惻隱言仁
或以羞惡言義固皆即情見性而惟之所發惟
愛親敬長之心出於天不係於人視夫有感而
應者尤為真切故孟子又指言之其欲人知仁
義不假外求而勇於用力者至矣以此為教猶
有曠安宅舍正路而弗居弗由者可勝嘆哉
易
===
觀天之神道而四時不忒
葉釗
同考試官訓導劉　批〔天之神道正在四時不忒上見作者多含糊不明此篇卓有所見是用錄出以〕
式來學
同考試官教諭潘　批〔說盡天道所以為觀之意而略不費力佳作也〕
同考試官教諭傅　批〔此題重在神道上而四時不忒乃神道行乎其間學者多昧此而兩析之不知本義所〕
punctuated:
仁，仁出於天下之同愛；敬長為義，義出於天下之同敬。仁義之在人如此，而可以不求乎？雖然，孟子七篇無非性善仁義之說，或以惻隱言仁，或以羞惡言義，固皆即情見性，而惟之所發，惟愛親敬長之心出於天，不係於人，視夫有感而應者尤為真切，故孟子又指言之。其欲人知仁義不假外求而勇於用力者至矣。以此為教，猶有曠安宅、舍正路而弗居弗由者，可勝嘆哉！

易

觀天之神道而四時不忒

葉釗

同考試官訓導劉，批〔天之神道正在四時不忒上見，作者多含糊不明，此篇卓有所見，是用錄出以〕式來學。

同考試官教諭潘，批〔說盡天道所以為觀之意，而略不費力，佳作也。〕

同考試官教諭傅，批〔此題重在神道上，而四時不忒乃神道行乎其間。學者多昧此而兩析之，不知本義所〕
translation_en:
…benevolence. Benevolence arises from the love shared by all under Heaven; respecting one's elders constitutes righteousness, and righteousness arises from the respect shared by all under Heaven. Since benevolence and righteousness exist in people in this way, can one fail to seek them? Nevertheless, the seven books of the Mengzi consist entirely of teachings about the goodness of human nature, benevolence, and righteousness. Sometimes compassion is used to explain benevolence, and sometimes shame and aversion to wrongdoing are used to explain righteousness. These certainly all reveal human nature through the feelings, in what they express [?]. Yet the heart that loves one's parents and respects one's elders comes from Heaven and does not depend on human effort. Compared with feelings that respond to an external stimulus, it is especially genuine and immediate. Thus Mengzi also singles it out for discussion. His desire that people understand that benevolence and righteousness need not be sought externally, and that they apply themselves resolutely, could not be greater. Even with this teaching, there are still those who leave the peaceful dwelling empty and abandon the right road, neither dwelling in the one nor following the other. Can one ever cease lamenting this?

Book of Changes

“Observe Heaven's numinous Way: the four seasons never deviate.”

Ye Zhao

Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Heaven's numinous Way is manifested precisely in the unfailing regularity of the four seasons. Writers are often vague and unclear about this. This essay displays exceptional insight, and has therefore been selected and recorded to serve as a model for future students.”

Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor, comments: “It fully explains the sense in which Heaven's Way constitutes ‘contemplation,’ without the slightest strain. An excellent composition.”

Associate Examiner Fu, Instructor, comments: “The emphasis of this topic lies in the numinous Way, while the unfailing regularity of the four seasons is that Way operating within them. Students often fail to understand this and analyze the two separately, not understanding what the Original Meaning …”

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
以立言之意此篇融貫昭晰而一結尤知所重故表出之
考試官教諭黄　批〔理致之學正如此〕
考試官學正韓　批〔易義明正可録〕
觀上天涵妙用而歲成見其所以為觀也盖天
道之神妙運於四時而歲功成焉其所為觀者
此耳宜彖傳以是極言觀道歟昔伏羲畫卦以
觀名文王既係其辭矣吾夫子彖傳至此極言
觀之道以謂觀之義著于易而其道見於天彼
立天之道曰陰與陽觀夫維天之命動而生陽
===
人知天之為天矣不知其道之神化無方動而
無動焉上天之載靜而生陰盖曰天之為天矣
不知其道之神妙莫測靜而無靜焉動靜無端
陰陽無始唯合一也又兩在也天道之涵其妙
用如此然而陰陽動靜闔闢變通互為其根故
自一陽之復起于冬至歷震離之間為春分以
至於乾為純陽此則皆鼓自陽動神道之出機
故時春而春時夏而夏各司其令無所差忒焉
自一陰之姤起于夏至歷坎艮之間為秋分以
punctuated:
以立言之意。此篇融貫昭晰，而一結尤知所重，故表出之。
考試官教諭黄批〔理致之學，正如此。〕
考試官學正韓批〔易義明正，可録。〕
觀上天涵妙用，而歲成見其所以為觀也。盖天道之神，妙運於四時，而歲功成焉。其所為觀者，此耳。宜彖傳以是極言觀道歟！昔伏羲畫卦，以觀名，文王既係其辭矣。吾夫子彖傳至此，極言觀之道，以謂觀之義著于易，而其道見於天。彼立天之道，曰陰與陽。觀夫維天之命，動而生陽，人知天之為天矣，不知其道之神，化無方，動而無動焉。上天之載，靜而生陰，盖曰天之為天矣，不知其道之神，妙莫測，靜而無靜焉。動靜無端，陰陽無始，唯合一也，又兩在也。天道之涵其妙用如此。然而陰陽動靜，闔闢變通，互為其根。故自一陽之復起于冬至，歷震離之間為春分，以至於乾為純陽，此則皆鼓自陽動，神道之出機。故時春而春，時夏而夏，各司其令，無所差忒焉。自一陰之姤起于夏至，歷坎艮之間為秋分，以
translation_en:
…the intention behind its formulation. This essay integrates its argument with luminous clarity, and its conclusion especially shows an understanding of what deserves emphasis. I have therefore singled it out.

Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔This is precisely what learning concerned with the principles of things should be like.〕

Examiner Han, Director of Studies, comments: 〔Its interpretation of the Changes is clear and correct; it merits inclusion.〕

Observe how Heaven above contains wondrous workings: in the completion of the year, one sees how it serves as an object of contemplation. For the numinous operation of Heaven’s Way works wondrously through the four seasons, bringing the year’s work to completion. This alone is what makes it an object of contemplation. Surely it is fitting that the Commentary on the Judgments should use this to expound fully the Way of Contemplation! Long ago, Fuxi drew the hexagrams and named one Contemplation (Guan); King Wen subsequently attached its statement. When our Master Confucius reached this point in the Commentary on the Judgments, he fully expounded the Way of Contemplation, holding that its meaning is made manifest in the Changes, while its Way is visible in Heaven. What establishes the Way of Heaven is called yin and yang. Consider Heaven’s mandate: through movement it generates yang. People recognize that this is what makes Heaven Heaven, but do not understand the numinous character of its Way: its transformations have no fixed bounds, and it moves without movement. The workings of Heaven above generate yin through stillness. This, one might say, is what makes Heaven Heaven; yet people do not understand the numinous character of its Way: its wondrousness is unfathomable, and it is still without stillness. Movement and stillness have no first point; yin and yang have no beginning. They are united as one, yet both are present. Such is the manner in which Heaven’s Way contains its wondrous workings.

Yet yin and yang, movement and stillness, closing and opening, transformation and continuity, each serve as the root of the other. Thus, beginning with Return (Fu), with its single yang line, at the winter solstice, the cycle passes through the interval between Zhen and Li at the spring equinox and reaches Qian, which is pure yang. All this is impelled by the movement of yang, the outgoing impulse of the numinous Way. Thus, when it is time for spring, spring comes; when it is time for summer, summer comes. Each administers its seasonal ordinance without deviation. Beginning with Encounter (Gou), with its single yin line, at the summer solstice, the cycle passes through the interval between Kan and Gen at the autumn equinox, and …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
至於坤為純陰此則皆鼓自陰靜神道之入機
故時秋而秋時冬而冬各循其度無所忒忒焉
其運於歲功之成者又如此吁四時以神道而
不忒天道以四時而為觀傳易以此極言觀道
其旨微矣抑論觀之為道誠大矣而聖人之所
以為觀者亦不外此蓋聖人順性命之理通幽
明之故以神道設教而天下服亦猶天道之神
使非神焉則非所謂天地無心而成化聖人有
心而無為者矣大傳曰陰陽不測之謂神孟子
曰聖而不可知之之謂神曰不測曰不可知非
知道者孰能識之
齊小大者存乎卦
王萱
同考試官訓導劉　批〔題本正大作者多於齊小大處講欠精切此篇獨用易說深合本旨故錄之〕
同考試官教諭潘　批〔無贅詞無冗字作易義正要如此〕
同考試官教諭傅　批〔天地間陰陽大分自然一〕
punctuated:
至於坤為純陰，此則皆鼓自陰靜，神道之入機。故時秋而秋，時冬而冬，各循其度，無所忒忒焉。其運於歲功之成者又如此。吁！四時以神道而不忒，天道以四時而為觀。傳易以此極言觀道，其旨微矣。抑論觀之為道，誠大矣，而聖人之所以為觀者亦不外此。蓋聖人順性命之理，通幽明之故，以神道設教而天下服，亦猶天道之神。使非神焉，則非所謂天地無心而成化，聖人有心而無為者矣。《大傳》曰：「陰陽不測之謂神。」《孟子》曰：「聖而不可知之之謂神。」曰不測，曰不可知，非知道者孰能識之？

齊小大者存乎卦。
王萱
同考試官訓導劉，批〔題本正大，作者多於齊小大處講欠精切。此篇獨用易說，深合本旨，故錄之。〕
同考試官教諭潘，批〔無贅詞，無冗字，作易義正要如此。〕
同考試官教諭傅，批〔天地間陰陽大分，自然一〕
translation_en:
…reaching Kun, which is pure yin. All this is set in motion by yin’s stillness: the inward-working mechanism of the numinous Way. Thus, when autumn is due, autumn comes; when winter is due, winter comes. Each follows its proper measure without deviation [the transcription repeats 忒]. Such, too, is its operation in completing the work of the year. Ah! Through the numinous Way, the four seasons proceed without error; through the four seasons, the Way of Heaven becomes an object of contemplation. The commentary on the Changes uses this to express fully the Way of Contemplation: its meaning is subtle indeed. Moreover, the Way of Contemplation is truly great, yet the means by which the sage becomes an exemplar likewise extend no further than this. The sage follows the principles of human nature and destiny and comprehends the workings of the unseen and the manifest. He establishes instruction through the numinous Way, and all under Heaven submit, just as they do to the numinous operation of Heaven’s Way. Were this not numinous, it would not accord with the saying that Heaven and Earth accomplish transformation without deliberate intention, while the sage has intention yet acts without contrivance. The Great Commentary says: “What cannot be fathomed in yin and yang is called numinous.” The Mencius says: “A sage who cannot be known is called numinous” [the transcription repeats 之]. Called “unfathomable” and “unknowable”—who but one who understands the Way could recognize it?

“Ordering the Small and the Great Rests with the Hexagrams.”
By Wang Xuan.

Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The topic is fundamentally correct and grand. Most writers lack precision and pertinence in explaining ‘ordering the small and the great.’ This essay alone employs explanations of the Changes that accord profoundly with the original meaning; hence its inclusion.”

Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor, comments: “There are no superfluous phrases or redundant words. This is precisely how an essay interpreting the Changes should be written.”

Associate Examiner Fu, Instructor, comments: “Between Heaven and Earth, the fundamental division between yin and yang is naturally …”

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
定特假手於聖人齊之耳而聖人作易豈有意於
其間亦自然之妙有不容言者達於文而造其理
無踰此篇
考試官教諭黃　批〔通暢有理〕
考試官學正韓　批〔精潔得旨〕
定易道之大分在易畫之大成蓋陽大陰小自
有一定之分而齊之寧不在於大成之卦畫哉
昔夫子大傳釋卦爻辭之通例而此以卦言之
意謂天地之間陰陽兩端而已陰則體柔性順
===
其道私其類悪偏滯狹隘而小也陽則體剛性
健其道公其類淑光明洞達而大也陰小如此
不有以齊之則混而無別矣唯齊其陰焉為小
而不得以加乎大其分截然以判而界限之正
凛不可踰陽大如此不有以定之則紊而無序
矣唯定其陽焉為大而不可以溺于小其等秩
然以分而區類之別昭不容掩此果何所存哉
蓋存乎卦也彼聖人畫卦定位之時因重而倍
有三十二之陰卦焉凡陰卦則稱為小原始要
punctuated:
定，特假手於聖人齊之耳。而聖人作易，豈有意於其間？亦自然之妙，有不容言者。達於文而造其理，無踰此篇。
考試官教諭黃　批〔通暢有理〕
考試官學正韓　批〔精潔得旨〕
定易道之大分，在易畫之大成。蓋陽大陰小，自有一定之分，而齊之寧不在於大成之卦畫哉？昔夫子大傳釋卦爻辭之通例，而此以卦言之。意謂天地之間，陰陽兩端而已。陰則體柔性順，其道私，其類悪，偏滯狹隘而小也。陽則體剛性健，其道公，其類淑，光明洞達而大也。陰小如此，不有以齊之，則混而無別矣。唯齊其陰焉為小，而不得以加乎大，其分截然以判，而界限之正，凛不可踰。陽大如此，不有以定之，則紊而無序矣。唯定其陽焉為大，而不可以溺于小，其等秩然以分，而區類之別，昭不容掩。此果何所存哉？蓋存乎卦也。彼聖人畫卦定位之時，因重而倍，有三十二之陰卦焉。凡陰卦則稱為小，原始要
translation_en:
…fixed; it merely works through the sages to set them in their proper order. When the sages made the Changes, how could they have imposed any deliberate intention upon this process? Here too is the subtle working of what is so of itself, something beyond expression. For conveying this in writing and penetrating its principle, no essay surpasses this one.
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔Fluent and well reasoned.〕
Examiner Han, School Director, comments: 〔Refined and concise; it captures the essential meaning.〕
Establishing the fundamental distinction within the Way of the Changes rests upon the full development of its drawn figures. For yang is great and yin is small: they inherently possess a fixed distinction. How, then, could setting them in their proper order fail to rest upon the fully developed hexagram figures? Formerly, the Master explained in the Great Commentary the general principles governing the hexagram and line statements; here he speaks in terms of the hexagrams. His meaning is that between Heaven and Earth there are only the two poles, yin and yang. Yin is yielding in substance and compliant in nature; its way is self-serving and its kind evil. Partial, obstructed, narrow, and confined, it is small. Yang is firm in substance and vigorous in nature; its way is impartial and its kind good. Luminous and thoroughly penetrating, it is great.
Since yin is small in this way, without something to set it in its proper order, all would be confused and undifferentiated. Only when yin is ordered as small and is not allowed to rise above the great is its allotted place decisively distinguished, with proper boundaries so imposing that they cannot be crossed. Since yang is great in this way, without something to establish it, all would be disordered and without sequence. Only when yang is established as great and cannot be submerged in the small are its ranks distinguished in due order, with the separation of categories so manifest that it cannot be obscured. Where, indeed, does this reside? It resides in the hexagrams.
When the sages drew the hexagrams and fixed their positions, they doubled the figures by superimposing them, producing thirty-two yin hexagrams. All yin hexagrams are designated small. Tracing their beginnings and examining…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
終有三十二之陽卦焉凡陽卦則稱爲大如自
姤之坤而屬于隂者其間爲遯爲否與夬爲巽
之諸隂卦雖不期小而自見其小斷斷乎不敢
與陽比矣分何其明邪自復之乾而列乎陽者
其中爲益爲夬與夬爲節之諸陽卦雖不期大
而自有其大卓卓乎不至與隂干矣分何其正
邪是則唯卦齊其小大如此所以然者盖天地
隂陽大分自然一定而聖人豈假絲毫知力爲
哉傳易之旨微矣大抵易爲君子謀也因例可
以槩見焉如小畜小過大畜大過之名小往大
来大往小来之義無非各指其所之或隂爲主
隂用事也或陽爲主陽用事也未嘗不致意於
抑揚之間使天下後世曉然知君子道長之爲
慶小人道消之爲幸學易者亦當致三絶韋編
方識聖人之所以爲心
書
帝光天之下至于海隅蒼生
李文潔
punctuated:
終，有三十二之陽卦焉，凡陽卦則稱爲大。如自姤之坤而屬于隂者，其間爲遯、爲否，與夬、爲巽之諸隂卦，雖不期小而自見其小，斷斷乎不敢與陽比矣，分何其明邪！自復之乾而列乎陽者，其中爲益、爲夬，與夬、爲節之諸陽卦，雖不期大而自有其大，卓卓乎不至與隂干矣，分何其正邪！是則唯卦齊其小大如此。所以然者，盖天地隂陽大分自然一定，而聖人豈假絲毫知力爲哉？傳易之旨微矣！大抵易爲君子謀也，因例可以槩見焉。如小畜、小過、大畜、大過之名，小往大来、大往小来之義，無非各指其所之：或隂爲主，隂用事也；或陽爲主，陽用事也。未嘗不致意於抑揚之間，使天下後世曉然知君子道長之爲慶，小人道消之爲幸。學易者亦當致三絶韋編，方識聖人之所以爲心。

書

帝光天之下，至于海隅蒼生。

李文潔
translation_en:
…to the end, there are thirty-two yang hexagrams; all yang hexagrams are termed great. Those belonging to yin extend from Gou to Kun. Among them are Dun and Pi, together with Guai and Xun [?], and the other yin hexagrams. Although they do not seek to be small, their smallness is self-evident: they assuredly dare not rank alongside yang. How clear the distinction is! Those ranked as yang extend from Fu to Qian. Among them are Yi and Guai, together with Guai and Jie [?], and the other yang hexagrams. Although they do not seek to be great, they possess greatness of themselves: standing distinctly apart, they do not encroach upon yin. How correct the distinction is!

Thus it is the hexagrams that order the small and the great in this way. The reason is that the fundamental division between yin and yang in Heaven and Earth is naturally fixed. How could the sage have needed even the slightest intellectual effort to bring this about? Subtle indeed is the purport of the commentary on the Changes! Broadly speaking, the Changes takes counsel for the noble man; its examples allow us to perceive this general intention. The names Lesser Taming and Lesser Exceeding, Greater Taming and Greater Exceeding, and the meanings of “the small departs and the great comes” and “the great departs and the small comes,” each indicate the direction of movement: sometimes yin is dominant and exercises power; sometimes yang is dominant and exercises power. The text never fails to attend to restraining one and advancing the other, so that all under Heaven and in later generations may clearly understand that the advance of the noble man's Way is cause for celebration, and the decline of the petty man's way is good fortune. Students of the Changes, too, should wear through the leather bindings three times through repeated study; only then will they understand the sage's intentions.

Book of Documents

“The Emperor's radiance illuminates all beneath Heaven, reaching even the common people at the ocean's edge.”

Li Wenjie

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭林　批〔形容虞廷大臣告君之意溢於言表殆究心於經學者〕
同考試官學正章　批〔經取合傳場中作者詞浮而與傳意矛盾惟此作得之是宜錄出〕
考試官教諭黄　批〔善摸寫光德氣象〕
考試官學正韓　批〔明快〕
期聖德所著之極盡聖世所純之地有虞大臣
然也夫莫遠於聖世之地尤莫著於聖人之德
使聖君之德之著而極於遠則天下豈有不化
===
之人哉昔禹未盡然舜用威之言而期之意謂
庶頑讒說加之以威不若明之以德誠使帝之
德允迪矣而光輝炫燿之愈隆形乎此則著乎
彼昭明有融何間耶使帝之德誕敷矣而光彩
燦爛之益盛發乎邇則見乎遠旁燭無疆何遺
耶罔愆之或寬或簡王顯於臨御之餘如日之
中而無不照重華之或哲或恭大彰於都俞之
頃如月之望而無不臨九州固在薰蒸之間而
海隅蒼生之境為何境德之光輝所至山川不
punctuated:
同考試官教諭林　批〔形容虞廷大臣告君之意，溢於言表，殆究心於經學者。〕
同考試官學正章　批〔經取合傳，場中作者詞浮而與傳意矛盾，惟此作得之，是宜錄出。〕
考試官教諭黄　批〔善摸寫光德氣象。〕
考試官學正韓　批〔明快。〕
期聖德所著之極，盡聖世所純之地，有虞大臣然也。夫莫遠於聖世之地，尤莫著於聖人之德。使聖君之德之著而極於遠，則天下豈有不化之人哉？昔禹未盡然舜用威之言，而期之，意謂：庶頑讒說，加之以威，不若明之以德。誠使帝之德允迪矣，而光輝炫燿之愈隆，形乎此則著乎彼，昭明有融，何間耶？使帝之德誕敷矣，而光彩燦爛之益盛，發乎邇則見乎遠，旁燭無疆，何遺耶？罔愆之或寬或簡，王顯於臨御之餘，如日之中而無不照；重華之或哲或恭，大彰於都俞之頃，如月之望而無不臨。九州固在薰蒸之間，而海隅蒼生之境為何境？德之光輝所至，山川不
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: 〔The portrayal of the intention with which the great minister at the court of Yu addressed his ruler conveys more than words alone express. The author is surely someone who has devoted himself to studying the Classics.〕
Associate Examiner Zhang, School Director, comments: 〔Interpretation of the Classic must accord with the commentary. The other candidates’ compositions are superficial in their wording and contradict the commentary’s meaning. This composition alone grasps it, and therefore deserves inclusion.〕
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔Skillfully depicts the character of radiant virtue.〕
Examiner Han, School Director, comments: 〔Clear and incisive.〕
To hope that the manifestation of sagely virtue would reach its utmost extent and encompass all the lands perfected by the sage’s age [?]—such was the great minister of Yu’s intention. Nothing extends farther than the lands of a sage’s age, and nothing is more manifest than the virtue of a sage. If the manifestation of the sage ruler’s virtue reaches even the most distant places, could anyone under Heaven remain untransformed?
In former times, Yu did not wholly approve of Shun’s words about employing severity, and expressed his hopes for him. His meaning was this: rather than impose severity upon the obstinate and those who utter slanders, it is better to enlighten them through virtue. If the emperor truly practices his virtue, and its dazzling radiance grows ever greater, what takes form here will become manifest there. Its brilliance shines far: what gap could remain? If the emperor spreads his virtue widely, and its splendid light grows ever more abundant, what issues forth nearby will be visible afar. It shines in every direction without limit: what could be left out?
His faultless qualities, whether generosity or simplicity, shine forth in his exercise of rulership [?], like the sun at noon, leaving nothing unilluminated. The qualities of Chonghua [Shun], whether wisdom or reverence, are fully displayed in the moments of approving exchanges with his ministers, like the full moon, overlooking everything. The Nine Provinces are certainly already steeped in his influence; but what of the territory inhabited by the people at the margins of the seas? Wherever the radiance of his virtue reaches, mountains and rivers cannot…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
能以限隔五服固在陶鎔之內而海隅蒼生之
鄉為何鄉德之光彩所及封疆不能以留礙其
地則沙漠不毛望之一蒼莽無涯也沛然聲教
之四訖孰不鼓舞於並生之仁其地則人迹不
到視之一蒼渺無際也浩然文命之四敷孰不
沐浴於無為之化夫以君德昭著而遍及天下
則萬邦黎獻共臣矣禎譏曾足介吾意哉抑觀
治莫盛於虞德莫加於舜何當時為君者以禎
譏為憂為臣者以明德為望盖慮其妨治而欲
===
刑之者聖君憂世無窮之心本之君身而欲化
之者聖臣愛君無窮之心舜非苟恃於刑而禹
亦豈不知舜之優於德耶刑之不可已亦德之
所不可廢也君明臣良相得盖彰有虞泰和之
治有由然哉
舉能其官惟爾之能
同考試官教諭林　批　〔題本平易作者多不知點綴〕
羅　　幹
上意惟此篇於周官一書隱括殆盡宜錄之以式後學
punctuated:
能以限隔。五服固在陶鎔之內，而海隅蒼生之鄉為何鄉？德之光彩所及，封疆不能以留礙。其地則沙漠不毛，望之一蒼莽無涯也；沛然聲教之四訖，孰不鼓舞於並生之仁？其地則人迹不到，視之一蒼渺無際也；浩然文命之四敷，孰不沐浴於無為之化？夫以君德昭著而遍及天下，則萬邦黎獻共臣矣，禎譏曾足介吾意哉？抑觀治莫盛於虞，德莫加於舜，何當時為君者以禎譏為憂，為臣者以明德為望？盖慮其妨治而欲刑之者，聖君憂世無窮之心；本之君身而欲化之者，聖臣愛君無窮之心。舜非苟恃於刑，而禹亦豈不知舜之優於德耶？刑之不可已，亦德之所不可廢也。君明臣良，相得盖彰，有虞泰和之治有由然哉！
舉能其官，惟爾之能。
同考試官教諭林批：〔題本平易，作者多不知點綴〕
羅幹
上意，惟此篇於《周官》一書隱括殆盡，宜錄之以式後學。
translation_en:
…cannot be divided or cut off by mountains and rivers. The five zones of submission are already within the transforming influence of his rule; what, then, of the lands inhabited by the common people at the edges of the seas? Wherever the radiance of his virtue reaches, territorial boundaries cannot obstruct it. Those lands are barren deserts, appearing as an endless, dim wilderness; yet, as his civilizing teachings abundantly reach all four quarters, who does not rejoice in the benevolence that gives life to all alike? Those lands are untouched by human footsteps, appearing as a boundless, hazy expanse; yet, as his civilizing influence spreads broadly in every direction, who does not bathe in the transforming power of government through nonaction? When the ruler’s virtue shines forth and extends throughout the world, the worthy among the people of the myriad states all become his subjects. Could malicious slander [?] then be enough to trouble his mind?
Yet consider: no government flourished more than that of Yu, and no virtue surpassed Shun’s. Why, then, did the ruler of that time worry about malicious slander [?], while his minister placed his hopes in making virtue manifest? The desire to punish it, out of concern that it would obstruct good government, expressed the sage ruler’s boundless concern for the world. The desire to transform it, taking the ruler’s own person as the foundation, expressed the sage minister’s boundless love for his sovereign. Shun did not merely rely on punishments; could Yu, for his part, have failed to recognize Shun’s excellence in virtue? Just as punishment cannot be dispensed with, so virtue cannot be abandoned. An enlightened ruler and a worthy minister complemented one another and thereby shone forth. Surely there was a reason for the supremely harmonious government of Yu!
“Recommend those capable of fulfilling their offices: therein lies your own ability.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: 〔The topic is fundamentally straightforward, but most writers do not know how to embellish it.〕
Luo Gan
The sovereign’s intent [?]. This essay alone encompasses almost the entirety of the Book of Zhou Offices; it should be recorded as a model for later students.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正章　批〔詞簡理備說出成王戒卿士薦賢之意閎之令人彌重宜居選列〕
考試官教諭黃　批〔是如此作〕

賢王言膺薦者之脩其職即主薦者之盡其職
蓋薦賢所以報主而因賢可以知人賢王戒卿
士之薦舉而示以責有所歸其意嚴矣且成王
申戒卿士之言及此蓋謂人君以用賢為心大
臣以薦賢為職汝念萬幾之分理在庶官凡有
===
屈於下僚而隱於草澤者盡在所舉不以功過
而或殊爾思萬務之分任在衆職凡有歌於碩
人而處於衡門者悉在所薦不以親讐而或避
宜公而資之燮理宜孤而貿之寅亮則四時順
序而兩儀奠位矣寧至於有負秉之譏宜卿而
資之倡率宜牧而資之阜成則百工惟熙而兆
民得所矣寧至於有具官之誚夫推賢而果得
其賢則賢寧不萃於汝之身乎有容之心休休

Associate Examiner Zhang, School Instructor, comments: 〔The language is concise and the reasoning complete. It expresses King Cheng’s intention in admonishing his ministers to recommend worthy men. Its expansive treatment inspires still greater esteem [?]; it deserves inclusion among the selected answers.〕
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔This is how it should be written.〕
Examiner Han, School Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning has been grasped.〕
The worthy king says that when those recommended discharge their duties, those responsible for recommending them thereby fulfill their own duties. Recommending worthy men is a means of repaying one’s lord, and through those worthy men one can assess those who recommend them. In admonishing his ministers concerning recommendations and showing where responsibility rests, the worthy king’s intention is stern indeed. When King Cheng’s renewed admonition to his ministers reaches this point, its meaning is that the ruler makes employing worthy men his concern, while great ministers make recommending worthy men their duty.
Consider that the myriad affairs of government are apportioned among the various officials: all those confined to subordinate posts or living hidden in the countryside should be put forward, without distinctions based on merits or faults. Reflect that responsibility for the myriad tasks is distributed among the various offices: all those celebrated as eminent men yet dwelling behind humble crossbar gates should be recommended, without passing anyone over because he is a relative or an enemy. Employ those suited to be dukes to harmonize yin and yang, and those suited to be junior guardians to reverently assist [?]; then the four seasons will follow their proper sequence, and Heaven and Earth will be firmly established in their places. How could there then be occasion for the reproach of ‘bearing the handle’ [?]? Employ those suited to be ministers to lead their subordinates, and those suited to be regional governors to enrich and perfect the people; then all officials will flourish in their work, and the myriad people will find their proper places. How could there then be occasion for the reproach of merely filling an office?
If, in advancing worthy men, you truly obtain men of worth, will their worth not gather in your own person? With a generous heart that readily accommodates others, you make all the virtue under Heaven your own. If, in yielding to the capable, you truly obtain capable men, then their ability …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
豈不歸於爾之躬乎無私之心坦坦而天下之
才皆其才矣雖不必汝自為公為孤陰陽之所
以燮理者在是天地之所以寅亮者在是以人
事君之道何忝哉雖不必爾自為卿為牧群屬
之所以倡率者在斯兆民之所以阜成者在斯
薦賢報國之責何愧哉吁因其薦舉之人驗其
薦舉之職任是責者其可不知所慎歟大抵天
生賢才以為君也君用賢才以圖治也而大臣
與君同體為國薦賢又其分之宜也然必有好
===
賢樂善之誠而又有體國奉公之志斯可以得
賢才而盡其用不然則所用非所求所求非所
用終歸於利而非義也是則得賢非難得薦賢
之人為難此又人君論相之所當知
詩
陟我高岡無矢我陵我陵我阿無飲我泉
我泉我池
張欽
同考試官教諭徐　批〔題旨自高岡一氣說下作〕
punctuated:
豈不歸於爾之躬乎？無私之心坦坦，而天下之才皆其才矣。雖不必汝自為公、為孤，陰陽之所以燮理者在是，天地之所以寅亮者在是，以人事君之道何忝哉？雖不必爾自為卿、為牧，群屬之所以倡率者在斯，兆民之所以阜成者在斯，薦賢報國之責何愧哉？吁！因其薦舉之人，驗其薦舉之職，任是責者，其可不知所慎歟？大抵天生賢才以為君也，君用賢才以圖治也，而大臣與君同體，為國薦賢，又其分之宜也。然必有好賢樂善之誠，而又有體國奉公之志，斯可以得賢才而盡其用。不然，則所用非所求，所求非所用，終歸於利而非義也。是則得賢非難，得薦賢之人為難，此又人君論相之所當知。

詩
陟我高岡，無矢我陵。我陵我阿，無飲我泉。我泉我池。
張欽

同考試官教諭徐，批〔題旨自高岡一氣說下，作〕
translation_en:
…how could ability fail to accrue to your own person? With an open and unselfish heart, you make all the talents of the realm your own. Though you need not yourself serve as a Duke or Junior Guardian, here lies the means of harmonizing yin and yang and reverently assisting Heaven and Earth. How could you fall short in the way of serving your ruler through worthy men? Though you need not yourself serve as a minister or regional governor, here lies the means of leading subordinate officials and bringing prosperity and stability to the people. What cause would you have for shame in discharging your responsibility to recommend worthy men and repay the state?

Ah! Judge the performance of those charged with recommending men by the men they recommend: can anyone bearing this responsibility fail to recognize the need for care? Heaven produces worthy and talented men for the ruler, and the ruler employs them to achieve good government. Great ministers form one body with their ruler; recommending worthy men for the state is therefore their proper duty. Yet only with genuine love of worthiness and delight in goodness, together with the resolve to take the state's concerns to heart and serve the public interest, can they obtain worthy and talented men and make full use of them. Otherwise, those employed will not be those sought, and those sought will not be those employed; the outcome will ultimately serve private advantage rather than righteousness. Thus, the difficulty lies less in finding worthy men than in finding those who will recommend them. This, too, is something a ruler must understand when assessing candidates for chief councillor.
