title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
者往往支離纏繞此篇脫落陳習說理造辭縝密
純雅而其氣亦悠然經生文字固當爾邪
同考試官教諭李　批〔分明寫出王師所至無敵氣〕
象凜凜可畏宜錄以爲學詩者式
同考試官學正楊　批〔陵阿泉池作者多戾朱傳此〕
作明白通暢正得詩人意思
考試官教諭黃　批〔能依朱註發揮可取〕
考試官學正韓　批〔一順說去允當〕
臨所有之地無敢敵之人王者之師也蓋王者
===
無敵理固然也聖人承天命以伐密則所臨之
地豈有敢與爲敵者哉昔文王當遏密之後遂
爲侵密之舉斯時也聖武布昭赫赫然而攖之
必摧王靈丕振凜凜然而觸之必靡師旅深入
于密方所陟之岡密人昔時以爲出沒矣今則
山谿不足以爲固而危峯四周皆我周之式廓
也車馬長驅于密地所登之岡密人向負以爲
掩襲矣今則封疆不足以爲界而崇山一帶皆
我周之境土也密地既我有矣密人敢復拒哉
punctuated:
者往往支離纏繞，此篇脫落陳習，說理造辭縝密純雅，而其氣亦悠然。經生文字固當爾邪？

同考試官教諭李批〔分明寫出王師所至無敵氣象，凜凜可畏，宜錄以爲學詩者式。

同考試官學正楊批〔陵阿泉池，作者多戾朱傳，此作明白通暢，正得詩人意思。

考試官教諭黃批〔能依朱註發揮，可取〕

考試官學正韓批〔一順說去，允當〕

臨所有之地，無敢敵之人，王者之師也。蓋王者無敵，理固然也。聖人承天命以伐密，則所臨之地，豈有敢與爲敵者哉？昔文王當遏密之後，遂爲侵密之舉。斯時也，聖武布昭，赫赫然而攖之必摧；王靈丕振，凜凜然而觸之必靡。師旅深入于密方，所陟之岡，密人昔時以爲出沒矣。今則山谿不足以爲固，而危峯四周，皆我周之式廓也。車馬長驅于密地，所登之岡，密人向負以爲掩襲矣。今則封疆不足以爲界，而崇山一帶，皆我周之境土也。密地既我有矣，密人敢復拒哉？
translation_en:
…writers often produce disjointed and convoluted work. This piece casts off conventional habits: its reasoning and phrasing are meticulous, pure, and elegant, while its spirit is also unhurried. Surely this is how students of the Classics ought to write!

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “It distinctly conveys the imposing presence of the royal army, invincible wherever it goes and fearsome in its majesty. It should be recorded as a model for students of the Book of Odes.”

Associate Examiner Yang, School Instructor, comments: “In treating the hills, slopes, springs, and pools, writers often depart from Zhu Xi’s commentary. This piece is clear and fluent, capturing precisely the poet’s meaning.”

Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “It develops its argument in accordance with Zhu Xi’s commentary and merits acceptance.”

Examiner Han, School Instructor, comments: “The exposition proceeds smoothly throughout and is entirely apt.”

Wherever it advances, the land becomes its possession, and no one dares oppose it: such is the army of a true king. That a true king has no adversary capable of resisting him is inherent in the order of things. When the sage received Heaven’s mandate to attack Mi, could anyone in the lands he entered have dared to oppose him? In former times, after King Wen had checked Mi, he proceeded to invade it. At that time his sagely martial might shone forth: so radiant was it that anyone who confronted it was certain to be crushed. His royal majesty rose in full force: so awe-inspiring was it that anyone who encountered it was certain to fall. His troops penetrated deep into the territory of Mi. The heights they climbed were places that the people of Mi had formerly used to emerge and withdraw. Now, however, mountains and ravines no longer sufficed as defenses, and the lofty peaks on every side all lay within the expanded domain of our Zhou [?]. Chariots and horses drove far into Mi’s lands. The heights they ascended were places on which the people of Mi had previously relied for surprise attacks. Now, however, territorial boundaries no longer sufficed to mark a limit, and the entire stretch of towering mountains belonged to the territory of our Zhou. With Mi’s lands already in our possession, did its people dare resist again?

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
彼高岡之上有陵阿焉非不可以陳兵也有泉
池焉非不可以飲水也然而天誅所在自有以
寒人之心密人聞其風聲而奔突竄伏之不暇
誰敢矢我陵矢我阿據險阻以抗我之兵邪天
討所臨自有以破人之膽密人覩其氣勢而喙
息逃遁之恐後孰敢飲我泉飲我池據地利以
困我之師邪吁王師隨所向而有無敵之勢如
此此文王膺天之命蓋亦因其可怒而怒之曷
嘗有畔援歆羡於其間哉抑因是而知周家之
===
興不偶然也大王能安民而獲西顧之眷王季
能長君而延上帝之祉至於文王先登于岸既
伐密而作程順帝之則又伐崇而作豐前後相
承一德無間是以天之眷命有隆無替夫豈私
於周也邪噫周人發先王之德如此為孫子者
當知天命所由集王業所由興而承之保之不
可以忽易歟
我龍受之蹻蹻王之造
劉節
punctuated:
彼高岡之上，有陵阿焉，非不可以陳兵也；有泉池焉，非不可以飲水也。然而天誅所在，自有以寒人之心。密人聞其風聲，而奔突竄伏之不暇，誰敢矢我陵、矢我阿，據險阻以抗我之兵邪？天討所臨，自有以破人之膽。密人覩其氣勢，而喙息逃遁之恐後，孰敢飲我泉、飲我池，據地利以困我之師邪？吁！王師隨所向而有無敵之勢如此，此文王膺天之命，蓋亦因其可怒而怒之，曷嘗有畔援歆羡於其間哉？抑因是而知周家之興不偶然也。大王能安民而獲西顧之眷，王季能長君而延上帝之祉。至於文王，先登于岸，既伐密而作程；順帝之則，又伐崇而作豐。前後相承，一德無間，是以天之眷命有隆無替，夫豈私於周也邪？噫！周人發先王之德如此，為孫子者，當知天命所由集、王業所由興，而承之保之，不可以忽易歟？

我龍受之，蹻蹻王之造。
劉節
translation_en:
On those high ridges were hills and slopes where troops could certainly be arrayed, and springs and pools from which water could certainly be drunk. Yet wherever Heaven’s punishment fell, it naturally struck terror into people’s hearts. Hearing the reports of its approach, the people of Mi could scarcely flee, scatter, and hide fast enough. Who would dare array troops on our hills and slopes, relying on difficult terrain to resist our soldiers? Wherever Heaven’s punitive expedition came, it naturally shattered people’s courage. Seeing its imposing might, the people of Mi fled breathlessly, fearing they would fall behind. Who would dare drink from our springs and pools, relying on advantageous ground to thwart our army? Ah! Such was the invincible might of the royal army wherever it advanced. In fulfilling Heaven’s mandate, King Wen merely directed his anger against what deserved it. When did willfulness or covetous desire ever enter into this?

From this, moreover, we know that the rise of the house of Zhou was no accident. King Tai brought peace to the people and won Heaven’s favor as it looked westward. Wang Ji fulfilled his roles as elder and ruler and secured the blessings of the Lord on High. When it came to King Wen, he was the first to ascend to firm ground: he attacked Mi and established Cheng; following the Lord’s rule, he then attacked Chong and established Feng. Predecessor and successor continued one another’s work, their virtue united without interruption. Thus Heaven’s favor and mandate grew ever greater and never declined. Could this have been mere partiality toward Zhou? Ah! Such was the way the people of Zhou proclaimed the virtue of their former kings. Should not their descendants understand what brought Heaven’s mandate to them and what caused their royal enterprise to flourish, and carry it forward and preserve it, never treating it lightly?

“We receive it with honor—the mighty accomplishment of the king.”
Liu Jie.

translation_en:

Yet candidates generally fail to grasp closely the passages about “gloriously receiving” and “the king’s achievements”; their writing is diffuse and redundant, with the order reversed—particularly tiresome. This essay’s language is incisive and disciplined, and its meaning resonates expansively. It brings richness out of spare simplicity [?]. Essays like this would scarcely require bending many fingers to count [?]. Include it.〕

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔In their essays, candidates generally devote much effort to “gloriously receiving.” Yet for “mighty indeed were the king’s achievements,” some even expound “not acting before the proper time” and “not collapsing after the proper time” as a contrasting pair. Others discuss the achievements first and only afterward their reception, reversing the order improperly. This essay’s language is disciplined and its force abundant: it is an outstanding example of mastery of the Classic [?].〕

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: 〔The two lines express a single idea, but students are often constrained by them, and few explain “gloriously receiving” with precision! They also repeat their wording from beginning to end. This essay is clear in principle and correct in expression, developing the meaning almost exhaustively. It should rank first in this examining room.〕

Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔Truly few essays explain “gloriously receiving” and “the king’s achievements” as precisely, concisely, and aptly as this one.〕

Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: 〔It captures the intent of praising King Wu.〕

What the succeeding king receives as a gracious inheritance is the preceding king’s great achievement. For the achievement of attaining kingship was the preceding king’s accomplishment, one rarely seen in any age. Its meaning is that, had the ancestors established nothing before them, what could their descendants receive afterward? text:

崇朝丕承之烈於文無愧也岐豐之地闢為鎬
京之區龥呺之臣入為祼將之士于以來謳歌
而歸訟獄〔三分〕〔末一〕者以之而一非家非國蹻
===
蹻然王者之造而氣勢非前日之可方也我之
寵承不在茲乎于以朝諸侯而賔四夷九年未
集者以之而集非公非侯蹻蹻然王者之功而
規模非昔日之可比也我之龍受不在是乎吁
武王以無競之功而垂裕後之休宜詩人於告
神之際必以是而頌之也歟抑考行師之道以
時為貴禹有三苗之征湯有南巢之放文有密
崇之伐一皆應天順人出於不得已而後舉耳
然則武王牧野之師酌時而動亦惟上師禹湯
punctuated: 之不足以為寵。今我子孫而膺曆數之傳者，踐祚之後，經營不必從事也，安居九重，實有寵承於前世；繼體之餘，締造不必勞心也，垂拱五位，實有龍受於先王。誠以我先王武王也，際純熙之時，興於鑠之師，戎衣一着，乾坤旋轉於會旦，惟揚之武，于湯有光也；黃鉞一揮，天地掀揭於崇朝，丕承之烈，於文無愧也。岐豐之地，闢為鎬京之區；龥呺之臣，入為祼將之士。于以來謳歌而歸訟獄，〔三分〕〔末一〕者以之而一，非家非國，蹻蹻然王者之造，而氣勢非前日之可方也。我之寵承不在茲乎？于以朝諸侯而賔四夷，九年未集者以之而集，非公非侯，蹻蹻然王者之功，而規模非昔日之可比也。我之龍受不在是乎？吁！武王以無競之功，而垂裕後之休，宜詩人於告神之際，必以是而頌之也歟！抑考行師之道，以時為貴。禹有三苗之征，湯有南巢之放，文有密崇之伐，一皆應天順人，出於不得已而後舉耳。然則武王牧野之師，酌時而動，亦惟上師禹湯
translation_en:
…to receive it would not suffice to constitute a glorious inheritance. Now we descendants, who have received the succession ordained by Heaven, need not undertake the work of establishing the realm after ascending the throne. Dwelling peacefully within the palace’s ninefold enclosure, we have indeed inherited glory from earlier generations. Having succeeded to the sovereign’s position, we need not trouble ourselves with founding a dynasty. With robes hanging loose and hands folded, we occupy the sovereign’s fifth position and have indeed received a magnificent inheritance from the former king.

This is truly because our former king was King Wu. At a time of pure splendor, he raised a glorious army. Once he donned his martial robes, Heaven and Earth were transformed at dawn [?]. His martial might, displayed abroad, added luster to Tang. With one sweep of his yellow battle-axe, Heaven and Earth were overturned within a single morning. His achievement in grandly continuing his inheritance did no discredit to King Wen. The territory of Qi and Feng was expanded into the domain of Haojing; ministers who had cried out [?] entered to serve as officers presenting libations. Thus he attracted those who sang his praises and became the authority to whom people brought their lawsuits. What had been divided was thereby united [small annotations: “three divisions”; “last one” [?]]. This was no mere household or regional state: majestic indeed was the founding work of a true king, whose power and momentum could not be compared with those of earlier days. Does not our glorious inheritance lie here?

Thus he received the feudal lords at court and entertained the peoples of the four outer regions as guests. What had remained unaccomplished for nine years was thereby accomplished. This was no achievement of a mere duke or marquis: majestic indeed was the accomplishment of a true king, whose scope could not be compared with that of former times. Does not our magnificent inheritance lie here? Ah! Through his unrivaled achievement, King Wu bequeathed the blessing of abundant provision for his descendants. It was surely fitting that, when addressing the spirits, the poet should praise him for this!

Yet, when we examine the proper way to deploy an army, timing is paramount. Yu undertook the expedition against the Sanmiao; Tang carried out the banishment to Nanchao; King Wen campaigned against Mi and Chong. All responded to Heaven and accorded with the people, acting only when compelled by necessity. Thus King Wu’s army at Muye moved after weighing the circumstances of the time; he too was simply taking the ancient Yu and Tang as his models…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
道歸文王而已夫豈有窮黷武憶載周有闕□
惟爾公允師子孫登歌以是而播之樂章其亦
知所以格神之道者歟
春秋
晉人秦人戰于河曲〔文公十有二年〕季孫行
父臧孫許叔孫僑如公孫嬰齊帥師會晉
郤克衛孫良夫曹公子首及齊侯戰于鞌
〔成公二年〕晉侯及楚子鄭伯戰于鄢陵〔成〕
〔公十有六年〕晉趙鞅帥師及鄭罕達帥師戰
于鐵〔哀公二年〕
===

晉人秦人戰于河曲〔文公十有二年〕。季孫行父、臧孫許、叔孫僑如、公孫嬰齊帥師，會晉郤克、衛孫良夫、曹公子首，及齊侯戰于鞌〔成公二年〕。晉侯及楚子、鄭伯戰于鄢陵〔成〕〔公十有六年〕。晉趙鞅帥師及鄭罕達帥師戰于鐵〔哀公二年〕。

Recalling what was recorded of Zhou [the text is garbled and one character illegible here: ?], “It is your achievement that truly serves as a model.” His descendants sang this in the ceremonial singing and disseminated it through musical compositions. Spring and Autumn Annals

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之晉爲盟主而列國皆與之戰夷考其事則霸
業之盛衰豈不於斯而可見乎何則春秋中葉
唐叔之晉世主夏盟其與秦齊楚戰也果何而
見其霸業猶振邪于時秦伯伐晉趙盾欒之而
戰于河曲齊人笑客郤克憤之而交戰于鞌楚
共救鄭厲公則與楚師戰于鄢陵焉之三役也
自常情觀之孰不以爲堂堂晉霸夷夏具瞻秦
齊何國也乃敢擅與師旅與晉爲敵楚共何人
也亦敢時出干紀與晉抗衡於理若弗順焉殊
===
不知秦以西陲雄長齊以東州大邦楚以南蠻
强國雖云抗霸猶敵體也地醜德齊力能相尚
亦人情之常耳噫春秋諸侯舍齊秦楚外胡敢
與晉抗哉胡敢與晉敵哉聖人於此不嫌於與
晉戰者以見晉國之盛威足以懾服諸侯義足
以主盟中夏况能挫秦敗齊射楚三戰交綏群
雄退聽其霸業之猶振也明矣若夫春秋叔世
傳至晉定猶掌霸權其與鄭罕達戰也又何而
見其霸業之不振邪于時晉政荐衰趙鞅當國
punctuated: 之晉爲盟主，而列國皆與之戰。夷考其事，則霸業之盛衰，豈不於斯而可見乎？何則？春秋中葉，唐叔之晉，世主夏盟。其與秦齊楚戰也，果何而見其霸業猶振邪？于時秦伯伐晉，趙盾欒之而戰于河曲；齊人笑客，郤克憤之而交戰于鞌；楚共救鄭，厲公則與楚師戰于鄢陵焉。之三役也，自常情觀之，孰不以爲堂堂晉霸，夷夏具瞻，秦齊何國也，乃敢擅與師旅，與晉爲敵？楚共何人也，亦敢時出干紀，與晉抗衡？於理若弗順焉。殊不知秦以西陲雄長，齊以東州大邦，楚以南蠻强國，雖云抗霸，猶敵體也。地醜德齊，力能相尚，亦人情之常耳。噫！春秋諸侯，舍齊秦楚外，胡敢與晉抗哉？胡敢與晉敵哉？聖人於此，不嫌於與晉戰者，以見晉國之盛，威足以懾服諸侯，義足以主盟中夏。况能挫秦敗齊射楚，三戰交綏，群雄退聽，其霸業之猶振也明矣。若夫春秋叔世，傳至晉定，猶掌霸權。其與鄭罕達戰也，又何而見其霸業之不振邪？于時晉政荐衰，趙鞅當國。
translation_en:
… Jin served as leader of the covenant, yet the various states all fought against it. Examining these events dispassionately, can we not discern here the flourishing and decline of its hegemony? Why is this so? In the middle period of the Spring and Autumn era, Jin, the state of Tang Shu, presided over the covenants of the Xia states for successive generations. How, then, do its battles with Qin, Qi, and Chu show that its hegemony remained vigorous? At that time, the Earl of Qin attacked Jin, and Zhao Dun responded [?] and fought at Hequ. The people of Qi mocked a visiting envoy; Xi Ke, angered by this, fought them at An. Duke Gong of Chu came to Zheng’s aid, and Duke Li of Jin fought the Chu army at Yanling. Viewing these three campaigns in the ordinary way, who would not think: “Jin’s imposing hegemony commands the attention of both the Yi and the Xia. What sort of states are Qin and Qi, that they dare to mobilize armies on their own authority and make enemies of Jin? Who is Duke Gong of Chu, that he too dares repeatedly to violate the established order and contend with Jin?” This would seem contrary to proper principle.

Such a view entirely overlooks that Qin dominated the western frontier, Qi was a great state in the east, and Chu was a powerful state among the southern Man. Although they challenged the hegemon, they were nevertheless its peers. With comparable territories and equal standing in virtue, and with strength sufficient to rival one another, their conduct was only natural. Ah! Among the lords of the Spring and Autumn era, apart from Qi, Qin, and Chu, who dared resist Jin? Who dared oppose it? In these instances, the Sage did not censure those who fought Jin, thereby revealing Jin’s greatness: its might sufficed to overawe the lords into submission, and its righteousness sufficed to preside over the covenants of the central Xia states. Moreover, it could check Qin, defeat Qi, and shoot the ruler of Chu. In these three battles the armies engaged and withdrew, and the contending powers fell back and submitted. Clearly, its hegemony remained vigorous.

But in the declining years of the Spring and Autumn era, when the succession reached Duke Ding of Jin, Jin still wielded hegemonic authority. How, then, does its battle with Han Da of Zheng show that its hegemony had lost its vigor? At that time, Jin’s government was deteriorating further and further, and Zhao Yang controlled the state …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
荀范謀逆反易天明自絕于君見逐于國齊人
黨之而輸其粟鄭卿送之而右其奸吉射尤悖
朋惡往逆趙簡子則出師禦鄭而戰于鐵焉之
一役也自庸情論之孰不以為鄭黨叛臣分所
當討趙鞅晉卿也伏弢嘔血鼓音不衰郵良晉
御也兩靷將絕力能止之其功若可錄焉殊不
知鄭國以蕞爾之區罕達以匹夫之勇地不大
於曹滕民不衆於邾莒以晉視之誠縣鄙也縱
與之戰雖勝不武降尊毀列恥不足言亦事勢
===
之變耳噫春秋諸侯鄭尚能相抗其餘皆敵與
晉敵矣皆敢與晉角矣聖人於此特嫌於與晉
戰者以見晉霸之衰雖不足以號召諸侯勢不
足以驅役列國況又遇敵震慄而失措群下務
伐而爭功其霸業之不振也宜哉吁同一晉也
始以交兵大國而見其盛終以交兵小國而見
其衰春秋豈容私於其間哉亦惟跡其勢而察
其幾耳大抵人莫貴於自强莫不貴於自棄自
强於為善則小可大弱可强而大國亦將為吾
punctuated:
荀、范謀逆，反易天明，自絕于君，見逐于國。齊人黨之而輸其粟，鄭卿送之而右其奸，吉射尤悖，朋惡往逆。趙簡子則出師禦鄭，而戰于鐵焉之一役也。自庸情論之，孰不以為鄭黨叛臣，分所當討？趙鞅，晉卿也，伏弢嘔血，鼓音不衰；郵良，晉御也，兩靷將絕，力能止之。其功若可錄焉。殊不知鄭國以蕞爾之區，罕達以匹夫之勇，地不大於曹、滕，民不衆於邾、莒，以晉視之，誠縣鄙也。縱與之戰，雖勝不武，降尊毀列，恥不足言，亦事勢之變耳。
噫！春秋諸侯，鄭尚能相抗，其餘皆敵與晉敵矣，皆敢與晉角矣。聖人於此特嫌於與晉戰者，以見晉霸之衰，雖不足以號召諸侯，勢不足以驅役列國。況又遇敵震慄而失措，群下務伐而爭功，其霸業之不振也宜哉！吁！同一晉也，始以交兵大國而見其盛，終以交兵小國而見其衰。《春秋》豈容私於其間哉？亦惟跡其勢而察其幾耳。大抵人莫貴於自强，莫不貴於自棄。自强於為善，則小可大，弱可强，而大國亦將為吾
translation_en:
…The Xun and Fan clans plotted rebellion, overturning Heaven’s manifest order, severing themselves from their lord, and being driven from their state. The people of Qi supported them and supplied them with grain; a minister of Zheng escorted the supplies and abetted their treachery. Ji She was especially rebellious, joining with evildoers and going out to receive them. Zhao Jianzi then dispatched troops to resist Zheng: this was the engagement fought at Tie [?]. Judged by ordinary sentiments, who would not think that Zheng, having sided with rebellious ministers, deserved to be attacked? Zhao Yang, a minister of Jin, bent over his bow case and vomited blood, yet the sound of his drum did not falter. You Liang [?], a charioteer of Jin, was strong enough to halt the horses when both harness straps were about to snap. Their achievements might seem worthy of record. Yet this overlooks the fact that Zheng possessed only a tiny territory, and Han Da only the courage of an ordinary man. Its lands were no greater than those of Cao or Teng, and its population no larger than those of Zhu or Ju. Viewed from Jin, it was truly no more than an outlying county. Even if Jin fought it and won, this would be no display of martial prowess. To lower its dignity and degrade its rank was a disgrace beyond words—another manifestation of the change in circumstances.
Alas! Among the feudal lords of the Spring and Autumn period, if even Zheng could stand against Jin, all the others could likewise confront Jin as equals [?], and all would dare to contend with it. That the Sage here particularly objects to describing the encounter as a battle against Jin reveals the decline of Jin’s hegemony: it could no longer summon the feudal lords [?], and its power was insufficient to command the various states. Moreover, its leaders trembled and lost their composure when encountering the enemy, while their subordinates sought distinction and competed for credit. No wonder its hegemony failed to flourish! Alas! It was the very same Jin: at first, its warfare against great states revealed its strength; in the end, its warfare against a small state revealed its decline. How could the Spring and Autumn Annals permit partiality in this? It merely traces the circumstances and examines the incipient signs. In general, nothing is more precious to a person than strengthening oneself; the next phrase reads, doubtfully, ‘none fails to value self-abandonment’ [?]. If one strengthens oneself in doing good, the small can become great and the weak can become strong, and even great states will become our…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
後自棄於不善人人得而侮之何强大之足恃
哉然原其失盖由利勝而義微政褻而拳散故
致諸侯之叛大夫之張外夷之横一潰而不可
復收矣末流之弊可勝言哉安能起桓文於九
京與之定恢復之計
宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯會晉師于棐林伐鄭
宣公元年　晉人宋人衛人陳人侵鄭〔宣公〕
二年　晉欒書帥師伐鄭〔成公九年〕晉侯及
楚子鄭伯戰于鄢陵〔成公十有六年〕公會尹
===
子單子晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯曹伯邾人伐
鄭公會單子晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊人邾
人伐鄭〔俱成公十有七年〕戍鄭虎牢楚公子
貞帥師救鄭〔襄公十年〕
劉藍
同考試官教諭張　批　〔春秋須識得筆削書法方〕
〔領會聖人微意所在諸作體認不真立辭多舛此〕
〔篇深究隱顯所以本旨是宜錄出〕
考試官教諭黃　批　〔得聖經書法隱顯褒貶之旨〕
punctuated:
後。自棄於不善，人人得而侮之，何强大之足恃哉？然原其失，盖由利勝而義微，政褻而拳散，故致諸侯之叛、大夫之張、外夷之横，一潰而不可復收矣。末流之弊，可勝言哉？安能起桓文於九京，與之定恢復之計？
宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯會晉師于棐林，伐鄭。宣公元年。晉人、宋人、衛人、陳人侵鄭。〔宣公〕二年。晉欒書帥師伐鄭。〔成公九年〕晉侯及楚子、鄭伯戰于鄢陵。〔成公十有六年〕公會尹子、單子、晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、邾人伐鄭。公會單子、晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊人、邾人伐鄭。〔俱成公十有七年〕戍鄭虎牢。楚公子貞帥師救鄭。〔襄公十年〕
劉藍
同考試官教諭張，批：〔春秋須識得筆削書法，方〕〔領會聖人微意所在。諸作體認不真，立辭多舛，此〕〔篇深究隱顯所以，本旨是，宜錄出。〕
考試官教諭黃，批：〔得聖經書法隱顯褒貶之旨。〕
translation_en:
…behind us. If we abandon ourselves to wrongdoing, anyone can insult us: what reliance can we place on strength and greatness? Yet, tracing these failures to their source, we find that advantage prevailed while righteousness waned, government was debased, and authority dissipated [?]. Thus the regional lords rebelled, the great officers grew overbearing, and the foreign peoples acted with impunity. Once everything collapsed, it could no longer be restored. Can the evils of this final decline be fully recounted? How could we raise Dukes Huan and Wen from the grave [?] and devise with them a plan for restoration?
“The Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao joined the army of Jin at Feilin and attacked Zheng.” First year of Duke Xuan. “Men of Jin, Song, Wei, and Chen invaded Zheng.” Second year 〔of Duke Xuan〕. “Luan Shu of Jin led an army to attack Zheng.” 〔Ninth year of Duke Cheng.〕 “The Marquis of Jin fought the Viscount of Chu and the Earl of Zheng at Yanling.” 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Cheng.〕 “The duke joined Viscount Yin, Viscount Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, and men of Zhu in attacking Zheng.” “The duke joined Viscount Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, and men of Qi and Zhu in attacking Zheng.” 〔Both in the seventeenth year of Duke Cheng.〕 “A garrison was stationed at Hulao in Zheng.” “Prince Zhen of Chu led an army to relieve Zheng.” 〔Tenth year of Duke Xiang.〕
Liu Lan.
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔In studying the Spring and Autumn Annals, one must understand its conventions of recording and deleting before〕〔one can grasp the subtle intentions of the Sage. The other essays fail to comprehend these accurately and contain many errors of expression. This〕〔essay probes deeply into the reasons for concealment and disclosure; its central purport is correct, and it should be selected for inclusion.〕
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔This essay grasps the intent behind the sacred classic’s conventions of concealment and disclosure, praise and blame.〕

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正韓　批〔按是非公予奪此作得之〕
霸主討貳近乎正春秋屢畧外夷恤患之名霸
主逼貳近乎專春秋特存外夷恤患之義此鄭
為夷夏必争之國故晉之屢伐楚之屢救各有
得失存焉春秋得不按是非而致隱顯之法哉
慨自桓文邁往霸統陵夷荆楚每垂涎於北圖
鄭人常掉臂於南向主霸圖者豈可置之而不
究厥心耶晉靈首會衆師棐林以聲鄭即楚之
罪而蔿賈之救隨至繼偕四國往侵以詰鄭伐
===
宋之由而鬬椒之救適臨景公命將欒書以致
伐將討鄭之貳於楚也子重迺討侵陳之策以
挽其謀厲公合兵鄢陵以謀戰將責鄭之叛夫
晉也楚子躬率救鄭之師以泄其憤夏之伐也
上屋尹單以臨戎而子重又興首止之次冬之
伐也再扳王臣以從事而子申復為汝上之援
曲沃之旅奔走於溱洧者無寧歲曾何挽其從
楚之輈江漢之衆應援於潁邦者無窮期及有
奪其慕華之幟春秋累書晉侵伐而不書楚救
punctuated:
考試官學正韓批〔按是非公予奪此作得之〕

霸主討貳，近乎正，春秋屢畧外夷恤患之名；霸主逼貳，近乎專，春秋特存外夷恤患之義。此鄭為夷夏必争之國，故晉之屢伐、楚之屢救，各有得失存焉。春秋得不按是非而致隱顯之法哉？慨自桓文邁往，霸統陵夷，荆楚每垂涎於北圖，鄭人常掉臂於南向。主霸圖者，豈可置之而不究厥心耶？晉靈首會衆師棐林，以聲鄭即楚之罪，而蔿賈之救隨至；繼偕四國往侵，以詰鄭伐宋之由，而鬬椒之救適臨。景公命將欒書以致伐，將討鄭之貳於楚也，子重迺討侵陳之策，以挽其謀；厲公合兵鄢陵以謀戰，將責鄭之叛夫晉也，楚子躬率救鄭之師，以泄其憤。夏之伐也，上屋尹單以臨戎，而子重又興首止之次；冬之伐也，再扳王臣以從事，而子申復為汝上之援。曲沃之旅奔走於溱洧者無寧歲，曾何挽其從楚之輈？江漢之衆應援於潁邦者無窮期，及有奪其慕華之幟。春秋累書晉侵伐而不書楚救
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Han, School Instructor: 〔In judging right and wrong and impartially granting or withholding approval, this composition gets it right.〕

When the hegemon punishes divided allegiance, his action approaches righteousness, and the Spring and Autumn Annals repeatedly omits the credit that foreign peoples might claim for relieving distress. When the hegemon coerces those of divided allegiance, his action approaches arbitrary domination, and the Annals expressly preserves the righteousness of foreign peoples’ relief of distress. Zheng was a state for which the foreign peoples and the central states were bound to contend. Thus Jin’s repeated attacks and Chu’s repeated rescues each had their merits and faults. Could the Annals fail to judge right and wrong and apply its method of concealment and disclosure?

Alas, after Dukes Huan and Wen had passed away, the succession of hegemons declined. Jing-Chu repeatedly cast covetous eyes northward, while the people of Zheng constantly swung their arms in unconcern as they turned southward. Could those directing the enterprise of hegemony leave this alone without investigating their intentions? Duke Ling of Jin first assembled the allied armies at Feilin to proclaim Zheng’s guilt in siding with Chu, but Wei Jia’s relief force promptly arrived. He subsequently joined four states in an invasion to demand an explanation for Zheng’s attack on Song, but Dou Jiao’s relief force arrived just then. Duke Jing ordered his general Luan Shu to launch an attack, intending to punish Zheng for its divided allegiance toward Chu; Zichong then considered a plan to invade Chen so as to thwart his design. Duke Li assembled troops at Yanling to give battle, intending to call Zheng to account for betraying Jin; the ruler of Chu personally led an army to rescue Zheng and vent his indignation.

In the summer attack, Shangwu Yin Dan [?] came to the battlefield, while Zichong in turn established an encampment at Shouzhi. In the winter attack, royal ministers were again drawn into the undertaking, while Zishen once more provided support on the Ru River. The troops of Quwo hurried back and forth along the Zhen and Wei rivers without a single peaceful year; yet how did they ever turn back Zheng’s carriage from following Chu? The hosts of the Jiang and Han rivers endlessly brought aid to the state on the Ying River, even taking away its banner of admiration for the central states [?]. The Spring and Autumn Annals repeatedly records Jin’s invasions and attacks but does not record Chu’s rescues…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
者良以晉尸霸權勤兵討貳所以□內夏外夷
之防楚本崛強睥睨諸姬不過爲猾夏陸梁之
計苟存而弗削則疑於予楚而罪晉矣故屢沒
其救以鄭無可救之義楚不得有能救之名也
迨夫悼公復霸鄭弗改圖載書雖聽命於五會
之詞玉帛猶懷疑於二境之待主夏盟者寧可
忽之而不慎厥念耶爰自虛朾嗣位以來無日
不以謀鄭爲事軍旅數興備申討貳之約洪壇
坫屢設蔑聞眼貳之成功使晉果能義以感鄭
===
則人無不懷夫何因其國難之多變遂即其巖
險以駐師倡集牛首之兵計爲虎牢之成謀非
不深也豈王者服遠之謨力非不足也豈大國
睦隣之道專其分地而紊亂周制有柔思城梧
及制而勞費財力有不恤既不能斷荊蠻之路
以蔽鄭又不能保小國之危以息爭反啓楚共
之謀得伸急病之義楚貞之救竊行拯溺之仁
春秋於戍鄭虎牢下而繼書公子貞之救者良
以悼欲復文襄之業扼險陵弱而道不足多楚
punctuated:
者，良以晉尸霸權，勤兵討貳，所以□內夏外夷之防。楚本崛強，睥睨諸姬，不過爲猾夏陸梁之計。苟存而弗削，則疑於予楚而罪晉矣。故屢沒其救，以鄭無可救之義，楚不得有能救之名也。
迨夫悼公復霸，鄭弗改圖，載書雖聽命於五會之詞，玉帛猶懷疑於二境之待。主夏盟者，寧可忽之而不慎厥念耶？爰自虛朾嗣位以來，無日不以謀鄭爲事。軍旅數興，備申討貳之約。洪壇坫屢設，蔑聞眼貳之成功。使晉果能義以感鄭，則人無不懷。夫何因其國難之多變，遂即其巖險以駐師，倡集牛首之兵，計爲虎牢之成？謀非不深也，豈王者服遠之謨？力非不足也，豈大國睦隣之道？專其分地而紊亂周制，有柔思；城梧及制而勞費財力，有不恤。既不能斷荊蠻之路以蔽鄭，又不能保小國之危以息爭，反啓楚共之謀，得伸急病之義；楚貞之救，竊行拯溺之仁。春秋於戍鄭虎牢下，而繼書公子貞之救者，良以悼欲復文襄之業，扼險陵弱，而道不足多，楚
translation_en:
…was precisely because Jin exercised the authority of hegemon and repeatedly mobilized troops to punish divided allegiance, thereby [illegible] the boundary that placed the Xia within and the Yi outside. Chu had always been stubbornly defiant, looking covetously upon the states of the Ji lineage; its schemes amounted to nothing more than disturbing the Xia and running rampant. Had the records of its relief expeditions been retained rather than omitted, this might have appeared to approve Chu and condemn Jin. Thus its relief expeditions were repeatedly left unrecorded: since there was no just cause for rescuing Zheng, Chu could not be credited with having rescued it.
When Duke Dao restored Jin’s hegemony, Zheng did not change its plans. Although in the covenant documents it accepted the terms pronounced at five meetings, its offerings of jade and silk still betrayed hesitation as it waited upon the two neighboring powers. Could the leader of the Xia alliance possibly disregard this and fail to give it careful thought? From his accession at Xuting onward, not a day passed without his making plans concerning Zheng. Armies were repeatedly raised, and agreements to punish divided allegiance were fully reaffirmed. Great covenant altars and ceremonial stands [?] were repeatedly set up, yet scarcely any success in overcoming divided allegiance [?] was heard of. Had Jin truly been able to move Zheng through righteousness, everyone would have felt drawn to it. Why, then, did it exploit the many upheavals afflicting that state, station troops in its rugged strongholds, take the lead in assembling an army at Niushou, and plan the fortification of Hulao? Its planning was certainly profound, but was this the strategy by which a true king wins the allegiance of distant peoples? Its strength was certainly sufficient, but was this the way a great state maintains harmony with its neighbors? It appropriated territory allotted to another state and disrupted Zhou institutions; the following words concerning conciliatory intentions are unclear [?]. It fortified Wu and Zhi [?], expending wealth and manpower without concern. It could neither block the routes of the Jing barbarians to shield Zheng nor safeguard the endangered small state and end the conflict. Instead, it opened the way for Duke Gong of Chu’s plans, allowing him to display the righteousness of hastening to aid those in distress; through his relief expedition, Zhen of Chu appropriated the benevolent role of rescuing the drowning.
The Spring and Autumn Annals follows its entry on garrisoning Zheng’s Hulao with an entry on Prince Zhen’s relief expedition precisely because Duke Dao wished to restore the achievements of Dukes Wen and Xiang, yet occupied strategic passes and bullied the weak: his conduct deserved little praise. Chu…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
雖效爲聞之尤假義安夏而名實可取茍削而
不書則疑於予晉而罪楚矣故特存其救許楚
有救患之義而著諸侯不仁之甚也吁伐者善
則救者非戍者非則救者善春秋彰善癉惡瑕
瑜莫掩明切有如是夫抑論之晉主諸夏之盟
鄭爲要領之國凡有兵爭皆閑於鄭靈景厲雖
致勤于貳爲楚所撓暫服卒離無足道矣悼公
此舉尚力而不尚德故楚得以間之厥後盟于
戲示不戰以服貳會蕭魚推至誠以感貳故鄭
===
亦以誠服不背晉者二十四年爲春秋一經之
盛舉誠非他霸所能匹也故曰悼公有君子之
資信夫
禮記
禮俗刑然後樂
徐盈
同考試官訓導孟　批　樂本於禮俗刑禮俗刑又
本於人君親親中來此作得之且文足以發其意必
深於禮者也
punctuated:
雖效爲聞之尤，假義安夏，而名實可取。茍削而不書，則疑於予晉而罪楚矣。故特存其救，許楚有救患之義，而著諸侯不仁之甚也。吁！伐者善則救者非，戍者非則救者善。《春秋》彰善癉惡，瑕瑜莫掩，明切有如是夫！抑論之，晉主諸夏之盟，鄭爲要領之國，凡有兵爭，皆閑於鄭。靈、景、厲雖致勤于貳，爲楚所撓，暫服卒離，無足道矣。悼公此舉，尚力而不尚德，故楚得以間之。厥後盟于戲，示不戰以服貳；會蕭魚，推至誠以感貳。故鄭亦以誠服，不背晉者二十四年，爲《春秋》一經之盛舉，誠非他霸所能匹也。故曰：「悼公有君子之資。」信夫！
禮記
禮俗刑然後樂。
徐盈
同考試官訓導孟批：樂本於禮俗刑，禮俗刑又本於人君親親中來。此作得之，且文足以發其意，必深於禮者也。
translation_en:
…though [Chu’s conduct is obscure in the transcription here: 效爲聞之尤, ?], it invoked righteousness to bring peace to the Xia states, and both its professed purpose and its actual achievement deserved recognition. If the account were deleted and left unrecorded, this might appear to approve of Jin and condemn Chu. Thus the relief expedition is expressly retained: Chu is credited with the righteousness of relieving distress, while the extreme inhumanity of the feudal lords is exposed. Ah! When the attacker is in the right, the rescuer is in the wrong; when the garrisoning party is in the wrong, the rescuer is in the right. The Spring and Autumn Annals makes goodness manifest and condemns evil, concealing neither faults nor virtues. How lucid and incisive it is!
To consider the matter further: Jin presided over the alliance of the Xia states, and Zheng occupied a pivotal position. Whenever armed conflict arose, it centered on Zheng [?]. Although Dukes Ling, Jing, and Li exerted themselves against Zheng’s divided allegiance, Chu thwarted them: Zheng submitted briefly but ultimately broke away. There is little worth recounting in this. In this undertaking Duke Dao prized force rather than virtue, so Chu was able to intervene. Later, at the covenant at Xi, he demonstrated that he could secure the submission of a wavering state without fighting; at the meeting at Xiaoyu, he extended his utmost sincerity to win it over. Zheng therefore submitted sincerely in return and did not turn against Jin for twenty-four years. This was a magnificent achievement in the entire Spring and Autumn Annals, truly beyond the ability of other hegemons to match. Thus it is said, “Duke Dao possessed the qualities of a gentleman.” How true!
Book of Rites
“Only after ritual customs have taken proper form is there joy.”
Xu Ying
Comment by Associate Examiner Meng, Assistant Instructor: Joy is rooted in ritual customs taking proper form; their taking proper form is in turn rooted in the ruler’s affection for his kin. This essay grasps that point, and its writing adequately develops its meaning. Its author must have a profound understanding of ritual.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭黃　批　可觀
考試官學正韓　批　說樂處最是
惟大化成於下斯至和充於上蓋禮俗大成非
人君親親不能致也下既成乎禮俗如此則上
豈不由之而樂也哉大傳君子知其然謂夫人
道莫先於親親親是以人君之親親也尊祖而敬
宗敬宗而收族推而至於庶民安矣百志成矣
自家而國咸知親親之禮雍雍乎上下和同而
乖爭凌犯之不作自國而天下皆知親親之道
===
藹藹乎長幼親睦而强梁鬬辨之不生三綱正
焉六禮脩焉民俗由是而至變也七教明焉六
紀敘焉禮俗由是而大成也遵道而遵路不虞
天性者何有耶會極而歸極不違帝典者何在
耶夫如是則協氣嘉生薰為大和三光全而寒
暑時五穀熟而民人育吾知人君垂紳於九重
之上恭己於南面之尊宗社安矣三才應矣內
患不必憂也外侮不必慮也歡忻之情自爾而
暢達鍾鼓云乎哉海宇寧矣四靈至矣無弗若
punctuated:
考試官教諭黃批：「可觀。」
考試官學正韓批：「說樂處最是。」
惟大化成於下，斯至和充於上。蓋禮俗大成，非人君親親不能致也。下既成乎禮俗如此，則上豈不由之而樂也哉？《大傳》君子知其然，謂夫人道莫先於親親親，是以人君之親親也，尊祖而敬宗，敬宗而收族，推而至於庶民安矣，百志成矣。自家而國，咸知親親之禮，雍雍乎上下和同，而乖爭凌犯之不作；自國而天下，皆知親親之道，藹藹乎長幼親睦，而强梁鬬辨之不生。三綱正焉，六禮脩焉，民俗由是而至變也；七教明焉，六紀敘焉，禮俗由是而大成也。遵道而遵路，不虞天性者何有耶？會極而歸極，不違帝典者何在耶？夫如是，則協氣嘉生，薰為大和，三光全而寒暑時，五穀熟而民人育。吾知人君垂紳於九重之上，恭己於南面之尊，宗社安矣，三才應矣，內患不必憂也，外侮不必慮也，歡忻之情自爾而暢達，鍾鼓云乎哉？海宇寧矣，四靈至矣，無弗若
translation_en:
Examiner Huang, Instructor of a County Confucian School, comments: “Worthy of attention.”
Examiner Han, Instructor of a Subprefectural Confucian School, comments: “The discussion of joy is especially apt.”
Only when the great moral transformation is accomplished below does perfect harmony fill the realm above. For the full realization of ritual and customary observances cannot be achieved unless the ruler cherishes his kin. Once these observances have been perfected below in this way, how could the ruler above fail to find joy in them? The gentleman who composed the “Great Tradition” (Da zhuan) understood why this was so: in the human way, nothing takes precedence over cherishing one’s kin [the transcription repeats 親 here]. Thus, in cherishing his kin, the ruler honors his ancestors and respects the lineage head; respecting the lineage head, he draws the clan together. Extended further, this brings peace to the common people and fulfills their manifold aspirations. From the family to the state, all understand the rites of cherishing kin. Superiors and inferiors live together in gracious harmony, and discord, contention, oppression, and encroachment do not arise. From the state to all under Heaven, all understand the way of cherishing kin. Elders and juniors live in warm affection and concord, and violence, fighting, and disputation do not arise. The Three Bonds are set right and the Six Rites cultivated: through these, popular customs are transformed to the utmost. The Seven Teachings are made clear and the Six Relationships put in order: through these, ritual and customary observances reach their fullest realization. Following the Way and its paths, who would fail to heed their natural disposition? Gathering at the supreme standard and returning to it, where are those who do not transgress the sovereign’s canons [?]?
When things are thus, harmonious energies and auspicious living things blend into great concord. The three celestial lights shine in their fullness, cold and heat come in season, the five grains ripen, and the people flourish. I know that the ruler, his ceremonial sash hanging down within the palace’s ninefold precincts, reverently conducts himself in the honored position facing south. The ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain are secure, and the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—respond in accord. He need not worry about internal troubles or fear insults from abroad. His feelings of delight naturally find full expression: can this be merely a matter of bells and drums? All within the seas is at peace, the Four Numinous Creatures arrive, and there are none who do not conform…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
於政者以賠其憂無弗化於訓者以拂其志悅
懌之意自爾而動盪管絃云乎哉群黎百姓鼓
舞於光天化日之下庶民小子踴躍於春臺玉
燭之中含哺而嬉鼓腹而樂所謂無斁於人者
此也日出而作日入而息所謂在彼無惡者此
也是則至和之充固本於禮俗之成而禮俗之
成實自人君親親中來也任君人之責者可不
加意於此哉嗟夫君道固以親親為本而親親
舍尊祖敬宗收族之外無他為也茍不親親則
===
家不齊安望國與天下而治而平哉觀帝堯之
萬邦協和始於九族之親睦帝舜之四方風動
始於五典之愼徽真萬世君人之龜鑑也故曰
聖人南面而治天下必自人道始良有以歟
流而不息合同而化而樂興焉
符錫
同考試官訓導孟　批〔通篇知樂興之旨者最少惟此卷認理真切措辭穩貼宜錄之以示後學〕
考試官教諭黃　批〔樂記我似此說理透徹而錄〕
punctuated:
於政者以賠其憂，無弗化於訓者以拂其志。悅懌之意，自爾而動盪，管絃云乎哉？群黎百姓鼓舞於光天化日之下，庶民小子踴躍於春臺玉燭之中，含哺而嬉，鼓腹而樂，所謂無斁於人者，此也；日出而作，日入而息，所謂在彼無惡者，此也。是則至和之充，固本於禮俗之成；而禮俗之成，實自人君親親中來也。任君人之責者，可不加意於此哉？嗟夫！君道固以親親為本，而親親舍尊祖、敬宗、收族之外，無他為也。茍不親親，則家不齊，安望國與天下而治而平哉？觀帝堯之萬邦協和，始於九族之親睦；帝舜之四方風動，始於五典之愼徽，真萬世君人之龜鑑也。故曰：「聖人南面而治天下，必自人道始。」良有以歟！

流而不息，合同而化，而樂興焉。
符錫

同考試官訓導孟，批〔通篇知樂興之旨者最少，惟此卷認理真切，措辭穩貼，宜錄之以示後學。〕

考試官教諭黃，批〔樂記我似此說理透徹而錄〕
translation_en:
…in governance so as to add to his worries [?]; none remains untransformed by instruction so as to thwart his wishes. Feelings of delight and joy naturally stir and surge: can this be merely a matter of pipes and strings? The common people rejoice beneath the bright heavens and the sun of transforming influence; ordinary folk and their children leap for joy as though upon a terrace in spring, amid the radiant harmony of the seasons. With food in their mouths they frolic; patting their full bellies, they rejoice. This is what is meant by “never wearying of others.” They rise to work at sunrise and rest at sunset. This is what is meant by “there, none bears ill will.” Thus, the fullness of perfect harmony rests upon the perfection of ritual and custom; and the perfection of ritual and custom truly originates in the ruler’s affection for his kin. Can those charged with ruling others fail to give this special attention?

Alas! The ruler’s way is indeed rooted in affection for kin, and such affection consists in honoring ancestors, revering the lineage’s progenitors, and drawing the clan together. If one does not cherish one’s kin, one’s household will be disordered. How, then, can one expect the state and all under Heaven to be well governed and at peace? Consider how Emperor Yao’s harmonizing of the myriad states began with affection and concord among the nine degrees of kinship, and how Emperor Shun’s influence spreading like the wind in all four directions began with his careful promotion of the five teachings governing human relationships. These truly are models for rulers in every age. Thus it is said: “When the sage faces south and governs all under Heaven, he must begin with the human way.” There is good reason for this indeed!

“They flow without ceasing, unite and transform, and music arises.”
Fu Xi

Associate Examiner Meng, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Very few understand throughout their essays the purport of ‘music arises.’ This paper alone grasps the principles truly and precisely, and its wording is sound and fitting. It should be recorded to instruct later students.”

Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “The Record of Music—[?] like this, explaining the principles thoroughly, and recording …”

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
句純和者絕少非子苦心於是經而旁通卦辭氣化之
說者不能用是錄之
考試官學正韓　批〔樂最難言此作可羨可羨〕
即和之運於兩間見樂之肇於兩間蓋樂以和
為主也造化運自然之和如此則樂不於是而
興乎記樂者知其然蓋謂樂雖作於聖人而始
則肇於天地彼天地之道一陰一陽而已陽氣
下降而摩蕩乎陰陰氣上躋而摩蕩乎陽但見
鼓之以雷霆奮之以風雨莫非陰陽之氣之鼓
===
奮無一息之或停也動之以四時煖之以日月
罔非陰陽之氣之動煖無一時之或息也至和
磅礴於兩間大化均調於宇宙由是若飛若潛
咸相育於訢合之中若動若植舉相養於絪緼
之內物類雖萬不齊也一化醇之天而不容以
獨異品彙雖萬不一也均合同之仁而不容以
群分造化示人以自然之樂情如此吾知樂有
五聲也實於此乎胚胎樂有八音也實於是乎
根柢清濁相應興於上躋下降之幾非人為之
punctuated:
句純和者絕少，非子苦心於是經而旁通卦辭氣化之說者不能，用是錄之。
考試官學正韓　批〔樂最難言，此作可羨，可羨！〕
即和之運於兩間，見樂之肇於兩間，蓋樂以和為主也。造化運自然之和如此，則樂不於是而興乎？記樂者知其然，蓋謂樂雖作於聖人，而始則肇於天地。彼天地之道，一陰一陽而已。陽氣下降而摩蕩乎陰，陰氣上躋而摩蕩乎陽。但見鼓之以雷霆，奮之以風雨，莫非陰陽之氣之鼓奮，無一息之或停也；動之以四時，煖之以日月，罔非陰陽之氣之動煖，無一時之或息也。至和磅礴於兩間，大化均調於宇宙。由是若飛若潛，咸相育於訢合之中；若動若植，舉相養於絪緼之內。物類雖萬不齊也，一化醇之天，而不容以獨異；品彙雖萬不一也，均合同之仁，而不容以群分。造化示人以自然之樂情如此。吾知樂有五聲也，實於此乎胚胎；樂有八音也，實於是乎根柢。清濁相應，興於上躋下降之幾，非人為之
translation_en:
…those whose sentences are pure and harmonious are exceedingly rare. Without your painstaking study of this classic and your broad understanding of the explanations of the hexagram statements and the transformations of vital energy, this could not be accomplished. For this reason, I have selected it for inclusion.
Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: 〔Music is most difficult to discuss. This composition is admirable, admirable!〕
In the operation of harmony between Heaven and Earth, one sees the origin of music between them, for harmony is the governing principle of music. Since the creative workings of Heaven and Earth circulate natural harmony in this way, does not music arise from this? The author of the Record of Music understood why this is so. His meaning was that although music was fashioned by the sages, its beginnings originated in Heaven and Earth. The Way of Heaven and Earth is simply the alternation of yin and yang. Yang energy descends, rubbing against and stirring yin; yin energy rises, rubbing against and stirring yang. We see things stirred by thunder and lightning and roused by wind and rain: these are all the stirring and rousing of yin and yang energies, never halting for a single breath. Things are moved by the four seasons and warmed by the sun and moon: these are all the movement and warming of yin and yang energies, never ceasing for a single moment. Perfect harmony pervades the space between Heaven and Earth, and the great process of transformation brings balanced accord throughout the universe.
Thus, creatures that fly and creatures that swim in the depths all nurture one another within this joyful union; moving creatures and rooted plants all nourish one another within this intermingling of vital energies. Though the myriad kinds of things differ, they share one Heaven that transforms them into fullness, allowing none to stand apart. Though the myriad categories of beings are diverse, they share equally in the benevolence that unites them, allowing no division into separate groups. Such are the natural dispositions of music that the creative workings of Heaven and Earth reveal to humanity. I know that music has five notes: here indeed they take embryonic form. Music has eight classes of instrumental sound: here indeed they have their roots. High and low tones respond to one another, arising from the incipient workings of ascent and descent, and are not something that human contrivance…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
所始也小大相成與於相摩相蕩之妙非私智
之所及也清明象乎天廣大象乎地何者不肇
始於造化乎終始象四時周旋象風雨何者不
權輿於造化乎是則造化至和之所在即樂之
所在也聖人作樂一本於此此大樂所以與天
地同和也歟嗟夫樂固本於天地之和而禮則
本於天地之序禮樂豈易作哉必有聖人之德
居天子之位斯可作樂以應天制禮以配地也
禮樂明備則天地生成各得其職矣是知天地
===
也者乃禮樂之本原聖人也者又禮樂之宗主
歟後世若叔孫朝儀之建孝孫雅樂之奏不過
糟粕之末而已烏足以語此
第貳場
論
人主務聰明之實
劉節
同考試官教諭徐　批〔議論泉涌山出豊而健約而〕
明辨而不激深而不晦紆徐婉曲含不盡之意有古人
punctuated:
所始也。小大相成，與於相摩相蕩之妙，非私智之所及也。清明象乎天，廣大象乎地，何者不肇始於造化乎？終始象四時，周旋象風雨，何者不權輿於造化乎？是則造化至和之所在，即樂之所在也。聖人作樂，一本於此，此大樂所以與天地同和也歟！嗟夫！樂固本於天地之和，而禮則本於天地之序，禮樂豈易作哉？必有聖人之德，居天子之位，斯可作樂以應天，制禮以配地也。禮樂明備，則天地生成各得其職矣。是知天地也者，乃禮樂之本原；聖人也者，又禮樂之宗主歟！後世若叔孫朝儀之建、孝孫雅樂之奏，不過糟粕之末而已，烏足以語此？

第貳場
論
人主務聰明之實
劉節

同考試官教諭徐，批〔議論泉涌山出，豊而健，約而〕明，辨而不激，深而不晦，紆徐婉曲，含不盡之意，有古人
translation_en:
…originated by human contrivance. The small and the great complete one another, participating in the wondrous workings of mutual interaction and agitation; this lies beyond the reach of individual cleverness. Its clarity and brightness resemble Heaven; its breadth and greatness resemble Earth. Which of these does not originate in the creative processes of nature? Its endings and beginnings resemble the four seasons; its circling movements resemble wind and rain. Which of these does not take its beginning from those creative processes? Thus, wherever the supreme harmony of nature’s creative processes resides, there too resides music. The sage’s making of music is rooted entirely in this. Is this not why great music shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth?

Alas! Music is indeed rooted in the harmony of Heaven and Earth, while ritual is rooted in their order. How could ritual and music be easy to establish? Only one who possesses the virtue of a sage and occupies the position of the Son of Heaven can make music to respond to Heaven and institute ritual to accord with Earth. When ritual and music are fully manifest and complete, Heaven and Earth each fulfill their functions of giving birth and bringing to maturity. From this we know that Heaven and Earth are the source of ritual and music, and that the sage is their presiding authority. Such later achievements as Shusun’s establishment of court ceremonial and Xiaosun’s performance of elegant music are merely residual dregs. How could they suffice for discussing this?

Second Session
Discourse
The Ruler Must Pursue the Substance of Perceptiveness and Understanding
Liu Jie

Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “The argument gushes like a spring and rises like a mountain: abundant yet vigorous, concise yet lucid, discriminating without being strident, profound without being obscure. Unhurried and gently indirect, it holds inexhaustible meaning and has the ancients’…”

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
諷諫體錄之豈但以其文而已哉
同考試官教諭季　批　閱卷多矣類能逞浮華而
鮮切實此作詞根乎理有抑揚有頓挫意新而奇
文字體當如此
同考試官學正楊　批　議論當理文字圓活非此
論不足以發朱夫子所言之旨筆力如此當三歎服
考試官教諭黄　批　此論詞源筆鋒與彭蠡匡
廬漾闘爭高秋闈作解舍子其誰
考試官學正韓　批　議論英發無一贅語可嘉
===
人君以知臨天下當于其大焉而于其小
者適足以為累也夫天下之事至繁至賾
一日萬幾綱之紀之皆主於人君之心心
之能應事者曰知知一也而所以為知者
二故任其公人審以求是是謂大知知至
於大則有以通天下之故當天下之至繁
任天下之至賾而天下稱哲稱聖苟惟私
人是任言輒信焉將以竦動乎人而不知
其蔽塞已甚自哲自聖昏愚係之所謂綱
punctuated:
諷諫體，錄之豈但以其文而已哉！
同考試官教諭季批：閱卷多矣，類能逞浮華而鮮切實。此作詞根乎理，有抑揚，有頓挫，意新而奇，文字體當如此。
同考試官學正楊批：議論當理，文字圓活，非此論不足以發朱夫子所言之旨。筆力如此，當三歎服。
考試官教諭黄批：此論詞源筆鋒，與彭蠡、匡廬漾闘爭高。秋闈作解，舍子其誰！
考試官學正韓批：議論英發，無一贅語，可嘉。
人君以知臨天下，當于其大焉，而于其小者，適足以為累也。夫天下之事，至繁至賾，一日萬幾，綱之紀之，皆主於人君之心。心之能應事者曰知。知一也，而所以為知者二。故任其公人審以求是，是謂大知。知至於大，則有以通天下之故，當天下之至繁，任天下之至賾，而天下稱哲稱聖。苟惟私人是任，言輒信焉，將以竦動乎人，而不知其蔽塞已甚，自哲自聖，昏愚係之，所謂綱
translation_en:
…the manner of the ancients’ indirect remonstrance. Could its inclusion here be merely for its literary merits?

Associate Examiner Ji, Instructor, comments: I have read many examination papers. Most display superficial ornament, and few address substantive matters. The language of this piece is rooted in principle; it has rises and falls, pauses and turns. Its ideas are fresh and unusual. This is how prose ought to be written.

Associate Examiner Yang, School Director, comments: The argument accords with principle, and the writing is fluent and lively. Nothing less than this discourse could bring out the meaning of Master Zhu’s words. Such strength of expression deserves repeated admiration.

Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: The wellspring of this discourse’s language and the sharpness of its brush contend with the surging waters of Pengli and vie with Kuanglu in height. Who but you should take first place in the autumn Provincial Examination?

Examiner Han, School Director, comments: The argument is brilliant and spirited, without a single superfluous phrase. Commendable.

When a ruler governs All-under-Heaven through understanding, he should attend to its greater aspects; attending to its lesser aspects serves only to encumber him. The affairs of All-under-Heaven are exceedingly numerous and intricate. Each day brings myriad matters requiring attention, and their ordering and regulation depend entirely upon the ruler’s mind. The mind’s capacity to respond to affairs is called understanding. Understanding is one, but there are two ways in which it operates. Thus, relying upon impartial men and examining matters to seek what is right [?] is called great understanding. When understanding attains greatness, it enables one to comprehend the circumstances of All-under-Heaven, manage its utmost complexity, and shoulder its most intricate affairs; then all acclaim the ruler as wise and sage. If, however, he employs only his personal adherents and believes whatever they say, hoping thereby to overawe others, he fails to recognize how severely his own perception has already been obstructed. He deems himself wise and sage, but benighted folly follows. What are called the guiding bonds…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
紀者紊矣其為知也不亦小乎宋儒朱子
進説於君欲其嚴朝廷之綱紀而申之以
人主當務聰明之實此蓋吾之所謂大知
者也知大知之説斯可與論聰明之實矣
且聰明者耳目之德也而心實主之人君
之心天下之主也而假其用於耳目耳一
也而欲周天下之聽目一也而欲周天下
之視其將能乎必也不自用而假諸人故
曰明四目達四聰舜之所以為大知者政
===
惟有得乎此爾世之人君孰不欲聰明先
物而稱大知哉耳目之德雖同於天下而
其心或出於公或出於私故同一任人而
所任者異則其為聰明也亦異焉今夫天
下之事夥矣節之有禮和之有樂道之有
政齊之有刑弛張損益舉置推移其在物
也有則其在民也有情其在人才也有品
有類可者否者是者非者常叢沓於人君
之前人君雖以制命為職然必謀之大臣
punctuated:
紀者紊矣，其為知也，不亦小乎？宋儒朱子進説於君，欲其嚴朝廷之綱紀，而申之以人主當務聰明之實。此蓋吾之所謂大知者也。知大知之説，斯可與論聰明之實矣。
且聰明者，耳目之德也，而心實主之。人君之心，天下之主也，而假其用於耳目。耳一也，而欲周天下之聽；目一也，而欲周天下之視，其將能乎？必也不自用而假諸人。故曰：「明四目，達四聰。」舜之所以為大知者，政惟有得乎此爾。世之人君，孰不欲聰明先物而稱大知哉？耳目之德雖同於天下，而其心或出於公，或出於私。故同一任人，而所任者異，則其為聰明也亦異焉。
今夫天下之事夥矣，節之有禮，和之有樂，道之有政，齊之有刑。弛張損益，舉置推移，其在物也有則，其在民也有情，其在人才也有品有類。可者否者，是者非者，常叢沓於人君之前。人君雖以制命為職，然必謀之大臣
translation_en:
…the ordering principles become disordered. Is such wisdom not petty? The Song Confucian Master Zhu submitted an explanation to his ruler, urging him to uphold strictly the court’s ordering principles, and further stressing that the ruler must attend to the substance of clear hearing and vision. This, surely, is what I call great wisdom. Only one who understands the teaching of great wisdom can discuss the substance of clear hearing and vision.
Now, clear hearing and vision are the virtues of the ears and eyes, but it is the mind that truly governs them. The ruler’s mind is master of all under Heaven, yet it exercises its function through the ears and eyes. With only his own ears, he wishes to encompass all that is heard under Heaven; with only his own eyes, he wishes to encompass all that is seen under Heaven. How could he accomplish this? He must avoid relying solely on himself and draw upon others. Thus it is said: “Make clear the eyes of the four quarters and open up the hearing of the four quarters.” Shun’s great wisdom consisted precisely in his grasp of this. What ruler would not wish to possess clear hearing and vision, anticipate events, and be acclaimed as greatly wise? Although rulers share the faculties of hearing and sight with everyone under Heaven, their minds may proceed either from public-mindedness or from private interest. Thus, although all alike entrust responsibilities to others, when those whom they employ differ, their clarity of hearing and vision also differs.
Now, the affairs of all under Heaven are multitudinous. Ritual regulates them; music harmonizes them; government guides them; punishments bring them into order. Relaxation and tightening, diminution and augmentation, appointment and dismissal, adjustment and change: in things there are governing patterns; among the people there are feelings and circumstances; among talented men there are grades and categories. What is acceptable and what is not, what is right and what is wrong, continually crowd together before the ruler. Although the ruler’s duty is to issue commands, he must consult his high ministers…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
焉而後應之蓋自人君下至百執事皆有
職業不可相侵此固朝廷之綱紀也是故
三公論道六卿分職諮之詢之稽之質之
博之侍從參之給舍使之反覆熟議以求
是非可否之所在吾之所主果得其當而
行且嚴之固吾之聽吾之明也如其不然
則舍己從人人皆曰是必誠是也吾從而
是之人皆曰非必誠非也吾從而非之人
皆曰可必誠可也人皆曰否必誠否也吾
===
從而可否之然後揚于王庭明出命令是
而可者行之非而否者罷之雖其計慮規
為不出於我而我能用之綱紀由是而振
爾朝廷由是而尊嚴即其事而觀之耳不
必聽而能極天下之聽目不必視而能極
天下之明豈非天下之大聰明者哉何也
聰者無所不聞之謂也有所不聞斯謂之
不聰矣明者無所不見之謂也有所不見
斯謂之不明矣今也以天下之人圖天下
punctuated: 焉而後應之。蓋自人君下至百執事，皆有職業，不可相侵，此固朝廷之綱紀也。是故三公論道，六卿分職，諮之詢之，稽之質之，博之侍從，參之給舍，使之反覆熟議，以求是非可否之所在。吾之所主果得其當，而行且嚴之，固吾之聽、吾之明也。如其不然，則舍己從人。人皆曰是，必誠是也，吾從而是之；人皆曰非，必誠非也，吾從而非之；人皆曰可，必誠可也；人皆曰否，必誠否也，吾從而可否之。然後揚于王庭，明出命令，是而可者行之，非而否者罷之。雖其計慮規為不出於我，而我能用之，綱紀由是而振爾，朝廷由是而尊嚴。即其事而觀之，耳不必聽，而能極天下之聽；目不必視，而能極天下之明。豈非天下之大聰明者哉？何也？聰者，無所不聞之謂也，有所不聞，斯謂之不聰矣；明者，無所不見之謂也，有所不見，斯謂之不明矣。今也，以天下之人圖天下
translation_en: …and only then respond to the matter. From the ruler down to the officials charged with conducting affairs, all have their own duties and must not encroach upon one another. This is indeed the governing order of the court. Thus the Three Dukes deliberate upon the Way, and the Six Ministers divide the responsibilities of office. The ruler consults and questions them, examines and verifies their proposals, broadens his consultations to the attendant officials, and checks them with the Supervising Secretaries and Secretariat Drafters. He has them deliberate thoroughly and repeatedly to determine what is right or wrong, acceptable or unacceptable. If what I, the ruler, favor proves appropriate, I put it into practice and enforce it strictly: this indeed constitutes my own discernment in hearing and seeing. If it does not, I set aside my own views and follow others. When all say something is right, it must truly be right, and I follow them in approving it. When all say something is wrong, it must truly be wrong, and I follow them in rejecting it. When all say something is acceptable, it must truly be acceptable; when all say it is unacceptable, it must truly be unacceptable. I follow them in accepting or rejecting it. Only then is it proclaimed in the royal court and clearly issued as a command: what is right and acceptable is carried out, and what is wrong and unacceptable is discontinued. Although the deliberations and plans do not originate with me, I can employ them. Through this the governing order is invigorated and the court acquires dignity and authority. Judging from these affairs, the ruler’s ears need not themselves listen for him to draw fully upon the hearing of all under Heaven; his eyes need not themselves look for him to draw fully upon the vision of all under Heaven. Is he not, then, a man of supreme discernment in hearing and seeing? Why is this so? Discernment in hearing means that there is nothing one does not hear; if there is something one does not hear, this is called a lack of discernment in hearing. Discernment in seeing means that there is nothing one does not see; if there is something one does not see, this is called a lack of discernment in seeing. Now, employing the people of all under Heaven to deliberate upon the affairs of all under Heaven…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之事吾任大臣而大臣者又合天下之耳
目以為吾一人聰明之助謂吾弗聰而吾
行無不當也有弗聞者能之乎故曰耳不
必聽而能極天下之聰謂吾弗明而吾行
無不中也有弗見者能之乎故曰目不必
視而能極天下之明曰哲曰聖頌聲流焉
書曰視遠惟明聽德惟聰又曰亶聰明作
元后其道如此此則所謂聰明之實者以
公心而任其公人也易曰知臨大君之宜
===
豈不信哉乃若好名者亦知任人矣然或
任非所任而偏聽輕信得其一言行則行
罷則罷自彼觀之可以發奸可以擿伏可
以破幽入隱可以致摠攬之名可以收獨
斷之譽而講張熒蠱顛倒易置卒不出其
術數之內遠之愈繆久之愈暗自以為聰
而實有未聞自以為明而實有未見名為
獨斷而主威不免於下移名為摠攬而國
政不免於參出由是綱紀紊而庶事以墮
punctuated:
之事，吾任大臣，而大臣者又合天下之耳目，以為吾一人聰明之助。謂吾弗聰，而吾行無不當也，有弗聞者能之乎？故曰：耳不必聽，而能極天下之聰。謂吾弗明，而吾行無不中也，有弗見者能之乎？故曰：目不必視，而能極天下之明。曰哲曰聖，頌聲流焉。《書》曰：「視遠惟明，聽德惟聰。」又曰：「亶聰明作元后。」其道如此。此則所謂聰明之實者，以公心而任其公人也。《易》曰：「知臨，大君之宜。」豈不信哉？
乃若好名者，亦知任人矣。然或任非所任，而偏聽輕信，得其一言，行則行，罷則罷。自彼觀之，可以發奸，可以擿伏，可以破幽入隱，可以致摠攬之名，可以收獨斷之譽。而講張熒蠱，顛倒易置，卒不出其術數之內。遠之愈繆，久之愈暗，自以為聰，而實有未聞；自以為明，而實有未見。名為獨斷，而主威不免於下移；名為摠攬，而國政不免於參出。由是綱紀紊，而庶事以墮。
translation_en:
…the affairs of all under Heaven. I entrust great ministers with responsibility, and these ministers in turn bring together the ears and eyes of all under Heaven to assist my own hearing and sight. You may say that I lack acuity of hearing, yet none of my actions is inappropriate. Could someone who failed to hear accomplish this? Thus it is said: the ears need not themselves listen to attain the fullest acuity of hearing in all under Heaven. You may say that I lack clarity of sight, yet none of my actions misses the mark. Could someone who failed to see accomplish this? Thus it is said: the eyes need not themselves look to attain the fullest clarity of sight in all under Heaven. Acclamations flow forth, calling him wise and sagely. The Book of Documents says: “Seeing far constitutes clear sight; heeding virtue constitutes acute hearing.” It also says: “One truly acute in hearing and clear in sight becomes the sovereign.” Such is the way. This is what is meant by the substance of perceptiveness: employing public-minded men with a public-minded heart. The Book of Changes says: “Wise oversight: what befits a great ruler.” Is this not indeed true?
As for those who love reputation, they too know to employ others. Yet they may employ unsuitable men, listen to only one side, and trust too readily. On receiving a single word from such a man, they proceed if he says to proceed and desist if he says to desist. From their own perspective, they can thereby expose wickedness, uncover concealed wrongdoing, penetrate obscurity and hidden matters, acquire a reputation for comprehensive control, and win praise for deciding independently. Yet through the elaboration of schemes and bewildering deception [?], through inversions and substitutions, they ultimately remain within the compass of those men’s manipulative arts. The further they go, the more mistaken they become; the longer this continues, the more benighted they grow. They consider their hearing acute, yet there are things they have not heard; they consider their sight clear, yet there are things they have not seen. In name they decide independently, yet the ruler’s authority inevitably passes down to his subordinates. In name they exercise comprehensive control, yet the government’s decisions inevitably issue from multiple quarters. Thus the governing order falls into confusion, and all affairs fall into neglect…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
蓋以私心而任私人其極必至於是所謂
自哲自聖而昏愚係之此之謂也夫求聰
明之名而乃為昏愚之歸其視圖任大臣
不求為聰明而大知歸焉者真所謂毫釐
千里矣人君不欲天下之治則已如欲求
治二者將孰務哉知之大小聰明之名實
不可不審也雖然亦在乎學而已矣舜之
告禹曰人心惟危道心惟微惟精惟一允
執厥中此萬世聖學之源也人君務聰明
===
之實以成大知者其必由聖學乎故朱子
他日告君又曰心正則視明聽聰由是觀
之不由聖學以正其心而求聰明則公私
交雜吾見求實而近僅止於名其知終不
足以有臨也此朱子此疏未及之意也故
併論之
表
擬宋以歐陽脩知制誥謝表〔慶曆三年〕
劉禔
punctuated:
蓋以私心而任私人，其極必至於是。所謂「自哲自聖而昏愚係之」，此之謂也。夫求聰明之名，而乃為昏愚之歸，其視圖任大臣、不求為聰明而大知歸焉者，真所謂毫釐千里矣。人君不欲天下之治則已，如欲求治，二者將孰務哉？知之大小、聰明之名實，不可不審也。雖然，亦在乎學而已矣。舜之告禹曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。」此萬世聖學之源也。人君務聰明之實以成大知者，其必由聖學乎？故朱子他日告君又曰：「心正則視明聽聰。」由是觀之，不由聖學以正其心而求聰明，則公私交雜。吾見求實而近僅止於名，其知終不足以有臨也。此朱子此疏未及之意也，故併論之。
表
擬宋以歐陽脩知制誥謝表〔慶曆三年〕
劉禔
translation_en:
For when a ruler appoints personal favorites out of selfish motives, things must ultimately reach this point. This is precisely what is meant by the saying, “Those who consider themselves wise and sagely are followed by darkness and folly.” To seek a reputation for perceptiveness, only to end in darkness and folly—compared with choosing and entrusting great ministers, thereby attaining great wisdom without seeking to appear perceptive—is truly a case of a hair’s breadth becoming a thousand miles. If a ruler does not desire good government throughout the realm, there is nothing more to say; but if he does seek it, which of these two courses should he pursue? The distinction between lesser and greater wisdom, and between the reputation and reality of perceptiveness, must be carefully examined.
Nevertheless, this too depends simply on learning. Shun’s admonition to Yu says: “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning and single-minded, and sincerely hold fast to the mean.” This is the source of sagely learning for all ages. Must not a ruler who pursues true perceptiveness in order to attain great wisdom proceed through sagely learning? Thus Master Zhu, on another occasion, also told his sovereign: “When the mind is rectified, sight becomes clear and hearing acute.” Viewed in this light, seeking perceptiveness without rectifying one’s mind through sagely learning allows public-mindedness and selfishness to intermingle. I see that one who seeks the reality comes close only to attaining the reputation [?]; his wisdom will ultimately be insufficient to govern. This is a point that Master Zhu did not address in this memorial, and I have therefore discussed it as well.
Memorial
A simulated memorial of thanks on Ouyang Xiu’s appointment as Drafter under the Song dynasty 〔Third year of Qingli〕
Liu Ti

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭張 批 著述有式摸倣得真方是
制作法歐文典雅渾純意趣高遠人鮮能之諸作
逞辭浮靡殊失本相又體貼職掌不類事實或
遺令人厭觀此篇古淡舂容宛然六一家風致噫
大羹玄酒咀之而有餘味義要能舍乎
考試官教諭黄 批 寫出歐陽公謦咳中真
意趣惟作也
考試官學正韓 批 得駢儷體可嘉
臣某言伏奉
===
制命蒙恩特授臣右正言知制誥者伏以人
文藻潤聿昭
雲漢之章道化鋪揚叵測
乾坤之大惟典謨渾灝誓誥渙汹迨相如諭
蜀之文敬輿奉天之詔皆能言為世式動
中事宜肆在
本朝特難是選豈期末學亦濫茲除攙濫羨
於
制詞沐
punctuated:
同考試官教諭張批：著述有式，摸倣得真，方是制作法。歐文典雅渾純，意趣高遠，人鮮能之。諸作逞辭浮靡，殊失本相；又體貼職掌不類，事實或遺，令人厭觀。此篇古淡舂容，宛然六一家風致。噫！大羹玄酒，咀之而有餘味，義要能舍乎？
考試官教諭黄批：寫出歐陽公謦咳中真意趣，惟作也。
考試官學正韓批：得駢儷體，可嘉。
臣某言：伏奉制命，蒙恩特授臣右正言知制誥者。伏以人文藻潤，聿昭雲漢之章；道化鋪揚，叵測乾坤之大。惟典謨渾灝，誓誥渙汹。迨相如諭蜀之文、敬輿奉天之詔，皆能言為世式，動中事宜。肆在本朝，特難是選。豈期末學，亦濫茲除？攙濫羨於制詞，沐
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Writing has its established forms; only imitation that captures their true character constitutes a proper method of composition. Ouyang’s prose is classically elegant, integrated and pure, with lofty meaning and spirit; few can achieve this. The other compositions flaunt their diction and indulge in superficial ornament, thoroughly losing his original character. Moreover, their representations of his official duties are incongruous, and they sometimes omit the facts, making them tiresome to read. This piece is antique and unadorned, expansive and unhurried, quite capturing the distinctive manner of Liuyi [Ouyang Xiu]. Ah! Like the unseasoned sacrificial broth and the plain water offered as “dark wine,” it leaves a lingering savor when tasted. Can its essential meaning be dispensed with [?]?
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: It conveys the true meaning and spirit in Lord Ouyang’s very voice—this composition alone [?].
Comment by Examiner Han, School Instructor: It captures the style of parallel prose and deserves praise.
Your servant, so-and-so, states: I have reverently received the imperial command, graciously appointing me Rectifier of Omissions of the Right and Drafter of Imperial Edicts. I humbly consider that the embellishment and refinement of literary culture manifest the splendor of the heavenly Milky Way; the dissemination of the Way’s transforming influence reveals the unfathomable greatness of Heaven and Earth. The Canons and Counsels are vast and profound; the Oaths and Announcements surge abundantly. Subsequently, such works as Sima Xiangru’s proclamation to Shu and Lu Jingyu’s edict issued at Fengtian made their language a model for the age, invariably fitting the needs of affairs. Thus, under our present dynasty, selecting a man for this office is particularly difficult. How could I, a man of meager learning, have expected to receive this appointment without deserving it? Amid the excessive praise in the wording of the decree [?], I am bathed in …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
殊恩於
宸注感先愧集責與憂并恭惟
○○○○道同天地
孝達神明仁恕根於心恭儉出其性禮隆
會慶履端先晉於
慈宮宅起睦親飽德每聯於
皇族恐戕物命思結人心正風俗則詔禁邪巫
勤政理則屏書無逸兵以不用爲武刑以
不殺爲威求言渙發乎
===
玉音問俗隱憂乎菜色剛惟獨斷職不下侵謂
鉛槧須責文儒而綸綍實關著述丁寧
天語誕告多方顯允
聖謨式昭
來裔紬惟内批之勤綣允資良史以發揮經
緯古作樞機今付竊念臣少罹孤疢閱歷
險艱長之技能校讎文字救趨時之弊力
去雕華守學古之勤徒成鄙樸頃備員於
管記竟落職於言階幸軫淹沉荐蒙甄敘
punctuated:
殊恩於宸注，感先愧集，責與憂并。恭惟○○○○，道同天地，孝達神明，仁恕根於心，恭儉出其性。禮隆會慶，履端先晉於慈宮；宅起睦親，飽德每聯於皇族。恐戕物命，思結人心。正風俗則詔禁邪巫，勤政理則屏書無逸。兵以不用爲武，刑以不殺爲威。求言渙發乎玉音，問俗隱憂乎菜色。剛惟獨斷，職不下侵。謂鉛槧須責文儒，而綸綍實關著述。丁寧天語，誕告多方。顯允聖謨，式昭來裔。紬惟内批之勤綣，允資良史以發揮。經緯古作，樞機今付。
竊念臣少罹孤疢，閱歷險艱。長之技能，校讎文字。救趨時之弊，力去雕華；守學古之勤，徒成鄙樸。頃備員於管記，竟落職於言階。幸軫淹沉，荐蒙甄敘。
translation_en:
…exceptional favor through Your Majesty’s attentive regard. Gratitude and shame gather together; responsibility and anxiety accompany one another. Reverently considering Your Majesty [○○○○: designation unclear], your Way accords with Heaven and Earth, and your filial devotion reaches the spirits. Benevolence and forbearance are rooted in your heart; reverence and frugality spring from your nature. Your ceremonies lend grandeur to festive gatherings; at the opening of the year, you first pay your respects at the palace of the imperial mother. You promote affection among kin [宅起?], and repeatedly join the imperial clan in feasting and enjoying your beneficence. You fear harming living creatures and seek to bind the people’s hearts to you. To rectify customs, you issue edicts prohibiting heterodox shamans; to attend diligently to government, you have “Against Luxurious Ease” inscribed upon a screen. You make refraining from warfare the measure of military prowess, and refraining from execution the source of penal authority. Your august voice generously issues calls for frank counsel; in inquiring into popular conditions, you harbor deep concern for those whose faces show hunger. Firmly, you alone decide; your authority is not encroached upon from below. You hold that the work of brush and writing tablet must be entrusted to learned men, and that imperial pronouncements are indeed matters of literary composition. Your earnest imperial words proclaim this widely. Your manifestly trustworthy and sagacious plans thereby illuminate generations to come. Reflecting upon the diligence and solicitude of your personally written rescripts, one recognizes that they truly require a worthy historian to expound them. The ordering of ancient writings and the crucial responsibilities of the present are now entrusted to me.
I humbly reflect that in youth I suffered bereavement and illness, passing through dangers and hardships. As I grew, my skill lay in collating texts. To remedy the faults of following contemporary fashions, I strove to eliminate ornate embellishment; persevering diligently in the study of antiquity, I achieved only a rustic simplicity. Recently I filled a secretarial post, but ultimately lost office on account of words [?]. Fortunately, you took thought for my prolonged obscurity, and I have repeatedly received favorable consideration and reappointment.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
通班冊府待罪諫垣謬參四禁之嚴超置
七人之列辭章懇乞
聖意重回忽遣使以臨門俾措躬而無地臣敢
不勉圖來效仰答
皇慈景服前脩翼成信史話言必記舉動特書
事深假于折衷意默存乎儆戒首復渾厚
之體特申懇至之詞俾
德意旁宣偕日月而普照
仁恩下浹等雨露以弘敷雖稽古未盡典謨而
紀實可知堯舜尚期補過助大塊於一塵
更勵匪躬煩尚方之一劍無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策
punctuated:
通班冊府，待罪諫垣，謬參四禁之嚴，超置七人之列。辭章懇乞，聖意重回，忽遣使以臨門，俾措躬而無地。臣敢不勉圖來效，仰答皇慈？景服前脩，翼成信史，話言必記，舉動特書。事深假于折衷，意默存乎儆戒。首復渾厚之體，特申懇至之詞，俾德意旁宣，偕日月而普照；仁恩下浹，等雨露以弘敷。雖稽古未盡典謨，而紀實可知堯舜。尚期補過，助大塊於一塵；更勵匪躬，煩尚方之一劍。無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁場
策
translation_en:
…admitted to the ranks of the palace library and serving, unworthily, in the remonstrance bureau, I have undeservedly entered the august company of the four inner precincts [?] and been advanced into the ranks of the seven men [?]. In a written submission I earnestly begged to decline, but Your Majesty again turned your gracious attention toward me. Suddenly you dispatched an envoy to my gate, leaving me nowhere to place myself in my embarrassment. How could your servant fail to strive for future service in repayment of your imperial kindness?

Reverently following the worthy men of the past, I shall assist in producing a trustworthy history, recording every utterance and expressly setting down every action. In treating events, I shall rely deeply upon balanced judgment; in my intentions, I shall silently preserve a concern for admonition. Above all, I shall restore a substantial and unadorned style and give particular expression to words of utmost sincerity, so that your virtuous intentions may be proclaimed everywhere, shining universally like the sun and moon, and your benevolent favor may reach those below, spreading broadly like rain and dew. Though my examination of antiquity may not fully encompass the Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents, a truthful record will make known a ruler like Yao or Shun. I still hope to remedy faults, contributing a single mote of dust to the vast work of creation; I shall further strengthen my selfless devotion, even requesting a sword from the Imperial Manufactories.

Gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sageliness, I cannot contain my fervent emotion and profound trepidation. I respectfully present this memorial to convey my thanks for your hearing.

Third Session
Policy Questions

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
第一問
葉釗
同考試官訓導劉　批〔我〕
聖祖制作之善正在有德以爲之本場中荅者類能知之但於制作詳
備處漫不究心此篇條荅如指諸掌非平日服膺
聖製而有志於當世務者不能讀之令人生忠愛意風簷寸晷之下
得士有此亦可爲
明時慶矣
同考試官教諭潘　批　詞氣浩然如長江大河㒺
===
國之文貴如此
同考試官教諭傅　批
皇祖一統天下之盛煥乎文章蕩蕩乎如天之難名此士歷陳而又能
知其所本可謂善鋪張
洪休揚厲偉績者矣
考試官教諭黄　批　鋪張
聖制之懿光昭萬世無踰於此者
考試官學正韓　批　書生能熟究
聖製而頃刻成文以對其英英用世之志久矣可敬可敬
punctuated:
第一問
葉釗

同考試官訓導劉批：〔我〕聖祖制作之善，正在有德以爲之本。場中荅者類能知之，但於制作詳備處，漫不究心。此篇條荅，如指諸掌，非平日服膺聖製而有志於當世務者不能。讀之令人生忠愛意。風簷寸晷之下，得士有此，亦可爲明時慶矣。

同考試官教諭潘批：詞氣浩然，如長江大河。㒺國之文，貴如此。

同考試官教諭傅批：皇祖一統天下之盛，煥乎文章，蕩蕩乎如天之難名。此士歷陳，而又能知其所本，可謂善鋪張洪休、揚厲偉績者矣。

考試官教諭黄批：鋪張聖制之懿，光昭萬世，無踰於此者。

考試官學正韓批：書生能熟究聖製，而頃刻成文以對，其英英用世之志久矣。可敬，可敬！
translation_en:
First Policy Question
Ye Zhao 葉釗

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu 劉, Assistant Instructor: The excellence of [our] sagely ancestor’s institutions lies precisely in the virtue that provided their foundation. Most candidates answering in this examination understood this, but they failed to examine carefully the particulars in which those institutions were comprehensive. This essay answers point by point, making everything as clear as something held in the palm. Only someone who habitually takes the sagely imperial ordinances to heart and aspires to address the affairs of the present age could accomplish this. Reading it inspires loyalty and devotion. To discover such a scholar within the brief time allotted beneath the windswept examination eaves is indeed cause to congratulate this enlightened age.

Comment by Associate Examiner Pan 潘, Instructor: The language has a vast, surging force, like the Yangzi and other great rivers. Writing that brings distinction to the state [?] should be valued for precisely these qualities.

Comment by Associate Examiner Fu 傅, Instructor: The magnificence of the imperial ancestor’s unification of All-under-Heaven shines forth in its cultural accomplishments, boundless and as difficult to describe as Heaven itself. This scholar sets these out in succession and also understands their foundation. He may indeed be said to excel at expounding the great blessings and extolling the magnificent achievements.

Comment by Examiner Huang 黄, Instructor: In expounding the excellence of the sagely imperial institutions, whose brilliance illuminates ten thousand generations, nothing surpasses this.

Comment by Examiner Han 韓, School Instructor: This scholar has thoroughly studied the sagely imperial ordinances and composed an essay in reply within a moment. His outstanding ambition to serve the world must be of long standing. Admirable, admirable!

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
對立法通天下萬世之大利者
聖人之業垂法洑天下萬世之大功者
聖人之德盖法制之立
聖人大業而為天下萬世利者也然其良法美
意垂之天下萬世其功莫大焉自非
聖人備聰明聖知之天德其孰能與於此哉孰
事首舉
皇祖制作下詢承學愚也幸生兹
聖明之世仰佩
===
聖謨久矣庸不能悉謹條其一二以對夫春秋
大一統者乃漢儒董仲舒之言本子思子
中庸之意也子思子曰王天下有三重焉
其寡過矣乎又曰非天子不議禮不制度
不考文言必聖人在天子之位而後行此
三重之道也非春秋大一統為天地之常
經古今之通義邪洪惟我
太祖高皇帝承
天膺曆變夷為華以
punctuated:
對：立法通天下萬世之大利者，聖人之業；垂法洑天下萬世之大功者，聖人之德。盖法制之立，聖人大業，而為天下萬世利者也。然其良法美意，垂之天下萬世，其功莫大焉。自非聖人備聰明聖知之天德，其孰能與於此哉？孰事首舉皇祖制作，下詢承學，愚也幸生兹聖明之世，仰佩聖謨久矣，庸不能悉，謹條其一二以對。
夫《春秋》大一統者，乃漢儒董仲舒之言，本子思子《中庸》之意也。子思子曰：「王天下有三重焉，其寡過矣乎！」又曰：「非天子，不議禮，不制度，不考文。」言必聖人在天子之位，而後行此三重之道也。非《春秋》大一統為天地之常經、古今之通義邪？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，承天膺曆，變夷為華，以
translation_en:
In reply: To establish laws that make the greatest benefits accessible to all under Heaven for ten thousand generations is the work of the sage; to hand down laws whose great achievements extend to [?] all under Heaven for ten thousand generations is the virtue of the sage. For establishing laws and institutions is the sage’s great undertaking, benefiting all under Heaven for ten thousand generations. Yet in transmitting his excellent laws and fine intentions to all under Heaven for ten thousand generations, his achievement is unsurpassed. Unless a sage possessed the Heaven-endowed virtues of perceptiveness, understanding, sagacity, and wisdom, who could participate in such an undertaking? You, sir [?], begin by citing the imperial ancestor’s institutional creations and condescend to question us students. Fortunate to have been born in this age of sagely enlightenment, I, in my ignorance, have long revered the imperial counsels. Though unable to encompass them all, I respectfully set out one or two points in reply.
The phrase “exalting unified rule” associated with the Spring and Autumn Annals is a saying of the Han scholar Dong Zhongshu, rooted in the meaning of Master Zisi’s Doctrine of the Mean. Master Zisi said: “He who rules all under Heaven has three weighty responsibilities; surely his errors will be few!” He also said: “Unless one is the Son of Heaven, one does not deliberate on rites, establish standards, or scrutinize written forms.” This means that a sage must occupy the position of Son of Heaven before he can carry out these three weighty responsibilities. Is not the exaltation of unified rule in the Spring and Autumn Annals the enduring norm of Heaven and Earth and the principle common to antiquity and the present? We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s mandate and assumed the imperial succession, transforming barbarian rule into Chinese civilization, by …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
天下之大聖行天下之大事制禮作樂爲百
王之法立教垂訓宏一代之規演諸
宸翰出自
淵衷
神功莫罄
聖德難言而其所仰見者則有所謂三重之
道焉夫自元俗亂華有
禮儀定式以議禮自夷教變夏有
稽古定制以制度自胡言混中土有
===
洪武正韻以考文此皆制作之大端所以新
天下之耳目一天下之心志萬世臣民所
當遵守而不敢違者也請述其旨自天尊
地卑之位定而禮于是乎形在人則親疎
之分貴賤之等截然而不可犯者皆是禮
也禮以議之上下辨矣若
定式所載爲條三十有七始之以朝參筵宴
之節終之以器皿床榻之類至於其間最
切而要者則
punctuated:
天下之大聖，行天下之大事，制禮作樂，爲百王之法；立教垂訓，宏一代之規。演諸宸翰，出自淵衷，神功莫罄，聖德難言。而其所仰見者，則有所謂三重之道焉。夫自元俗亂華，有《禮儀定式》以議禮；自夷教變夏，有《稽古定制》以制度；自胡言混中土，有《洪武正韻》以考文。此皆制作之大端，所以新天下之耳目，一天下之心志，萬世臣民所當遵守而不敢違者也。
請述其旨。自天尊地卑之位定，而禮于是乎形。在人，則親疎之分、貴賤之等，截然而不可犯者，皆是禮也。禮以議之，上下辨矣。若《定式》所載，爲條三十有七，始之以朝參筵宴之節，終之以器皿床榻之類。至於其間最切而要者，則
translation_en:
…as the great sage of All under Heaven, he undertook its great affairs. He established rites and made music, providing a model for all kings; he instituted teachings and bequeathed instructions, giving broad scope to the standards of his dynasty. These were set forth in his imperial writings and issued from the depths of his heart. His divine achievements cannot be exhaustively recounted; his sagely virtue is difficult to express. Yet what we can discern in reverent contemplation includes the Way of the Three Weighty Matters. Since Yuan customs had thrown Chinese civilization into disorder, there was the Prescribed Forms of Ritual and Ceremony (Liyi dingshi) to deliberate upon rites. Since barbarian teachings had transformed the ways of the Chinese, there was the Established Institutions Based on Antiquity (Jigu dingzhi) to establish institutions. Since foreign speech had become intermixed with that of the Central Lands, there was the Correct Rhymes of the Hongwu Reign (Hongwu zhengyun) to examine written forms. These were all major acts of institutional creation, intended to renew what all under Heaven heard and saw and to unify their hearts and purposes. They are what subjects and people for ten thousand generations must observe and dare not contravene.
Let me explain their purport. Once the positions of Heaven above and Earth below were fixed, ritual took shape therein. Among human beings, the distinctions between close and distant kin and the gradations between noble and lowly, clearly demarcated and inviolable, all constitute ritual. Through deliberation upon rites, the distinction between superior and inferior becomes clear. The Prescribed Forms, for example, contains thirty-seven articles, beginning with the observances for court attendance and banquets and ending with such categories as vessels and utensils, beds and couches. As for what is most immediately pertinent and essential among them, it is…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖諭所謂毋放肆怠聽思為省身克已之道是
已自天圓地方之體設而度于是乎寓在
人則室廬之限輿皁之制秩然而不可踰
者皆是度也度以制之等威殊矣若
定制所編類皆經常之法斟酌夫李唐趙宋
之制燕舉夫藝祖英宗之言至於其間語
及財利者則
聖意以為食禄之家不當與民爭利故爾自天
玄地黃之色著而文于是乎顯在人則形
之點畫播之聲音皆是文也文以考之形
===
聲正矣若
正韻一書去沈約之謬而成經緯之交其雅
音則取於中原其註釋則依於毛晃他如
東冬清青之二韻併而為一虞模麻遮之
一韻析而為二孰非
宸慮之所在乎爰自
聖祖以來迄今百三十餘年政不異政俗不殊
俗誠一統文明之治足以比隆唐虞三代
punctuated:
聖諭所謂「毋放肆怠聽，思為省身克已之道」，是已。自天圓地方之體設，而度于是乎寓。在人，則室廬之限、輿皁之制，秩然而不可踰者，皆是度也。度以制之，等威殊矣。若《定制》所編，類皆經常之法，斟酌夫李唐趙宋之制，燕舉夫藝祖英宗之言。至於其間語及財利者，則聖意以為食禄之家不當與民爭利，故爾。
自天玄地黃之色著，而文于是乎顯。在人，則形之點畫，播之聲音，皆是文也。文以考之，形聲正矣。若《正韻》一書，去沈約之謬，而成經緯之交。其雅音則取於中原，其註釋則依於毛晃。他如東冬清青之二韻，併而為一；虞模麻遮之一韻，析而為二，孰非宸慮之所在乎？
爰自聖祖以來，迄今百三十餘年，政不異政，俗不殊俗，誠一統文明之治，足以比隆唐虞三代
translation_en:
…precisely what the sacred instruction means by: “Do not be unrestrained or remiss in heeding instruction; consider how to examine yourself and master yourself.” Once the forms of round Heaven and square Earth were established, standards were embodied in them. In human affairs, the limits governing dwellings and the regulations governing carriages and grooms, orderly and admitting no transgression, are all such standards. When these standards regulate affairs, the distinctions of rank and dignity are clear. The provisions compiled in the Established Regulations (Dingzhi) are generally enduring rules. They weigh the institutions of the Li house of Tang and the Zhao house of Song, and cite [?] the words of Yizu and Yingzong. Where they discuss wealth and profit, this is because His Majesty holds that households supported by official stipends should not compete with the people for profit.
Once the colors of dark Heaven and yellow Earth became manifest, patterned expression was revealed in them. In human affairs, whatever takes shape in dots and strokes or is conveyed through sounds belongs to this patterned expression. By examining it, written forms and sounds are made correct. The Correct Rhymes (Zhengyun), for example, eliminates Shen Yue’s errors and establishes the interconnections of warp and weft. Its standard pronunciation is drawn from the Central Plains, and its annotations follow Mao Huang. Other examples include combining the two rhyme categories dong 東 and dong 冬, and qing 清 and qing 青, into one in each case; and dividing the single rhyme categories yu–mo 虞模 and ma–zhe 麻遮 into two in each case. Which of these was not an object of imperial consideration?
From the time of the sagely founding emperor down to the present, more than 130 years have passed. Government has remained consistent, and customs have remained uniform. This is truly a unified and culturally enlightened rule, worthy of comparison in its splendor with Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之盛所謂建諸天地而不悖質諸鬼神而
無疑百世以俟聖人而不惑者也至求其
制作之本則存乎
聖祖本諸身而有中庸之德焉耳夫自昔聖人
三重之制不過因前代之舊而損益其間
故功業在天下或十世百世而止我
聖祖恢復帝王自有之疆土膺撃今古所無之
戎狄因元人斁敗禮樂典章彝倫之後禮
以制行度以為法文以合俗其利則天下
===
萬世之利者也
聖人之業何如其大邪其功則天下萬世之功
者也
聖人之德何如其盛邪惟
聖祖道德之高制作之善功業之成如此而欲
鋪張揚厲猶摸天地而繪日月也然吾夫
子有曰大哉堯之為君也巍巍乎唯天為
大唯堯則之蕩蕩乎民無能名焉巍巍乎
其有成功也煥乎其有文章愚生殆忘
punctuated: 之盛，所謂「建諸天地而不悖，質諸鬼神而無疑，百世以俟聖人而不惑」者也。至求其制作之本，則存乎聖祖本諸身而有中庸之德焉耳。夫自昔聖人三重之制，不過因前代之舊而損益其間，故功業在天下，或十世百世而止。我聖祖恢復帝王自有之疆土，膺撃今古所無之戎狄，因元人斁敗禮樂典章彝倫之後，禮以制行，度以為法，文以合俗，其利則天下萬世之利者也。聖人之業何如其大邪！其功則天下萬世之功者也。聖人之德何如其盛邪！惟聖祖道德之高、制作之善、功業之成如此，而欲鋪張揚厲，猶摸天地而繪日月也。然吾夫子有曰：「大哉，堯之為君也！巍巍乎！唯天為大，唯堯則之。蕩蕩乎！民無能名焉。巍巍乎，其有成功也！煥乎，其有文章！」愚生殆忘
translation_en:
…in their flourishing grandeur. This is what is meant by: “Established before Heaven and Earth, it does not conflict with them; tested before ghosts and spirits, it admits of no doubt; awaiting a sage a hundred generations hence, it gives no cause for uncertainty.” If we seek the foundation of these institutions, it lies simply in the Sagely Founder’s grounding them in his own person and possessing the virtue of the Mean. Since antiquity, the institutions established by sages concerning the three weighty matters have merely followed the precedents of earlier dynasties, making additions and reductions. Thus their achievements in the world endured perhaps ten or a hundred generations, and then ceased. Our Sagely Founder recovered the territories that rightfully belonged to the emperors and kings, and struck down Rong and Di enemies unparalleled in ancient or recent times. After the men of the Yuan had corrupted rites, music, statutes, institutions, and the enduring human relationships, he used ritual to regulate conduct, standards to establish rules, and writing to unify customs. The benefits he brought are benefits for all under Heaven through myriad generations. How great are the undertakings of the sage! His achievements are achievements for all under Heaven through myriad generations. How abundant is the virtue of the sage!

Such were the loftiness of the Sagely Founder’s Way and virtue, the excellence of his institutions, and the perfection of his achievements that attempting to expound and extol them would be like depicting Heaven and Earth and painting the sun and moon. Yet our Master said: “Great indeed was Yao as a ruler! How lofty! Heaven alone is great, and Yao alone took it as his model. How boundless! The people could find no words to name it. How lofty were his accomplishments! How brilliant were his cultural forms!” I, this unworthy student, have perhaps forgotten…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
堯天之下平日之所誦習者唯此而已更復何
言謹對
第二問
張鉞
同考試官教諭徐　批〔考究精密深悉儒先道統〕
淵源有養之士也可嘉
同考試官教諭季　批〔敷演出正學一本意匪泰否〕
抱負者鮮能
同考試官學正楊　批〔荅有根據足見博洽之學〕
===
考試官教諭黃　批〔此子所荅殆如親立門墻而〕
摳趨考亭者乎
考試官學正韓　批〔一部道學淵源盡在此子〕
腹中方能隨叩隨鳴
道係於天有不可終絕之統道屬於人有
不可苟得之傳惟其不可終絕也故或異
地而同心惟其不可苟得也故或同時而
異學然則道之係於天而屬於人者豈可
以輕論哉請畧陳之道統之傳始於羲皇
punctuated:
堯天之下，平日之所誦習者唯此而已，更復何言？謹對。

第二問
張鉞
同考試官教諭徐　批〔考究精密，深悉儒先道統〕淵源，有養之士也，可嘉。
同考試官教諭季　批〔敷演出正學一本意，匪泰否〕抱負者鮮能。
同考試官學正楊　批〔荅有根據，足見博洽之學。〕
考試官教諭黃　批〔此子所荅，殆如親立門墻而〕摳趨考亭者乎！
考試官學正韓　批〔一部道學淵源，盡在此子〕腹中，方能隨叩隨鳴。

道係於天，有不可終絕之統；道屬於人，有不可苟得之傳。惟其不可終絕也，故或異地而同心；惟其不可苟得也，故或同時而異學。然則道之係於天而屬於人者，豈可以輕論哉？請畧陳之。道統之傳，始於羲皇，
translation_en:
…beneath Yao’s heaven, this alone is what I have regularly recited and studied. What more can I say? Respectfully submitted in reply.

Second Question
Zhang Yue

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “His investigation is precise and thorough, and he understands deeply the origins and development of the earlier Confucian masters’ succession to the Way. He is a man of cultivated character, worthy of commendation.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Ji, Instructor: “He expounds the meaning of the single foundation of orthodox learning. Few without such intellectual resources could accomplish this [the wording 匪泰否 is doubtful].”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, School Instructor: “His answer is well grounded, amply demonstrating his broad and thorough learning.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “This candidate’s answer makes it seem as though he had personally stood within the master’s school, lifting the hem of his robe to approach respectfully at Kaoting [the school of Zhu Xi]!”

Comment by Examiner Han, School Instructor: “The entire history of the origins and development of the Learning of the Way is stored in this candidate’s mind; only thus could he respond whenever questioned.”

The Way is bound to Heaven, possessing a succession that cannot remain severed forever; the Way is entrusted to human beings, possessing a transmission that cannot be acquired casually.
