Precisely because its succession cannot remain severed forever, people in different places may share the same mind; precisely because its transmission cannot be acquired casually, people living at the same time may differ in their learning. How, then, could one lightly discuss the Way as bound to Heaven and entrusted to human beings? Allow me to set this forth briefly. The transmission of the succession to the Way began with the sovereign Fuxi…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
盛於堯舜大成於孔子至孟子而中絶焉
有宋周程朱子起而承之周子生于舂陵
南方之人也而程子受學於南安故吾與
點也之意遂得於心領之餘程子生於河
洛北方之人也而楊中立從學於潁昌故
吾道南矣之歎遂發於目送之際楊之再
傳復得朱子以集諸儒之大成焉周范造
詣固殊程張契悟亦異此朱子荅或人之
問也蓋范文正之極高明而道中庸不過
===
庶幾焉耳其視周之默契道體固為不同
張因范公勸讀中庸歸而求之久乃有得
與程之一見即悟者抑亦異矣然朱子承
命章齋禀學延平以上泝濂洛之淵源則
周程之道朱實承之故朱子記周之祠有
上接洙泗下啓河洛之語其於學庸孟子
止言程子則以周之圖書專明易學而註
述未及於三書故耳豈謂周之學有異於
程哉周子之寓江西當時若歐陽脩曾鞏
punctuated: 盛於堯舜，大成於孔子，至孟子而中絶焉。有宋周程朱子起而承之。周子生于舂陵，南方之人也，而程子受學於南安，故「吾與點也」之意遂得於心領之餘。程子生於河洛，北方之人也，而楊中立從學於潁昌，故「吾道南矣」之歎遂發於目送之際。楊之再傳，復得朱子以集諸儒之大成焉。「周范造詣固殊，程張契悟亦異」，此朱子荅或人之問也。蓋范文正之「極高明而道中庸」，不過庶幾焉耳，其視周之默契道體，固為不同。張因范公勸讀《中庸》，歸而求之，久乃有得，與程之一見即悟者，抑亦異矣。然朱子承命章齋，禀學延平，以上泝濂洛之淵源，則周程之道，朱實承之。故朱子記周之祠，有「上接洙泗，下啓河洛」之語。其於《學》《庸》《孟子》止言程子，則以周之圖書專明《易》學，而註述未及於三書故耳。豈謂周之學有異於程哉？周子之寓江西，當時若歐陽脩、曾鞏，
translation_en:
…flourished under Yao and Shun, attained its fullest expression in Confucius, and was interrupted after Mencius. In the Song dynasty, Masters Zhou, Cheng, and Zhu arose to continue this transmission. Master Zhou was born in Chungling and was a southerner, while Master Cheng received instruction from him in Nan’an. Thus, through inward apprehension, Cheng came to grasp the meaning of “I am with Dian.” Master Cheng was born in the He–Luo region and was a northerner, while Yang Zhongli studied under him in Yingchang. Hence, as Cheng watched Yang depart, he exclaimed, “My Way is going south!” Two generations after Yang in the line of transmission, Master Zhu appeared and brought the achievements of the various Confucian masters to their fullest expression.

“Zhou and Fan certainly differed in their attainments, and Cheng and Zhang also differed in their intuitive understanding”: this was Master Zhu’s answer to someone’s question. For Fan Wenzheng’s attainment of “reaching the utmost heights of illumination while following the Mean” was only an approximation. Compared with Zhou’s tacit apprehension of the substance of the Way, it was certainly different. At Lord Fan’s urging, Zhang read the Doctrine of the Mean; he returned home and investigated it, gaining understanding only after a long time. This, too, differed from Cheng’s immediate awakening upon first meeting Zhou.

Yet Master Zhu received instruction at Zhangzhai [?] and studied under Yanping, thereby tracing the tradition upstream to its sources in Lian and Luo. Zhu thus truly inherited the Way of Zhou and Cheng. Accordingly, in his account of Zhou’s shrine, Master Zhu wrote that Zhou “reached back to connect with the Zhu and Si rivers and opened the way for the He and Luo rivers”—that is, he linked the tradition of Confucius with that of the Cheng masters. When Zhu spoke only of Master Cheng in connection with the Great Learning, the Doctrine of the Mean, and the Mencius, it was merely because Zhou’s diagrams and writings concentrated on elucidating the learning of the Book of Changes, and his commentaries had not extended to those three books. How could this imply that Zhou’s learning differed from Cheng’s? When Master Zhou resided in Jiangxi, among his contemporaries were Ouyang Xiu and Zeng Gong…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
黃庭堅李覯各以文學鳴而於性命之說
未肯降心以從其始從終背又有若王安
石者此無他所志異也朱子宦遊南康往
來饒信諸郡士游其門者甚衆嘗與象山
陸氏胥會鵝湖屢相問辨而卒未能會其
說于一者此無他所見異也雖然庭堅游
于蘇門而光風霽月之贊乃善形容周子
之氣象吳澄主於陸學而元亨利貞之論
乃獨係屬朱子之統緒斯道之中正公論
===
在人不可誣也彼所見所志之異者烏能
與於斯哉嗟夫道統之傳絕於千載而續
於一時或自南而北或自北而南遠近見
聞不嘗符契此皆係於天焉非人之所能
為也若夫所志所見之異而不能以強同
者雖由乎人而亦豈非天哉愚也有志於
道方欲上師古人而未知所從敢因明問
而請質焉惟進而教之幸甚
第三問
punctuated:
黃庭堅、李覯各以文學鳴，而於性命之說，未肯降心以從。其始從終背，又有若王安石者。此無他，所志異也。朱子宦遊南康，往來饒信諸郡，士游其門者甚衆。嘗與象山陸氏胥會鵝湖，屢相問辨，而卒未能會其說于一者，此無他，所見異也。雖然，庭堅游于蘇門，而光風霽月之贊，乃善形容周子之氣象；吳澄主於陸學，而元亨利貞之論，乃獨係屬朱子之統緒。斯道之中正，公論在人，不可誣也。彼所見所志之異者，烏能與於斯哉？嗟夫！道統之傳絕於千載，而續於一時，或自南而北，或自北而南，遠近見聞不嘗符契，此皆係於天焉，非人之所能為也。若夫所志所見之異，而不能以強同者，雖由乎人，而亦豈非天哉？愚也有志於道，方欲上師古人，而未知所從，敢因明問而請質焉。惟進而教之，幸甚！

第三問
translation_en:
…Huang Tingjian and Li Gou each won renown for literary learning, yet were unwilling to humble themselves and follow the teachings concerning human nature and destiny. There were also those, such as Wang Anshi, who followed at first but ultimately turned away. This was for no other reason than that their aspirations differed. While serving in Nankang, Master Zhu traveled among the prefectures of Raozhou, Xinzhou, and elsewhere, and very many scholars studied under him. He once met with Lu Xiangshan at Ehu. They repeatedly questioned and debated one another, but ultimately could not bring their teachings into agreement. This was for no other reason than that their views differed.

Nevertheless, although Tingjian studied in Su Shi’s circle, his praise of Master Zhou as a “clear breeze and a moon after rain” aptly portrayed Zhou’s bearing. Although Wu Cheng upheld Lu’s learning, his discussion of “origination, smooth progress, benefit, and constancy” attached the line of succession specifically to Master Zhu. The balance and correctness of this Way are recognized in people’s impartial judgment and cannot be misrepresented. How could those whose views and aspirations differ have a share in this?

Alas! The transmission of the succession of the Way was interrupted for a thousand years, yet resumed within a single age. Sometimes it passed from south to north, sometimes from north to south; what was seen and heard, far and near, did not coincide [?]. All this depended upon Heaven; it was beyond human power to accomplish. As for differences in aspirations and views that cannot forcibly be brought into agreement, although they arise from human beings, are they not also due to Heaven?

Ignorant though I am, I aspire to the Way. I now wish to take the ancients as my teachers, but do not yet know whom to follow. I venture to take your illuminating question as an occasion to seek clarification. If you would advance me through your instruction, I would be most fortunate!

Third Policy Question

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
李文潔
同考試官教諭林　批　能言之士疎而陋大而誇亦
習弊也此篇詞氣渾厚於鄉邦人物感慨抑揚而意
思含蓄不暴末復以神明之機存乎人乃根本之論
况餘策皆偉譬之入海探珠徃寸先得奇寶有
所歸矣
同考試官學正章　批　道德風俗卓有定見而士
夫人物歴舉不遺豈嘗誦其書而追慕其人者歟
考試官教諭黄　批　考據詳悉鋪敘整嚴策
===
學觧有其儼
考試官學正韓　批　議論風俗由道德又推原
其本在
朝廷其機在士夫誠爲有見
道有升降政由俗革風化之本在朝廷其
儀不忒正是四國風化之機在士夫盖上
有所好下必有甚焉者矣况朝廷者四方
之根本士夫者鄉國之領袖轉移感動豈
非影響之必然哉粤自先王之時以民之
punctuated:
李文潔

同考試官教諭林批：能言之士，疎而陋，大而誇，亦習弊也。此篇詞氣渾厚，於鄉邦人物感慨抑揚，而意思含蓄不暴。末復以神明之機存乎人，乃根本之論。况餘策皆偉，譬之入海探珠，徃寸先得奇寶，有所歸矣。

同考試官學正章批：道德風俗，卓有定見，而士夫人物歴舉不遺，豈嘗誦其書而追慕其人者歟？

考試官教諭黄批：考據詳悉，鋪敘整嚴，策學觧有其儼。

考試官學正韓批：議論風俗由道德，又推原其本在朝廷，其機在士夫，誠爲有見。

道有升降，政由俗革。風化之本在朝廷，其儀不忒，正是四國；風化之機在士夫，盖上有所好，下必有甚焉者矣。况朝廷者，四方之根本；士夫者，鄉國之領袖。轉移感動，豈非影響之必然哉？粤自先王之時，以民之
translation_en:
Li Wenjie

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Men skilled in expression can be superficial and crude, grandiose and boastful: these too are entrenched faults. This essay has a rich, substantial diction and tone. In discussing the figures of his native region, the writer expresses deep feelings, with praise and censure, yet keeps his meaning implicit rather than laying it bare. At the end, he further locates the vital agency of spiritual illumination in human beings—a discussion that reaches the fundamentals. Moreover, his other policy essays are all outstanding. It is like entering the sea to seek pearls: scarcely advancing an inch [?], one already finds a rare treasure and has something to bring home.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, School Instructor: On morality and customs, he has notably firm views, and he enumerates the scholar-officials and other figures in turn, omitting none. Surely he has read their writings and looked back on these men with admiration?

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: The supporting evidence is detailed and thorough, and the exposition orderly and rigorous. His learning and interpretation in policy essays possess a certain dignity [?].

Comment by Examiner Han, School Instructor: In discussing customs, he traces them to morality, and further traces their roots to the imperial court and their motive agency to scholar-officials. This indeed shows insight.

The Way rises and declines; government changes with customs. The foundation of moral transformation lies in the imperial court: “With no error in his deportment, he sets the states of the four quarters right.” The motive agency of moral transformation lies in scholar-officials, for whatever those above favor, those below will inevitably pursue still more intensely. Moreover, the imperial court is the foundation of all regions, and scholar-officials are the leaders of their localities and the realm. In bringing about change and moving others, must their influence not follow as inevitably as a shadow or an echo? Now, in the time of the former kings, because the people’s …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
視聽不可不一上之好惡不可不示也於
是教民以五禮六樂無異教也道王之德
意志慮無異政也通其貨財同其度量無
異尚也除其所怨同其所好無異情也道
四方之政和上下之志無異心也齊道德
一風俗者如此自秦以來始皇變詐峻刻
而民俗薄漢高改制易俗而民俗厚孝武
好大喜功而民俗虛孝宣綜核名實而民
俗實魏晉賤守節樂清曠而民俗浮唐太
===
宗約己治人崇儒重道而民俗醇宋承五
代之弊深仁厚澤涵養天下其俗之仁厚
又自不言可知矣升降因革循環無端固
皆上之化也若夫縣無復盜實感太丘二
絹之遺路不拾遺又激彥方一布之惠陽
城行古道居晉鄙薰德而善良者幾千人
李善存孤兒隱山陽感行而脩義者遍閭
里此又士大夫之立身行義風範乎鄉者
也江右控引荊越襟帶江湖山川特秀人
punctuated: 視聽不可不一，上之好惡不可不示也。於是教民以五禮六樂，無異教也；道王之德意志慮，無異政也；通其貨財，同其度量，無異尚也；除其所怨，同其所好，無異情也；道四方之政，和上下之志，無異心也。齊道德、一風俗者如此。自秦以來，始皇變詐峻刻，而民俗薄；漢高改制易俗，而民俗厚；孝武好大喜功，而民俗虛；孝宣綜核名實，而民俗實；魏晉賤守節、樂清曠，而民俗浮；唐太宗約己治人、崇儒重道，而民俗醇；宋承五代之弊，深仁厚澤涵養天下，其俗之仁厚，又自不言可知矣。升降因革，循環無端，固皆上之化也。若夫縣無復盜，實感太丘二絹之遺；路不拾遺，又激彥方一布之惠。陽城行古道，居晉鄙，薰德而善良者幾千人；李善存孤兒，隱山陽，感行而脩義者遍閭里。此又士大夫之立身行義，風範乎鄉者也。江右控引荊越，襟帶江湖，山川特秀，人
translation_en:
…what the people saw and heard had to be made uniform, and the likes and dislikes of those above had to be made manifest. Thus, the people were taught through the five rites and six forms of music, so that there were no divergent teachings; the king’s virtue, intentions, aspirations, and deliberations were conveyed, so that there were no divergent policies; goods and wealth were circulated and weights and measures standardized, so that there were no divergent preferences; what the people resented was removed and what they favored was brought into accord, so that there were no divergent sentiments; the policies of the four quarters were communicated and the aspirations of those above and below harmonized, so that there were no divergent purposes. Such were the means of bringing morality into accord and unifying customs.

From the Qin onward, the First Emperor was deceitful and harsh, and popular customs became mean. Gaozu of Han reformed institutions and changed customs, and popular customs became generous. Emperor Xiaowu delighted in grand undertakings and military achievements, and popular customs became hollow. Emperor Xiaoxuan comprehensively examined names against realities, and popular customs became substantial. Under the Wei and Jin, steadfast integrity was disparaged and carefree detachment prized, and popular customs became frivolous. Taizong of Tang restrained himself in governing others, honored Confucian learning, and esteemed the Way, and popular customs became pure. The Song inherited the abuses of the Five Dynasties, yet nurtured all under Heaven with profound benevolence and abundant beneficence. The humanity and generosity of its customs can therefore be understood without further explanation. Rise and decline, continuity and change, revolved without end: all were indeed effects of the transforming influence of those above.

As for the county in which theft ceased, this was truly due to the inspiration of the gift of two lengths of silk by the magistrate of Taiqiu. That people did not pick up things lost on the road was likewise inspired by Yanfang’s kindness in giving a length of cloth. Yang Cheng practiced the ancient Way while living in the outlying country of Jin; nearly a thousand people became good through the pervasive influence of his virtue. Li Shan preserved an orphan’s life and lived in seclusion in Shanyang; throughout the neighborhoods and villages, people were moved by his conduct to cultivate righteousness. These, in turn, were scholar-officials whose personal conduct and practice of righteousness served as models for their local communities.

Jiangyou commands the approaches to Jing and Yue and is girdled by rivers and lakes. Its mountains and streams are exceptionally beautiful, and its people…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
物萃止服德當時思賢異世南州高士徐
孺子也完節先朝血食後代宋室忠臣文
信公也彭龜年當僞學之禁不以流俗而
變劉安世傷羨餘之諷遂以設教而歸數
君子之文學道德所以端鄉國之習者固
已久矣久則難變也何者人情安於所習
而駭於所未見商君廢井田民怨固也王
莽復井田而民亦怨武靈王變華效胡民
怨固也魏孝文變胡效華而民亦怨習素
===
善驅之惡不能入猶習素惡驅之善不能
變也然則江右道風文物諸先正之功不
誣而鼓鑄鑪冶則
聖朝之化斯賴生斯世居斯鄉作者不無人焉
然未敢為執事道也
第四問
徐盈
同考試官訓導孟 批 策場浩如望洋鮮難窮究
此作考證古今沿革之異評訂功用次第之詳古稱
punctuated:
物萃止。服德當時，思賢異世，南州高士徐孺子也；完節先朝，血食後代，宋室忠臣文信公也。彭龜年當僞學之禁，不以流俗而變；劉安世傷羨餘之諷，遂以設教而歸。數君子之文學道德，所以端鄉國之習者，固已久矣。久則難變也。何者？人情安於所習，而駭於所未見。商君廢井田，民怨固也；王莽復井田，而民亦怨。武靈王變華效胡，民怨固也；魏孝文變胡效華，而民亦怨。習素善，驅之惡不能入，猶習素惡，驅之善不能變也。然則江右道風文物，諸先正之功不誣，而鼓鑄鑪冶，則聖朝之化斯賴。生斯世，居斯鄉，作者不無人焉，然未敢為執事道也。

第四問

徐盈

同考試官訓導孟，批：「策場浩如望洋，鮮難窮究。此作考證古今沿革之異，評訂功用次第之詳，古稱
translation_en:
…talented men gather here. His contemporaries submitted to his virtue, and later generations cherished his worth: such was Xu Ruzi, the eminent scholar of the southern region. He preserved his integrity under the former dynasty and received blood sacrifices in later ages: such was Lord W信, the loyal minister of the Song house, Wen Tianxiang. During the prohibition of “false learning,” Peng Guinian did not change with prevailing fashions. Liu Anshi, grieved by the admonition concerning surplus revenues [?], consequently returned home to teach. The literary learning and moral virtue of these gentlemen have long served to rectify the customs of their native region. What has endured long is difficult to change. Why? Human beings feel secure with what they are accustomed to and are alarmed by what they have never seen. When Lord Shang abolished the well-field system, the people's resentment was understandable; yet when Wang Mang restored it, the people also resented it. When King Wuling changed Chinese practices to imitate those of the Hu, the people's resentment was understandable; yet when Emperor Xiaowen of Wei changed Hu practices to imitate Chinese ones, the people also resented it. When established habits are good, attempts to drive people toward evil cannot gain entry, just as, when established habits are evil, attempts to drive them toward goodness cannot change them.

Thus, the contributions of the former worthies to Jiangyou's moral traditions and cultural accomplishments cannot be denied. Yet their further molding and refinement depend upon the transforming influence of our sagely dynasty. Among those born in this age and dwelling in this region, there are indeed men who rise to achievement; but I have not ventured to speak of them to you, honored examiners.

Fourth Question

Xu Ying

This work examines and verifies the differences between ancient and present institutions, tracing what was retained and what was changed, and assesses in detail their effectiveness and the sequence of their application. The ancients called …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
子產博物君子吾子殆庶幾乎
考試官教諭黄　批　文勢遒健獨超衆作其秦
華峯巔忽見秋隼者歟
考試官學正韓　批　隨筆條荅敘事不遺策學
沉潜之密如此頗覺良工心獨苦矣
考法制於三代之前必求其意議法制於
三代之後不必泥其迹蓋必求其意者道
之同也不如是不足以經世也不必泥其
迹者世之異也世既異矣而膠膠然惟以
===
復古為事吾見迂緩濶畧治終不可得而
致也善經世者固如是哉執事舉三代之
法制以問諸生盖欲激昂其經世之志而
申儆乎流俗之陋意甚盛矣雖不敏敢不
承乎盖嘗觀古之為國者有井田以為養
有封建以為治有學校以為教有肉刑以
為禁其於學也俟明實興所以取士受成
獻馘所以論政春秋禮樂有事於絃冬夏
詩書有事於誦此皆堯舜禹湯文武之所
punctuated:
子產博物君子，吾子殆庶幾乎！
考試官教諭黄批：文勢遒健，獨超衆作，其秦華峯巔忽見秋隼者歟？
考試官學正韓批：隨筆條荅，敘事不遺，策學沉潜之密如此，頗覺良工心獨苦矣。
考法制於三代之前，必求其意；議法制於三代之後，不必泥其迹。蓋必求其意者，道之同也，不如是不足以經世也；不必泥其迹者，世之異也。世既異矣，而膠膠然惟以復古為事，吾見迂緩濶畧，治終不可得而致也。善經世者固如是哉？執事舉三代之法制以問諸生，盖欲激昂其經世之志，而申儆乎流俗之陋，意甚盛矣。雖不敏，敢不承乎？盖嘗觀古之為國者，有井田以為養，有封建以為治，有學校以為教，有肉刑以為禁。其於學也，俟明實興，所以取士；受成獻馘，所以論政。春秋禮樂，有事於絃；冬夏詩書，有事於誦。此皆堯舜禹湯文武之所
translation_en:
…Zichan was a gentleman of broad learning; you, sir, surely come close to him!
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: The writing is vigorous and forceful, surpassing all the other compositions. Is it not like suddenly sighting an autumn falcon above the summit of Mount Hua in Qin?
Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: Following the flow of his brush, he answers point by point, omitting nothing in his account. Such is the depth and thoroughness of his learning for policy essays that one truly appreciates the painstaking effort known only to a master craftsman.
When examining laws and institutions before the Three Dynasties, one must seek their underlying intent; when discussing laws and institutions after the Three Dynasties, one need not cling to their outward forms. One must seek their intent because the Way remains the same: without doing so, one cannot order the world. One need not cling to their forms because the times differ. When times have changed, if one stubbornly makes restoring antiquity one's sole concern, I foresee impractical delays and sweeping omissions; orderly government will ultimately remain unattainable. Surely those skilled in ordering the world would not act thus! You, honored examiners, have questioned us students about the laws and institutions of the Three Dynasties, presumably wishing to inspire our ambition to order the world and renew your admonitions against the shortcomings of prevailing customs. Your intention is most admirable. Though I lack ability, how could I dare fail to respond?
I have observed that those who governed states in antiquity had the well-field system to provide sustenance, hereditary enfeoffment to provide government, schools to provide instruction, and corporal mutilation to enforce prohibitions. As for their schools, they awaited discernment and promoted those of substance [?], thereby selecting men for service; they received completed plans and presented the severed ears of slain enemies, thereby deliberating on government. In spring and autumn, rites and music were practiced with stringed instruments; in winter and summer, the Odes and Documents were recited. These were all things that Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
講畫而施行者其爲法制盖精且備矣迨
秦孝公開阡陌始皇置郡縣漢文景用笞
定令於是井田封建肉刑三者俱廢而學
校僅存然博士弟子員之設止爲經訓則
絃與論政取士者又廢此宋蘇軾有感焉
而發於南安軍之學記也然軾之時學校
未遍於天下其所誦亦未能如今日經說
之歸一則今之時稍異於軾之時矣然士
非進取不由學校學校非科舉之文則不
===
誦也抑豈先王之遺意哉必也學校之中
惟以成德達材爲務讀書爲文専於明理
以適世用痛抑浮靡之習則今之學即古
之學今之誦即古之誦矣所當致力者在
此而已若夫絃與取士論政既難復古而
所謂井田封建肉刑其勢又有甚難者亦
何必論其緩急先後哉然井田廢矣而唐
高祖有口分世業之令董仲舒有限田之
請封建廢矣而漢宣帝有政平訟理之託
punctuated: 講畫而施行者，其爲法制盖精且備矣。迨秦孝公開阡陌，始皇置郡縣，漢文景用笞定令，於是井田、封建、肉刑三者俱廢，而學校僅存。然博士弟子員之設，止爲經訓，則絃與論政、取士者又廢。此宋蘇軾有感焉，而發於南安軍之學記也。然軾之時，學校未遍於天下，其所誦亦未能如今日經說之歸一，則今之時稍異於軾之時矣。然士非進取不由學校，學校非科舉之文則不誦也，抑豈先王之遺意哉？必也學校之中，惟以成德達材爲務，讀書爲文，専於明理，以適世用，痛抑浮靡之習，則今之學即古之學，今之誦即古之誦矣。所當致力者，在此而已。若夫絃與取士、論政，既難復古，而所謂井田、封建、肉刑，其勢又有甚難者，亦何必論其緩急先後哉？然井田廢矣，而唐高祖有口分世業之令，董仲舒有限田之請；封建廢矣，而漢宣帝有政平訟理之託，
translation_en:
…deliberated upon, planned, and put into practice. As laws and institutions, they were indeed refined and comprehensive. When Duke Xiao of Qin opened up the field boundaries, the First Emperor established commanderies and counties, and Emperors Wen and Jing of Han enacted statutes prescribing beating with the bamboo, the well-field system, the enfeoffment system, and mutilating punishments were all abolished; schools alone survived. Yet the establishment of student places under the Erudites served only to provide instruction in the Classics. Thus musical recitation, deliberation on government, and the selection of worthy men were also abandoned. It was this that moved Su Shi of the Song to express his feelings in his Record of the School of Nan’an Military Prefecture.

In Su Shi’s time, however, schools had not yet spread throughout the realm, and what they recited had not achieved the uniformity of interpretation of the Classics found today. Our age therefore differs somewhat from his. Yet men enter schools only to seek advancement, and schools have their students recite only writings for the civil-service examinations. Can this possibly preserve the intentions of the former kings? Schools must devote themselves solely to perfecting virtue and developing talent. Reading books and composing prose must concentrate on understanding principles so as to meet the practical needs of the world, while resolutely curbing habits of superficial ornamentation. Then the learning of today will be the learning of antiquity, and today’s recitation will be that of antiquity. This alone is where effort should be directed.

As for musical recitation, the selection of worthy men, and deliberation on government, restoring ancient practice is already difficult. The circumstances surrounding the well-field system, enfeoffment, and mutilating punishments make their restoration still more difficult. Why, then, must we debate their relative urgency or the order in which to undertake them? Nevertheless, although the well-field system was abolished, Emperor Gaozu of Tang issued ordinances concerning per-capita allotments and hereditary holdings, and Dong Zhongshu petitioned for limits on landholdings. Although enfeoffment was abolished, Emperor Xuan of Han entrusted officials with ensuring equitable government and properly adjudicated lawsuits…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
柳子厚有擇守之論肉刑廢矣而釋之有
不信之對王通有無赦之言取士雖廢而
朱子議貢舉在通經史論政雖廢而程子
詳學制在勵風俗至於絃雖廢而陽城有
忠孝之訓韓子有傳道受業解惑之説皆
得乎先王之遺意者誠取其意而行之則
不必更張而治可復三代之盛豈但如吾
前所謂學校與誦而已哉夫孔子大聖也
而用必從乎周禮孟子大賢也而論不必
合於周制然其經世之志固各有在矣故
君子論事以是謂之善論處事以是謂之
善處惟夫不知本於道而茍以狥世者則
非君子所貴也豈敢瀆於高明哉謹對
第五問
===
劉節
同考試官教諭徐　批　備邊一策
國之大計書生熊備畫之是見平日之留心時務矣
同考試官教諭李　批　此策於古名將之成功今備
punctuated:
柳子厚有擇守之論。肉刑廢矣，而釋之有不信之對，王通有無赦之言。取士雖廢，而朱子議貢舉，在通經史；論政雖廢，而程子詳學制，在勵風俗；至於絃雖廢，而陽城有忠孝之訓，韓子有傳道受業解惑之説，皆得乎先王之遺意者。誠取其意而行之，則不必更張，而治可復三代之盛，豈但如吾前所謂學校與誦而已哉！夫孔子大聖也，而用必從乎周禮；孟子大賢也，而論不必合於周制。然其經世之志，固各有在矣。故君子論事以是，謂之善論；處事以是，謂之善處。惟夫不知本於道，而茍以狥世者，則非君子所貴也。豈敢瀆於高明哉？謹對。

第五問

劉節

同考試官教諭徐批：備邊一策，國之大計。書生熊備畫之，是見平日之留心時務矣。

同考試官教諭李批：此策於古名將之成功、今備
translation_en:
…Liu Zihou offered a discussion of selecting prefects. Corporal mutilation was abolished, yet Shizhi gave his reply concerning a failure to keep faith, and Wang Tong spoke of granting no pardons. Although the selection of officials through the schools had fallen into disuse, Master Zhu, in discussing recruitment by recommendation and examination, emphasized mastery of the classics and histories. Although discussion of government in the schools had fallen into disuse, Master Cheng, in elaborating a system of education, emphasized improving social customs. As for instruction through string music [?], although it too had fallen into disuse, Yang Cheng taught loyalty and filial devotion, and Master Han spoke of transmitting the Way, imparting learning, and resolving doubts. All these captured the surviving intentions of the former kings. If we sincerely grasp these intentions and put them into practice, government can recover the flourishing condition of the Three Dynasties without a wholesale reordering of institutions. How could this apply only to the schools and recitation I mentioned earlier?

Confucius was a great sage, yet in practice he invariably followed the rites of Zhou. Mencius was a great worthy, yet his arguments did not invariably accord with Zhou institutions. Nevertheless, each had his own purpose in seeking to order the world. Thus, when a gentleman discusses affairs on this basis, it is called sound discussion; when he handles affairs on this basis, it is called sound management. Those who do not understand how to ground themselves in the Way, but merely accommodate themselves to the age, are not esteemed by the gentleman. How would I dare trouble your enlightened judgment with such things? Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fifth Question

Liu Jie

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: A policy for frontier defense is a matter of great consequence to the state. That a scholar can lay out comprehensive plans for it [?] shows his habitual attention to contemporary affairs.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: This policy essay, concerning the achievements of famous generals of antiquity and present-day preparations for…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
邊之意務敷揚條畫殆盡其文事武備之究意者乎
同考試官學正楊　批　毛鉌子秀才不出鄉國於
邊事已能博古知今區畫布置綽有可採他日若
得用事閫外必使羯胡北奔慄慄危懼而不敢南
嚮牧馬
考試官教諭黃　批　此樣策乎非胸中有甲兵
者不能
考試官學正韓　批　識時務者在俊傑豈可謂
舉子中無人
===
中國之有夷狄猶君子之有小人此氣化
之自然而古今之所不能免也然君子之
去小人不可以無法而中國之禦夷狄不
可以無策故王者畧其治而春秋謹其辨
焉辨之以必辨治之以不治我
聖祖謹備胡戎之訓豈不遠出前代之策而並
駕乎帝王也哉竊嘗仰窺
祖訓之意若謂有必備之國蓋胡戎之近西北
者有不征之國盖朝鮮安南琉球日本之
punctuated:
邊之意務，敷揚條畫殆盡，其文事武備之究意者乎！
同考試官學正楊，批：「毛鉌子秀才，不出鄉國，於邊事已能博古知今，區畫布置，綽有可採。他日若得用事閫外，必使羯胡北奔，慄慄危懼，而不敢南嚮牧馬。」
考試官教諭黃，批：「此樣策乎！非胸中有甲兵者不能。」
考試官學正韓，批：「識時務者在俊傑，豈可謂舉子中無人？」
中國之有夷狄，猶君子之有小人，此氣化之自然，而古今之所不能免也。然君子之去小人，不可以無法；而中國之禦夷狄，不可以無策。故王者畧其治，而春秋謹其辨焉。辨之以必辨，治之以不治。我聖祖謹備胡戎之訓，豈不遠出前代之策，而並駕乎帝王也哉！竊嘗仰窺祖訓之意，若謂有必備之國，蓋胡戎之近西北者；有不征之國，盖朝鮮、安南、琉球、日本之
translation_en:
…the aims and tasks of frontier defense: its exposition and detailed planning are nearly exhaustive. Surely its author has thoroughly grasped both civil affairs and military preparedness!
Associate Examiner Yang, School Instructor, comments: “This young scholar [?], though he has never left his native region, already displays broad knowledge of past and present frontier affairs. His plans and arrangements offer much worth adopting. If one day he is entrusted with military command beyond the gates, he will surely drive the Jie and Hu northward, trembling with fear and not daring to turn south to pasture their horses.”
Examiner Huang, School Instructor, comments: “Such a policy essay! [?] Only someone with armies arrayed in his mind could produce it.”
Examiner Han, School Instructor, comments: “Those who understand the needs of the times are outstanding talents. How can anyone say there are no capable men among the examination candidates?”
That the Central Kingdom has Yi and Di peoples is like the gentleman’s having petty men around him. This arises naturally from the transformations of vital force and has been unavoidable throughout history. Yet gentlemen cannot dispense with methods for removing petty men, nor can the Central Kingdom dispense with policies for resisting the Yi and Di. Thus true kings govern them only loosely, while the Spring and Autumn Annals carefully maintains the distinction between them and us. Make the distinction because it must be made; govern them by not governing them. Does not our Sagely Founder’s injunction to maintain vigilant defenses against the Hu and Rong far surpass the policies of earlier dynasties and rank alongside those of the ancient emperors and kings?
I have ventured to examine reverently the meaning of the Ancestral Injunctions. They seem to say that there are countries against which defenses must be maintained—namely, the Hu and Rong near the northwestern frontier—and countries that are not to be attacked, namely Chaoxian, Annan, Liuqiu, and Riben …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
屬在東與南者其備胡戎則曰選將練兵
而不及乎他烏乎無怠無荒四夷來王帝
王自治之策莫過於此我
聖祖蓋得之矣故嘗考之古人謂周之薄伐為
得中策漢之出師為得下策秦之築城以
㢢中國則為無策者嚴尤之論也謂周之
惠綏為得上策秦之設險為得中策漢之
和親以輕中國則為無策者此宋祁之論
也然祁之論周漢是也以秦之策為中則
===
非矣尤之論周漢非也以秦之策為無則
是矣祁譏尤辨而未詳愚謂祁亦詳而未
當何則周之薄伐惠綏政有合於
聖祖乃或以為中而顧取於秦漢之事此所以
互有得失也今燕薊以西甘凉以東大鎮
數十小鎮數百
聖祖之所謹備者盖在於此桼何承平以來邊
事日廢其為將者求如趙之李牧漢之周
亞夫趙充國唐之李晟李德裕宋之韓琦
punctuated:
屬，在東與南者。其備胡戎，則曰選將練兵，而不及乎他。烏乎！「無怠無荒，四夷來王。」帝王自治之策，莫過於此。我聖祖蓋得之矣。故嘗考之，古人謂周之薄伐為得中策，漢之出師為得下策，秦之築城以㢢中國則為無策者，嚴尤之論也。謂周之惠綏為得上策，秦之設險為得中策，漢之和親以輕中國則為無策者，此宋祁之論也。然祁之論周、漢，是也；以秦之策為中，則非矣。尤之論周、漢，非也；以秦之策為無，則是矣。祁譏尤辨而未詳，愚謂祁亦詳而未當。何則？周之薄伐、惠綏，政有合於聖祖，乃或以為中，而顧取於秦、漢之事，此所以互有得失也。
今燕薊以西、甘凉以東，大鎮數十，小鎮數百，聖祖之所謹備者，盖在於此。桼何承平以來，邊事日廢，其為將者，求如趙之李牧、漢之周亞夫、趙充國、唐之李晟、李德裕、宋之韓琦
translation_en:
…and others of that kind, situated to the east and south. As for guarding against the Hu and Rong, he spoke of selecting generals and training troops, without extending his instructions to other measures. Ah! “Be neither idle nor remiss, and the barbarians of the four quarters will come to acknowledge your kingship.” No strategy by which emperors and kings put their own realm in order surpasses this. Our Sagely Progenitor surely grasped it.
I have examined the views of earlier writers. Yan You held that the Zhou’s limited punitive expeditions were a middling strategy, that the Han’s dispatch of armies was an inferior strategy, and that the Qin’s building of walls to the detriment of the Central Realm [?] amounted to having no strategy at all. Song Qi held that the Zhou’s benevolent pacification was the best strategy, that the Qin’s establishment of defensive barriers was a middling strategy, and that the Han’s marriage alliances, which diminished the standing of the Central Realm, amounted to having no strategy at all. Yet Qi was right in his assessment of the Zhou and Han, but wrong to rank the Qin’s strategy as middling. You was wrong in his assessment of the Zhou and Han, but right to judge the Qin as having no strategy. Qi criticized You’s argument as discriminating but insufficiently thorough; I humbly submit that Qi’s own argument, though thorough, was not entirely sound. Why? The Zhou’s limited punitive expeditions and benevolent pacification accorded precisely with the practice of our Sagely Progenitor. Yet some ranked these as merely middling and instead found merit in the actions of the Qin and Han. This explains why each assessment had both strengths and failings.
Today, west of Yan and Ji and east of Gan and Liang, there are several dozen large garrisons and several hundred small ones. It was surely here that our Sagely Progenitor took care to maintain defenses. Yet why [?], since the advent of lasting peace, have frontier affairs fallen into increasing neglect? Among those serving as generals, if one seeks men like Li Mu of Zhao, Zhou Yafu and Zhao Chongguo of the Han, Li Sheng and Li Deyu of the Tang, or Han Qi of the Song…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
范仲淹者既不可得則稽閱為擾召募為
玩安輯之而愈逃閑習之而愈惰鼓作之
而愈怯亦無足怪者必也求之於貪緣犇
走之外試之以古今常變之畧儲之於位
望未隆之時難之以卒然難應之機用之
於羽檄交馳之地志於忠義者則感之以
忠信志於富貴者則歆之以爵禄重以專
制之權嚴以失律之法論出于衆制掌於
一而它無與焉則必有若人者出于尋常
===
而成功豈不可責與蓋既有一韓一范之
望而加之以充國取勝之計亞夫不聞詔
之威平時運德裕之籌當事圖李晟之備
則牧之所謂戰守者有不足為矣雖然稽
閱召募不可偏廢而習藝作氣之方當自
安輯始今之邊將誠無科率之煩使屯操
之人歲有實賜月無虛支由是以稽則實
以閱則精以召募則得藝不習而自閑氣
不鼓而自作守固戰克何憂乎胡戎之侵
punctuated:
范仲淹者既不可得，則稽閱為擾，召募為玩，安輯之而愈逃，閑習之而愈惰，鼓作之而愈怯，亦無足怪者。必也求之於貪緣犇走之外，試之以古今常變之畧，儲之於位望未隆之時，難之以卒然難應之機，用之於羽檄交馳之地。志於忠義者，則感之以忠信；志於富貴者，則歆之以爵禄。重以專制之權，嚴以失律之法，論出于衆，制掌於一，而它無與焉，則必有若人者出于尋常而成功，豈不可責與？蓋既有一韓一范之望，而加之以充國取勝之計、亞夫不聞詔之威，平時運德裕之籌，當事圖李晟之備，則牧之所謂戰守者，有不足為矣。
雖然，稽閱召募不可偏廢，而習藝作氣之方，當自安輯始。今之邊將誠無科率之煩，使屯操之人歲有實賜，月無虛支，由是以稽則實，以閱則精，以召募則得，藝不習而自閑，氣不鼓而自作，守固戰克，何憂乎胡戎之侵
translation_en:
…or Fan Zhongyan cannot be found, it is hardly surprising that inspections and musters become a nuisance, recruitment becomes a mere game, efforts to settle and reassure the troops only increase desertion, training only increases their indolence, and efforts to rouse them only increase their timidity. Such men must surely be sought outside the ranks of those who chase advancement through greedy connections [?]. Test them on strategies for ordinary and changing circumstances, ancient and modern; keep them in reserve before their rank and reputation have risen high; challenge them with sudden crises that are difficult to meet; and employ them where urgent military dispatches fly back and forth. Those whose aspirations lie in loyalty and righteousness should be moved by loyalty and trustworthiness; those whose aspirations lie in wealth and eminence should be enticed with rank and emoluments. Give them weight through authority to exercise independent command, and hold them strictly accountable under the laws against breaches of military discipline. Let deliberation proceed from many, but command rest with one, with no interference from others. Then men of this kind will surely emerge from ordinary circumstances and achieve success. Could success not be required of them? Once there is someone with the prestige of a Han Qi or a Fan Zhongyan, supplement this with Zhao Chongguo’s plans for victory and Zhou Yafu’s commanding authority, which admitted no imperial edict. In quiet times, employ Li Deyu’s strategic calculations; when action comes, devise preparations like Li Sheng’s. Then what Li Mu called fighting and defending would be no difficult undertaking.
Nevertheless, neither inspections and musters nor recruitment may be neglected, and the means of training military skills and rousing morale must begin with settling and reassuring the troops. If today’s frontier commanders truly refrained from burdensome exactions, ensuring that those engaged in garrison service and drill received actual grants each year and that monthly disbursements were not fictitious, then inspections would reveal genuine strength, musters would display well-trained troops, and recruitment would secure suitable men. Skills would become proficient without drilling, and morale would rise without exhortation. With defenses secure and battles victorious, what fear need there be of incursions by the Hu and Rong…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
何壓乎
九重西北之顧哉此所謂不治之治必辨之
辨哉
聖祖之謨畧眞帝王之上策也抑又念之駿求
千金艾畜三年今之選將急矣而食也器
也馬也又兵家之所當備者執事何以濟
之愚也操觚待試而每聞邊報輙詟于懷
故涉筆至此非敢出位也將以為芹曝之
獻也
punctuated: 何壓乎九重西北之顧哉？此所謂不治之治，必辨之辨哉！聖祖之謨畧，眞帝王之上策也。抑又念之：駿求千金，艾畜三年。今之選將急矣，而食也、器也、馬也，又兵家之所當備者，執事何以濟之？愚也操觚待試，而每聞邊報，輙詟于懷，故涉筆至此，非敢出位也，將以為芹曝之獻也。
translation_en: …What could weigh upon [?] His Majesty’s concern for the northwest? Is this not what is called governing without governing, and making the necessary dispositions [?]? The plans of the sagely founder are truly the highest strategy of an emperor or king. Yet I reflect further: a fine steed is sought at a price of a thousand pieces of gold, and mugwort must be stored for three years. Selecting commanders is now urgent; but provisions, weapons, and horses are also things that military planners must have ready. By what means will you, honored examiners, supply them? I, in my ignorance, hold my writing tablet and await examination, yet whenever I hear reports from the frontier, fear strikes my heart. Thus my writing has ventured into these matters. I do not presume to speak beyond my station; I merely offer this as a humble gift of cress and warming sunshine.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
弘治辛酉秋八月江西藩司
試十三郡之士饗以賓禮而
貢于
朝制也既如制從事得士九十
五人列第氏名刻其文之尤
為錄以
===
獻秩執冊而讀之曰猗盛哉此
古之所謂鄉書也其所錄者
一鄉之士也士由文取故并
錄其文猶有所伺以通于天
下故其試曰鄉錄亦曰鄉然
是錄
獻之
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

弘治辛酉秋八月，江西藩司試十三郡之士，饗以賓禮，而貢于朝，制也。既如制從事，得士九十五人，列第氏名，刻其文之尤，為錄以獻。秩執冊而讀之，曰：「猗，盛哉！此古之所謂鄉書也。其所錄者，一鄉之士也。士由文取，故并錄其文，猶有所伺以通于天下，故其試曰鄉，錄亦曰鄉。然是錄獻之
translation_en:
Afterword to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the xinyou year of the Hongzhi reign [1501], the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission examined the scholars of its thirteen prefectures, entertained them with the ceremonial honors accorded to guests, and recommended them to the court, as prescribed by established regulations. Having conducted the proceedings according to these regulations, it selected ninety-five scholars, listed their ranks and names, and had the finest of their compositions printed to make a record for presentation.

Zhi 秩 took up the volume, read it, and said: “Ah, how splendid! This is what the ancients called the ‘register of local worthies’ (xiangshu). Those recorded in it are scholars of a single region. Since scholars are selected through their writing, their compositions are recorded as well. There still remains something to await [?] before they gain recognition throughout the realm; hence the examination is called ‘provincial,’ and its record is likewise called ‘provincial.’ Yet this record is presented to …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
天府而先達之于春官合兩京十
三省所錄士而群試之擇可
進者入與
廷對遂稱天下士天下士豈出
鄉士外哉故士必有天下之
志與學而德以將之才以達
之藏器蓄力載以攸往乃能
===
成天下之功而副乎其望夫
是之謂天下之士文也者言
乎是者也試也者取乎是者
也錄也者將以徵乎是者也
是之不務而或下焉則誠鄉
士而已矣又下焉爲鄙爲野
冒士之名以忝於鄉上之所
punctuated: 天府，而先達之于春官，合兩京十三省所錄士而群試之，擇可進者入與廷對，遂稱天下士。天下士豈出鄉士外哉？故士必有天下之志與學，而德以將之，才以達之，藏器蓄力，載以攸往，乃能成天下之功而副乎其望。夫是之謂天下之士。文也者，言乎是者也；試也者，取乎是者也；錄也者，將以徵乎是者也。是之不務而或下焉，則誠鄉士而已矣。又下焉，爲鄙爲野，冒士之名以忝於鄉。上之所
translation_en: …to the imperial repository, first transmitting it to the Ministry of Rites. The scholars recorded by the two capitals and thirteen provinces are assembled and examined together. Those deemed fit to advance are selected to enter and participate in the court examination, and are thereupon called scholars of the realm. Yet how could scholars of the realm come from outside the ranks of local scholars? A scholar must therefore possess aspirations and learning that encompass the whole realm, with virtue to guide them and ability to bring them to fruition. Storing up his capabilities and gathering his strength, he proceeds toward his purpose; only then can he accomplish deeds for the realm and meet the expectations placed upon him. Such a person is what we call a scholar of the realm. Examination writing gives expression to these qualities; examinations select men for these qualities; examination records are intended to attest to these qualities. If a man fails to cultivate them and falls below this standard, he is indeed merely a local scholar. If he falls still lower, becoming crude and uncultivated, he usurps the name of scholar and brings disgrace upon his locality. Those whom the authorities…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
取者將爲天下用而乃如此
豈士之自期者哉今夫耕且
蠶者其樹藝同其桑繅同其
所獲粟帛或衣食天下或僅
給其一方或不足自給而年
之豐歉世之休咎事事者之
勤與惰皆係焉取士之得否
===
何以異是秩嘗聞諸君子志
以伊尹學以顔淵此蓋天下
之論至要其成必如臯陶之
所謂有常而後可以言德必
如周公之所謂攸濟而後可
以言才必如吉甫之所謂克
舉而後可以言器可以言肅
punctuated:
取者將爲天下用，而乃如此，豈士之自期者哉？今夫耕且蠶者，其樹藝同，其桑繅同，其所獲粟帛，或衣食天下，或僅給其一方，或不足自給，而年之豐歉、世之休咎、事事者之勤與惰皆係焉。取士之得否，何以異是？
秩嘗聞諸君子：「志以伊尹，學以顔淵。」此蓋天下之論。至要其成，必如臯陶之所謂「有常」，而後可以言德；必如周公之所謂「攸濟」，而後可以言才；必如吉甫之所謂「克舉」，而後可以言器，可以言肅。
translation_en:
…those selected are to serve all under Heaven; yet if they are like this, can that be what scholars aspire to for themselves? Consider those who till the fields and raise silkworms: their planting and cultivation are alike, as are their tending of mulberries and reeling of silk. Yet the grain and cloth they produce may feed and clothe all under Heaven, may barely supply their own locality, or may not even suffice for themselves. All this depends upon whether the harvest is abundant or poor, whether the times are favorable or adverse, and whether those doing the work are diligent or idle. How is success or failure in selecting scholars any different?
I, Zhi, have heard from gentlemen: “In aspiration, take Yi Yin as your model; in learning, take Yan Yuan.” This, surely, is a judgment shared by all under Heaven. But to assess their ultimate attainment, only when they possess what Gao Yao called “constancy” can one speak of virtue; only when they achieve what the Duke of Zhou called “bringing matters to completion” can one speak of talent; only when they accomplish what Jifu called “capably discharging one’s duties” can one speak of capacity and of reverence…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
由是勵修惇裕以興禮樂以
堯舜其君民而後可以言天
下之功其文之傳亦庶幾乎
數納明揚而得與於所謂不
朽者然則士欲不局於鄉而
稱于天下求免夫鄙且野者
可不知所務哉今諸士表表
===
產兹土得於山川若是其秀
游歌
聖化若是其久且深而文獻在耳
目者又若是其足徵也其間
豈無以天下士自期者若期
而未自信者若自限若自放
若自盈侈謂不必期者蓋亦
punctuated: 由是勵修惇裕，以興禮樂，以堯舜其君民，而後可以言天下之功。其文之傳，亦庶幾乎數納明揚，而得與於所謂不朽者。然則士欲不局於鄉而稱于天下，求免夫鄙且野者，可不知所務哉？今諸士表表，產兹土，得於山川若是其秀，游歌聖化若是其久且深，而文獻在耳目者，又若是其足徵也。其間豈無以天下士自期者？若期而未自信者，若自限，若自放，若自盈侈謂不必期者，蓋亦
translation_en:
…From this foundation, they must diligently cultivate themselves, deepen their virtue and broaden their capacities, promote rites and music, and bring their ruler and people to the ideal exemplified by Yao and Shun. Only then may we speak of achievements benefiting all under Heaven. Through the transmission of their writings, they might also hope to be repeatedly received and publicly commended [?], and thus take their place among those deemed immortal. If scholars wish to win recognition throughout the realm rather than remain confined to their native district, and seek to avoid narrowness and uncouthness, can they fail to understand what they must pursue?

Now these outstanding scholars were born in this land and have received such exceptional gifts from its mountains and rivers. They have lived and sung under the sage ruler’s transforming influence for so long and so profoundly; moreover, the writings and worthy men known to their eyes and ears provide such ample testimony. Among them, surely there are those who aspire to be scholars of the whole realm? As for those who aspire to this but lack confidence, those who set limits upon themselves, those who abandon themselves, and those who, full of conceit and arrogance, declare that such aspiration is unnecessary, there presumably also …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
有之繼自今定則力疑則决
或改而圖焉則吾所錄者將
不皆天下士乎一方耕之而
天下食之一方蠶之而天下
衣之是錄也吾固曰一鄉之
書而天下觀者乃將曰是所
錄者皆天下士而其文與在
===
焉謂天下之書可也獨鄉云
乎哉雖然終是錄者題有名
碑注有選籍稽有功載覈有
臺評書有史筆而復定之以
君子之論夫然後天下之士
可得而稱矣秩不佞敬書于
末簡用爲諸士子告
punctuated:
有之。繼自今，定則力，疑則决，或改而圖焉，則吾所錄者將不皆天下士乎？一方耕之而天下食之，一方蠶之而天下衣之。是錄也，吾固曰一鄉之書，而天下觀者乃將曰：「是所錄者皆天下士，而其文與在焉，謂天下之書可也，獨鄉云乎哉？」
雖然，終是錄者，題有名碑，注有選籍，稽有功載，覈有臺評，書有史筆，而復定之以君子之論。夫然後天下之士可得而稱矣。秩不佞，敬書于末簡，用爲諸士子告。
translation_en:
…there are such men. From now onward, if those whose resolve is settled exert themselves, those who doubt make their decision, and others reform themselves and pursue this aim, will not all those I have recorded become men of worth for all under Heaven? One region tills the fields, and all under Heaven eat its produce; one region raises silkworms, and all under Heaven wear its silk. This record I have indeed called the book of a single province, yet readers throughout the realm will say: “Those recorded here are all men of worth for all under Heaven, and their writings are included here as well. It may properly be called a book of all under Heaven. Why speak only of a province?”
Nevertheless, what ultimately completes this record will be their names inscribed on stelae, their entries in registers of official selection, their achievements examined in records of service, their conduct assessed in evaluations by the Censorate, and their deeds written down by historians, with judgment further settled by the considered opinions of gentlemen. Only then may they rightly be called men of worth for all under Heaven. I, Zhi 秩, untalented as I am, respectfully write these words at the end of the volume to admonish the candidates.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
山東東昌府高唐州夏津縣
儒學教諭黃秩謹序

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之功也夫心有不純者欲累之也能無所累則
自慊矣君子謹獨之功一何至哉中庸卒章言
君子下學之事至此引小雅正月之詩而申之
若曰潛伏之地雖隱微而難知事理之幾則顯
著而易見君子於此豈待徵於色而後省耶幾
一動也人雖不知而已則獨知即從而省之何
者為公何者為私私間乎公心之病也必純乎
公而私不能間則吾心無所病焉抑豈待發於
聲而後察耶念一萌也人雖不見而已則獨見
===
即從而察之何者為誠何者為僞僞雜乎誠心
之疵也必純乎誠而僞不能雜則吾心無所疵
焉内省不疚如此又豈有所惡於志哉蓋志者
心之所之公而無私天之則也私或病焉未能
無愧矣今也既純乎公則所發者揆諸天則而
允協于神明之舍夫何有所怍乎誠而無僞天
之命也僞或疵焉未能無惡矣今也既純乎誠
則所發者質諸天命而信乎于虛靈之境夫何
有所惡乎君子謹獨而能自慊如此此其所以為
punctuated: 之功也。夫心有不純者，欲累之也。能無所累，則自慊矣。君子謹獨之功，一何至哉！中庸卒章言君子下學之事，至此引小雅正月之詩而申之。若曰：潛伏之地，雖隱微而難知，事理之幾，則顯著而易見。君子於此，豈待徵於色而後省耶？幾一動也，人雖不知，而已則獨知，即從而省之：何者為公？何者為私？私間乎公，心之病也。必純乎公而私不能間，則吾心無所病焉。抑豈待發於聲而後察耶？念一萌也，人雖不見，而已則獨見，即從而察之：何者為誠？何者為僞？僞雜乎誠，心之疵也。必純乎誠而僞不能雜，則吾心無所疵焉。内省不疚如此，又豈有所惡於志哉？蓋志者，心之所之。公而無私，天之則也；私或病焉，未能無愧矣。今也既純乎公，則所發者揆諸天則，而允協于神明之舍，夫何有所怍乎？誠而無僞，天之命也；僞或疵焉，未能無惡矣。今也既純乎誠，則所發者質諸天命，而信乎于虛靈之境，夫何有所惡乎？君子謹獨而能自慊如此，此其所以為
translation_en:
…such is the work involved. When the heart is not pure, it is because desires encumber it. If it can remain unencumbered, one will be satisfied within oneself. How consummate is the gentleman’s work of vigilance in solitude! The final chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean discusses the gentleman’s learning through everyday affairs. At this point it quotes the poem “First Month” from the Lesser Odes to elaborate upon this. It is as though it were saying: although what lies concealed is obscure and difficult to know, the incipient workings of affairs and principles are manifest and easy to perceive. In this, would the gentleman wait until something showed in his countenance before examining himself? As soon as an incipient impulse stirs, although others do not know it, he alone knows it, and immediately examines it: which part is impartial, and which selfish? Selfishness intruding upon impartiality is a sickness of the heart. Only when impartiality is pure and selfishness cannot intrude will my heart be free of sickness.

Or would he wait until something found expression in his voice before scrutinizing it? As soon as a thought sprouts, although others do not see it, he alone sees it, and immediately scrutinizes it: which part is sincere, and which false? Falsehood mingling with sincerity is a blemish upon the heart. Only when sincerity is pure and falsehood cannot mingle with it will my heart be free of blemish. With inward examination thus revealing no cause for remorse, how could there be anything shameful in one’s intentions?

Intentions are, indeed, that toward which the heart moves. To be impartial and without selfishness is Heaven’s rule. If selfishness should afflict the heart, one cannot yet be free of shame. Now, however, once one is wholly impartial, what issues from the heart, measured against Heaven’s rule, accords truly with the abode of spiritual intelligence. What cause could there be for shame? To be sincere and without falsehood is Heaven’s mandate. If falsehood should blemish the heart, one cannot yet be free of shame. Now, however, once one is wholly sincere, what issues from the heart, tested against Heaven’s mandate, is trustworthy within the realm of the heart’s receptive awareness. What cause could there be for shame? Such is the gentleman’s ability to attain inward satisfaction through vigilance in solitude; this is why it constitutes…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
為已之學而有不可及也歟大抵君子為已之
學莫要於省察尤莫要於存養聖賢相傳心法
實在於斯子思於首章既揭以示人而此復推
言之其曰不動而敬不言而信即首章所謂戒
慎恐懼也若內省之說所以申謹獨者則尤切
矣蓋必如是而後可以馴致乎不賞民勸不怒
民威篤恭而天下平之效焉中和位育之化豈
外於一心也哉故君子志於學者當自立心始
親親仁也敬長義也
===
葉釗
同考試官訓導劉　批　連日閱卷類多以愛親敬
長盡於孝弟之節者言之不知出於童幼自然之
性而此篇詞理明暢發出孟子之意親切是可
與論性學矣
同考試官教諭潘　批　雖不掉弄文法而意義自
足深得本領文字體
同考試官教諭傅　批　孟子七篇仁義惟此章從
人良知良能說來最為精切此卷辭純縝而理亦
punctuated:
為已之學，而有不可及也歟？大抵君子為已之學，莫要於省察，尤莫要於存養。聖賢相傳心法，實在於斯。子思於首章既揭以示人，而此復推言之。其曰「不動而敬，不言而信」，即首章所謂戒慎恐懼也。若內省之說，所以申謹獨者，則尤切矣。蓋必如是，而後可以馴致乎不賞民勸、不怒民威、篤恭而天下平之效焉。中和位育之化，豈外於一心也哉？故君子志於學者，當自立心始。

親親，仁也；敬長，義也。

葉釗

同考試官訓導劉批：連日閱卷，類多以愛親敬長盡於孝弟之節者言之，不知出於童幼自然之性。而此篇詞理明暢，發出孟子之意，親切，是可與論性學矣。

同考試官教諭潘批：雖不掉弄文法，而意義自足，深得本領文字體。

同考試官教諭傅批：孟子七篇仁義，惟此章從人良知良能說來，最為精切。此卷辭純縝，而理亦
translation_en:
…learning for one's own sake, with an excellence beyond others' reach? In general, in the gentleman's learning for his own sake, nothing is more essential than self-examination, and still more essential is preserving and nurturing the mind. Here indeed lies the teaching of the mind transmitted by sages and worthies. Zisi already set it forth for readers in the opening chapter, and here develops it further. The words “reverent without acting, trustworthy without speaking” refer precisely to the watchfulness, caution, apprehension, and fear spoken of in the opening chapter. The discussion of inward examination, which elaborates vigilance when alone, is especially pertinent. Only through this can one gradually attain the results whereby the people are encouraged without rewards, held in awe without anger, and the world brought to peace through earnest reverence. Could the transforming influence by which equilibrium and harmony give all things their proper places and nurture their growth lie outside this single mind? Thus, gentlemen intent upon learning should begin by firmly establishing their minds.

“Affection for one's kin is benevolence; respect for one's elders is righteousness.”

Ye Zhao

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor: In reading examination papers over successive days, I have found that most discuss affection for parents and respect for elders solely in terms of fulfilling the duties of filial piety and fraternal deference. They fail to recognize that these arise from the spontaneous nature of young children. This essay, however, is clear and fluent in both expression and reasoning, bringing out Mencius's meaning with direct relevance. Its author is someone with whom one may discuss the study of human nature.

Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor: Though it does not flaunt compositional technique, its meaning is complete in itself. It thoroughly grasps the essential manner of writing [?].

Comment by Associate Examiner Fu, Instructor: Of the discussions of benevolence and righteousness in the seven books of Mencius, this chapter alone approaches them through people's innate knowledge and innate capacity, and is supremely precise and pertinent. This paper's language is pure and closely woven, and its reasoning is also…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
精緻一結尤得孟子之心其殆有道者歟
考試官教諭黄　批〔得旨〕
考試官學正韓　批〔發明仁義之旨殆盡〕
大賢指良心之所發者爲本心之所具者盖愛
親敬長發於良心者然也則夫仁義之具於本
心者豈有外於是哉昔孟子之意盖謂立人之
道曰仁與義仁義之心不爲人皆有乎彼子之
於親分於一體故人當夫幼也無不知愛其親
欣慕之意藹然於孩抱之間眷戀之情油然於
===
提携之頃此果何爲而然哉人有此心即具此
仁仁主於愛而愛莫切於愛親惟帝降衷自有
不能已者借曰非仁則有待於習矣然則親親
不謂之仁而何哉弟之於兄出於一氣故人及
其長也無不知敬其兄一飲食歟而推讓之不
忽一起居歟而順遜之有序此又何爲而然哉
人有此心即有此義義主於敬而敬莫先於敬
兄惟民秉彝自有不容遏者借曰非義則有事
於脩矣然則敬長不謂之義而何哉吁親親爲
punctuated:
精緻，一結尤得孟子之心，其殆有道者歟！
考試官教諭黄批〔得旨〕
考試官學正韓批〔發明仁義之旨殆盡〕
大賢指良心之所發者爲本心之所具者。盖愛親敬長，發於良心者然也，則夫仁義之具於本心者，豈有外於是哉？昔孟子之意，盖謂立人之道曰仁與義，仁義之心，不爲人皆有乎？彼子之於親，分於一體，故人當夫幼也，無不知愛其親。欣慕之意，藹然於孩抱之間；眷戀之情，油然於提携之頃。此果何爲而然哉？人有此心，即具此仁。仁主於愛，而愛莫切於愛親。惟帝降衷，自有不能已者。借曰非仁，則有待於習矣。然則親親不謂之仁而何哉？弟之於兄，出於一氣，故人及其長也，無不知敬其兄。一飲食歟，而推讓之不忽；一起居歟，而順遜之有序。此又何爲而然哉？人有此心，即有此義。義主於敬，而敬莫先於敬兄。惟民秉彝，自有不容遏者。借曰非義，則有事於脩矣。然則敬長不謂之義而何哉？吁！親親爲
translation_en:
…refined and meticulous. The conclusion especially captures Mencius’s intent. Surely its author is someone who possesses the Way!
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔Captures the purport.〕
Examiner Han, School Director, comments: 〔Elucidates the purport of benevolence and righteousness almost exhaustively.〕
The great worthy identifies what issues from the innate moral heart as what the original heart inherently possesses. Loving one’s parents and respecting one’s elders are indeed expressions of the innate moral heart. Could the benevolence and righteousness inherent in the original heart lie anywhere beyond these? Mencius’s meaning was surely this: what establishes the human Way is benevolence and righteousness. Does not everyone possess a heart of benevolence and righteousness? A child derives from the same body as its parents; hence, in childhood, no one fails to know to love their parents. Joyful affection flourishes while the infant is held in the arms; feelings of attachment arise spontaneously while the child is led by the hand. What makes this so? To possess this heart is already to possess this benevolence. Benevolence centers on love, and no love is more intimate than love for one’s parents. Because the Lord on High has bestowed this moral nature, something within it cannot cease of itself. If we supposed that this were not benevolence, benevolence would have to await learning through practice. What, then, should affection for one’s parents be called, if not benevolence?
A younger brother and his elder brother arise from the same vital force; hence, as people grow older, none fails to know to respect their elder brothers. In eating and drinking, they never neglect to yield precedence; in everyday conduct, their compliance and deference follow the proper order. What, again, makes this so? To possess this heart is already to possess this righteousness. Righteousness centers on respect, and in respect nothing takes precedence over respecting one’s elder brother. Because the people hold fast to their constant moral nature, something within it cannot be suppressed. If we supposed that this were not righteousness, righteousness would require deliberate cultivation. What, then, should respecting one’s elders be called, if not righteousness? Ah! Affection for one’s parents constitutes…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
仁仁出於天下之同愛敬長為義義出於天下
之同敬仁義之在人如此而可以不求乎雖然
孟子七篇無非性善仁義之說或以惻隱言仁
或以羞惡言義固皆即情見性而情之所發惟
愛親敬長之心出於天不係於人視夫有感而
應者尤為真切故孟子又指言之其欲人知仁
義不假外求而勇於用力者至矣以此為教猶
有曠安宅舍正路而弗居弗由者可勝嘆哉
易
===
觀天之神道而四時不忒　　葉釗
同考試官訓導劉　批〔天之神道正在四時不忒上見作者多含糊不明此篇卓有所見是用錄出以〕
式來學
同考試官教諭潘　批〔說盡天道所以為觀之意而略不費力佳作也〕
同考試官教諭傅　批〔此題重在神道上而四時不忒乃神道行乎其間學者多昧此而兩折之不知本義所〕
punctuated:
仁，仁出於天下之同愛；敬長為義，義出於天下之同敬。仁義之在人如此，而可以不求乎？雖然，孟子七篇無非性善仁義之說，或以惻隱言仁，或以羞惡言義，固皆即情見性。而情之所發，惟愛親敬長之心出於天，不係於人，視夫有感而應者尤為真切，故孟子又指言之。其欲人知仁義不假外求而勇於用力者至矣！以此為教，猶有曠安宅、舍正路而弗居弗由者，可勝嘆哉！

易

觀天之神道而四時不忒。葉釗。

同考試官訓導劉，批〔天之神道正在四時不忒上見，作者多含糊不明。此篇卓有所見，是用錄出以〕式來學。

同考試官教諭潘，批〔說盡天道所以為觀之意，而略不費力，佳作也。〕

同考試官教諭傅，批〔此題重在神道上，而四時不忒乃神道行乎其間。學者多昧此而兩折之，不知本義所〕
translation_en:
…benevolence. Benevolence arises from the affection shared by all under Heaven; respecting one’s elders constitutes righteousness, and righteousness arises from the respect shared by all under Heaven. Since benevolence and righteousness exist in people in this way, can one fail to seek them? Nevertheless, the seven books of the Mencius consist entirely of discussions of the goodness of human nature, benevolence, and righteousness. Sometimes compassion is used to explain benevolence, and sometimes shame and aversion to wrongdoing are used to explain righteousness. These all disclose human nature through the feelings. Yet among the manifestations of feeling, the heart that loves one’s parents and respects one’s elders comes from Heaven and does not depend upon human agency. Compared with feelings that respond to an external stimulus, these are especially genuine and immediate. Thus Mencius also singles them out for discussion. His desire that people understand that benevolence and righteousness need not be sought outside themselves, and boldly exert themselves, could not be greater! Even with such teaching, there are still those who leave the peaceful dwelling vacant and abandon the correct road, neither dwelling in the one nor following the other. How could one lament this enough!

Book of Changes

“Observe Heaven’s numinous Way: the four seasons do not err.” By Ye Zhao.

Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Heaven’s numinous Way is manifest precisely in the unfailing course of the four seasons. Writers are often vague and unclear about this. This essay displays outstanding insight; it has therefore been selected and transcribed to serve as a model for future students.”

Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor, comments: “It fully explains the sense in which the Way of Heaven serves as something to contemplate, without the slightest strain. An excellent composition.”

Associate Examiner Fu, Instructor, comments: “The emphasis of this topic lies in the numinous Way, while the unfailing course of the four seasons is the numinous Way operating within them. Students are often unaware of this and split the two apart, failing to understand what the Original Meaning [of the Book of Changes]…”

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
以至言之意此篇融貫昭晰而一結尤知所重故表出之
考試官教諭黃　批　理致之學正如此
考試官學正韓　批　易義明正可錄
觀上天涵妙用而歲成見其所以為觀也蓋天
道之神妙運於四時而歲功成焉其所為觀者
此耳宜彖傳以是極言觀道歟昔伏羲畫卦以
觀名文王既係其辭矣吾夫子彖傳至此極言
觀之道以謂觀之義著于易而其道見於天彼
立天之道曰陰與陽觀夫維天之命動而生陽
===
人知天之為天矣不知其道之神化無方動而
無動焉上天之載靜而生陰蓋曰天之為天矣
不知其道之神妙莫測靜而無靜焉動靜無端
陰陽無始唯合一也又兩在也天道之涵其妙
用如此然而陰陽動靜闔闢變通互為其根故
自一陽之復起于冬至歷震離之間為春分以
至於乾為純陽此則皆鼓自陽動神道之出機
故時春而春時夏而夏各司其令無所差忒焉
自一陰之姤起于夏至歷坎艮之間為秋分以
punctuated:
以至言之意。此篇融貫昭晰，而一結尤知所重，故表出之。
考試官教諭黃，批：理致之學正如此。
考試官學正韓，批：易義明正，可錄。
觀上天涵妙用，而歲成見其所以為觀也。蓋天道之神，妙運於四時，而歲功成焉。其所為觀者，此耳。宜彖傳以是極言觀道歟！昔伏羲畫卦，以觀名，文王既係其辭矣。吾夫子彖傳至此，極言觀之道，以謂觀之義著于易，而其道見於天。彼立天之道曰陰與陽。觀夫維天之命，動而生陽，人知天之為天矣，不知其道之神，化無方，動而無動焉。上天之載，靜而生陰，蓋曰天之為天矣，不知其道之神，妙莫測，靜而無靜焉。動靜無端，陰陽無始，唯合一也，又兩在也。天道之涵其妙用如此。然而陰陽動靜，闔闢變通，互為其根。故自一陽之復起于冬至，歷震離之間為春分，以至於乾為純陽，此則皆鼓自陽動，神道之出機。故時春而春，時夏而夏，各司其令，無所差忒焉。自一陰之姤起于夏至，歷坎艮之間為秋分，以
translation_en:
…the intention behind the words “to the utmost.” This essay integrates its argument with clarity, and its conclusion shows particular understanding of where the emphasis belongs. I have therefore singled it out.
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: Learning that penetrates principle is precisely like this.
Examiner Han, School Instructor, comments: Its interpretation of the Changes is clear and correct, and merits inclusion.
Observe how Heaven above contains wondrous workings: in the completion of the year, we see how it presents itself for contemplation. The spiritual efficacy of Heaven’s Way operates wondrously through the four seasons, bringing the year’s work to completion. This alone is what it presents for contemplation. How fitting that the Commentary on the Judgments should use this to expound the way of Contemplation to the utmost!
Long ago, Fuxi drew the hexagram and named it Guan, “Contemplation”; King Wen then appended its statement. When our Master Confucius reached this point in his Commentary on the Judgments, he expounded the way of Contemplation to the utmost. His meaning was that the significance of Contemplation is manifest in the Changes, while its way is visible in Heaven. “What establishes the Way of Heaven is called yin and yang.” Consider Heaven’s enduring mandate: through movement it generates yang. People recognize in this what makes Heaven Heaven, but they do not recognize the spiritual efficacy of its Way: its transformations have no fixed direction, and it moves without movement. The workings of Heaven above generate yin through stillness. People presumably call this what makes Heaven Heaven, but they do not recognize the spiritual efficacy of its Way: its subtlety is unfathomable, and it is still without stillness. Movement and stillness have no initial point; yin and yang have no beginning. They unite as one, yet both are present. Such are the wondrous workings contained in Heaven’s Way.
Yet yin and yang, movement and stillness, closing and opening, transformation and free passage are each rooted in the other. Thus, beginning with Fu, “Return,” in which a single yang line arises at the winter solstice, the cycle passes between Zhen and Li at the spring equinox and reaches Qian, which is pure yang. All this is impelled by the movement of yang, the mechanism through which the spiritual Way issues forth. Thus, when it is time for spring, spring comes; when it is time for summer, summer comes. Each presides over its seasonal ordinance without deviation. Beginning with Gou, “Encounter,” in which a single yin line arises at the summer solstice, the cycle passes between Kan and Gen at the autumn equinox, and…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
至於坤爲純陰此則皆鼓自陰靜神道之入識
故時秋而秋時冬而冬各循其度無所愆忒焉
其運於歲功之成者又如此吁四時以神道而
不忒天道以四時而爲觀傳易以此極言觀道
其旨微矣抑論觀之爲道誠大矣而聖人之所
以爲觀者亦不外此蓋聖人順性命之理通幽
明之故以神道設教而天下服亦猶天道之神
使非神焉則非所謂天地無心而成化聖人有
心而無爲者矣大傳曰陰陽不測之謂神孟子
曰聖而不可知之之謂神曰不測曰不可知非
知道者孰能識之
===
齊小大者存乎卦
王萱
同考試官訓導劉 批 題本正大作者多於齊小大
處講欠精切此篇獨用易說深合本旨故錄之
同考試官教諭潘 批 無贅詞無冗字作易義
正要如此
同考試官教諭傅 批 天地間陰陽大分自然一
punctuated:
至於坤爲純陰，此則皆鼓自陰靜，神道之入識。故時秋而秋，時冬而冬，各循其度，無所愆忒焉。其運於歲功之成者又如此。吁！四時以神道而不忒，天道以四時而爲觀。傳易以此極言觀道，其旨微矣。抑論觀之爲道，誠大矣，而聖人之所以爲觀者亦不外此。蓋聖人順性命之理，通幽明之故，以神道設教而天下服，亦猶天道之神。使非神焉，則非所謂天地無心而成化、聖人有心而無爲者矣。大傳曰：「陰陽不測之謂神。」孟子曰：「聖而不可知之之謂神。」曰不測，曰不可知，非知道者孰能識之？

齊小大者存乎卦。
王萱

同考試官訓導劉批：題本正大，作者多於齊小大處講欠精切。此篇獨用易說，深合本旨，故錄之。

同考試官教諭潘批：無贅詞，無冗字，作易義正要如此。

同考試官教諭傅批：天地間陰陽大分，自然一
translation_en:
…until it reaches Kun, becoming pure yin. All this is set in motion by the stillness of yin, the inward operation [?] of the numinous Way. Thus, when autumn is due, autumn comes; when winter is due, winter comes. Each follows its proper measure without deviation. Such, too, is its operation in bringing the work of the year to completion. Ah! Through the numinous Way the four seasons proceed without error; through the four seasons Heaven’s Way becomes a manifestation for contemplation. The commentary on the Changes uses this to expound fully the Way of Contemplation: its purport is subtle indeed. Moreover, the Way of Contemplation is truly great, yet the means by which the sage provides a model for contemplation do not go beyond this. The sage follows the principles of human nature and destiny, comprehends the workings of the hidden and the manifest, and establishes instruction through the numinous Way, so that all under Heaven submit. This resembles the numinous efficacy of Heaven’s Way. Were it not numinous, it would not accord with the saying that Heaven and Earth accomplish transformation without conscious intent, while the sage possesses conscious intent yet acts without contrivance. The Great Commentary says: “What cannot be fathomed in yin and yang is called numinous.” Mencius says: “To be sagely yet beyond comprehension is called numinous.” ‘Unfathomable,’ ‘beyond comprehension’: who but one who understands the Way could recognize this?

“Bringing the small and the great into due order rests with the hexagrams.”
By Wang Xuan.

Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor, comments: The topic is inherently upright and grand. Most writers fail to explain the phrase ‘bringing the small and the great into due order’ with sufficient precision. This essay alone employs an interpretation of the Changes that accords closely with the original purport; hence its inclusion.

Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor, comments: There is no superfluous phrase and no redundant word. This is precisely how an essay on the meaning of the Changes should be written.

Associate Examiner Fu, Instructor, comments: The fundamental division between yin and yang in Heaven and Earth is naturally one…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
定特假手於聖人齊之耳而聖人作易豈有意於
其間亦自然之妙有不容言者達於文而造其理
無論此篇
考試官教諭黃　批〔通暢有理〕
考試官學正韓　批〔精潔得旨〕
定易道之大分在易畫之大成蓋陽大陰小自
有一定之分而齊之寧不在於大成之卦畫哉
昔夫子大傳釋卦爻辭之通例而此以卦言之
意謂天地之間陰陽兩端而已陰則體柔性順
===
其道私其類慝偏滯狹隘而小也陽則體剛性
健其道公其類淑光明洞達而大也陰小如此
不有以齊之則混而無別矣唯齊其陰焉為小
而不得以加乎大其分截然以判而界限之正
凜不可踰陽大如此不有以定之則紊而無序
矣唯定其陽焉為大而不可以溺于小其等秩
然以分而區類之別昭不容掩此果何所存哉
蓋存乎卦也彼聖人畫卦定位之時因重再倍
有三十二之陰卦焉凡陰卦則稱為小原始要
punctuated:
定，特假手於聖人齊之耳。而聖人作易，豈有意於其間？亦自然之妙，有不容言者。達於文而造其理，無論此篇。
考試官教諭黃，批〔通暢有理〕。
考試官學正韓，批〔精潔得旨〕。
定易道之大分，在易畫之大成。蓋陽大陰小，自有一定之分，而齊之寧不在於大成之卦畫哉？
昔夫子大傳釋卦爻辭之通例，而此以卦言之。意謂天地之間，陰陽兩端而已。陰則體柔性順，其道私，其類慝，偏滯狹隘而小也。陽則體剛性健，其道公，其類淑，光明洞達而大也。陰小如此，不有以齊之，則混而無別矣。唯齊其陰焉為小，而不得以加乎大，其分截然以判，而界限之正，凜不可踰。陽大如此，不有以定之，則紊而無序矣。唯定其陽焉為大，而不可以溺于小，其等秩然以分，而區類之別，昭不容掩。此果何所存哉？蓋存乎卦也。彼聖人畫卦定位之時，因重再倍，有三十二之陰卦焉。凡陰卦，則稱為小。原始要
translation_en:
…fixed; it merely works through the sages’ hands to set them in order. Yet when the sages made the Changes, did they impose any deliberate intent upon it? Here too is the subtle working of nature, something that cannot be put into words. Fluent in expression and penetrating its principles—“no need to discuss this essay” [?].
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔Clear and fluent, with sound reasoning.〕
Examiner Han, School Director, comments: 〔Refined and concise, grasping the essential meaning.〕
Establishing the great distinction within the Way of the Changes rests upon the full development of its hexagram lines. Yang is great and yin small: they inherently possess a fixed distinction. How, then, could setting them in order fail to reside in the fully developed hexagram figures?
Formerly, the Master’s Great Commentary explained the general principles governing the hexagram and line statements; here, however, he speaks in terms of the hexagrams. His meaning is that between Heaven and Earth there are only the two poles, yin and yang. Yin is yielding in substance and compliant in nature; its way is private, and its kind wicked. Partial, obstructed, narrow, and confined, it is small. Yang is firm in substance and vigorous in nature; its way is public, and its kind good. Luminous and penetrating, it is great. Since yin is small in this way, without something to set it in order, all would be confused and undifferentiated. Only by assigning yin its place as the small, so that it cannot rise above the great, is the distinction sharply drawn; the proper boundary stands forbiddingly clear and cannot be crossed. Since yang is great in this way, without something to establish its place, all would be disordered and without sequence. Only by establishing yang as the great, so that it cannot be submerged in the small, are their ranks distinguished in orderly fashion; the distinction between their categories is manifest and cannot be obscured. Where, then, does this truly reside? It resides in the hexagrams.
When the sages drew the hexagrams and established their positions, they doubled them and doubled them again, producing thirty-two yin hexagrams. All yin hexagrams are designated small. Tracing their beginnings and seeking …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
終有三十二之陽卦焉凡陽卦則稱為大如自
姤之坤而屬乎陰者其間為遯為否與夬為巽
之諸陰卦雖不期小而自見其小斷斷乎不敢
與陽比矣分何其明邪自復之乾而列乎陽者
其中為益為夬與夬為節之諸陽卦雖不期大
而自有其大卓卓乎不至與陰干矣分何其正
邪是則唯卦齊其小大如此所以然者盖天地
陰陽大分自然一定而聖人豈假絲毫知力為
哉傳易之旨微矣大抵易為君子謀也因例可
===
以槩見焉如小畜小過大畜大過之名小往大
来大往小来之義無非各指其所之或陰為主
陰用事也或陽為主陽用事也未嘗不致意於
抑揚之間使天下後世曉然知君子道長之為
慶小人道消之為幸學易者亦當效三絕韋編
方識聖人之所以為心
書
帝光天之下至于海隅蒼生
李文潔
punctuated:
終，有三十二之陽卦焉，凡陽卦則稱為大。如自姤之坤而屬乎陰者，其間為遯、為否，與夬、為巽之諸陰卦，雖不期小而自見其小，斷斷乎不敢與陽比矣，分何其明邪！自復之乾而列乎陽者，其中為益、為夬，與夬、為節之諸陽卦，雖不期大而自有其大，卓卓乎不至與陰干矣，分何其正邪！是則唯卦齊其小大如此。所以然者，盖天地陰陽大分，自然一定，而聖人豈假絲毫知力為哉？傳易之旨微矣！大抵易為君子謀也，因例可以槩見焉。如小畜、小過、大畜、大過之名，小往大来、大往小来之義，無非各指其所之。或陰為主，陰用事也；或陽為主，陽用事也。未嘗不致意於抑揚之間，使天下後世曉然知君子道長之為慶，小人道消之為幸。學易者亦當效三絕韋編，方識聖人之所以為心。

書
帝光天之下，至于海隅蒼生。
李文潔
translation_en:
…the end, there are thirty-two yang hexagrams; all yang hexagrams are termed “great.” Those belonging to yin extend from Gou to Kun. Among them are Dun, Pi, and the yin hexagrams listed as Guai and Xun [?]. Though not intended to be small, they naturally manifest their smallness and decidedly dare not rank alongside yang. How clear the distinction is! Those ranked as yang extend from Fu to Qian. Among them are Yi, Guai, and the yang hexagrams listed as Guai and Jie [?]. Though not intended to be great, they naturally possess their greatness; standing distinctly apart, they do not encroach upon yin. How proper the distinction is! Thus it is through the hexagrams that the small and the great are duly ordered in this way. The reason is that the fundamental division between yin and yang in Heaven and Earth is naturally fixed. How could the sage have needed to expend even the slightest intellectual effort to bring this about? Subtle indeed is the purport of the commentary on the Changes!

Broadly speaking, the Changes takes counsel for the noble man. Its examples allow us to grasp this general principle. The names Lesser Taming (Xiaoxu), Lesser Exceeding (Xiaoguo), Great Taming (Daxu), and Great Exceeding (Daguo), and the meanings of “the small departs and the great comes” and “the great departs and the small comes,” each indicate the direction of events. Sometimes yin is dominant and exercises power; sometimes yang is dominant and exercises power. The text always attends carefully to disparagement and commendation, so that all under Heaven and later generations may clearly understand that the growth of the noble man's way is cause for celebration, and the decline of the petty man's way is good fortune. Students of the Changes should likewise emulate the study that wore through the leather bindings three times; only then can they understand the sage's guiding intentions.

Book of Documents

“The emperor's radiance shone upon all beneath Heaven, reaching the common people at the farthest shores of the seas.”

Li Wenjie

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭林　批〔形容虞廷大臣告君之意溢於言表殆究心於經學者〕
同考試官學正章　批〔經取合傳場中作者詞浮而與傳意矛盾惟此作得之是宜錄出〕
考試官教諭黃　批〔善模寫光德氣象〕
考試官學正韓　批〔明快〕
期聖德所著之極盡聖世所統之地有虞大臣
然也夫莫遠於聖世之地尤莫著於聖人之德
使聖君之德之著而極於遠則天下豈有不化
===
之人哉昔禹夾畫然舜用威之言而期之意謂
庶頑讒說加之以威不若明之以德誠使帝之
德允迪矣而光輝炫燿之愈隆形乎此則著乎
彼昭明有融何間耶使帝之德誕敷矣而光彩
燦爛之益盛發乎邇則見乎遠旁燭無疆何遺
耶罔愆之或寬或簡王顯於臨御之餘如日之
中而無不照重華之或哲或恭大彰於都俞之
頃如月之望而無不臨九州固在薰蒸之間而
海隅蒼生之境爲何境德之光輝所至山川不
punctuated:
同考試官教諭林批〔形容虞廷大臣告君之意，溢於言表，殆究心於經學者。〕
同考試官學正章批〔經取合傳，場中作者詞浮而與傳意矛盾，惟此作得之，是宜錄出。〕
考試官教諭黃批〔善模寫光德氣象。〕
考試官學正韓批〔明快。〕
期聖德所著之極，盡聖世所統之地，有虞大臣然也。夫莫遠於聖世之地，尤莫著於聖人之德。使聖君之德之著而極於遠，則天下豈有不化之人哉？昔禹夾畫然舜用威之言而期之，意謂庶頑讒說，加之以威，不若明之以德。誠使帝之德允迪矣，而光輝炫燿之愈隆，形乎此則著乎彼，昭明有融，何間耶？使帝之德誕敷矣，而光彩燦爛之益盛，發乎邇則見乎遠，旁燭無疆，何遺耶？罔愆之或寬或簡，王顯於臨御之餘，如日之中而無不照；重華之或哲或恭，大彰於都俞之頃，如月之望而無不臨。九州固在薰蒸之間，而海隅蒼生之境爲何境？德之光輝所至，山川不
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Lin, a county Confucian School Instructor, comments: 〔The portrayal of the intent with which the great ministers at the court of Yu addressed their ruler conveys more than the words themselves express. The author must have devoted himself to the study of the Classics.〕
Associate Examiner Zhang, a subprefectural Confucian School Instructor, comments: 〔The interpretation of the Classic accords with the commentary. Other writers in the examination hall employ superficial language that contradicts the commentary’s meaning. This essay alone gets it right and therefore deserves inclusion.〕
Examiner Huang, a county Confucian School Instructor, comments: 〔Skillfully depicts the character of radiant virtue.〕
Examiner Han, a subprefectural Confucian School Instructor, comments: 〔Clear and brisk.〕
To hope that the utmost reach of the sage’s manifest virtue would encompass all the lands governed in his age: such was the aspiration of the great ministers of Yu. Nothing extends farther than the lands of a sage’s age, and nothing is more manifest than a sage’s virtue. If the manifestation of a sage ruler’s virtue reaches even the most distant places, could anyone under Heaven remain untransformed? Formerly, Yu responded [?] to Shun’s words about employing punitive authority and expressed this hope for him. His meaning was that, with the obstinate and those who utter slander, imposing authority upon them is inferior to enlightening them through virtue. If the emperor truly puts his virtue into practice, and its dazzling radiance grows ever greater, what takes form here becomes manifest there. Its brilliant light spreads: what could interrupt it? If the emperor spreads his virtue far and wide, and its brilliant splendor grows ever stronger, what issues forth nearby becomes visible far away. It shines in every direction without limit: what could it leave out? His faultless qualities, whether magnanimity or simplicity, become royally manifest [?] as he presides over government, like the sun at noon, leaving nothing unilluminated. The qualities of Chonghua [Shun], whether wisdom or reverence, become greatly manifest amid the court’s exchanges of assent, like the full moon, overlooking nothing. The Nine Provinces certainly lie within this permeating influence; but what sort of realm is that of the common people in the remotest coastal reaches? Wherever the radiance of virtue reaches, mountains and rivers cannot…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
能以限隔五服囿在陶鎔之内而海隅蒼生之
鄉為何鄉德之光彩所及封疆不能以留礙其
地則沙漠不毛望之一蒼莽無涯也沛然聲教
之四訖孰不鼓舞於並生之仁其地則人迹不
到視之一蒼渺無際也浩然文命之四敷孰不
沐浴於無為之化夫以君德昭著而遍及天下
則萬邦黎獻共臣矣禎譏曾足介吾意哉抑觀
治莫盛於虞德莫加於舜何當時為君者以禎
譏為憂為臣者以明德為望蓋慮其妨治而欲
=
刑之者聖君憂世無窮之心本之君身而欲化
之者聖臣愛君無窮之心舜非茍恃於刑而禹
亦豈不知舜之優於德耶刑之不可已亦德之
所不可廢也君明臣良相得益彰有虞泰和之
治有由然哉
舉能其官惟爾之能
羅幹
同考試官教諭林　批　題本平易作者多不知點綴
上意惟此篇於周官一書隱括殆盡宜録之以式後學
punctuated:
能以限隔。五服囿在陶鎔之内，而海隅蒼生之鄉為何鄉？德之光彩所及，封疆不能以留礙。其地則沙漠不毛，望之一蒼莽無涯也。沛然聲教之四訖，孰不鼓舞於並生之仁？其地則人迹不到，視之一蒼渺無際也。浩然文命之四敷，孰不沐浴於無為之化？夫以君德昭著而遍及天下，則萬邦黎獻共臣矣，禎譏曾足介吾意哉？抑觀治莫盛於虞，德莫加於舜，何當時為君者以禎譏為憂，為臣者以明德為望？蓋慮其妨治而欲刑之者，聖君憂世無窮之心；本之君身而欲化之者，聖臣愛君無窮之心。舜非茍恃於刑，而禹亦豈不知舜之優於德耶？刑之不可已，亦德之所不可廢也。君明臣良，相得益彰，有虞泰和之治有由然哉！

舉能其官，惟爾之能。
羅幹

同考試官教諭林批：題本平易，作者多不知點綴上意。惟此篇於《周官》一書隱括殆盡，宜録之以式後學。
translation_en:
…cannot set limits or create barriers. The five zones of submission all lie within his transforming influence; what, then, of the lands inhabited by the common people at the sea’s edge? Wherever the radiance of his virtue reaches, territorial boundaries cannot obstruct it. Those places are barren deserts, appearing as one boundless, dusky expanse. As his proclamations and instruction flow abundantly to the four extremities, who would not rejoice in the benevolence that nurtures all life together? Those places are beyond the reach of human footsteps, appearing as one hazy, limitless expanse. As his civilizing commands spread widely in all four directions, who would not bathe in the transforming influence of government through nonaction? When the ruler’s virtue shines manifestly throughout the world, the worthy among the people of the myriad states all serve as his subjects. Could such criticism [?] possibly trouble my mind?

Yet consider: no government flourished more than that of Yu, and no virtue surpassed Shun’s. Why, then, did the ruler of that time worry about such criticism [?], while his minister placed his hopes in making virtue manifest? Concern that these people would obstruct good government, and the wish to punish them, expressed the sage ruler’s unending concern for the world. Looking to the ruler’s own person as the foundation, and wishing to transform these people, expressed the sage minister’s unending devotion to his ruler. Shun did not merely rely on punishment; nor could Yu have been unaware of Shun’s surpassing virtue. That punishment cannot be dispensed with is itself something that virtue cannot disregard. An enlightened ruler and a worthy minister complement one another, each enhancing the other’s excellence. The reign of great harmony under Yu surely had its grounds!

“To recommend men capable of fulfilling their offices: this is your own capability.”
Luo Gan

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: The topic is straightforward, yet most writers do not know how to develop the underlying intent. This essay alone incorporates almost the whole of Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) in its treatment. It should be recorded as a model for later students.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正章　批〔詞簡理備說出成王戒卿士薦賢之意閎之令人珎重宜居選列〕
考試官教諭黄　批〔是如此作〕
考試官學正韓　批〔意得〕
賢王言膺薦者之倘其職即主薦者之盡其職
盖薦賢所以報主而因賢可以知人賢王戒卿
士之薦舉而示以責有所歸其意嚴矣且成王
申戒卿士之言及此盖謂人君以用賢為心大
臣以薦賢為職汝念萬幾之分理在庶官凡有
屈於下僚而隱於草澤者盡在所舉不以功過
而或殊爾思萬務之分任在衆職凡有歌於碩
人而處於衡門者悉在所薦不以親讐而或避
宜公而資之爕理宜孤而貸之寅亮則四時順
===
序而兩儀奠位矣寧至於有負秉之譏宜卿而
資之倡率宜牧而資之阜成則百工惟煕而兆
民得所矣寧至於有具官之誚夫推賢而果得
其賢則賢寧不萃於汝之身乎有容之心休休
而天下之德皆其德矣讓能而果得其能則能
punctuated:
同考試官學正章批〔詞簡理備，說出成王戒卿士薦賢之意，閎之令人珎重，宜居選列。〕
考試官教諭黄批〔是如此作。〕
考試官學正韓批〔意得。〕
賢王言膺薦者之倘其職，即主薦者之盡其職。盖薦賢所以報主，而因賢可以知人。賢王戒卿士之薦舉，而示以責有所歸，其意嚴矣。且成王申戒卿士之言及此，盖謂人君以用賢為心，大臣以薦賢為職。汝念萬幾之分理在庶官，凡有屈於下僚而隱於草澤者，盡在所舉，不以功過而或殊。爾思萬務之分任在衆職，凡有歌於碩人而處於衡門者，悉在所薦，不以親讐而或避。宜公而資之爕理，宜孤而貸之寅亮，則四時順序而兩儀奠位矣，寧至於有負秉之譏？宜卿而資之倡率，宜牧而資之阜成，則百工惟煕而兆民得所矣，寧至於有具官之誚？夫推賢而果得其賢，則賢寧不萃於汝之身乎？有容之心休休，而天下之德皆其德矣。讓能而果得其能，則能
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zhang, Director of Studies, comments: 〔The language is concise and the reasoning complete. It brings out King Cheng’s intention in admonishing his ministers to recommend worthy men. Its amplification [?] makes one prize it; it deserves a place among the selected essays.〕
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔This is how it should be written.〕
Examiner Han, Director of Studies, comments: 〔The meaning is grasped.〕
The worthy king says that when a recommended man proves suited to his office [?], the person responsible for recommending him has thereby fulfilled his own duty. For recommending worthy men is how one repays one’s ruler, and through those worthy men one can discern the character of their recommenders. The worthy king admonishes his ministers about their recommendations and makes clear where responsibility rests: his intention is stern indeed. King Cheng’s reiterated admonition to his ministers reaches this point because the ruler makes employing worthy men his concern, while great ministers make recommending worthy men their duty.
Consider that the myriad affairs of government are apportioned among the various officials. All those confined to subordinate posts or hidden away in the countryside should be included among your nominees, without distinction on account of their merits or faults. Reflect that responsibility for the myriad tasks is divided among the many offices. All those celebrated as eminent men in song and dwelling behind humble crossbar gates should be included among your recommendations, without avoiding anyone because he is a relative or an enemy.
If a man is suited to be one of the Three Dukes, rely on him to harmonize yin and yang; if suited to be one of the Three Solitary Dignitaries, entrust him [?] with reverently assisting that work. Then the four seasons will follow their proper sequence, and Heaven and Earth will be firmly established in their places. How could there then be occasion for the reproach of ‘bearing the sheaf’ [?]? If a man is suited to be a minister, rely on him to lead by example; if suited to be a regional governor, rely on him to bring prosperity and order. Then the many officials will flourish in their work, and the multitude of the people will find their proper places. How could there then be occasion for the reproach that men merely occupy their offices?
Now, if in advancing worthy men you truly obtain their worthiness, will that worthiness not gather in your own person? With an accommodating heart, generous and broad, you make all the virtue under Heaven your own. If in yielding place to capable men you truly obtain their abilities, then those abilities…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
豈不歸於爾之躬乎無私之心坦坦而天下之
才皆其才矣雖不必汲汲自為公為孤陰陽之所
以燮理者在是天地之所以寅亮者在是以人
事君之道何忝哉雖不必爾自為卿為牧群屬
之所以倡率者在斯兆民之所以阜成者在斯
薦賢報國之責何愧哉吁因其薦舉之人驗其
薦舉之職任是責者其可不知所慎歟大抵天
生賢才以為君也君用賢才以圖治也而大臣
與君同體為國薦賢又其分之宜也然必有好
===
賢樂善之誠而又有體國奉公之志斯可以得
賢才而盡其用不然則所用非所求所求非所
用終歸於利而非義也是則得賢非難得薦賢
之人為難此又人君論相之所當知
詩
陟我高岡無矢我陵我陵我阿無飲我泉
我泉我池
張欽
同考試官教諭徐 批 題旨自高岡一氣說下作
punctuated:
豈不歸於爾之躬乎？無私之心坦坦，而天下之才皆其才矣。雖不必汲汲自為公為孤，陰陽之所以燮理者在是，天地之所以寅亮者在是，以人事君之道何忝哉？雖不必爾自為卿為牧，群屬之所以倡率者在斯，兆民之所以阜成者在斯，薦賢報國之責何愧哉？吁！因其薦舉之人，驗其薦舉之職，任是責者，其可不知所慎歟？大抵天生賢才以為君也，君用賢才以圖治也，而大臣與君同體，為國薦賢，又其分之宜也。然必有好賢樂善之誠，而又有體國奉公之志，斯可以得賢才而盡其用。不然，則所用非所求，所求非所用，終歸於利而非義也。是則得賢非難，得薦賢之人為難。此又人君論相之所當知。

詩
陟我高岡，無矢我陵。我陵我阿，無飲我泉。我泉我池。
張欽

同考試官教諭徐批：題旨自高岡一氣說下，作
translation_en:
…would not ability accrue to your own person? With an open and impartial heart, you make all the talents of the realm your own. Though you need not eagerly seek to serve personally as a Duke or an Orphan, the means of harmonizing yin and yang and reverently assisting Heaven and Earth lie here. How could this disgrace the way of serving the ruler through worthy men? Though you need not personally serve as a minister or a regional governor, the means of leading subordinate officials and bringing prosperity and stability to the people lie here. How could you fall short of your responsibility to recommend the worthy and repay the state? Ah! Judge the performance of those charged with recommending men by the men they recommend: can those entrusted with this responsibility fail to exercise caution? In general, Heaven produces worthy and talented men for the ruler, and the ruler employs them to achieve good government. Great ministers form one body with their ruler; recommending worthy men for the state is also their proper duty. Yet only with a sincere love of worthiness and goodness, together with a resolve to have the state's interests at heart and serve the public good, can they obtain worthy and talented men and make full use of them. Otherwise, those employed will not be those sought, and those sought will not be those employed; ultimately this amounts to pursuing profit rather than righteousness. Thus, obtaining worthy men is not the difficulty; obtaining men who will recommend the worthy is the difficulty. This, too, is something a ruler must understand when assessing candidates for chief councillor.

Book of Odes
“Ascend our high ridge; do not array your forces on our heights. Our heights and our slopes—do not drink from our springs. Our springs and our pools.”
Zhang Qin
