title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
者往往支離纏繞此篇脫落陳習說理造辭縝密
純雅而其氣亦悠然經生文字固當爾邪
同考試官教諭李　批　分明寫出王師所至無敵氣
象凜凜可畏宜錄以為學詩者式
同考試官學正楊　批　陵阿泉池作者多泥朱傳此
作明白通暢正得詩人意思
考試官教諭黃　批　能依朱註發揮可取
考試官學正韓　批　一順說去允當
臨所有之地無敢敵之人王者之師也蓋王者
===
無敵理固然也聖人承天命以伐密則所臨之
地豈有敢與為敵者哉昔文王當遏密之後遂
為侵密之舉斯時也聖武布昭赫赫然而攖之
必摧王靈丕振凜凜然而觸之必靡師旅深入
于密方所陟之岡密人昔恃以為出沒矣今則
山谿不足以為固而危峯四周皆我周之式廓
也車馬長驅于密地所登之岡密人向負以為
掩襲矣今則封疆不足以為界而崇山一帶皆
我周之境土也密地既我有矣密人敢復拒哉
punctuated:
者往往支離纏繞，此篇脫落陳習，說理造辭縝密純雅，而其氣亦悠然。經生文字固當爾邪？

同考試官教諭李批：分明寫出王師所至無敵氣象，凜凜可畏，宜錄以為學詩者式。

同考試官學正楊批：陵阿泉池，作者多泥朱傳，此作明白通暢，正得詩人意思。

考試官教諭黃批：能依朱註發揮，可取。

考試官學正韓批：一順說去，允當。

臨所有之地，無敢敵之人，王者之師也。蓋王者無敵，理固然也。聖人承天命以伐密，則所臨之地，豈有敢與為敵者哉？昔文王當遏密之後，遂為侵密之舉。斯時也，聖武布昭，赫赫然而攖之必摧；王靈丕振，凜凜然而觸之必靡。師旅深入于密方，所陟之岡，密人昔恃以為出沒矣。今則山谿不足以為固，而危峯四周皆我周之式廓也。車馬長驅于密地，所登之岡，密人向負以為掩襲矣。今則封疆不足以為界，而崇山一帶皆我周之境土也。密地既我有矣，密人敢復拒哉？
translation_en:
…writers often become disjointed and entangled. This piece casts off stale conventions; its reasoning and phrasing are meticulous, pure, and elegant, while its spirit is also unhurried. Surely this is how a student of the Classics ought to write?

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: It vividly depicts the awe-inspiring and fearsome might of the royal army, invincible wherever it goes. It should be included as a model for students of the Book of Poetry.

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: In treating the hills, slopes, springs, and pools, writers often cling too rigidly to Zhu Xi’s commentary. This piece is clear and fluent, capturing precisely the poet’s meaning.

Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: It develops the meaning in accordance with Zhu Xi’s annotations and merits acceptance.

Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: The exposition proceeds smoothly throughout and is entirely appropriate.

To advance upon every place and find no one who dares oppose it: such is the army of a true king. That a true king is invincible is indeed the natural order of things. When the sage received Heaven’s mandate to attack Mi, could anyone in the lands he approached dare to oppose him? In former times, after King Wen had checked Mi, he proceeded to invade it. At that time his sagely martial power shone far and wide, so resplendent that whoever challenged it was certain to be crushed; his royal might was greatly roused, so awe-inspiring that whoever encountered it was certain to fall. His troops penetrated deep into the territory of Mi. The ridges they ascended were those upon which the people of Mi had formerly relied for their sorties and retreats. Now, however, mountains and ravines no longer afforded a secure defense, and the land on every side of those lofty peaks became part of our Zhou’s expanded domain. Chariots and horses drove far into the lands of Mi. The ridges they climbed were those upon which the people of Mi had previously relied for surprise attacks. Now, however, territorial boundaries could no longer serve to hold them back, and the entire belt of lofty mountains became the territory of our Zhou. Once the lands of Mi were ours, would its people dare resist again?

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
彼高岡之上有陵阿焉非不可以陳兵也有泉
池焉非不可以飲水也然而天誅所在自有以
寒人之心密人聞其風聲而奔突竄伏之不暇
誰敢矢我陵矢我阿據險阻以抗我之兵邪天
討所臨自有以破人之膽密人覩其氣勢而喙
息逃遁之恐後孰敢飲我泉飲我池據地利以
困我之師邪吁王師隨所向而有無敵之勢如
此此文王膺天之命蓋亦因其可怒而怒之曷
嘗有畔援歆羨於其間哉抑因是而知周家之
===
興不偶然也大王能安民而獲西顧之眷王季
能長君而延上帝之祉至於文王先登于岸既
伐密而作程順帝之則又伐崇而作豐前後相
承一德無間是以天之眷命有隆無替夫豈私
於周也邪噫周人發先王之德如此為孫子者
當知天命所由集王業所由興而承之保之不
可以忽易歟
我龍受之蹻蹻王之造
劉節
punctuated:
彼高岡之上，有陵阿焉，非不可以陳兵也；有泉池焉，非不可以飲水也。然而天誅所在，自有以寒人之心。密人聞其風聲，而奔突竄伏之不暇，誰敢矢我陵、矢我阿，據險阻以抗我之兵邪？天討所臨，自有以破人之膽。密人覩其氣勢，而喙息逃遁之恐後，孰敢飲我泉、飲我池，據地利以困我之師邪？吁！王師隨所向而有無敵之勢如此，此文王膺天之命，蓋亦因其可怒而怒之，曷嘗有畔援歆羨於其間哉？抑因是而知周家之興不偶然也。大王能安民而獲西顧之眷，王季能長君而延上帝之祉。至於文王，先登于岸，既伐密而作程；順帝之則，又伐崇而作豐。前後相承，一德無間，是以天之眷命有隆無替，夫豈私於周也邪？噫！周人發先王之德如此，為孫子者，當知天命所由集、王業所由興，而承之保之，不可以忽易歟？

我龍受之，蹻蹻王之造。

劉節
translation_en:
On those high ridges were hills and slopes where troops could indeed be arrayed, and springs and pools from which water could indeed be drunk. Yet wherever Heaven’s punishment falls, it naturally chills men’s hearts. Hearing word of its approach, the people of Mi scarcely had time to scatter, flee, and hide. Who would dare array troops on our hills and slopes, relying on rugged terrain to resist our soldiers? Wherever Heaven’s punitive expedition arrives, it naturally breaks men’s courage. Seeing its imposing force, the people of Mi fled breathlessly, fearing they would fall behind. Who would dare drink from our springs and pools, relying on advantages of terrain to distress our army?

Ah! Such was the invincible might of the royal army wherever it turned. In receiving Heaven’s mandate, King Wen merely directed his anger against what deserved anger. How could willful pursuit or covetous desire have entered into it? From this we also know that the rise of the house of Zhou was no accident. King Tai secured peace for the people and won Heaven’s favor as it looked westward. Wang Ji excelled among rulers and extended the blessings bestowed by the Lord on High. As for King Wen, he was the first to ascend to the heights: after attacking Mi, he established Cheng; following the Lord’s rule, he also attacked Chong and established Feng. Successive generations carried on the same virtue without interruption. Thus Heaven’s favor and mandate grew ever greater and never declined. Could this have been mere partiality toward Zhou?

Ah! Such was the way the people of Zhou proclaimed the virtue of their former kings. Their descendants should understand how Heaven’s mandate came to rest upon them and how the royal enterprise arose, and should carry it forward and preserve it. Could they treat it carelessly or lightly?

“We receive it with honor—the mighty achievement of the king.”

Liu Jie

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭徐　批〔題本明白士子於龍受王造處多失體貼浮冗倒置殊為可厭詞鋒峻整意趣悠揚出數䏻於枯淡如此篇者指未許多屈也錄之〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔集中士子於龍受處多著力而蹻蹻王造至有以不先時而動不後時而靡相對講又有先講功而後及受者倒置不倫此篇詞整而氣充䏻經之翹楚者〕
同考試官學正揚　批〔二句本一意學者多為所窘而龍受處鮮能言之親切或又前後詞語重複此篇理明詞正發揮殆盡宜冠本房〕
===

考試官學正韓　批〔得頌武王旨〕
後王所寵承者前王之大功也盖王者之功前
王不世之功也後王寵承於已安敢忘所自哉
此詩頌武王而作意謂非祖宗有所創於前則
子孫何所受於後使有家有國功止乎家國耳
受之不足以為龍為公為侯功止乎公侯耳受
punctuated:
同考試官教諭徐批〔題本明白，士子於龍受王造處多失體貼，浮冗倒置，殊為可厭。詞鋒峻整，意趣悠揚，出數䏻於枯淡如此篇者，指未許多屈也。錄之。〕
同考試官教諭李批〔集中士子於龍受處多著力，而蹻蹻王造，至有以不先時而動、不後時而靡相對講，又有先講功而後及受者，倒置不倫。此篇詞整而氣充，䏻經之翹楚者。〕

translation_en:
Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: 〔The topic itself is clear. In treating “gloriously receiving” and “the king’s accomplishment,” candidates often fail to grasp the precise meaning; their writing is diffuse and repetitious, with the order of ideas reversed—truly tiresome. This essay’s language is incisive and well ordered, and its meaning unfolds with lingering resonance. Essays like this, which bring forth several strengths from a dry and plain subject [?], scarcely require bending many fingers to count [?]. Record it.〕
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔Among the collected essays, candidates mostly concentrate their efforts on “gloriously receiving.” As for “mighty indeed, the king’s accomplishment,” some go so far as to explain it through paired statements about not acting before the proper time and not falling away after it [?]. Others discuss the achievement first and only afterward its reception, reversing the order without coherence. This essay’s language is orderly and its vital force abundant: an outstanding work in the classic [?].〕
Associate Examiner Yang 揚, Instructor, comments: 〔The two lines fundamentally express a single idea, yet candidates are often stymied by them. Few explain “gloriously receiving” with precision; others repeat their wording before and after. This essay’s reasoning is clear and its language correct; its exposition is nearly exhaustive. It deserves first place in this examining room.〕
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔Few essays explain “gloriously receiving” and “the king’s accomplishment” as precisely, concisely, and aptly as this one.〕
Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: 〔It grasps the intent of the hymn praising King Wu.〕
What the succeeding king inherits as a glorious favor is the preceding king’s great achievement. For this kingly achievement is the preceding king’s achievement unparalleled in his age. Having himself inherited it as a glorious favor, how could the succeeding king dare forget its source? This poem was composed in praise of King Wu. Its meaning is that, had the ancestors established nothing before them, what could their descendants receive afterward? If one possessed a household or a domain, one’s achievement would extend only to that household or domain; receiving it would not suffice to be called glorious. If one became a duke or a marquis, one’s achievement would extend only to that dukedom or marquisate; receiving …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之不足以爲寵今我子孫而膺曆數之傳者踐
祚之後經營不必從事也安居九重實有寵承
於前世繼體之餘締造不必勞心也垂拱五位
實有寵受於先王誠以我先王武王也際純熙
之時興於鑠之師戎衣一着乾坤旋轉於會旦
惟揚之武于湯有光也黃鉞一揮天地掀揭於
崇朝丕承之烈於文無愧也岐豐之地闢爲鎬
京之區獬㬐之臣入爲祼將之士于以來謳歌
而歸訟獄三分未一者以之而一非家非國蹻
===
蹻然王者之造而氣勢非前日之可方也我之
寵承不在兹乎于以朝諸侯而賓四夷九年未
集者以之而集非公非侯蹻蹻然王者之功而
規模非昔日之可比也我之寵受不在是乎嗚
武王以無競之功而垂裕後之休宜詩人於告
神之際必以是而頌之也歟抑考行師之道以
時爲貴禹有三苗之征湯有南巢之放文有密
崇之伐一皆應天順人出於不得已而後舉耳
然則武王牧野之師酌時而動亦惟上師禹湯
punctuated:
之不足以爲寵。今我子孫而膺曆數之傳者，踐祚之後，經營不必從事也，安居九重，實有寵承於前世；繼體之餘，締造不必勞心也，垂拱五位，實有寵受於先王。誠以我先王武王也，際純熙之時，興於鑠之師，戎衣一着，乾坤旋轉於會旦，惟揚之武，于湯有光也；黃鉞一揮，天地掀揭於崇朝，丕承之烈，於文無愧也。岐豐之地，闢爲鎬京之區；獬㬐之臣，入爲祼將之士。于以來謳歌而歸訟獄，三分未一者，以之而一，非家非國，蹻蹻然王者之造，而氣勢非前日之可方也。我之寵承，不在兹乎？于以朝諸侯而賓四夷，九年未集者，以之而集，非公非侯，蹻蹻然王者之功，而規模非昔日之可比也。我之寵受，不在是乎？嗚！武王以無競之功而垂裕後之休，宜詩人於告神之際，必以是而頌之也歟！

抑考行師之道，以時爲貴。禹有三苗之征，湯有南巢之放，文有密崇之伐，一皆應天順人，出於不得已而後舉耳。然則武王牧野之師，酌時而動，亦惟上師禹湯
translation_en:
…to receive it would not suffice to count as an honor. Now we descendants, who have received the transmitted succession ordained by Heaven, need not undertake the work of establishing dominion after ascending the throne. Dwelling peacefully within the ninefold palace, we have indeed inherited an honored legacy from earlier generations. Having succeeded to the throne, we need not trouble our minds with founding the realm. With robes hanging and hands folded, we occupy the sovereign’s fifth position and have indeed received an honored legacy from the former king. This is truly because our former king was King Wu. At a time of pure brilliance, he raised a glorious army. Once he donned his battle robes, Heaven and Earth were transformed at daybreak: his martial might, grandly displayed, added luster to Tang. With one sweep of his yellow battle-axe, Heaven and Earth were overturned within a morning: his achievement in magnificently carrying on the legacy did no dishonor to King Wen. The lands of Qi and Feng were expanded into the domain of Haojing; the ministers described as ‘獬㬐’ [?] entered service as officers presenting sacrificial libations. Thus he attracted those who sang his praises and those who brought their lawsuits for judgment. What had been divided into three and not yet united was thereby made one. This was the mighty creation of a king, extending beyond a household or a regional state, and its force and grandeur could not be compared with those of former days. Does not our honored inheritance lie in this? Thus he received the regional lords at court and welcomed the peoples of the four quarters as guests. What had not been accomplished in nine years was thereby accomplished. This was the mighty achievement of a king, surpassing that of a duke or marquis, and its scope could not be compared with that of earlier times. Does not the honored legacy we have received lie in this? Ah! Through his unrivaled achievement, King Wu bequeathed the blessing of abundant provision for his descendants. Surely it was fitting that the poet, when making his announcement to the spirits, should praise him for this!

Yet, on examining the principles of deploying an army, we find that proper timing is paramount. Yu campaigned against the Sanmiao; Tang banished his opponent to Nanchao; King Wen attacked Mi and Chong. All responded to Heaven and accorded with the people, undertaking military action only when compelled by necessity. Thus King Wu’s army at Muye moved after weighing the moment, likewise simply taking as its distant models Yu and Tang…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
近師文王而已夫豈有窮黷哉噫載用有嗣實
惟爾公允師子孫登歌以是而播之樂章其亦
知所以格神之道者歟
春秋

===
于鐵〔哀公二年〕

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之晉爲盟主而列國皆與之戰夷考其事則霸
業之盛衰豈不於斯而可見乎何則春秋中葉
唐叔之晉世主夏盟其與秦齊楚戰也果何而
見其霸業猶振耶于時秦伯伐晉趙盾禦之而
戰于河曲齊人笑客郤克憤之而交戰于鞌楚
共救鄭厲公則與楚師戰于鄢陵焉之三役也
自常情觀之孰不以爲堂堂晉霸夷夏具瞻秦
齊何國也乃敢擅興師旅與晉爲敵楚共何人
也亦敢時出干紀與晉抗衡於理若弗順焉殊
===
不知秦以西陲雄長齊以東州大邦楚以南蠻
强國雖云抗霸猶敵體也地醜德齊力能相尚
亦人情之常耳噫春秋諸侯舍齊秦楚外胡敢
與晉抗哉胡敢與晉敵哉聖人於此不嫌於與
晉戰者以見晉國之盛威足以慴服諸侯義足
以主盟中夏况能挫秦敗齊射楚三戰交綏群
雄退聽其霸業之猶振也明矣若夫春秋叔世
傳至晉定猶掌霸權其與鄭罕達戰也又何而
見其霸業之不振耶于時晉政荐衰趙鞅當國
punctuated: 之晉爲盟主，而列國皆與之戰。夷考其事，則霸業之盛衰，豈不於斯而可見乎？何則？春秋中葉，唐叔之晉世主夏盟，其與秦齊楚戰也，果何而見其霸業猶振耶？于時秦伯伐晉，趙盾禦之，而戰于河曲；齊人笑客，郤克憤之，而交戰于鞌；楚共救鄭，厲公則與楚師戰于鄢陵焉。之三役也，自常情觀之，孰不以爲堂堂晉霸，夷夏具瞻，秦齊何國也，乃敢擅興師旅，與晉爲敵？楚共何人也，亦敢時出干紀，與晉抗衡？於理若弗順焉。殊不知秦以西陲雄長，齊以東州大邦，楚以南蠻强國，雖云抗霸，猶敵體也。地醜德齊，力能相尚，亦人情之常耳。噫！春秋諸侯，舍齊秦楚外，胡敢與晉抗哉？胡敢與晉敵哉？聖人於此不嫌於與晉戰者，以見晉國之盛，威足以慴服諸侯，義足以主盟中夏。况能挫秦敗齊射楚，三戰交綏，群雄退聽，其霸業之猶振也明矣。若夫春秋叔世，傳至晉定，猶掌霸權，其與鄭罕達戰也，又何而見其霸業之不振耶？于時晉政荐衰，趙鞅當國，
translation_en:
…Jin served as leader of the covenant, yet the other states all fought against it. Examining these events impartially, can we not discern in them the flourishing and decline of its hegemony? Why is this so? In the middle of the Spring and Autumn period, Jin, the state of Tang Shu, presided over the covenants of the Xia states for successive generations. How, precisely, do its wars with Qin, Qi, and Chu show that its hegemony remained vigorous? At that time, the Earl of Qin attacked Jin; Zhao Dun resisted him, and they fought at Hequ. The people of Qi mocked their visiting guest; Xi Ke was angered, and battle was joined at An. King Gong of Chu came to Zheng’s aid; Duke Li then fought the Chu army at Yanling. Looking at these three campaigns from an ordinary standpoint, who would not think: “Majestic Jin, the hegemon, was looked up to by both the Yi and the Xia. What sort of states were Qin and Qi, that they dared raise armies on their own authority and make themselves Jin’s enemies? Who was King Gong of Chu, that he too dared venture forth to violate the established order and contend with Jin?” This might seem contrary to proper principles.

Yet such a view entirely overlooks the fact that Qin was the dominant power on the western frontier, Qi a great state in the eastern region, and Chu a powerful state among the southern Man. Though they challenged the hegemon, they were nevertheless its equals in standing. Comparable in territory and equal in virtue, they could rival one another in strength: this, too, was only normal human behavior. Ah! Among the lords of the Spring and Autumn period, apart from Qi, Qin, and Chu, who dared resist Jin? Who dared make an enemy of Jin? Here the Sage takes no exception to those who fought Jin, thereby revealing Jin’s flourishing power: its might sufficed to overawe the other lords into submission, and its righteousness sufficed to preside over the covenants of the central Xia states. Moreover, it could check Qin, defeat Qi, and strike Chu with an arrow. After three encounters in battle, the rival powers withdrew and obeyed. Clearly, its hegemony remained vigorous.

But in the latter days of the Spring and Autumn period, when the succession reached Duke Ding of Jin, Jin still wielded hegemonic authority. How, then, does its battle with Han Da of Zheng show that its hegemony had lost its vigor? At that time, Jin’s government was declining ever further, and Zhao Yang controlled the affairs of state…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
荀范謀逆反易天明自絕于君見逐于國齊人
黨之而輸其粟鄭卿送之而右其奸吉射尤悖
朋惡往迎趙簡子則出師禦鄭而戰于鐵焉之
一役也自庸情論之孰不以為鄭黨叛臣分所
當討趙鞅晉卿也伏弢嘔血鼓音不衰郵良晉
御也兩靷將絕力能止之其功若可錄焉殊不
知鄭國以蕞爾之區罕達以匹夫之勇地不大
於曹滕民不衆於邾莒以晉視之誠縣鄙也縱
與之戰雖勝不武降尊毀列恥不足言亦事勢
===
之變耳噫春秋諸侯鄭尚能相抗其餘皆敢與
晉敵矣皆敢與晉角矣聖人於此特嫌於與晉
戰者以見晉霸之衰權不足以號召諸侯勢不
足以驅役列國況又遇敵震慄而失措群下矜
伐而爭功其霸業之不振也宜哉吁同一晉也
始以交兵大國而見其盛終以交兵小國而見
其衰春秋豈容私於其間哉亦惟跡其勢而察
其幾耳大抵人莫貴於自強莫不貴於自棄自
強於為善則小可大弱可強而大國亦將為吾
punctuated:
荀、范謀逆，反易天明，自絕于君，見逐于國。齊人黨之而輸其粟，鄭卿送之而右其奸，吉射尤悖，朋惡往迎。趙簡子則出師禦鄭，而戰于鐵焉。之一役也，自庸情論之，孰不以為鄭黨叛臣，分所當討？趙鞅，晉卿也，伏弢嘔血，鼓音不衰；郵良，晉御也，兩靷將絕，力能止之。其功若可錄焉。殊不知鄭國以蕞爾之區，罕達以匹夫之勇，地不大於曹、滕，民不衆於邾、莒，以晉視之，誠縣鄙也。縱與之戰，雖勝不武，降尊毀列，恥不足言，亦事勢之變耳。
噫！春秋諸侯，鄭尚能相抗，其餘皆敢與晉敵矣，皆敢與晉角矣。聖人於此特嫌於與晉戰者，以見晉霸之衰，權不足以號召諸侯，勢不足以驅役列國。況又遇敵震慄而失措，群下矜伐而爭功，其霸業之不振也宜哉！吁！同一晉也，始以交兵大國而見其盛，終以交兵小國而見其衰。《春秋》豈容私於其間哉？亦惟跡其勢而察其幾耳。大抵人莫貴於自強，莫不貴於自棄。自強於為善，則小可大，弱可強，而大國亦將為吾
translation_en:
…The Xun and Fan clans plotted rebellion, overturning Heaven’s manifest order. They severed themselves from their lord and were driven from their state. The people of Qi sided with them and supplied them with grain; a minister of Zheng escorted the supplies, abetting their wrongdoing. Jishe was especially rebellious: joining with the wicked, he went to meet them. Zhao Jianzi thereupon dispatched troops to resist Zheng and fought at Tie. In this engagement [?], judging by ordinary sentiments, who would not think that Zheng, having sided with rebellious ministers, deserved to be punished as a matter of duty? Zhao Yang, a minister of Jin, bent over his bow case and vomited blood, yet the sound of his drum did not weaken. You Liang, a charioteer of Jin, was able by sheer strength to halt the horses when both harness straps were about to snap. Their achievements might seem worthy of recording.
Yet this overlooks the fact that Zheng possessed only a tiny territory, and Han Da only the courage of an individual fighter. Its territory was no greater than those of Cao and Teng, its population no larger than those of Zhu and Ju. In Jin’s eyes, it was truly no more than an outlying county. Even if Jin fought it and won, the victory would bring no martial honor. To lower its dignity and debase its standing was a disgrace scarcely worth discussing; this, too, was simply a change in the circumstances of affairs.
Alas! Among the lords of the Spring and Autumn period, if even Zheng could resist Jin, all the others would dare to oppose Jin and contend with it. That the Sage here particularly disapproved of an opponent’s fighting Jin shows the decline of Jin’s hegemony: its authority no longer sufficed to summon the lords, nor its power to command the other states. Moreover, its leader trembled and lost his composure on encountering the enemy, while his subordinates boasted and competed for credit. It was only fitting that its hegemony should fail to recover!
Ah! It was the very same Jin: at first, its warfare against great states revealed its ascendancy; in the end, its warfare against a small state revealed its decline. How could the Spring and Autumn Annals admit partiality in this? It merely traces the course of circumstances and examines the subtle signs of change. In general, nothing is more valuable for a person than striving to strengthen himself, and nothing less valuable than abandoning himself [?; the transcription appears corrupt here]. If one strives to strengthen oneself in doing good, the small can become great and the weak can become strong, and even great states will come to stand behind us…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
後自棄於不善人人得而侮之何強大之足恃
哉然原其失蓋由利勝而義微政褻而拳散故
致諸侯之叛大夫之張外夷之橫一潰而不可
復收矣末流之弊可勝言哉安能起桓文於九
京與之定恢復之計
宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯會晉師于棐林伐鄭〔宣公元年〕
晉人宋人衛人陳人侵鄭〔宣公二年〕
晉欒書帥師伐鄭〔成公九年〕晉侯及
楚子鄭伯戰于鄢陵〔成公十有六年〕公會尹
子單子晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯曹伯邾人伐
鄭公會單子晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊人邾
人伐鄭〔俱成公十有七年〕戍鄭虎牢楚公子
貞帥師救鄭〔襄公十年〕
劉藍
同考試官教諭張　批　春秋須識得筆削書法方
領會聖人微意所在諸作體認不真立辭多舛此
篇深究隱顯所以本旨是宜錄出
考試官教諭黃　批　得聖經書法隱顯襃貶之旨
punctuated:
後。自棄於不善，人人得而侮之，何強大之足恃哉？然原其失，蓋由利勝而義微，政褻而拳散，故致諸侯之叛、大夫之張、外夷之橫，一潰而不可復收矣。末流之弊，可勝言哉？安能起桓文於九京，與之定恢復之計？
宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯會晉師于棐林，伐鄭。〔宣公元年〕晉人、宋人、衛人、陳人侵鄭。〔宣公二年〕晉欒書帥師伐鄭。〔成公九年〕晉侯及楚子、鄭伯戰于鄢陵。〔成公十有六年〕公會尹子、單子、晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、邾人伐鄭。公會單子、晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊人、邾人伐鄭。〔俱成公十有七年〕戍鄭虎牢。楚公子貞帥師救鄭。〔襄公十年〕
劉藍。
同考試官教諭張批：春秋須識得筆削書法，方領會聖人微意所在。諸作體認不真，立辭多舛。此篇深究隱顯所以，本旨是宜錄出。
考試官教諭黃批：得聖經書法隱顯襃貶之旨。
translation_en:
…behind us. If we abandon ourselves to wrongdoing, anyone can humiliate us: what reliance can be placed on strength and greatness? Yet, tracing the source of these failures, they arose because profit prevailed and righteousness waned, government was debased, and authority dissipated [?]. Thus the feudal lords rebelled, the great officers grew overbearing, and the foreign peoples acted with impunity. Once everything collapsed, it could never be restored. Could one fully recount the evils of this final decline? How could we raise Dukes Huan and Wen from their graves and devise with them a plan for restoration?
The Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao joined the army of Jin at Feilin and attacked Zheng. 〔First year of Duke Xuan.〕 Men of Jin, Song, Wei, and Chen invaded Zheng. 〔Second year of Duke Xuan.〕 Luan Shu of Jin led an army to attack Zheng. 〔Ninth year of Duke Cheng.〕 The Marquis of Jin fought the Viscount of Chu and the Earl of Zheng at Yanling. 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Cheng.〕 The Duke joined Viscount Yin, Viscount Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, and men of Zhu to attack Zheng. The Duke joined Viscount Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, and men of Qi and Zhu to attack Zheng. 〔Both in the seventeenth year of Duke Cheng.〕 A garrison was stationed at Hulao in Zheng. Prince Zhen of Chu led an army to relieve Zheng. 〔Tenth year of Duke Xiang.〕
Liu Lan.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: In studying the Spring and Autumn Annals, one must understand its conventions of inclusion and deletion before one can grasp the Sage’s subtle intentions. The various essays lack a true understanding, and their formulations contain many errors. This essay probes deeply into the reasons for concealment and disclosure; for its grasp of the underlying meaning, it deserves to be selected for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: This essay grasps the purport of the sacred classic’s conventions of concealment and disclosure, praise and blame.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正韓　批〔按是非公予奪此作得之〕
霸主討貳近乎正春秋屢書外夷恤患之名霸
主逼貳近乎專春秋特存外夷恤患之義此鄭
為夷夏必爭之國故晉之屢伐楚之屢救各有
得失存焉春秋得不按是非而致隱顯之法哉
慨自桓文邁往霸統陵夷荊楚每垂涎於北圖
鄭人常掉臂於南向主霸圖者豈可置之而不
究厥心耶晉靈首會衆師棐林以聲鄭即楚之
罪而蔿賈之救隨至繼偕四國徃侵以詰鄭伐
===
宋之由而鬬椒之救適臨景公命將欒書以致
伐將討鄭之貳於楚也子重迺訂侵陳之策以
撓其謀厲公合兵鄢陵以謀戰將責鄭之叛夫
晉也楚子躬率救鄭之師以泄其憤夏之伐也
上屢尹單以臨戎而子重又興首止之次冬之
伐也再扳王臣以從事而子申復為汝上之援
曲沃之旅奔走於溱洧者無寧歲曾何撓其從
楚之輮江漢之衆應援於潁邦者無窮期反有
奪其慕華之幟春秋累書晉侵伐而不書楚救
punctuated:
考試官學正韓，批〔按是非，公予奪，此作得之。〕

霸主討貳近乎正，《春秋》屢書外夷恤患之名；霸主逼貳近乎專，《春秋》特存外夷恤患之義。此鄭為夷夏必爭之國，故晉之屢伐、楚之屢救，各有得失存焉。《春秋》得不按是非而致隱顯之法哉？

慨自桓文邁往，霸統陵夷，荊楚每垂涎於北圖，鄭人常掉臂於南向，主霸圖者豈可置之而不究厥心耶？晉靈首會衆師棐林，以聲鄭即楚之罪，而蔿賈之救隨至；繼偕四國徃侵，以詰鄭伐宋之由，而鬬椒之救適臨。景公命將欒書以致伐，將討鄭之貳於楚也，子重迺訂侵陳之策以撓其謀；厲公合兵鄢陵以謀戰，將責鄭之叛夫晉也，楚子躬率救鄭之師以泄其憤。夏之伐也，上屢尹單以臨戎，而子重又興首止之次；冬之伐也，再扳王臣以從事，而子申復為汝上之援。曲沃之旅奔走於溱洧者無寧歲，曾何撓其從楚之輮？江漢之衆應援於潁邦者無窮期，反有奪其慕華之幟。《春秋》累書晉侵伐而不書楚救
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Han, School Instructor: 〔In judging right and wrong and impartially granting or withholding approval, this composition has grasped the point.〕

When the hegemon punishes divided allegiance, his action approaches rectitude, yet the Spring and Autumn Annals repeatedly records the reputation that foreign peoples gain for relieving distress. When the hegemon coerces those of divided allegiance, his action approaches arbitrary domination, and the Annals expressly preserves the righteousness of foreign peoples’ relief of distress. Zheng was a state over which the foreign peoples and the Xia necessarily contended. Thus Jin’s repeated attacks and Chu’s repeated rescues each had their merits and faults. Could the Annals fail to weigh right and wrong and apply its method of concealment and disclosure?

Alas, since Dukes Huan and Wen passed away, the succession of hegemons had declined. Jing-Chu constantly coveted expansion northward, while the people of Zheng repeatedly turned southward with a defiant swing of their arms. Could those directing the hegemon’s enterprise simply leave them alone without examining their intentions? Duke Ling of Jin first assembled the allied armies at Feilin to proclaim Zheng’s guilt in attaching itself to Chu, but Wei Jia’s relieving force promptly arrived. He subsequently invaded together with four states to call Zheng to account for its attack on Song, but Dou Jiao’s relieving force arrived just then. Duke Jing ordered his general Luan Shu to launch an attack, intending to punish Zheng for its divided allegiance in favor of Chu; Zichong thereupon devised a plan to invade Chen and frustrate his designs. Duke Li massed troops at Yanling to seek battle, intending to call Zheng to account for betraying Jin; the ruler of Chu personally led an army to rescue Zheng and vent his anger. In the summer campaign, Yin and Shan were repeatedly brought forward to oversee the fighting [?], while Zichong once again established an encampment at Shouzhi. In the winter campaign, royal ministers were again drawn into the undertaking, while Zishen once more provided support on the Ru River. The troops of Quwo rushed about between the Zhen and Wei rivers without a single peaceful year; yet how did they ever weaken Zheng’s pliant submission to Chu [?]? The armies of the Jiang and Han rivers endlessly came to the aid of the state on the Ying River, instead threatening to wrest away its banner of admiration for Hua civilization [?]. The Annals repeatedly records Jin’s invasions and attacks but does not record Chu’s rescues…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
者良以晉尸霸權勤兵討貳所以立內夏外夷
之防楚本崛強睥睨諸姬不過為猾夏陸梁之
計苟存而弗剪則疑於予楚而罪晉矣故屢沒
其救以鄭無可救之善楚不得有能救之名也
迨夫悼公復霸鄭弗改圖載書雖聽命於五會
之詞玉帛猶懷疑於二境之待主夏盟者寧可
忽之而不慎厥念耶爰自虛朾嗣位以來無日
不以謀鄭為事軍旅數興備申討貳之約法壇
坫屢設蔑聞服貳之成功使晉果能義以感鄭
===
則人無不懷夫何因其國難之多變遂即其巖
險以駐師倡集牛首之兵計為虎牢之戍謀非
不深也豈王者服遠之謨力非不足也豈大國
睦隣之道專其分地而紊亂周制有來思城梧
及制而勞費財力有不恤既不能斷荊蠻之路
以蔽鄭又不能保小國之危以息爭反啓楚共
之謀得伸急病之義楚貞之救竊行拯溺之仁
春秋於戍鄭虎牢下而繼書公子貞之救者良
以悼欲復文襄之業扼險凌弱而道不足多楚
punctuated:
者，良以晉尸霸權，勤兵討貳，所以立內夏外夷之防。楚本崛強，睥睨諸姬，不過為猾夏陸梁之計。苟存而弗剪，則疑於予楚而罪晉矣。故屢沒其救，以鄭無可救之善，楚不得有能救之名也。
迨夫悼公復霸，鄭弗改圖，載書雖聽命於五會之詞，玉帛猶懷疑於二境之待。主夏盟者，寧可忽之而不慎厥念耶？爰自虛朾嗣位以來，無日不以謀鄭為事。軍旅數興，備申討貳之約法；壇坫屢設，蔑聞服貳之成功。使晉果能義以感鄭，則人無不懷。夫何因其國難之多變，遂即其巖險以駐師，倡集牛首之兵，計為虎牢之戍？謀非不深也，豈王者服遠之謨？力非不足也，豈大國睦隣之道？專其分地而紊亂周制，有來思；城梧及制而勞費財力，有不恤。既不能斷荊蠻之路以蔽鄭，又不能保小國之危以息爭，反啓楚共之謀，得伸急病之義；楚貞之救，竊行拯溺之仁。春秋於戍鄭虎牢下，而繼書公子貞之救者，良以悼欲復文襄之業，扼險凌弱，而道不足多，楚
translation_en:
…the reason is precisely that Jin held hegemonic authority and repeatedly mobilized troops to punish divided allegiance, thereby establishing the distinction that placed the Xia states within and the foreign peoples outside. Chu, inherently recalcitrant, looked disdainfully upon the states ruled by the Ji lineage; its designs amounted merely to disturbing the Xia states and running rampant. Had these accounts been retained without deletion, it might have seemed that Chu was being commended and Jin condemned. Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals repeatedly suppresses mention of Chu’s relief efforts: Zheng possessed no goodness that warranted rescue, and Chu could not be allowed the reputation of being its rescuer.
When Duke Dao restored Jin’s hegemony, Zheng did not change its plans. Although it accepted commands in the wording of the covenant documents at five meetings, its offerings of jade and silk still betrayed uncertainty as it dealt with the two neighboring powers. Could the leader of the Xia alliance neglect this and fail to give it careful thought? From his accession at Xuting onward, not a day passed without his making plans concerning Zheng. Armies were repeatedly raised, and the covenant provisions for punishing divided allegiance were fully reiterated; altars and ceremonial stands were repeatedly set up, yet no successful subjugation of the wavering state was heard of. Had Jin truly been able to move Zheng through righteousness, everyone would have turned to it with affection. Why, then, did it take advantage of the many upheavals within Zheng to station troops at its rugged strongholds, call together the forces at Niushou, and plan a garrison at Hulao? Its strategy was certainly profound, but was this a true king’s strategy for winning the submission of distant peoples? Its strength was certainly sufficient, but was this the way a great state should maintain friendly relations with its neighbors? It appropriated Zheng’s allotted territory and disrupted the institutions of Zhou, with the accompanying phrase obscure [?]; it fortified Wu and Zhi, heedlessly exhausting wealth and manpower. It could neither block the routes of the southern peoples of Jing to shield Zheng nor secure the endangered small state and end the conflict. Instead, it opened the way for King Gong of Chu’s designs, allowing him to display the righteousness of hastening to another’s distress; through his relief expedition, Zhen of Chu claimed for himself the benevolence of rescuing the drowning. The reason the Spring and Autumn Annals follows its entry on garrisoning Hulao in Zheng with an account of Prince Zhen’s relief expedition is precisely that Duke Dao sought to restore the achievements of Dukes Wen and Xiang by seizing strategic positions and bullying the weak, while his conduct deserved little praise; Chu …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
雖斂爲闕之亢假義安夏而名實可取茍削而
不書則疑於予晉而罪楚矣故特存其救許楚
有救患之義而著諸侯不仁之甚也吁伐者善
則救者非戍者非則救者善春秋彰善癉惡瑕
瑜莫掩明切有如是夫抑論之晉主諸夏之盟
鄭爲要領之國凡有兵爭皆關於鄭靈景厲雖
致勤于貳爲楚所撓暫服卒離無足道矣悼公
此舉尚力而不尚德故楚得以間之厥後盟于
戲示不戰以服貳會蕭魚推至誠以感貳故鄭
===
亦以誠服不背晉者二十四年爲春秋一經之
盛舉誠非他霸所能匹也故曰悼公有君子之
資信夫
禮記
禮俗刑然後樂
徐盈
同考試官訓導孟　批〔樂本於禮俗刑禮俗刑又本於人君親親中來此作得之且文足以發其意必深於禮者也〕
punctuated:
雖斂爲闕之亢，假義安夏，而名實可取。茍削而不書，則疑於予晉而罪楚矣。故特存其救，許楚有救患之義，而著諸侯不仁之甚也。吁！伐者善則救者非，戍者非則救者善。《春秋》彰善癉惡，瑕瑜莫掩，明切有如是夫！抑論之，晉主諸夏之盟，鄭爲要領之國，凡有兵爭，皆關於鄭。靈、景、厲雖致勤于貳，爲楚所撓，暫服卒離，無足道矣。悼公此舉，尚力而不尚德，故楚得以間之。厥後盟于戲，示不戰以服貳；會蕭魚，推至誠以感貳。故鄭亦以誠服，不背晉者二十四年，爲《春秋》一經之盛舉，誠非他霸所能匹也。故曰：「悼公有君子之資。」信夫！

禮記
禮俗刑然後樂
徐盈

同考試官訓導孟，批〔樂本於禮俗刑，禮俗刑又本於人君親親中來。此作得之，且文足以發其意，必深於禮者也。〕
translation_en:
…although Chu restrained its arrogance [?], and invoked righteousness to bring peace to the Xia states, both its professed purpose and its actual deeds were commendable. If its intervention were deleted and left unrecorded, this might appear to approve of Jin and condemn Chu. Thus the record expressly preserves its rescue, acknowledging Chu’s righteousness in relieving distress and exposing the extreme inhumanity of the feudal lords. Ah! When the attacker is right, the rescuer is wrong; when the power establishing a garrison is wrong, the rescuer is right. The Spring and Autumn Annals displays goodness and condemns evil, concealing neither flaws nor merits: how clear and incisive it is!

To consider the matter further: Jin presided over the alliance of the Xia states, and Zheng occupied a pivotal position. Every armed conflict involved Zheng. Although Dukes Ling, Jing, and Li exerted themselves against its wavering allegiance, Chu thwarted them: Zheng submitted briefly but ultimately broke away. There is little worth praising in this. In this undertaking, Duke Dao prized force rather than virtue, and thus Chu was able to intervene. Later, at the covenant at Xi, he demonstrated that he could secure the submission of a wavering state without fighting; at the meeting at Xiaoyu, he extended the utmost sincerity to win it over. Zheng therefore submitted sincerely in return and did not betray Jin for twenty-four years. This was an outstanding achievement in the entire Spring and Autumn Annals, truly beyond the capacity of other hegemons to match. Thus it is said: “Duke Dao possessed the qualities of a gentleman.” How true!

Book of Rites
“Only after ritual and custom have taken form is there joy.”
Xu Ying

Comment by Associate Examiner Meng, Instructor: 〔Joy is rooted in ritual and custom taking form; their taking form, in turn, originates in the ruler’s affection for his kin. This composition grasps that point, and its writing adequately develops the meaning. Its author must have a profound understanding of ritual.〕

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭黃　批　可觀
考試官學正韓　批〔說樂處最是〕
惟大化成於下斯至和充於上盖禮俗大成非
人君親親不能致也下既成乎禮俗如此則上
豈不由之而樂也哉大傅君子知其然謂夫人
道莫先於親親是以人君之親親也尊祖而敬
宗敬宗而收族推而至於庶民安矣百志成矣
自家而國咸知親親之禮雍雍乎上下和同而
乖爭凌犯之不作自國而天下皆知親親之道
===
藹藹乎長幼親睦而強梁鬬辨之不生三綱正
焉六禮脩焉民俗由是而至變也七教明焉六
紀叙焉禮俗由是而大成也遵道而遵路不虞
天性者何有耶會極而歸極不迪率典者何在
耶夫如是則協氣嘉生薰爲大和三光全而寒
暑時五穀熟而民人育吾知人君垂紳於九重
之上恭己於南面之尊宗社安矣三才應矣内
患不必憂也外侮不必慮也歡忻之情自爾而
暢達鐘鼓云乎哉海宇寧矣四靈至矣無弗若
punctuated:
考試官教諭黃，批：可觀。
考試官學正韓，批〔說樂處最是〕
惟大化成於下，斯至和充於上。盖禮俗大成，非人君親親不能致也。下既成乎禮俗如此，則上豈不由之而樂也哉？大傅君子知其然，謂夫人道莫先於親親。是以人君之親親也，尊祖而敬宗，敬宗而收族，推而至於庶民安矣，百志成矣。自家而國，咸知親親之禮，雍雍乎上下和同，而乖爭凌犯之不作；自國而天下，皆知親親之道，藹藹乎長幼親睦，而強梁鬬辨之不生。三綱正焉，六禮脩焉，民俗由是而至變也；七教明焉，六紀叙焉，禮俗由是而大成也。遵道而遵路，不虞天性者何有耶？會極而歸極，不迪率典者何在耶？夫如是，則協氣嘉生，薰爲大和，三光全而寒暑時，五穀熟而民人育。吾知人君垂紳於九重之上，恭己於南面之尊，宗社安矣，三才應矣，内患不必憂也，外侮不必慮也。歡忻之情，自爾而暢達，鐘鼓云乎哉？海宇寧矣，四靈至矣，無弗若
translation_en:
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Worthy of attention.”
Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: 〔The discussion of joy is especially apt.〕
Only when the great transforming influence is fully realized below does perfect harmony fill the realm above. For the full establishment of rites and customs cannot be achieved unless the ruler cherishes his kin. Once rites and customs have thus been established below, how could the ruler above fail to find joy in them? The gentleman who composed the Great Commentary (Da zhuan) [?] understood this, holding that, in the human way, nothing takes precedence over cherishing one’s kin. Thus, in cherishing his kin, the ruler honors his ancestors and respects the lineage head; by respecting the lineage head, he draws the clansmen together. Extended further, this brings peace to the common people and fulfills their many aspirations. From the family to the state, all understand the rites of cherishing kin: those above and below live together in concord, and discord, contention, oppression, and transgression do not arise. From the state to all under Heaven, all understand the way of cherishing kin: elders and juniors live in affectionate harmony, and violence, fighting, and disputation do not arise.
The Three Bonds are set right, and the Six Rites are cultivated; through these, popular customs are transformed to the utmost. The Seven Teachings are made clear, and the Six Relationships are put in order; through these, rites and customs reach full perfection. All follow the Way and its path: who could remain heedless of their Heaven-endowed nature? All gather at and return to the supreme standard: where could there be anyone who does not follow the established norms?
When matters are thus, harmonious vital energies and auspicious living things mingle to produce supreme harmony. The three celestial lights are unimpaired, cold and heat arrive in season, the five grains ripen, and the people flourish. I know that the ruler, his ceremonial sash hanging down within the palace’s ninefold depths, will comport himself reverently in the honored position facing south. The ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain are secure; the Three Powers respond in accord. He need not worry about internal troubles or be anxious about insults from abroad. Feelings of delight naturally find full expression. Can this be merely a matter of bells and drums? The realm is at peace, the Four Numinous Creatures appear, and there are none who fail to conform…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
於政者以貽其憂無弗化於訓者以拂其志悅
懌之意自爾而動盈管絃云乎哉群黎百姓鼓
舞於光天化日之下庶民小子踴躍於春臺玉
燭之中含哺而嬉鼓腹而樂所謂無斁於人者
此也日出而作日入而息所謂在彼無惡者此
也是則至和之充固本於禮俗之成而禮俗之
成實自人君親親中來也任君人之責者可不
加意於此哉嗟夫君道固以親親為本而親親
舍尊祖敬宗收族之外無他為也茍不親親則
===
家不齊安望國與天下而治而平哉觀帝堯之
萬邦協和始於九族之親睦帝舜之四方風動
始於五典之慎徽真萬世君人之龜鑑也故曰
聖人南面而治天下必自人道始良有以歟
流而不息合同而化而樂興焉
同考試官訓導孟　批通篇知樂與之旨者最少
惟此卷認理真切措辭穩貼宜錄之以示後學
符錫
考試官教諭黃　批樂記義似此說理透徹而錄
punctuated:
於政者以貽其憂，無弗化於訓者以拂其志，悅懌之意自爾而動盈，管絃云乎哉？群黎百姓鼓舞於光天化日之下，庶民小子踴躍於春臺玉燭之中，含哺而嬉，鼓腹而樂，所謂無斁於人者，此也；日出而作，日入而息，所謂在彼無惡者，此也。是則至和之充，固本於禮俗之成；而禮俗之成，實自人君親親中來也。任君人之責者，可不加意於此哉？嗟夫！君道固以親親為本，而親親舍尊祖、敬宗、收族之外，無他為也。茍不親親，則家不齊，安望國與天下而治而平哉？觀帝堯之萬邦協和，始於九族之親睦；帝舜之四方風動，始於五典之慎徽，真萬世君人之龜鑑也。故曰：「聖人南面而治天下，必自人道始。」良有以歟！
流而不息，合同而化，而樂興焉。
同考試官訓導孟批：通篇知樂與之旨者最少，惟此卷認理真切，措辭穩貼，宜錄之以示後學。
符錫
考試官教諭黃批：樂記義似此說理透徹而錄
translation_en:
…in government to cause him concern, nor anyone who fails to be transformed by his instruction and thus frustrates his purpose. Feelings of delight naturally stir and overflow: can this be merely a matter of pipes and strings? The common people dance beneath the radiant heavens and the sun of transforming influence; ordinary folk and their children leap with joy amid the pleasures of a spring terrace and the harmony of the seasons. They play with food in their mouths and pat their full bellies in happiness. This is what is meant by “never wearying of others.” They rise to work at sunrise and rest at sunset. This is what is meant by “incurring no hatred among them.” Thus, the fullness of perfect harmony rests upon the perfection of rites and customs; and the perfection of rites and customs truly proceeds from the ruler’s affection for his kin. Can those charged with ruling others fail to give this their attention?
Alas! The way of the ruler is indeed rooted in affection for kin, and this consists simply in honoring ancestors, revering the lineage’s ancestral head, and drawing together the clansmen. If one does not cherish one’s kin, one’s household will not be well ordered. How, then, can one expect the state and all under Heaven to be governed and brought to peace? Consider how Emperor Yao’s harmonizing of the myriad states began with affection and concord among the nine degrees of kinship, and how Emperor Shun’s influence upon the four quarters began with his careful cultivation of the five cardinal relationships. These are truly models for rulers throughout all ages. Hence the saying: “When the sage faces south and governs all under Heaven, he must begin with the way of human relationships.” Surely there is good reason for this!
“It flows without ceasing, unites and transforms, and music arises therein.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Meng, an Assistant Instructor: Among all the essays, very few grasp the purport of music’s arising [?]. This paper alone apprehends the principles truly and precisely, and its wording is sound and apt. It should be included in the record to instruct later students.
Fu Xi
Comment by Examiner Huang, an Instructor: Expositions of the Record of Music that explain the principles as thoroughly as this and whose writing [?]…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
句純和者絕少非子苦心於是經而旁通卦辭氣化之
說者不能用是錄之
考試官學正韓　批〔樂最難言此作可羨〕〔可羨〕
即和之運於兩間見樂之肇於兩間蓋樂以和
為主也造化運自然之和如此則樂不於是而
興乎記樂者知其然蓋謂樂雖作於聖人而始
則肇於天地彼天地之道一陰一陽而已陽氣
下降而摩蕩乎陰陰氣上躋而摩蕩乎陽但見
鼓之以雷霆奮之以風雨莫非陰陽之氣之鼓
===
奮無一息之或停也動之以四時煖之以日月
罔非陰陽之氣之動煖無一時之或息也至和
磅礴於兩間大化均調於宇宙由是若飛若潛
咸相育於訢合之中若動若植舉相養於絪縕
之內物類雖萬不齊也一化醇之天而不容以
獨異品彙雖萬不一也均合同之仁而不容以
群分造化示人以自然之樂情如此吾知樂有
五聲也實於此乎胚胎樂有八音也實於是乎
根柢清濁相應與於上躋下降之幾非人為之
punctuated:
句純和者絕少。非子苦心於是經，而旁通卦辭氣化之說者不能，用是錄之。
考試官學正韓　批〔樂最難言，此作可羨〕〔可羨〕
即和之運於兩間，見樂之肇於兩間，蓋樂以和為主也。造化運自然之和如此，則樂不於是而興乎？記樂者知其然，蓋謂樂雖作於聖人，而始則肇於天地。彼天地之道，一陰一陽而已。陽氣下降而摩蕩乎陰，陰氣上躋而摩蕩乎陽。但見鼓之以雷霆，奮之以風雨，莫非陰陽之氣之鼓奮，無一息之或停也；動之以四時，煖之以日月，罔非陰陽之氣之動煖，無一時之或息也。至和磅礴於兩間，大化均調於宇宙。由是若飛若潛，咸相育於訢合之中；若動若植，舉相養於絪縕之內。物類雖萬不齊也，一化醇之天，而不容以獨異；品彙雖萬不一也，均合同之仁，而不容以群分。造化示人以自然之樂情如此，吾知樂有五聲也，實於此乎胚胎；樂有八音也，實於是乎根柢。清濁相應，與於上躋下降之幾，非人為之
translation_en:
…whose phrasing is pure and harmonious are exceedingly few. You could not have achieved this without painstaking study of this classic and a broad understanding of the explanations of the hexagram statements and the transformations of vital energy. For this reason, I have selected it for inclusion.
Examiner Han, Instructor: Comment: 〔Music is most difficult to discuss; this composition is admirable.〕〔Admirable.〕
In the operation of harmony between heaven and earth, we see the origins of music between heaven and earth, for music takes harmony as its governing principle. When the creative processes of nature circulate spontaneous harmony in this way, must not music arise from it? The author of the Record of Music understood why this is so: although music was fashioned by the sages, its beginnings originated in heaven and earth. The Way of heaven and earth consists simply of yin and yang. Yang energy descends and stirs against yin; yin energy rises and stirs against yang. We see things roused by thunder and thunderbolts, stirred by wind and rain: all this is the rousing and stirring of yin and yang energies, which never cease for a single breath. Things are moved by the four seasons and warmed by the sun and moon: all this is the movement and warmth of yin and yang energies, which never cease for a single moment. Supreme harmony fills the space between heaven and earth; the great transforming process brings even concord throughout the universe. Thus, creatures that fly and those that dwell beneath the waters all nurture one another amid joyful union; moving creatures and rooted plants all sustain one another within the intermingling of vital energies. Although the myriad kinds of things differ, they share one heaven whose transformations bring them to fullness, permitting none to stand apart. Although the myriad categories of beings are diverse, they partake equally in the benevolence that joins them together, permitting no division into separate groups. Such are the spontaneous feelings of music that nature’s creative processes reveal to us. I know that music’s five notes are indeed conceived here, and that its eight classes of instrumental sound are indeed rooted here. The mutual resonance of high and low tones participates in the incipient workings of ascent and descent; it is not something that human artifice…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
所始也小大相成與於相摩相蕩之妙非私智
之所及也清明象乎天廣大象乎地何者不肇
始於造化乎終始象四時周旋象風雨何者不
權輿於造化乎是則造化至和之所在即樂之
所在也聖人作樂一本於此此大樂所以與天
地同和也與嗟夫樂固本於天地之和而禮則
本於天地之序禮樂豈易作哉必有聖人之德
居天子之位斯可作樂以應天制禮以配地也
禮樂明備則天地生成各得其職矣是知天地
===
也者乃禮樂之本原聖人也者又禮樂之宗主
與後世若叔孫朝儀之建孝孫雅樂之奏不過
糟粕之末而已烏足以語此
第貳場
論
人主務聰明之實
同考試官教諭徐　批
明辨而不激深而不晦紆徐婉曲含不盡之意有古人〔議論泉涌山出豐而徤約而〕
punctuated:
所始也。小大相成，與於相摩相蕩之妙，非私智之所及也。清明象乎天，廣大象乎地，何者不肇始於造化乎？終始象四時，周旋象風雨，何者不權輿於造化乎？是則造化至和之所在，即樂之所在也。聖人作樂，一本於此，此大樂所以與天地同和也與！嗟夫！樂固本於天地之和，而禮則本於天地之序。禮樂豈易作哉？必有聖人之德，居天子之位，斯可作樂以應天，制禮以配地也。禮樂明備，則天地生成，各得其職矣。是知天地也者，乃禮樂之本原；聖人也者，又禮樂之宗主與！後世若叔孫朝儀之建、孝孫雅樂之奏，不過糟粕之末而已，烏足以語此！

第貳場
論
人主務聰明之實

同考試官教諭徐　批：
明辨而不激，深而不晦，紆徐婉曲，含不盡之意，有古人〔議論泉涌山出，豐而徤，約而〕
translation_en:
…originated by human contrivance. The small and the great complete one another, participating in the wondrous workings of mutual friction and agitation; this lies beyond the reach of individual ingenuity. Its purity and brilliance image Heaven; its breadth and grandeur image Earth: what does not originate in the processes of creation? Its endings and beginnings image the four seasons; its circling movements image wind and rain: what does not have its inception in creation? Thus, wherever the supreme harmony of creation resides, there too resides music. In making music, the sages took this alone as their foundation. This is why great music shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth!

Alas! Music is indeed rooted in the harmony of Heaven and Earth, while ritual is rooted in their order. How could ritual and music be easy to establish? Only one who possesses the virtue of a sage and occupies the position of the Son of Heaven can make music to respond to Heaven and institute ritual to accord with Earth. When ritual and music are manifest and complete, Heaven and Earth each fulfill their proper functions of bringing forth and nurturing things. We therefore know that Heaven and Earth are the ultimate source of ritual and music, while the sages are their supreme masters! Such later achievements as Shusun’s establishment of court ceremonial and Xiaosun’s performance of court music amount merely to leftover dregs. How could they suffice for discussing this!

Second Session
Discourse
“The Ruler Must Strive for Genuine Acuity and Discernment”

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor:
“Discriminating without being vehement, profound without being obscure, measured and gently indirect, it holds inexhaustible meaning and possesses the ancients’ …” 〔“Its arguments gush like a spring and rise like mountains [?]; abundant yet vigorous, concise yet …”〕

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
諷諫體録之豈但以其文而已哉
同考試官教諭季　批　閱卷多矣類能逞浮華而
鮮切實此作詞根乎理有抑揚有頓挫意新而奇
文字體當如此
同考試官學正楊　批　議論當理文字圓活非此
論不足以發朱夫子所言之旨筆力如此當三歎服
考試官教諭黄　批　此論詞源筆鋒與彭蠡匡
廬漾闘爭高秋闈作解舍子其誰
考試官學正韓　批　議論英發無一贅語可嘉
===
人君以知臨天下當于其大焉而于其小
者適足以爲累也夫天下之事至繁至賾
一日萬幾綱之紀之皆主於人君之心心
之能應事者曰知知一也而所以爲知者
二故任其公人審以求是是謂大知知至
於大則有以通天下之故當天下之至繁
任天下之至賾而天下稱哲稱聖苟惟私
人是任言輒信焉將以竦動乎人而不知
其蔽塞已甚自哲自聖昏愚係之所謂綱
punctuated:
諷諫體，録之豈但以其文而已哉！

同考試官教諭季批：閱卷多矣，類能逞浮華而鮮切實。此作詞根乎理，有抑揚，有頓挫，意新而奇，文字體當如此。

同考試官學正楊批：議論當理，文字圓活，非此論不足以發朱夫子所言之旨。筆力如此，當三歎服。

考試官教諭黄批：此論詞源筆鋒，與彭蠡匡廬漾闘爭高。秋闈作解，舍子其誰！

考試官學正韓批：議論英發，無一贅語，可嘉。

人君以知臨天下，當于其大焉，而于其小者，適足以爲累也。夫天下之事，至繁至賾，一日萬幾，綱之紀之，皆主於人君之心。心之能應事者曰知。知一也，而所以爲知者二。故任其公人，審以求是，是謂大知。知至於大，則有以通天下之故，當天下之至繁，任天下之至賾，而天下稱哲稱聖。苟惟私人是任，言輒信焉，將以竦動乎人，而不知其蔽塞已甚。自哲自聖，昏愚係之，所謂綱
translation_en:
…the manner of indirect remonstrance. Could its selection for inclusion be merely on account of its literary qualities?

Comment by Associate Examiner Ji, Instructor: I have read many examination scripts. Most display superficial ornament, while few address matters of substance. This composition’s language is rooted in principle; it has modulation and rhythmic pauses, and its ideas are fresh and striking. This is how prose ought to be written.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, School Instructor: The argument accords with principle, and the writing is rounded and lively. Only an essay such as this could bring out the purport of Master Zhu’s words. Such power of expression deserves repeated admiration.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: This essay’s wellspring of language and cutting edge of expression vie with the surging waters of Pengli and the soaring heights of Kuanglu [?]. Who but you should take first place in the autumn Provincial Examination!

Comment by Examiner Han, School Instructor: The argument unfolds brilliantly, without a single superfluous phrase. Commendable.

When a ruler governs the world through understanding, he should attend to its greater form; its lesser form serves only to encumber him. The affairs of the world are exceedingly numerous and intricate. In a single day there are myriad matters requiring attention; ordering and regulating them all depends upon the ruler’s mind. The mind’s capacity to respond to affairs is called understanding. Understanding is one, yet there are two ways of exercising it. Thus, entrusting matters to impartial men [?] and examining carefully to seek what is right is called great understanding. When understanding attains greatness, it enables one to comprehend the workings of the world, manage its utmost complexity, and undertake its most intricate affairs; all under Heaven then acclaim the ruler as wise and sagely. But if he employs only his personal favorites and readily believes whatever they say, intending thereby to overawe others, he does not realize how profoundly his own understanding has already been obstructed. He deems himself wise and sagely, yet benightedness and folly follow. What are called the guiding principles…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
紀者紊矣其為知也不亦小乎宋儒朱子
進說於君欲其嚴朝廷之綱紀而申之以
人主當務聰明之實此蓋吾之所謂大知
者也知大知之說斯可與論聰明之實矣
且聰明者耳目之德也而心實主之人君
之心天下之主也而假其用於耳目耳一
也而欲周天下之聽目一也而欲周天下
之視其將能乎必也不自用而假諸人故
曰明四目達四聰舜之所以為大知者政
===
惟有得乎此爾世之人君孰不欲聰明先
物而稱大知哉耳目之德雖同於天下而
其心或出於公或出於私故同一任人而
所任者異則其為聰明也亦異焉今夫天
下之事夥矣節之有禮和之有樂道之有
政齊之有刑弛張損益舉置推移其在物
也有則其在民也有情其在人才也有品
有類可者否者是者非者常叢沓於人君
之前人君雖以制命為職然必謀之大臣
punctuated:
紀者紊矣，其為知也，不亦小乎？宋儒朱子進說於君，欲其嚴朝廷之綱紀，而申之以人主當務聰明之實。此蓋吾之所謂大知者也。知大知之說，斯可與論聰明之實矣。
且聰明者，耳目之德也，而心實主之。人君之心，天下之主也，而假其用於耳目。耳一也，而欲周天下之聽；目一也，而欲周天下之視，其將能乎？必也不自用而假諸人，故曰：「明四目，達四聰。」舜之所以為大知者，政惟有得乎此爾。世之人君，孰不欲聰明先物而稱大知哉？耳目之德雖同於天下，而其心或出於公，或出於私。故同一任人，而所任者異，則其為聰明也亦異焉。
今夫天下之事夥矣，節之有禮，和之有樂，道之有政，齊之有刑。弛張損益，舉置推移，其在物也有則，其在民也有情，其在人才也有品有類。可者否者，是者非者，常叢沓於人君之前。人君雖以制命為職，然必謀之大臣
translation_en:
…the governing order is thrown into confusion. Is such wisdom not petty? The Song Confucian Zhu Xi offered counsel to his ruler, urging him to uphold strictly the governing order of the court, and further explaining that the ruler must attend to the substance of clear hearing and vision. This, surely, is what I call great wisdom. Only one who understands the teaching of great wisdom can discuss the substance of clear hearing and vision.
Clear hearing and vision are the virtues of the ears and eyes, yet it is the mind that truly governs them. The ruler’s mind is the master of all under Heaven, yet it exercises its functions through the ears and eyes. With only one person’s ears, can he hear everything throughout the realm? With only one person’s eyes, can he see everything throughout the realm? He must refrain from relying solely on himself and draw upon others. Thus it is said: “Make clear the vision in all four directions; open the hearing in all four directions.” Shun’s great wisdom lay precisely [?] in his grasp of this. What ruler does not wish to possess hearing and vision that anticipate events, and to be acclaimed as greatly wise? Although rulers share the faculties of hearing and vision with everyone under Heaven, their minds may proceed either from public concern or from private interest. Thus, although all entrust tasks to others, the people they employ differ, and so too does their clarity of hearing and vision.
Now, the affairs of the realm are numerous. There are rites to regulate them, music to harmonize them, government to guide them, and punishments to bring them into order. Relaxing and tightening, reducing and augmenting, employing and setting aside, adapting and changing: things have their principles, the people have their feelings, and talented men have their grades and categories. What is acceptable and what is not, what is right and what is wrong, constantly crowd before the ruler. Although issuing commands is the ruler’s duty, he must nevertheless deliberate upon these matters with his high ministers…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
焉而後應之盖自人君下至百執事皆有
職業不可相侵此固朝廷之綱紀也是故
三公論道六卿分職諮之詢之稽之質之
愽之詩從衆之給舍使之反覆熟議以求
是非可否之所在吾之所主果得其當而
行且嚴之固吾之聽吾之明也如其不然
則舍己從人人皆曰是必誠是也吾從而
是之人皆曰非必誠非也吾從而非之人
皆曰可必誠可也人皆曰否必誠否也吾
===
從而可否之然後揚于王庭明出命令是
而可者行之非而否者罷之雖其計慮規
為不出於我而我能用之綱紀由是而振
肅朝廷由是而尊嚴即其事而觀之耳不
必聽而能極天下之聽目不必視而能極
天下之明豈非天下之大聰明者哉何也
聰者無所不聞之謂也有所不聞斯謂之
不聰矣明者無所不見之謂也有所不見
斯謂之不明矣今也以天下之人圖天下
punctuated: 焉，而後應之。盖自人君下至百執事，皆有職業，不可相侵，此固朝廷之綱紀也。是故三公論道，六卿分職，諮之詢之，稽之質之，愽之詩從衆之給舍，使之反覆熟議，以求是非可否之所在。吾之所主，果得其當，而行且嚴之，固吾之聽、吾之明也。如其不然，則舍己從人。人皆曰是，必誠是也，吾從而是之；人皆曰非，必誠非也，吾從而非之；人皆曰可，必誠可也；人皆曰否，必誠否也，吾從而可否之。然後揚于王庭，明出命令：是而可者行之，非而否者罷之。雖其計慮規為不出於我，而我能用之，綱紀由是而振肅，朝廷由是而尊嚴。即其事而觀之，耳不必聽而能極天下之聽，目不必視而能極天下之明，豈非天下之大聰明者哉？何也？聰者，無所不聞之謂也；有所不聞，斯謂之不聰矣。明者，無所不見之謂也；有所不見，斯謂之不明矣。今也，以天下之人圖天下
translation_en:
…and only then respond to the matter. From the ruler down to the hundred functionaries, all have their own duties, and none may encroach upon another’s responsibilities. These are indeed the governing principles of the court. Thus the Three Dukes discuss the Way, and the Six Ministers divide their duties. They are consulted and questioned; matters are examined and verified with them, and deliberation is extended to the supervising secretaries and Secretariat drafters [?]. They are made to discuss matters repeatedly and thoroughly, seeking to determine what is right or wrong, acceptable or unacceptable. If what I advocate is indeed appropriate, I put it into practice and enforce it strictly: this is indeed my own keenness of hearing and clarity of sight. If it is not, I set aside my own view and follow others. When all say something is right, it must truly be right, and I accordingly approve it. When all say something is wrong, it must truly be wrong, and I accordingly reject it. When all say something is acceptable, it must truly be acceptable; when all say something is unacceptable, it must truly be unacceptable. I accordingly accept or reject it.

Only then is it proclaimed in the royal court and clearly issued as a command: what is right and acceptable is carried out; what is wrong and unacceptable is discontinued. Although these plans, deliberations, and arrangements do not originate with me, I am able to employ them. Through this, the governing order is made disciplined and firm, and the court acquires dignity and authority. Considered in terms of these affairs, my ears need not themselves listen, yet I can draw fully upon the hearing of all under Heaven; my eyes need not themselves look, yet I can draw fully upon the clear sight of all under Heaven. Am I not, then, one possessed of the greatest keenness of hearing and clarity of sight under Heaven? Why is this so? Keenness of hearing means that nothing goes unheard; if anything goes unheard, this is called a lack of keenness of hearing. Clarity of sight means that nothing goes unseen; if anything goes unseen, this is called a lack of clarity of sight. Now, employing the people of all under Heaven to deliberate upon the affairs of all under Heaven…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之事吾任大臣而大臣者又合天下之耳
目以為吾一人聰明之助謂吾弗聰而吾
行無不當也有弗聞者能之乎故曰耳不
必聽而能極天下之聰謂吾弗明而吾行
無不中也有弗見者能之乎故曰目不必
視而能極天下之明曰哲曰聖頌聲流焉
書曰視遠惟明聽德惟聰又曰亶聰明作
元后其道如此此則所謂聰明之實者以
公心而任其公人也易曰知臨大君之宜
===
豈不信哉乃若好名者亦知任人矣然或
任非所任而偏聽輕信得其一言行則行
罷則罷自彼觀之可以發奸可以擿伏可
以破幽入隱可以致摠攬之名可以救獨
斷之誉而譸張熒蠱顛倒易置卒不出其
術數之内遠之愈繆久之愈暗自以為聰
而實有未聞自以為明而實有未見名為
獨斷而主威不免於下移名為摠攬而國
政不免於參出由是綱紀紊而庶事以隳
punctuated:
之事，吾任大臣，而大臣者又合天下之耳目，以為吾一人聰明之助。謂吾弗聰，而吾行無不當也，有弗聞者能之乎？故曰：耳不必聽，而能極天下之聰。謂吾弗明，而吾行無不中也，有弗見者能之乎？故曰：目不必視，而能極天下之明。曰哲曰聖，頌聲流焉。《書》曰：「視遠惟明，聽德惟聰。」又曰：「亶聰明作元后。」其道如此。此則所謂聰明之實者，以公心而任其公人也。《易》曰：「知臨，大君之宜。」豈不信哉？

乃若好名者，亦知任人矣。然或任非所任，而偏聽輕信，得其一言，行則行，罷則罷。自彼觀之，可以發奸，可以擿伏，可以破幽入隱，可以致摠攬之名，可以救獨斷之誉。而譸張熒蠱，顛倒易置，卒不出其術數之内。遠之愈繆，久之愈暗。自以為聰，而實有未聞；自以為明，而實有未見。名為獨斷，而主威不免於下移；名為摠攬，而國政不免於參出。由是綱紀紊，而庶事以隳。
translation_en:
…the affairs of the realm. I entrust great ministers with responsibility, and these ministers in turn bring together the ears and eyes of all under Heaven to assist the hearing and vision of me, their sole ruler. Suppose one says that my hearing lacks discernment: yet none of my actions is inappropriate. Could someone who failed to hear something achieve this? Thus it is said: the ears need not themselves listen to attain the fullest discernment of hearing in the realm. Suppose one says that my vision lacks clarity: yet none of my actions misses the mark. Could someone who failed to see something achieve this? Thus it is said: the eyes need not themselves look to attain the fullest clarity of vision in the realm. Acclamations of “Wise!” and “Sagely!” spread abroad. The Book of Documents says: “To see far is clarity of vision; to heed virtue is discernment of hearing.” It also says: “One truly discerning in hearing and clear in vision becomes the supreme sovereign.” Such is the way to achieve this. This is what is meant by the substance of discerning hearing and clear vision: to employ impartial men with an impartial mind. The Book of Changes says: “Approaching with wisdom: this befits a great ruler.” Is this not indeed true?

As for those who crave a reputation, they too know to entrust others with responsibility. Yet they may entrust those who ought not to be entrusted, listening to one side and believing too readily. Upon receiving a single word from such a person, they proceed if told to proceed and desist if told to desist. From their own perspective, they can thereby expose wrongdoing, uncover concealed misconduct, penetrate obscurity and hidden matters, gain a reputation for comprehensive control, and salvage a reputation for independent decision-making [?]. Yet amid fabrication and deception, bewilderment and delusion, inversions and substitutions, they ultimately never escape the compass of those men's manipulative arts. The further they pursue this, the more mistaken they become; the longer it continues, the more benighted they grow. They consider themselves discerning in hearing, yet there are things they have not heard; they consider themselves clear in vision, yet there are things they have not seen. In name they decide independently, yet the ruler's authority inevitably shifts to those below. In name they exercise comprehensive control, yet the government of the state inevitably issues from multiple sources. Consequently, the framework of order falls into confusion, and the manifold affairs of government fall into ruin…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
蓋以私心而任私人其極必至於是所謂
自哲自聖而昏愚係之此之謂也夫求聰
明之名而乃為昏愚之歸其視圖任大臣
不求為聰明而大知歸焉者真所謂毫釐
千里矣人君不欲天下之治則已如欲求
治二者將孰務哉知之大小聰明之名實
不可不審也雖然亦在乎學而已矣舜之
告禹曰人心惟危道心惟微惟精惟一允
執厥中此萬世聖學之源也人君務聰明
===
之實以成大知者其必由聖學乎故朱子
他日告君又曰心正則視明聽聰由是觀
之不由聖學以正其心而求聰明則公私
交雜吾見求實而近僅止於名其知終不
足以有臨也此朱子此疏未及之意也故
併論之
表
擬宋以歐陽脩知制誥謝表〔慶曆三年〕
劉禔
punctuated:
蓋以私心而任私人，其極必至於是。所謂「自哲自聖，而昏愚係之」，此之謂也。夫求聰明之名，而乃為昏愚之歸，其視圖任大臣、不求為聰明而大知歸焉者，真所謂毫釐千里矣。人君不欲天下之治則已，如欲求治，二者將孰務哉？知之大小，聰明之名實，不可不審也。雖然，亦在乎學而已矣。舜之告禹曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。」此萬世聖學之源也。人君務聰明之實以成大知者，其必由聖學乎！故朱子他日告君又曰：「心正則視明聽聰。」由是觀之，不由聖學以正其心而求聰明，則公私交雜。吾見求實而近僅止於名，其知終不足以有臨也。此朱子此疏未及之意也，故併論之。

表

擬宋以歐陽脩知制誥謝表〔慶曆三年〕
劉禔
translation_en:
…For when a ruler acts from selfish motives and employs his own partisans, matters must ultimately reach this point. This is what is meant by the saying, “He deems himself wise and sagely, yet darkness and folly follow.” Seeking a reputation for perceptiveness, he instead ends in darkness and folly. Compared with one who considers carefully whom to entrust with high office and, without seeking to appear perceptive, gains great wisdom, this is truly what is meant by a hair’s breadth of difference leading a thousand miles astray. If a ruler does not desire good government throughout the realm, there is nothing more to say; but if he seeks it, which of these two courses should he pursue? The distinction between lesser and greater wisdom, and between the reputation and reality of perceptiveness, must be carefully examined.

Yet this, too, depends upon learning alone. Shun told Yu: “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning and single-minded; hold fast to the mean.” This is the source of sagely learning for all ages. Surely a ruler who pursues genuine perceptiveness in order to attain great wisdom must follow sagely learning! Thus Master Zhu, addressing his sovereign on another occasion, also said: “When the mind is rectified, sight becomes clear and hearing acute.” Viewed in this light, if one seeks perceptiveness without rectifying one’s mind through sagely learning, public and private motives become intermingled. I see that, though seeking the reality, one scarcely gets beyond the reputation [?]; one’s wisdom will ultimately be insufficient to preside over the realm. This is a point that Master Zhu did not reach in this memorial, and so I discuss it here as well.

Memorial

A simulated memorial of thanks on Ouyang Xiu’s appointment as Drafter under the Song dynasty. 〔Third year of Qingli, 1043〕
By Liu Zhi.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭張　批〔著述有式摸倣得真方是〕
〔制作法歐文典雅渾純意趣高遠人鮮能之諸作〕
〔遲辭浮麗殊失本相又體貼職掌不類事實或〕
〔遺令人厭觀此篇古淡春容宛然六一家風致噫〕
〔大羹玄酒咀之而有餘味彖𥫗能舍乎〕
考試官教諭黄　批〔寫出歐陽公謦咳中真〕
〔意趣性作也〕
考試官學正韓　批〔得駢儷體可嘉〕
臣某言伏奉
===
制命蒙恩特授臣右正言知制誥者伏以人
文藻潤聿昭
雲漢之章道化鋪揚叵測
乾坤之大惟典謨渾灝誥誓渙汹追相如諭
蜀之文敦興奉天之詔皆能言為世式動
中事宜肆在
本朝特難是選豈期末學亦濫兹除擂濫美
於
制詞沐
punctuated:
同考試官教諭張　批〔著述有式，摸倣得真，方是〕〔制作法。歐文典雅渾純，意趣高遠，人鮮能之。諸作〕〔遲辭浮麗，殊失本相；又體貼職掌不類事實，或〕〔遺，令人厭觀。此篇古淡春容，宛然六一家風致。噫！〕〔大羹玄酒，咀之而有餘味，彖𥫗能舍乎？〕
考試官教諭黄　批〔寫出歐陽公謦咳中真〕〔意趣，性作也。〕
考試官學正韓　批〔得駢儷體，可嘉。〕
臣某言：伏奉制命，蒙恩特授臣右正言、知制誥者。伏以人文藻潤，聿昭雲漢之章；道化鋪揚，叵測乾坤之大。惟典謨渾灝，誥誓渙汹。追相如諭蜀之文，敦興奉天之詔，皆能言為世式，動中事宜。肆在本朝，特難是選。豈期末學，亦濫兹除。擂濫美於制詞，沐
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Writing has its established forms; only imitation that captures the original truly〕〔constitutes a method of composition. Ouyang’s prose is classical and elegant, integrated and pure; its conception and spirit are lofty and far-reaching. Few can achieve this. The other compositions〕〔have ornate, superficial wording [?] and greatly lose the original character. Moreover, their treatment of the duties of the office does not accord with the facts, or〕〔contains omissions, making them tiresome to read. This piece has an antique simplicity and a springlike ease, vividly embodying the style of the Master of Six Ones [Ouyang Xiu]. Ah!〕〔Like unseasoned broth and plain water offered in sacrifice, it leaves a lingering savor when tasted. … could one set it aside? [The characters 彖𥫗 are unclear.]〕
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔It conveys the true〕〔spirit and meaning in Lord Ouyang’s very voice—a composition of innate feeling [?].〕
Examiner Han, Director of Studies, comments: 〔It achieves the style of parallel prose: commendable.〕
Your servant So-and-so states: I have reverently received the imperial command graciously appointing me Reminder of the Right and Drafter of Proclamations. I humbly consider that the embellishments of human culture make manifest the brilliance of the Milky Way; the Way’s transforming influence spreads abroad, immeasurable as the vastness of Heaven and Earth. The Canons and Counsels are profound and expansive; the Announcements and Oaths surge forth in abundance. Following such works as Xiangru’s proclamation to Shu and carrying forward the edict issued at Fengtian [?], all these writings could serve as models for the age, invariably fitting the needs of affairs. Thus, in our dynasty, selecting someone for this office is especially difficult. How could I, a man of meager learning, have expected undeservedly to receive this appointment? Favored with extravagant praise in the words of the imperial appointment [?], I am bathed in …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
誕恩於
宸注感先愧集責與憂并恭惟
〇〇〇〇道同天地
孝達神明仁恕根於心恭儉出其性禮隆
會慶履端先晉於
慈宮宅起睦親飽德每聯於
皇族恐戕物命思結人心正風俗則詔禁邪巫
勤政理則屏書無逸兵以不用為武刑以
不殺為威求言渙發乎
===
玉音問俗隱憂乎菜色剛惟獨斷職不下侵謂
鉛槧須責文儒而綸綍實關著述丁寧
天語誕告多方顯允
聖謨式昭
來裔緬惟内批之勤綣允資良史以發揮經
緯古作樞機今付竊念臣少罹孤疢閱歷
險艱長乏技能校讎文字救趨時之弊力
去雕華守學古之勤徒成鄙樸頃備員於
管記竟落職於言階幸軫淹沉荐蒙甄敘
punctuated:
誕恩於宸注，感先愧集，責與憂并。恭惟〇〇〇〇，道同天地，孝達神明，仁恕根於心，恭儉出其性。禮隆會慶，履端先晉於慈宮；宅起睦親，飽德每聯於皇族。恐戕物命，思結人心。正風俗則詔禁邪巫，勤政理則屏書無逸。兵以不用為武，刑以不殺為威。求言渙發乎玉音，問俗隱憂乎菜色。剛惟獨斷，職不下侵。謂鉛槧須責文儒，而綸綍實關著述。丁寧天語，誕告多方。顯允聖謨，式昭來裔。緬惟内批之勤綣，允資良史以發揮。經緯古作，樞機今付。

竊念臣少罹孤疢，閱歷險艱；長乏技能，校讎文字。救趨時之弊，力去雕華；守學古之勤，徒成鄙樸。頃備員於管記，竟落職於言階。幸軫淹沉，荐蒙甄敘。
translation_en:
…vast favor through Your Majesty’s attentive regard. Gratitude comes first, followed by shame; responsibility and anxiety arise together. Reverently considering Your Majesty [〇〇〇〇, an unfilled honorific]: your Way accords with Heaven and Earth, and your filial devotion reaches the spirits. Benevolence and forbearance are rooted in your heart; reverence and frugality issue from your nature. You magnify the rites of birthday celebration, first proceeding to the Palace of Maternal Benevolence at the opening of the year. In fostering affection among kin [宅起, unclear], you repeatedly gather the imperial clan to feast upon your bounty. You fear harming living creatures and seek to bind the people’s hearts to you. To rectify customs, you issue edicts prohibiting heterodox shamans; to encourage diligence in government, you have “Against Idleness” (Wuyi) inscribed upon a screen. In military affairs, you make refraining from using arms your martial achievement; in punishments, you make refraining from killing your awe-inspiring authority. Your august voice generously issues calls for counsel; in inquiring into popular conditions, you harbor deep concern for the people’s famished appearance. Resolute, you decide alone, yet do not encroach upon the duties of those below. You hold that the work of brush and tablet must be entrusted to literary scholars, and that imperial pronouncements are indeed matters for written record. Your earnest imperial words are proclaimed widely. Your manifestly trustworthy and sagely counsels shall illuminate generations to come. Reflecting upon the diligence and solicitude of your personal written directives, we must indeed rely upon capable historians to expound them. The ordering of ancient writings and the crucial responsibility are now entrusted to me [?].

I humbly reflect that, orphaned and afflicted in youth, I passed through dangers and hardships. Grown older, I lacked skills and abilities, occupying myself with collating texts. To remedy the faults of following contemporary fashions, I strove to discard ornate embellishment; diligently adhering to the study of antiquity, I achieved only uncouth simplicity. Recently I served among those charged with keeping records, but ultimately lost my post in the remonstrance service. Fortunately, Your Majesty took thought for my prolonged obscurity, and I repeatedly received consideration and reappointment.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
通班冊府待罪諫垣謬參四禁之嚴超置
七人之列辭章懇乞
聖意重回忽遣使以臨門俾措躬而無地臣敢
不勉圖來效仰荅
皇慈景服前脩翼成信史話言必記舉動特書
事深假于折衷意默存乎儆戒首復渾厚
之體特申懇至之詞俾
德意旁宣偕日月而普照
仁恩下浹等雨露以弘敷雖稽古未盡典謨而
===
紀實可知堯舜尚期補過助大塊於一塵
更勵匪躬煩尚方之一劍無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策
punctuated:
通班冊府，待罪諫垣，謬參四禁之嚴，超置七人之列。辭章懇乞，聖意重回，忽遣使以臨門，俾措躬而無地。臣敢不勉圖來效，仰荅皇慈！景服前脩，翼成信史；話言必記，舉動特書。事深假于折衷，意默存乎儆戒。首復渾厚之體，特申懇至之詞，俾德意旁宣，偕日月而普照；仁恩下浹，等雨露以弘敷。雖稽古未盡典謨，而紀實可知堯舜。尚期補過，助大塊於一塵；更勵匪躬，煩尚方之一劍。無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁場
策
translation_en:
… admitted to the ranks of the imperial library and serving, unworthily, in the remonstrance offices, I have undeservedly joined the august company of the four forbidden precincts [?] and been advanced beyond my station into the ranks of the seven. In a written submission I earnestly begged to decline, but Your Majesty again reconsidered and suddenly dispatched an envoy to my door, leaving me nowhere to place myself in my embarrassment. How could your servant fail to strive to render service hereafter and repay Your Majesty’s gracious kindness!

I shall revere and follow the worthy men of earlier times and assist in completing a trustworthy history. Your words shall invariably be recorded, and your actions expressly set down. In treating events, I shall rely profoundly upon balanced judgment, while silently maintaining an intent to admonish and caution. I shall first restore a substantial and dignified style and give particular expression to words of earnest sincerity, so that your virtuous intentions may be proclaimed everywhere, shining universally like the sun and moon, and your benevolent favor may penetrate below, spreading widely like rain and dew. Although my examination of antiquity may not fully encompass the Canons and Counsels, a truthful record will nevertheless make known a Yao and Shun.

I still hope to remedy faults, contributing a single mote of dust to the great earth. I shall further steel myself to serve without regard for my own person, even at the cost of calling forth a sword from the Palace Workshops. Looking up to Heaven and reverently contemplating Your Majesty, I am overwhelmed by fervent emotion, trembling and apprehension. I respectfully submit this memorial to convey my thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
第一問　葉釗
同考試官訓導劉　批〔我〕
聖祖制作之善正在有德以為之本場中答者類能知之但於制作詳
備處漫不究心此篇條荅如指諸掌非平日服膺
聖製而有志於當世務者不能讀之令人生忠愛意風簷寸晷之下
得士有此亦可為
明時慶矣
同考試官教諭潘　批　詞氣浩然如長江大河華
===
國之文貴如此
同考試官教諭傅　批
皇祖一統天下之盛煥乎文章蕩蕩乎如天之難名此士歷陳而又能
知其所本可謂善鋪張
洪休揚厲偉績者矣
考試官教諭黃　批　鋪張
聖制之懿光昭萬世無踰於此者
考試官學正韓　批　書生能熟究
聖製而頃刻成文以對其英英用世之志久矣可敬可敬
punctuated:
第一問，葉釗。

同考試官訓導劉批：〔我〕聖祖制作之善，正在有德以為之本。場中答者類能知之，但於制作詳備處漫不究心。此篇條荅，如指諸掌，非平日服膺聖製而有志於當世務者不能。讀之令人生忠愛意。風簷寸晷之下，得士有此，亦可為明時慶矣。

同考試官教諭潘批：詞氣浩然，如長江大河。華國之文，貴如此。

同考試官教諭傅批：皇祖一統天下之盛，煥乎文章，蕩蕩乎如天之難名。此士歷陳，而又能知其所本，可謂善鋪張洪休、揚厲偉績者矣。

考試官教諭黃批：鋪張聖制之懿，光昭萬世，無踰於此者。

考試官學正韓批：書生能熟究聖製，而頃刻成文以對，其英英用世之志久矣。可敬！可敬！
translation_en:
First policy question. Ye Zhao.

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor: The excellence of our sagely founder’s institutions lies precisely in the virtue that provided their foundation. Most candidates answering this question understood this, but gave little thought to the institutions’ comprehensiveness and detail. This essay answers point by point, making everything as clear as something displayed in one’s palm. Only someone who habitually takes the sagely imperial institutions to heart and aspires to address the affairs of the age could accomplish this. Reading it inspires loyalty and devotion. To find such a scholar under the windswept examination eaves, within so brief an allotted time, is indeed cause for congratulation in this enlightened age.

Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor: The language and spirit are vast and flowing, like the Yangzi and Yellow Rivers. Such is the writing prized for bringing glory to the state.

Comment by Associate Examiner Fu, Instructor: The imperial founder’s magnificent unification of all under Heaven shone with cultural brilliance; its grandeur, like Heaven itself, defies description. This scholar sets it forth in detail and also understands its foundation. He may indeed be called adept at expounding its abundant blessings and extolling its mighty achievements.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: In expounding the excellence of the sagely imperial institutions, whose radiance illuminates ten thousand generations, nothing surpasses this.

Comment by Examiner Han, School Instructor: This scholar has thoroughly studied the sagely imperial institutions and composed an essay in response within moments. His outstanding aspiration to serve the world must be of long standing. Admirable! Admirable!

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
對立法通天下萬世之大利者
聖人之業垂法妝天下萬世之大功者
聖人之德葢法制之立
聖人大業而為天下萬世利者也然其良法美
意垂之天下萬世其功莫大焉自非
聖人備聰明聖知之天德其孰能與於此哉孰
事首舉
皇祖制作下詢承學愚也幸生玆
聖明之世仰佩
===
聖謨久矣庸不能悉謹條其一二以對夫春秋
大一統者乃漢儒董仲舒之言本子思子
中庸之意也子思子曰王天下有三重焉
其寡過矣乎又曰非天子不議禮不制度
不考文言必聖人在天子之位而後行此
三重之道也非春秋大一統為天地之常
經古今之通義邪洪惟我
太祖高皇帝承
天膺曆變夷為華以
punctuated:
對：立法通天下萬世之大利者，聖人之業；垂法妝天下萬世之大功者，聖人之德。葢法制之立，聖人大業，而為天下萬世利者也。然其良法美意，垂之天下萬世，其功莫大焉。自非聖人備聰明聖知之天德，其孰能與於此哉？孰事首舉皇祖制作，下詢承學。愚也幸生玆聖明之世，仰佩聖謨久矣。庸不能悉，謹條其一二以對。
夫《春秋》大一統者，乃漢儒董仲舒之言，本子思子《中庸》之意也。子思子曰：「王天下有三重焉，其寡過矣乎！」又曰：「非天子，不議禮，不制度，不考文。」言必聖人在天子之位，而後行此三重之道也。非《春秋》大一統為天地之常經、古今之通義邪？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，承天膺曆，變夷為華，以
translation_en:
Your servant replies: Establishing laws that extend great benefits to all under Heaven for ten thousand generations is the sage’s undertaking; handing down laws that bring great achievement to all under Heaven for ten thousand generations [?] is the sage’s virtue. Establishing laws and institutions is the sage’s great undertaking, benefiting all under Heaven for ten thousand generations. Yet in transmitting these excellent laws and beneficent intentions to all under Heaven for ten thousand generations, his achievement is unsurpassed. Unless a sage possessed Heaven-given virtue—keen hearing, clear sight, sagacity, and wisdom—who could participate in this undertaking? At the outset, you, sir [?], invoke the imperial ancestor’s institutional creations and condescend to question those who have received instruction. Fortunate to have been born in this age of sagely enlightenment, I, in my ignorance, have long revered the sage imperial counsels. Though unable to recount them fully, I respectfully set out one or two points in reply.
The phrase “the grand unity of the Spring and Autumn Annals” comes from the Han scholar Dong Zhongshu and is rooted in Master Zisi’s meaning in the Doctrine of the Mean. Master Zisi said: “In ruling all under Heaven, there are three weighty matters. With these, surely one will make few errors!” He also said: “Unless one is the Son of Heaven, one does not deliberate on rites, establish standards, or examine written forms.” This means that only when a sage occupies the position of Son of Heaven can he carry out the way of these three weighty matters. Is not the grand unity of the Spring and Autumn Annals the enduring norm of Heaven and Earth and the principle common to antiquity and the present? Reverently considering our Taizu, the Exalted Emperor: he obeyed Heaven and received the mandate of dynastic succession, transformed barbarian rule into Chinese civilization, and with …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
天下之大聖行天下之大事制禮作樂爲百
王之法立教垂訓宏一代之規演諸
宸翰出自
淵衷
神功莫磬
聖德難言而其所仰見者則有所謂三重之
道焉夫自元俗亂華有
禮儀定式以議禮自夷教變夏有
稽古定制以制度自胡言混中土有
===
洪武正韻以考文此皆制作之大端所以新
天下之耳目一天下之心志萬世臣民所
當遵守而不敢違者也請述其旨自天尊
地卑之位定而禮于是乎形在人則親疎
之分貴賤之等截然而不可犯者皆是禮
也禮以議之上下辨矣若
定式所載爲條三十有七始之以朝叅筵宴
之節終之以器皿床榻之類至於其間最
切而要者則
punctuated:
天下之大聖，行天下之大事，制禮作樂，爲百王之法；立教垂訓，宏一代之規。演諸宸翰，出自淵衷。神功莫磬，聖德難言，而其所仰見者，則有所謂三重之道焉。夫自元俗亂華，有《禮儀定式》以議禮；自夷教變夏，有《稽古定制》以制度；自胡言混中土，有《洪武正韻》以考文。此皆制作之大端，所以新天下之耳目，一天下之心志，萬世臣民所當遵守而不敢違者也。

請述其旨。自天尊地卑之位定，而禮于是乎形。在人，則親疎之分、貴賤之等，截然而不可犯者，皆是禮也。禮以議之，上下辨矣。若《定式》所載，爲條三十有七，始之以朝叅筵宴之節，終之以器皿床榻之類。至於其間最切而要者，則
translation_en:
…as the great sage of the realm, he undertook the great affairs of the realm, establishing rites and creating music to serve as a model for all kings, instituting teachings and transmitting admonitions to extend the grand standards of his dynasty. These were set forth through his imperial brush and issued from his profound heart. His divine achievements cannot be exhausted [?], and his sagely virtue is difficult to express. Yet what we can discern as we look up to him includes the way of the so-called three weighty duties. Since Yuan customs had thrown Chinese civilization into disorder, there was the Established Forms of Ritual and Ceremony (Liyi dingshi), by which to deliberate upon rites; since foreign teachings had transformed Chinese ways, there was the Established Institutions Based on Antiquity (Jigu dingzhi), by which to establish regulations; and since foreign speech had confused the Central Lands, there was the Correct Rhymes of the Hongwu Reign (Hongwu zhengyun), by which to examine and standardize writing. These were all major acts of institutional creation, intended to renew what all under Heaven heard and saw and to unite their hearts and purposes. They are what subjects and people for ten thousand generations ought to observe, without daring to transgress.

Allow me to explain their purport. Once the positions of Heaven above and Earth below were settled, ritual thereby took form. Among human beings, distinctions between close and distant kin and gradations between noble and lowly—all clearly demarcated and inviolable—are ritual. Through deliberation upon ritual, those above and below are distinguished. The Established Forms, for example, contains thirty-seven articles, beginning with the ceremonial procedures for court attendance and banquets and ending with such categories as vessels, beds, and couches. As for what is most pertinent and essential among them, it is…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖諭所謂毋放肆怠聽思為省身克己之道是
己自天圓地方之體設而度于是乎寓在
人則室廬之限輿皁之制秩然而不可踰
者皆是度也度以制之等威殊矣若
定制所編類皆經常之法斟酌夫李唐趙宋
之制兼舉夫藝祖英宗之言至於其間語
及財利者則
聖意以為食祿之家不當與民爭利故爾自天
玄地黃之色著而文于是乎顯在人則形
===
之點畫播之聲音皆是文也文以考之形
聲正矣若
正韻一書去沈約之謬而成經緯之交其雅
音則取於中原其註釋則依於毛晃他如
東冬清青之二韻併而為一虞模麻遮之
一韻析而為二孰非
宸慮之所在乎爰自
聖祖以來迄今百三十餘年政不異政俗不殊
俗誠一統文明之治足以比隆唐虞三代
punctuated:
聖諭所謂「毋放肆怠聽，思為省身克己之道」，是己。自天圓地方之體設，而度于是乎寓。在人，則室廬之限、輿皁之制，秩然而不可踰者，皆是度也。度以制之，等威殊矣。若《定制》所編，類皆經常之法，斟酌夫李唐趙宋之制，兼舉夫藝祖英宗之言。至於其間語及財利者，則聖意以為食祿之家不當與民爭利故爾。
自天玄地黃之色著，而文于是乎顯。在人，則形之點畫、播之聲音，皆是文也。文以考之，形聲正矣。若《正韻》一書，去沈約之謬，而成經緯之交。其雅音則取於中原，其註釋則依於毛晃。他如東冬、清青之二韻併而為一，虞模、麻遮之一韻析而為二，孰非宸慮之所在乎？爰自聖祖以來，迄今百三十餘年，政不異政，俗不殊俗，誠一統文明之治，足以比隆唐虞三代
translation_en:
…what the imperial admonition calls “Do not act wantonly or listen inattentively; consider the way to examine oneself and overcome selfish desires” [?]—this is precisely it. Once the forms of round Heaven and square Earth were established, measures were embodied therein. In human affairs, the limits prescribed for dwellings and the regulations governing carriages and stables, ordered and inviolable, are all such measures. By regulating things through measures, distinctions of rank and authority are maintained. The provisions compiled in the Established Regulations (Dingzhi) are all enduring norms. They weigh the institutions of the Tang of the Li house and the Song of the Zhao house, and also cite the words of the Song emperors Yizu and Yingzong. Where they speak of wealth and profit, this is because the imperial intention is that households receiving official stipends should not compete with the people for profit.
Once the colors of dark Heaven and yellow Earth became manifest, patterned expression appeared therein. In human affairs, what takes shape in written strokes and what is conveyed in sounds are both patterned expression. By examining these through standards of writing, written forms and sounds are rectified. The book Correct Rhymes (Zhengyun), for example, eliminates Shen Yue’s errors and establishes an interlocking framework like warp and weft. Its standard pronunciations are drawn from the Central Plain, and its annotations follow Mao Huang. Other instances include combining the two rhyme categories dong 東 and dong 冬, and qing 清 and qing 青, into one category for each pair, and dividing the single categories yu–mo 虞模 and ma–zhe 麻遮 into two each. Which of these was not an object of imperial consideration? From the time of the sage founding emperor down to the present, more than 130 years have passed. Government has remained consistent, and customs have not diverged. Truly, this is a unified and cultured order, worthy of comparison in its grandeur with the age of Tang Yao and Yu Shun and the Three Dynasties…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之盛所謂建諸天地而不悖質諸鬼神而
無疑百世以俟聖人而不惑者也至求其
制作之本則存乎
聖祖本諸身而有中庸之德焉耳夫自昔聖人
三重之制不過因前代之舊而損益其間
故功業在天下或十世百世而止我
聖祖恢復帝王自有之疆土膺擊今古所無之
戎狄因元人斁敗禮樂典章彝倫之後禮
以制行度以為法文以合俗其利則天下
===
萬世之利者也
聖人之業何如其大邪其功則天下萬世之功
者也
聖人之德何如其盛邪惟
聖祖道德之高制作之善功業之成如此而欲
鋪張揚厲猶摸天地而繪日月也然吾夫
子有曰大哉堯之為君也巍巍乎唯天為
大唯堯則之蕩蕩乎民無能名焉巍巍乎
其有成功也煥乎其有文章愚生殆忘
punctuated: 之盛，所謂建諸天地而不悖，質諸鬼神而無疑，百世以俟聖人而不惑者也。至求其制作之本，則存乎聖祖本諸身而有中庸之德焉耳。夫自昔聖人三重之制，不過因前代之舊而損益其間，故功業在天下，或十世百世而止。我聖祖恢復帝王自有之疆土，膺擊今古所無之戎狄，因元人斁敗禮樂典章彝倫之後，禮以制行，度以為法，文以合俗，其利則天下萬世之利者也。聖人之業何如其大邪？其功則天下萬世之功者也。聖人之德何如其盛邪？惟聖祖道德之高、制作之善、功業之成如此，而欲鋪張揚厲，猶摸天地而繪日月也。然吾夫子有曰：「大哉，堯之為君也！巍巍乎，唯天為大，唯堯則之。蕩蕩乎，民無能名焉！巍巍乎，其有成功也！煥乎，其有文章！」愚生殆忘
translation_en:
…in their flourishing grandeur. This is what is meant by “established before Heaven and Earth without contradiction, tested before ghosts and spirits without doubt, and awaiting a sage a hundred generations hence without perplexity.” If we seek the foundation of his institutions, however, it lies simply in the Sagely Founder's grounding them in his own person and possessing the virtue of the Mean. Since ancient times, sages’ institutions concerning the three weighty matters—rituals, standards, and written forms—have merely followed the precedents of earlier dynasties, making additions and reductions along the way. Thus their achievements in the world endured perhaps ten or a hundred generations and no more. Our Sagely Founder recovered the territory that rightfully belonged to the emperors and kings and struck down Rong and Di foes without parallel in ancient or recent times. After the men of the Yuan had corrupted rites and music, statutes and institutions, and the enduring human relationships, he regulated conduct through ritual, established rules through standards, and unified customs through written forms. Their benefits are benefits for all under Heaven for ten thousand generations. How great is the sage's undertaking! His accomplishments are accomplishments for all under Heaven for ten thousand generations. How abundant is the sage's virtue!

Such are the loftiness of the Sagely Founder's Way and virtue, the excellence of his institutions, and the fulfillment of his achievements that attempting to expound and extol them would be like depicting Heaven and Earth and painting the sun and moon. Yet our Master said: “Great indeed was Yao as a ruler! How lofty! Heaven alone is great, and Yao alone took it as his model. So vast was he that the people could find no name for him! Lofty were his accomplishments! Resplendent were his cultural forms!” This humble student has perhaps forgotten …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
堯天之下平日之所誦習者唯此而已更復何
言謹對
第二問
張鉞
同考試官教諭徐　批　考究精審深悉儒先道統
淵源有養之士也可嘉
同考試官教諭李　批　敷演出正學一本意匪素有
抱負者鮮能
同考試官學正楊　批　荅有根據足見博洽之學
===
考試官教諭黄　批　此子薦荅殆如親立門室而
樞趍考亭者乎
考試官學正韓　批　一部道學淵源盡在此子
腹中方能随叩随鳴
道係於天有不可終絶之統道屬於人有
不可苟得之傳惟其不可終絶也故或異
地而同心惟其不可苟得也故或同時而
異學然則道之係於天而屬於人者豈可
以輕論哉請畧陳之道統之傳始於羲皇
punctuated:
堯天之下，平日之所誦習者唯此而已，更復何言？謹對。

第二問
張鉞

同考試官教諭徐批：考究精審，深悉儒先道統淵源，有養之士也，可嘉。

同考試官教諭李批：敷演出正學一本意，匪素有抱負者鮮能。

同考試官學正楊批：荅有根據，足見博洽之學。

考試官教諭黄批：此子薦荅，殆如親立門室而樞趍考亭者乎？

考試官學正韓批：一部道學淵源，盡在此子腹中，方能随叩随鳴。

道係於天，有不可終絶之統；道屬於人，有不可苟得之傳。惟其不可終絶也，故或異地而同心；惟其不可苟得也，故或同時而異學。然則道之係於天而屬於人者，豈可以輕論哉？請畧陳之。道統之傳，始於羲皇
translation_en:
…beneath Yao’s heaven, this alone is what I have regularly recited and studied. What more can I say? Respectfully submitted in reply.

Second Question
Zhang Yue

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: His investigation is meticulous and discerning. He thoroughly understands the origins and transmission of the succession of the Way among earlier Confucian masters. He is a man of cultivated character, worthy of praise.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: He develops the meaning of orthodox learning’s single foundation. Few could accomplish this without long-held aspirations.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, School Instructor: The answer is well grounded, amply demonstrating broad and thorough learning.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: This candidate’s submitted answer [?] makes it seem as though he had personally stood within the master’s school and respectfully approached [?] Kaoting—that is, Zhu Xi.

Comment by Examiner Han, School Instructor: The entire history of the origins and transmission of the Learning of the Way is within this candidate’s breast; only thus can he respond to every inquiry as a bell sounds whenever struck.

The Way is bound to Heaven, with a succession that can never be permanently severed; the Way is entrusted to human beings, with a transmission that cannot be acquired casually.
