Precisely because its succession cannot be permanently severed, people in different places may share the same mind. Precisely because its transmission cannot be acquired casually, people living at the same time may pursue different teachings. How, then, could one lightly discuss the Way as bound to Heaven and entrusted to human beings? Allow me to set it forth briefly. The transmission of the succession of the Way began with Sovereign Fuxi…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
盛於堯舜大成於孔子至孟子而中絕焉
有宋周程朱子起而承之周子生于春陵
南方之人也而程子受學於南安故吾與
點也之意遂得於心領之餘程子生於河
洛北方之人也而楊中立從學於潁昌故
吾道南矣之歎遂發於目送之際楊之再
傳復得朱子以集諸儒之大成焉周范造
詣固殊程張契悟亦異此朱子荅或人之
問也盖范文正之極高明而道中庸不過
===
庶幾焉耳其視周之默契道體固為不同
張因范公勸讀中庸歸而求之久乃有得
與程之一見即悟者抑亦異矣然朱子承
命帝齋稟學延平以上泝濂洛之淵源則
周程之道朱實承之故朱子記周之祠有
上接洙泗下啓河洛之語其於學庸孟子
止言程子則以周之圖書專明易學而註
述未及於三書故耳豈謂周之學有異於
程哉周子之寓江西當時若歐陽脩曾鞏
punctuated: 盛於堯舜，大成於孔子，至孟子而中絕焉。有宋周程朱子起而承之。周子生于春陵，南方之人也，而程子受學於南安，故「吾與點也」之意，遂得於心領之餘。程子生於河洛，北方之人也，而楊中立從學於潁昌，故「吾道南矣」之歎，遂發於目送之際。楊之再傳，復得朱子以集諸儒之大成焉。「周范造詣固殊，程張契悟亦異」，此朱子荅或人之問也。盖范文正之極高明而道中庸，不過庶幾焉耳，其視周之默契道體，固為不同。張因范公勸讀《中庸》，歸而求之，久乃有得，與程之一見即悟者，抑亦異矣。然朱子承命帝齋，稟學延平，以上泝濂洛之淵源，則周程之道，朱實承之。故朱子記周之祠，有「上接洙泗，下啓河洛」之語。其於《學》《庸》《孟子》止言程子，則以周之圖書專明易學，而註述未及於三書故耳。豈謂周之學有異於程哉？周子之寓江西，當時若歐陽脩、曾鞏
translation_en:
…flourished under Yao and Shun, reached its fullest expression in Confucius, and was interrupted after Mencius. In the Song dynasty, Masters Zhou, Cheng, and Zhu arose to carry it on. Master Zhou was born in Chunling and was a southerner, while Master Cheng studied under him in Nan’an. Thus Cheng came to grasp the meaning of “I am with Dian” through inward understanding. Master Cheng was born in the He–Luo region and was a northerner, while Yang Zhongli studied under him in Yingchang. Thus, as he watched Yang depart, he exclaimed, “My Way is going south!” Two generations of transmission after Yang, Master Zhu emerged to bring the achievements of the various scholars to their fullest synthesis.

“Zhou and Fan certainly differed in their attainments, and Cheng and Zhang also differed in their intuitive understanding”: this was Master Zhu’s answer to someone’s question. For Fan Wenzheng’s attainment of “reaching the utmost loftiness and brilliance while following the Mean” was no more than an approximation. It was certainly different from Zhou’s tacit apprehension of the substance of the Way. At Lord Fan’s urging, Zhang read the Doctrine of the Mean; he returned home and investigated it, gaining understanding only after a long time. This, too, differed from Cheng’s immediate comprehension upon first encountering it.

Yet Master Zhu “received a command at the imperial study” [?] and received instruction from Yanping, thereby tracing the teaching back to its sources in Lian and Luo. Thus Zhu truly inherited the Way of Zhou and Cheng. Hence, in his account of Zhou’s shrine, Master Zhu wrote that Zhou “connected above with the tradition of the Zhu and Si rivers and opened the way below for that of the He and Luo rivers.” That he mentioned only Master Cheng in connection with the Great Learning, the Doctrine of the Mean, and the Mencius was simply because Zhou’s diagram and writings were devoted to elucidating the learning of the Changes, and his commentaries had not extended to those three books. How could this mean that Zhou’s learning differed from Cheng’s? During Master Zhou’s residence in Jiangxi, such contemporaries as Ouyang Xiu and Zeng Gong…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
黃庭堅李覯各以文學鳴而於性命之說
未肯降心以從其始從終背又有若王安
石者此無他所志異也朱子宦遊南康往
來饒信諸郡士遊其門者甚衆嘗與象山
陸氏胥會鵝湖屢相問辨而卒未能會其
說于一者此無他所見異也雖然庭堅遊
于蘇門而光風霽月之贊乃善形容周子
之氣象吳澄主於陸學而元亨利貞之論
乃獨係屬朱子之統緒斯道之中正公論
===
在人不可誣也彼所見所志之異者烏能
與於斯哉嗟夫道統之傳絕於千載而續
於一時或自南而北或自北而南遠近見
聞不啻符契此皆係於天焉非人之所能
為也若夫所志所見之異而不能以強同
者雖由乎人而亦豈非天哉愚也有志於
道方欲上師古人而未知所從敢因明問
而請質焉惟進而教之幸甚
第三問
punctuated:
黃庭堅、李覯各以文學鳴，而於性命之說，未肯降心以從。其始從終背，又有若王安石者。此無他，所志異也。朱子宦遊南康，往來饒信諸郡，士遊其門者甚衆。嘗與象山陸氏胥會鵝湖，屢相問辨，而卒未能會其說于一者，此無他，所見異也。雖然，庭堅遊于蘇門，而光風霽月之贊，乃善形容周子之氣象；吳澄主於陸學，而元亨利貞之論，乃獨係屬朱子之統緒。斯道之中正，公論在人，不可誣也。彼所見所志之異者，烏能與於斯哉！
嗟夫！道統之傳，絕於千載而續於一時。或自南而北，或自北而南，遠近見聞，不啻符契。此皆係於天焉，非人之所能為也。若夫所志所見之異而不能以強同者，雖由乎人，而亦豈非天哉！愚也有志於道，方欲上師古人，而未知所從。敢因明問而請質焉，惟進而教之，幸甚！
第三問
translation_en:
… Huang Tingjian and Li Gou each won renown for literary learning, yet were unwilling to humble themselves and follow the teaching on human nature and destiny. There were also men such as Wang Anshi, who followed it at first but ultimately turned away. This was for no other reason than that their aspirations differed. Master Zhu held office in Nankang and traveled among the prefectures of Raozhou, Xinzhou, and elsewhere; very many scholars studied under him. He once met with Lu Xiangshan at Ehu. They repeatedly questioned and debated one another, yet ultimately could not bring their teachings into agreement. This was for no other reason than that their views differed. Nevertheless, although Tingjian studied in Su Shi’s circle, his praise of Master Zhou as a “clear breeze and a moon emerging after rain” aptly conveyed Zhou’s bearing. Although Wu Cheng adhered to Lu’s learning, his discussion of “the origin, free course, benefit, and steadfastness” attached the succession of the Way exclusively to Master Zhu. That this Way is balanced and correct is a matter of public judgment lodged in people’s hearts; it cannot be misrepresented. How could those whose views and aspirations diverged have a part in this?
Alas! The transmission of the succession of the Way was broken for a thousand years and then renewed within a single age. Some teachings passed from south to north, others from north to south; what was seen and heard, far and near, matched like the halves of a tally. All this depended upon Heaven; it was beyond human powers to accomplish. As for differences in aspirations and views that cannot be forcibly reconciled, although they arise from human beings, are they not also due to Heaven? I, in my ignorance, aspire to the Way and now wish to take the ancients as my teachers, yet do not know whom to follow. Emboldened by your discerning question, I venture to seek your judgment. I would count it a great fortune if you would lead me forward and instruct me!
Third Policy Question

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
李文潔
同考試官教諭林批能言之士踈而陋大而誇亦
習弊也此篇詞氣渾厚於鄉邦人物感慨抑揚而意
思含蓄不暴末復以神明之機存乎人乃根本之論
況餘策皆偉譬之人入海探珠徑寸先得奇寶有
所歸矣
同考試官學正章批道德風俗卓有定見而士
夫人物歷舉不遺豈嘗誦其書而追慕其人者歟
考試官教諭黃批考據詳悉鋪敘整嚴策
===
學鮮有其儷
考試官學正韓批議論風俗由道德又推原
其本在
朝廷其機在士夫識為有見
道有升降政由俗革風化之本在朝廷其
儀不忒正是四國風化之機在士夫蓋上
有所好下必有甚焉者矣況朝廷者四方
之根本士夫者鄉國之領袖轉移感動豈
非影響之必然哉粵自先王之時以民之
punctuated:
李文潔

同考試官教諭林批：能言之士，踈而陋，大而誇，亦習弊也。此篇詞氣渾厚，於鄉邦人物感慨抑揚，而意思含蓄不暴。末復以神明之機存乎人，乃根本之論。況餘策皆偉，譬之人入海探珠，徑寸先得，奇寶有所歸矣。

同考試官學正章批：道德風俗，卓有定見，而士夫人物歷舉不遺，豈嘗誦其書而追慕其人者歟？

考試官教諭黃批：考據詳悉，鋪敘整嚴，策學鮮有其儷。

考試官學正韓批：議論風俗由道德，又推原其本在朝廷，其機在士夫，識為有見。

道有升降，政由俗革。風化之本在朝廷，「其儀不忒，正是四國」；風化之機在士夫，蓋「上有所好，下必有甚焉者矣」。況朝廷者，四方之根本；士夫者，鄉國之領袖。轉移感動，豈非影響之必然哉？粵自先王之時，以民之
translation_en:
Li Wenjie

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Men skilled in argument may be superficial and crude, grandiose and boastful: these too are habitual faults. This essay’s language and spirit are full and substantial. In discussing the figures of his native region, the writer expresses deep feeling, with praise and censure, yet keeps his meaning implicit rather than exposing it bluntly. At the end he further argues that the motive power of spiritual illumination resides in human beings—an argument that reaches the root of the matter. Moreover, his other policy essays are all outstanding. It is like someone diving into the sea for pearls and obtaining at once one an inch across: a rare treasure has found its possessor.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: On morality and customs, he has notably firm judgments, and he enumerates the individual scholar-officials without omission. Surely he has read their writings and looked back upon these men with admiration?

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: His examination of sources is detailed and thorough, and his exposition orderly and rigorous. Few can rival his learning in policy essays.

Comment by Examiner Han, Instructor: He argues that customs derive from morality, then further traces their origin: their foundation lies in the imperial court, and their motive power lies in the scholar-officials. His understanding shows insight.

The Way rises and declines; governance changes with customs. The foundation of moral transformation lies in the imperial court: “With his deportment free from error, he rectifies the states in all four quarters.” The motive power of moral transformation lies in the scholar-officials, for “Whatever those above favor, those below will invariably pursue still more ardently.” Moreover, the imperial court is the foundation of all four quarters, and the scholar-officials are the leaders of their localities and the realm. Are not the changes and responses they bring about as inevitable as shadows and echoes? From the time of the former kings, because the people’s …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
視聽不可不一上之好惡不可不示也於
是教民以五禮六樂無異教也道王之德
意志慮無異政也通其貨財同其度量無
異尚也除其所怨同其所好無異情也道
四方之政和上下之志無異心也齊道德
一風俗者如此自秦以來始皇變詐峻刻
而民俗薄漢高政制易俗而民俗厚孝武
好大喜功而民俗壷孝宣綜核名實而民
俗實魏晉賤守節樂清曠而民俗浮唐太
===
宗約已治人崇儒重道而民俗醇宋承五
代之弊深仁厚澤涵養天下其俗之仁厚
又自不言可知矣升降因革循環無端固
皆上之化也若夫縣無復盜實感太丘二
絹之遺路不拾遺又激彥方一布之惠陽
城行古道居晉鄙薰德而善良者幾千人
李善存孤兒隱山陽感行而脩義者遍閭
里此又士大夫之立身行義風範乎鄉者
也江右控引荆越襟帶江湖山川特秀人
punctuated:
視聽不可不一，上之好惡不可不示也。於是教民以五禮六樂，無異教也；道王之德意志慮，無異政也；通其貨財，同其度量，無異尚也；除其所怨，同其所好，無異情也；道四方之政，和上下之志，無異心也。齊道德、一風俗者如此。自秦以來，始皇變詐峻刻，而民俗薄；漢高政制易俗，而民俗厚；孝武好大喜功，而民俗壷；孝宣綜核名實，而民俗實；魏晉賤守節，樂清曠，而民俗浮；唐太宗約已治人，崇儒重道，而民俗醇。宋承五代之弊，深仁厚澤涵養天下，其俗之仁厚，又自不言可知矣。升降因革，循環無端，固皆上之化也。
若夫縣無復盜，實感太丘二絹之遺；路不拾遺，又激彥方一布之惠。陽城行古道，居晉鄙，薰德而善良者幾千人；李善存孤兒，隱山陽，感行而脩義者遍閭里。此又士大夫之立身行義，風範乎鄉者也。
江右控引荆越，襟帶江湖，山川特秀，人
translation_en:
…what the people saw and heard had to be made uniform, and the likes and dislikes of those above had to be made manifest. Thus, the people were taught through the five rites and six kinds of music, so that instruction did not differ; the king’s virtuous intentions and purposes were conveyed, so that government did not differ; goods and wealth were circulated and weights and measures standardized, so that what people esteemed did not differ; what they resented was removed and what they cherished brought into accord, so that their feelings did not differ; government throughout the realm was guided and the intentions of superiors and inferiors harmonized, so that their minds did not differ. Such were the means of bringing morality into accord and unifying customs. From the Qin onward, the First Emperor was deceitful and harsh, and popular customs became mean. Gaozu of Han transformed customs through his governmental institutions, and popular customs became generous. Emperor Xiaowu delighted in grand undertakings and achievements, and popular customs became [壷: unclear, ?]. Emperor Xiaoxuan comprehensively examined names against realities, and popular customs became substantial. Under the Wei and Jin, steadfast integrity was disparaged and untrammeled aloofness prized, and popular customs became frivolous. Taizong of Tang restrained himself in governing others, honored Confucian learning, and esteemed the Way, and popular customs became pure. Inheriting the abuses of the Five Dynasties, the Song nurtured the realm with profound benevolence and abundant beneficence. That its customs were humane and generous is evident without further explanation. Through rise and decline, continuity and change, the cycle had no end: all this was assuredly the transforming influence of those above.
As for the disappearance of theft from a county, this was truly inspired by the gift of two lengths of silk from the Magistrate of Taiqiu; that people left lost articles untouched on the road was likewise prompted by Yanfang’s kindness in giving a length of cloth. Yang Cheng practiced the ancient Way while living in a remote district of Jin; nearly a thousand people became good through the influence of his virtue. Li Shan preserved an orphan’s life and lived in seclusion in Shanyang; throughout the neighborhoods, people were moved by his conduct to cultivate righteousness. These, in turn, exemplify how scholar-officials established their character and practiced righteousness, setting a moral example for their communities.
Jiangyou commands the approaches to Jing and Yue and is girdled by rivers and lakes. Its mountains and rivers are exceptionally beautiful, and its people…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
物萃止服德當時思賢異世南州高士徐
孺子也完節先朝血食後代宋室忠臣文
信公也彭龜年當僞學之禁不以流俗而
變劉安世傷羨餘之諷遂以設教而歸歟
君子之文學道德所以端鄉國之習者固
已久矣久則難變也何者人情安於所習
而駭於所未見商君廢井田民怨固也王
莽復井田而民亦怨武靈王變華效胡民
怨固也魏孝文變胡效華而民亦怨習素
善驅之惡不能入猶習素惡驅之善不能
變也然則江右道風文物諸先正之功不
誣而鼓鑄鑪冶則
聖朝之化斯賴生斯世居斯鄉作者不無人焉
然未敢為執事道也
===
第四問
徐盈
同考試官訓導孟　批　策場浩如望洋辭難窮究
此作考證古今沿革之異評訂功用次第之詳古稱
punctuated:
物萃止，服德當時，思賢異世，南州高士徐孺子也；完節先朝，血食後代，宋室忠臣文信公也。彭龜年當僞學之禁，不以流俗而變；劉安世傷羨餘之諷，遂以設教而歸歟？君子之文學道德，所以端鄉國之習者，固已久矣。久則難變也。何者？人情安於所習，而駭於所未見。商君廢井田，民怨固也；王莽復井田，而民亦怨。武靈王變華效胡，民怨固也；魏孝文變胡效華，而民亦怨。習素善，驅之惡不能入，猶習素惡，驅之善不能變也。然則江右道風文物，諸先正之功不誣，而鼓鑄鑪冶，則聖朝之化斯賴。生斯世，居斯鄉，作者不無人焉，然未敢為執事道也。

第四問
徐盈

同考試官訓導孟批：策場浩如望洋，辭難窮究。此作考證古今沿革之異，評訂功用次第之詳。古稱
translation_en:
…men of distinction gather here. He whose virtue commanded respect in his own time and whose worth was remembered in later ages was Xu Ruzi, the eminent scholar of the southern region. He who preserved his integrity under the former dynasty and received sacrificial offerings in later generations was Lord Wen, Duke of Xin, a loyal minister of the Song ruling house. Peng Guinian, during the prohibition of “false learning,” did not change with prevailing opinion. Liu Anshi, distressed by the admonition concerning surplus revenues [?], thereupon returned to devote himself to teaching, did he not? The literary learning and moral virtue of these gentlemen have long served to rectify the customs of their native region. What has endured long is difficult to change. Why? Human feelings are comfortable with the familiar and alarmed by what they have never seen. When Lord Shang abolished the well-field system, popular resentment was understandable; yet when Wang Mang restored it, the people also resented this. When King Wuling changed Chinese ways to imitate those of the Hu, popular resentment was understandable; yet when Emperor Xiaowen of Wei changed Hu ways to imitate Chinese ones, the people also resented this. Where established habits are good, efforts to drive people toward evil cannot take hold, just as, where established habits are evil, efforts to drive people toward goodness cannot change them. Thus, the contributions of former worthies to the moral traditions and cultural achievements of Jiangyou are undeniable; yet their continued molding and refinement depend upon the transforming influence of our sagely dynasty. Among those born in this age and dwelling in this region, there are indeed people who carry this work forward, but I have not presumed to speak of them to you, honored examiner.

Fourth Question
Xu Ying

This composition examines and verifies differences in institutional continuity and change between antiquity and the present, and assesses in detail their practical effects and order of development. title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
子產博物君子吾子殆庶幾乎
考試官教諭黄　批　文勢遒健獨超衆作其叅
華峯巔忽見秋隼者歟
考試官學正韓　批　随筆條荅叙事不遺策學
沉潛之密如此頗覺良工心獨苦矣
考法制於三代之前必求其意議法制於
三代之後不必泥其迹盖必求其意者道
之同也不如是不足以經世也不必泥其
迹者世之異也世既異矣而嘐嘐然惟以
===
復古為事吾見迂緩濶畧治終不可得而
致也善經世者固如是哉執事舉三代之
法制以問諸生盖欲激昂其經世之志而
申儆乎流俗之陋意甚盛矣雖不敏敢不
承乎盖嘗觀古之為國者有井田以為養
有封建以為治有學校以為教有肉刑以
為禁其於學也侯明賓興所以取士受成
獻馘所以論政春秋禮樂有事於絃冬夏
詩書有事於誦此皆堯舜禹湯文武之所
punctuated:
子產博物君子，吾子殆庶幾乎！
考試官教諭黄批：文勢遒健，獨超衆作，其叅華峯巔忽見秋隼者歟？
考試官學正韓批：随筆條荅，叙事不遺，策學沉潛之密如此，頗覺良工心獨苦矣。
考法制於三代之前，必求其意；議法制於三代之後，不必泥其迹。盖必求其意者，道之同也，不如是不足以經世也；不必泥其迹者，世之異也。世既異矣，而嘐嘐然惟以復古為事，吾見迂緩濶畧，治終不可得而致也。善經世者固如是哉？執事舉三代之法制以問諸生，盖欲激昂其經世之志，而申儆乎流俗之陋，意甚盛矣。雖不敏，敢不承乎？盖嘗觀古之為國者，有井田以為養，有封建以為治，有學校以為教，有肉刑以為禁。其於學也，侯明賓興，所以取士；受成獻馘，所以論政；春秋禮樂，有事於絃；冬夏詩書，有事於誦。此皆堯舜禹湯文武之所
translation_en:
… Zichan was a gentleman of broad learning; you, sir, surely come close to him!
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: The writing has vigorous momentum and stands alone above the other submissions. Is it like climbing to the summit of Mount Hua [?] and suddenly seeing an autumn falcon?
Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: The points are answered in sequence as the brush moves, and no matters are omitted from the account. Such thoroughness in the deep study underlying this policy essay makes one keenly appreciate the painstaking effort known only to the skilled craftsman.
In examining laws and institutions before the Three Dynasties, one must seek their intent; in discussing laws and institutions after the Three Dynasties, one need not cling to their outward forms. One must seek their intent because the Way remains the same: without doing so, one cannot order the world. One need not cling to their outward forms because the times differ. When the times have changed, if one grandly proclaims that restoring antiquity is one's sole concern, I foresee impractical delays and sweeping omissions; good government will ultimately remain unattainable. Is this truly how those skilled in ordering the world proceed? You, sir, have put the laws and institutions of the Three Dynasties before us students as a question, surely wishing to stir our ambition to order the world and to renew your admonitions against the shortcomings of prevailing custom. Your intention is most generous. Though I am slow of understanding, how could I dare not respond?
I have observed that those who governed states in antiquity had the well-field system to provide sustenance, the enfeoffment system to provide government, schools to provide instruction, and mutilating punishments to enforce prohibitions. As for their schools, through ‘hou ming’ [?] and the ceremonial honoring and recommendation of worthy men, they selected men for service; through receiving completed plans and presenting the severed ears of slain enemies, they assessed government. In spring and autumn, rites and music involved practice on stringed instruments; in winter and summer, the Odes and Documents involved recitation. These were all what Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
講畫而施行者其為法制盖精且備矣迨
秦孝公開阡陌始皇置郡縣漢文景用晉
定令於是井田封建肉刑三者俱廢而學
校僅存然博士弟子員之設止為經訓則
絃與論政取士者又廢此宋蘇軾有感焉
而發於南安軍之學記也然軾之時學校
未遍於天下其所論亦未能如今日經說
之歸一則今之時稍異於軾之時矣然士
非進取不由學校學校非科舉之文則不
===
論也抑豈先王之遺意哉必也學校之中
惟以成德達材為務讀書為文專於明理
以適世用痛抑浮鑿之習則今之學即古
之學今之論即古之論矣所當致力者在
此而已若夫絃與取士論政既難復古而
所謂井田封建肉刑其勢又有甚難者亦
何必論其緩急先後哉然井田廢矣而唐
高祖有口分世業之令董仲舒有限田之
請封建廢矣而漢宣帝有政平訟理之託
punctuated: 講畫而施行者，其為法制盖精且備矣。迨秦孝公開阡陌，始皇置郡縣，漢文景用晉定令，於是井田、封建、肉刑三者俱廢，而學校僅存。然博士弟子員之設，止為經訓，則絃與論政、取士者又廢。此宋蘇軾有感焉，而發於南安軍之學記也。然軾之時，學校未遍於天下，其所論亦未能如今日經說之歸一，則今之時稍異於軾之時矣。然士非進取不由學校，學校非科舉之文則不論也，抑豈先王之遺意哉？必也學校之中，惟以成德達材為務，讀書為文，專於明理，以適世用，痛抑浮鑿之習，則今之學即古之學，今之論即古之論矣。所當致力者，在此而已。若夫絃與取士、論政，既難復古，而所謂井田、封建、肉刑，其勢又有甚難者，亦何必論其緩急先後哉？然井田廢矣，而唐高祖有口分世業之令，董仲舒有限田之請；封建廢矣，而漢宣帝有政平訟理之託。
translation_en:
…planned and put into practice. Their laws and institutions were indeed refined and comprehensive. When Duke Xiao of Qin opened up the field boundaries, the First Emperor established commanderies and counties, and Emperors Wen and Jing of Han employed the ordinances established by Jin [?], the well-field system, hereditary enfeoffment, and mutilating punishments were all abolished; only the schools survived. Yet the establishment of student places under the Erudites served only instruction in the Classics, while musical instruction on stringed instruments, deliberation on government, and the selection of worthy men were also abandoned. Su Shi of the Song was moved by this and expressed his thoughts in his Record of the School of Nan'an Military Prefecture. In Su Shi’s time, however, schools had not yet spread throughout the realm, nor had the matters he discussed reached the present-day uniformity of interpretations of the Classics. Our own time thus differs somewhat from his. Yet men enter schools only to seek advancement, and schools discuss only compositions for the civil-service examinations. Can this really preserve the intentions of the former kings?

Within the schools, the sole task must be to perfect virtue and develop talent. Reading and composition must concentrate on clarifying principles so as to meet the practical needs of the world, and habits of superficiality and strained interpretation must be firmly checked. Then the learning of today will be the learning of antiquity, and the discussions of today will be the discussions of antiquity. This alone is where effort should be directed. As for musical instruction on stringed instruments, the selection of worthy men, and deliberation on government, restoring ancient practices is already difficult; circumstances make the restoration of the well-field system, hereditary enfeoffment, and mutilating punishments still more difficult. Why, then, must we discuss their relative urgency or the order in which to restore them? Nevertheless, although the well-field system was abolished, Emperor Gaozu of Tang issued ordinances concerning per-capita allotments and hereditary holdings, and Dong Zhongshu proposed limiting landholdings. Although hereditary enfeoffment was abolished, Emperor Xuan of Han entrusted officials with ensuring equitable government and the proper adjudication of lawsuits…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
柳子厚有擇守之論肉刑廢矣而釋之有
不信之對王通有無赦之言取士雖廢而
朱子議貢舉在通經史論政雖廢而程子
詳學制在勵風俗至於絃雖廢而陽城有
忠孝之訓韓子有傳道受業解惑之說皆
得乎先王之遺意者誠取其意而行之則
不必更張而治可復三代之盛豈但如吾
前所謂學校與誦而已哉夫孔子大聖也
而用必從乎周禮孟子大賢也而論不必
===
合於周制然其經世之志固各有在矣故
君子論事以是謂之善論處事以是謂之
善處惟夫不知本於道而苟以狥世者則
非君子所貴也豈敢瀆於高明哉謹對
第五問　劉節
同考試官教諭徐　批〔備邊一策〕
國之大計書生能備畫之是見平日之留心時務矣
同考試官教諭李　批〔此策於古名將之成功今備〕
punctuated:
柳子厚有擇守之論。肉刑廢矣，而釋之有不信之對，王通有無赦之言。取士雖廢，而朱子議貢舉，在通經史；論政雖廢，而程子詳學制，在勵風俗。至於絃雖廢，而陽城有忠孝之訓，韓子有傳道受業解惑之說，皆得乎先王之遺意者。誠取其意而行之，則不必更張，而治可復三代之盛，豈但如吾前所謂學校與誦而已哉！夫孔子大聖也，而用必從乎周禮；孟子大賢也，而論不必合於周制。然其經世之志，固各有在矣。故君子論事以是，謂之善論；處事以是，謂之善處。惟夫不知本於道，而苟以狥世者，則非君子所貴也。豈敢瀆於高明哉！謹對。

第五問　劉節

同考試官教諭徐　批〔備邊一策〕國之大計，書生能備畫之，是見平日之留心時務矣。

同考試官教諭李　批〔此策於古名將之成功、今備〕
translation_en:
…Liu Zihou offered a discourse on selecting prefects. Mutilating punishments have been abolished, yet Shizhi gave his reply concerning the breach of trust, and Wang Tong spoke of granting no pardons. Although the ancient system of selecting officials has fallen out of use, Master Zhu, in discussing recommendation and examination, emphasized mastery of the Classics and histories. Although the ancient practice of discussing government has fallen out of use, Master Cheng, in elaborating a school system, emphasized improving customs. As for instruction through string music [?], although it has fallen out of use, Yang Cheng taught loyalty and filial devotion, and Master Han spoke of transmitting the Way, imparting learning, and resolving doubts. All these captured something of the intentions bequeathed by the former kings. If we sincerely grasp those intentions and put them into practice, government can recover the flourishing condition of the Three Dynasties without wholesale institutional change. How could this apply merely to the schools and recitation [?] I mentioned earlier? Confucius was a great sage, and in practice he insisted on following Zhou ritual. Mencius was a great worthy, yet his arguments did not necessarily accord with Zhou institutions. Nevertheless, each had his own purpose in seeking to order the world. Thus, when a gentleman discusses affairs on this basis, it is called sound discussion; when he handles affairs on this basis, it is called sound conduct. Those who do not understand that they must take the Way as their foundation, but merely follow the fashions of their age, are not esteemed by gentlemen. How would I dare trouble your enlightened judgment with such views? Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fifth Question — Liu Jie

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: 〔This policy essay on frontier defense〕 concerns a great matter of state. That a scholar can plan it comprehensively shows his habitual attention to current affairs.
