title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
邊之意務敷揚條畫殆盡其文事武備之究意者乎
同考試官學正楊　批〔毛錐子秀才不出鄉國於邊事已能博古知今區畫布置綽有可採他日若得用事閫外必能羯胡北奔慄慄危懼而不敢南〕
嚮牧馬
考試官教諭黃　批〔此樣策手非胸中有甲兵者不能〕
考試官學正韓　批〔識時務者在俊傑豈可謂舉子中無人〕
===
中國之有夷狄猶君子之有小人此氣化
之自然而古今之所不能免也然君子之
去小人不可以無法而中國之禦夷狄不
可以無策故王者畧其治而春秋謹其辨
焉辨之以必辨治之以不治我
聖祖謹備胡戎之訓豈不遠出前代之策而並
駕乎帝王也哉竊嘗仰窺
祖訓之意若謂有必備之國蓋胡戎之近西北
者有不征之國蓋朝鮮安南琉球日本之
punctuated:
邊之意，務敷揚條畫殆盡，其文事武備之究意者乎？
同考試官學正楊，批〔毛錐子秀才，不出鄉國，於邊事已能博古知今，區畫布置，綽有可採。他日若得用事閫外，必能羯胡北奔，慄慄危懼而不敢南〕嚮牧馬。
考試官教諭黃，批〔此樣策手，非胸中有甲兵者不能。〕
考試官學正韓，批〔識時務者在俊傑，豈可謂舉子中無人？〕
中國之有夷狄，猶君子之有小人，此氣化之自然，而古今之所不能免也。然君子之去小人，不可以無法；而中國之禦夷狄，不可以無策。故王者畧其治，而春秋謹其辨焉。辨之以必辨，治之以不治。我聖祖謹備胡戎之訓，豈不遠出前代之策，而並駕乎帝王也哉？竊嘗仰窺祖訓之意，若謂有必備之國，蓋胡戎之近西北者；有不征之國，蓋朝鮮、安南、琉球、日本之
translation_en:
…the intent of frontier defense, striving to expound and set out its measures almost exhaustively. Is he perhaps one who has thoroughly grasped civil affairs and military preparedness?
Associate Examiner Yang, an Instructor, comments: “This scholar wielding a writing brush has never left his native region, yet in frontier affairs he already possesses broad knowledge of antiquity and an understanding of the present. His plans and dispositions offer much worth adopting. If someday he should exercise military command beyond the gates, he will surely make the Jie and Hu flee northward, trembling in fear and not daring to turn south to pasture their horses.”
Examiner Huang, an Instructor, comments: “Only someone with armies arrayed in his mind could write a policy essay like this.”
Examiner Han, an Instructor, comments: “Those who understand the affairs of their time are outstanding talents. How can anyone say there are no capable men among the examination candidates?”
That the Central Kingdom has Yi and Di barbarians is like the fact that gentlemen have petty men: this arises naturally from the transformations of vital energy and has been unavoidable throughout antiquity and the present. Yet gentlemen cannot dispense with methods for removing petty men, and the Central Kingdom cannot dispense with strategies for defending against the Yi and Di. Thus the true king leaves their governance unattended, while the Spring and Autumn Annals carefully maintains the distinction between them and us. Distinguish them by insisting upon that distinction; govern them by leaving them ungoverned. Do not our Sagely Progenitor’s instructions to guard vigilantly against the Hu and Rong far surpass the strategies of earlier dynasties and rank alongside those of the ancient emperors and kings?
I have ventured to examine reverently the meaning of the Ancestral Instructions. They seem to say that there are states against which defenses must be maintained—namely, the Hu and Rong close to the northwest—and states that must not be attacked, namely such countries as Chaoxian, Annan, Liuqiu, and Riben …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
屬在東與南者其備胡戎則曰選將練兵
而不及乎他烏乎無怠無荒四夷來王帝
王自治之策莫過於此我
聖祖蓋得之矣故嘗考之古人謂周之薄伐為
得中策漢之出師為得下策秦之築城以
撤中國則為無策者嚴尤之論也謂周之
惠綏為得上策秦之設險為得中策漢之
和親以輕中國則為無策者此宋祁之論
也然祁之論周漢是也以秦之策為中則
===
非矣尤之論周漢非也以秦之策為無則
是矣祁識尤辨而未詳愚謂祁亦詳而未
當何則周之薄伐惠綏政有合於
聖祖乃或以為中而顧取於秦漢之事此所以
互有得失也今燕薊以西甘凉以東大鎮
數十小鎮數百
聖祖之所謹備者蓋在於此棄何承平以來邊
事日廢其為將者求如趙之李牧漢之周
亞夫趙充國唐之李晟李德裕宋之韓琦
punctuated:
屬，在東與南者。其備胡戎，則曰選將練兵，而不及乎他。烏乎！無怠無荒，四夷來王，帝王自治之策莫過於此，我聖祖蓋得之矣。故嘗考之，古人謂周之薄伐為得中策，漢之出師為得下策，秦之築城以撤中國則為無策者，嚴尤之論也。謂周之惠綏為得上策，秦之設險為得中策，漢之和親以輕中國則為無策者，此宋祁之論也。然祁之論周漢，是也；以秦之策為中，則非矣。尤之論周漢，非也；以秦之策為無，則是矣。祁識尤辨而未詳，愚謂祁亦詳而未當。何則？周之薄伐惠綏，政有合於聖祖，乃或以為中，而顧取於秦漢之事，此所以互有得失也。
今燕薊以西、甘凉以東，大鎮數十，小鎮數百，聖祖之所謹備者，蓋在於此。棄何承平以來，邊事日廢，其為將者，求如趙之李牧、漢之周亞夫、趙充國、唐之李晟、李德裕、宋之韓琦，
translation_en:
…and the like, situated to the east and south. As for guarding against the Hu and Rong, the injunction speaks only of selecting generals and training troops, without extending to other measures. Ah! “Be neither negligent nor idle, and the barbarians of the four quarters will come to acknowledge your kingship.” No policy by which emperors and kings put their own realms in order surpasses this. Our Sagely Progenitor surely grasped it.
I have examined the judgments of earlier writers. That Zhou’s limited punitive expeditions constituted a middling policy, that Han’s dispatch of armies constituted an inferior policy, and that Qin’s construction of walls, thereby weakening [?] the Central Realm, amounted to having no policy at all—this was Yan You’s argument. That Zhou’s benevolent pacification constituted the best policy, that Qin’s establishment of defensive barriers constituted a middling policy, and that Han’s marriage alliances, which diminished the standing of the Central Realm, amounted to having no policy at all—this was Song Qi’s argument. Yet Qi’s judgments of Zhou and Han were correct, while his ranking of Qin’s policy as middling was wrong. You’s judgments of Zhou and Han were wrong, while his assessment that Qin had no policy was correct. Qi considered You discerning but insufficiently thorough; in my humble view, Qi too was thorough without being sound. Why? Zhou’s limited punitive expeditions and benevolent pacification were policies consonant with those of our Sagely Progenitor. Yet some ranked them as merely middling and instead approved the practices of Qin or Han. This is why each judgment had both merits and faults.
Today, west of Yan and Ji and east of Gan and Liang, there are scores of large garrisons and hundreds of small ones. These are surely the places where our Sagely Progenitor took particular care to maintain defenses. Yet how is it [?] that, during the long peace, frontier affairs have fallen into increasing neglect? Among those serving as generals, if we seek men like Li Mu of Zhao; Zhou Yafu and Zhao Chongguo of Han; Li Sheng and Li Deyu of Tang; and Han Qi of Song…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
范仲淹者既不可得則稽閱為擾召募為
玩安輯之而愈愈逃閑習之而愈愈惰鼓作之
而愈怯亦無足怪者必也求之於貪縁奔
走之外試之以古今常變之畧儲之於位
望未隆之時難之以卒然難應之機用之
於羽檄交馳之地志於忠義者則感之以
忠信志於富貴者則歆之以爵禄重以專
制之權嚴以失律之法論出于衆制掌於
一而它無與焉則必有若人者出乎尋常
===
而成功豈不可責與蓋既有一韓一范之
望而加之以充國取勝之計亞夫不聞詔
之威平時運德裕之籌當事圖李晟之備
則牧之所謂戰守者有不足為矣雖然稽
閱召募不可偏廢而習藝作氣之方當自
安輯始今之邊將誠無科率之煩使屯操
之人歲有實賜月無虚支由是以稽則實
以閱則精以召募則得藝不習而自閑氣
不鼓而自作守固戰克何憂乎胡戎之侵
punctuated: 范仲淹者既不可得，則稽閱為擾，召募為玩，安輯之而愈愈逃，閑習之而愈愈惰，鼓作之而愈怯，亦無足怪者。必也求之於貪縁奔走之外，試之以古今常變之畧，儲之於位望未隆之時，難之以卒然難應之機，用之於羽檄交馳之地。志於忠義者，則感之以忠信；志於富貴者，則歆之以爵禄。重以專制之權，嚴以失律之法，論出于衆，制掌於一，而它無與焉，則必有若人者出乎尋常，而成功豈不可責與？蓋既有一韓一范之望，而加之以充國取勝之計、亞夫不聞詔之威，平時運德裕之籌，當事圖李晟之備，則牧之所謂戰守者，有不足為矣。雖然，稽閱召募不可偏廢，而習藝作氣之方，當自安輯始。今之邊將誠無科率之煩，使屯操之人歲有實賜，月無虚支，由是以稽則實，以閱則精，以召募則得，藝不習而自閑，氣不鼓而自作，守固戰克，何憂乎胡戎之侵
translation_en:
…or Fan Zhongyan cannot be found, then inspections and musters become harassment, and recruitment becomes a sham. Attempts to settle and reassure the troops only make them desert all the more [?]; training only makes them more idle [?]; efforts to rouse their spirits only make them more timid. None of this is surprising. One must seek such commanders outside the ranks of those who greedily pursue connections and advancement, test them on strategies for ordinary and exceptional circumstances past and present, and hold them in reserve before their rank and reputation have risen high. Challenge them with sudden situations difficult to meet, and employ them where urgent military dispatches fly back and forth. Those whose aspirations lie in loyalty and righteousness should be moved by loyalty and trustworthiness; those who aspire to wealth and distinction should be attracted by rank and emoluments. Reinforce their position with authority to act independently, and impose strict penalties for breaches of military discipline. Let deliberation proceed from many, but control rest with one, with no interference from others. Then men of this kind will surely rise above the ordinary; could success not be demanded of them?

Once there is a commander with the prestige of a Han Qi or a Fan Zhongyan, give him also Zhao Chongguo’s plans for victory and Zhou Yafu’s commanding authority in declining to heed an imperial edict. In peacetime, let him apply Li Deyu’s strategic calculations; when action is required, let him arrange preparations like Li Sheng’s. Then even what Li Mu called fighting and defending would be no difficult undertaking. Nevertheless, neither inspections and musters nor recruitment may be neglected. The methods of training skills and raising morale must begin with settling and reassuring the troops. If today’s frontier commanders truly ceased troubling them with levies and exactions, so that those engaged in garrison farming and military drill received actual grants each year and their monthly disbursements were not merely on paper, then inspections would disclose real strength, musters would reveal well-trained troops, and recruitment would obtain suitable men. Their skills would become proficient without drilling, and their spirits would rise without exhortation. With defenses secure and battles won, why fear incursions by the Hu and Rong…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
何釐乎
九重西北之顧哉此所謂不治之治必辨之
辨我
聖祖之謨畧眞帝王之上策也抑又念之駿求
千金芟畜三年今之選將急矣而食也器
也馬也又兵家之所當備者執事何以濟
之愚也操觚待試而毎聞邊報輙警于懷
故涉筆至此非敢出位也將以爲芹曝之
獻也
punctuated: 何釐乎九重西北之顧哉？此所謂不治之治、必辨之辨，我聖祖之謨畧，眞帝王之上策也。抑又念之：駿求千金，芟畜三年。今之選將急矣，而食也、器也、馬也，又兵家之所當備者，執事何以濟之？愚也操觚待試，而毎聞邊報，輙警于懷，故涉筆至此，非敢出位也，將以爲芹曝之獻也。
translation_en:
…and what concern would remain [?] to trouble His Majesty over the northwest? This is what is called governing without governing, and the discernment that must discern [?]. The plans of our sage founder are truly the highest strategy of an emperor.

Yet I reflect further: a thousand pieces of gold are offered in seeking a fine steed, and fodder is cut and stored for three years [?]. Selecting generals is now urgent; but provisions, weapons, and horses are also things that military commanders must have ready. How will you, honored officials, meet these needs? Holding my writing tablet as I await examination, I am alarmed whenever I hear reports from the frontier. Thus my writing has ventured this far. I do not presume to exceed my station; I intend only a humble offering, like the gifts of celery and the sun’s warmth.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
弘治辛酉秋八月江西藩司
試十三郡之士饗以賓禮而
貢于
朝制也既如制從事得士九十
五人列第氏名刻其文之尤
為錄以
===
獻秩執冊而讀之曰猗盛哉此
古之所謂鄉書也其所錄者
一鄉之士也士由文取故并
錄其文猶有所伺以通于天
下故其試曰鄉錄亦曰鄉然
是錄
獻之
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

弘治辛酉秋八月，江西藩司試十三郡之士，饗以賓禮，而貢于朝，制也。既如制從事，得士九十五人，列第氏名，刻其文之尤，為錄以獻。秩執冊而讀之，曰：「猗，盛哉！此古之所謂鄉書也。其所錄者，一鄉之士也。士由文取，故并錄其文，猶有所伺以通于天下，故其試曰鄉，錄亦曰鄉。然是錄獻之
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In autumn, in the eighth month of the xinyou year of the Hongzhi reign [1501], the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission examined the scholars of its thirteen prefectures, entertained them at a banquet with the ceremonies due to honored guests, and recommended them to the court: this was the prescribed procedure. Having conducted matters according to these regulations, it selected ninety-five scholars, listed their ranks and names, and had their finest compositions printed to form a record for presentation.

Zhi took up the volume and read it, saying: “Ah, how splendid! This is what the ancients called the ‘provincial register’ (xiangshu). Those recorded in it are the scholars of a single province. Since scholars are selected through their compositions, their compositions are recorded as well. They still await something through which to advance into the wider realm [?]; hence their examination is called ‘provincial,’ and its record is likewise called ‘provincial.’ Yet this record is presented to …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
天府而先達之于春官合兩京十
三省所錄士而群試之擇可
進者入與
廷對遂稱天下士天下士豈出
鄉士外哉故士必有天下之
志與學而德以將之才以達
之藏器蓄力載以俟乃能
成天下之功而副乎其望夫
是之謂天下之士文也者言
乎是者也試也者取乎是者
也錄也者將以徵乎是者也
是之不務而或下焉則誠鄉
士而已矣又下焉爲鄙爲野
冐士之名以忝於鄉上之所
punctuated: 天府，而先達之于春官，合兩京十三省所錄士而群試之，擇可進者入與廷對，遂稱天下士。天下士豈出鄉士外哉？故士必有天下之志與學，而德以將之，才以達之，藏器蓄力，載以俟，乃能成天下之功而副乎其望。夫是之謂天下之士。文也者，言乎是者也；試也者，取乎是者也；錄也者，將以徵乎是者也。是之不務，而或下焉，則誠鄉士而已矣。又下焉，爲鄙爲野，冐士之名以忝於鄉。上之所
translation_en: …to the imperial archives, first submitting it to the Ministry of Rites. The men selected by the two capital regions and the thirteen provinces are assembled and examined together; those deemed fit to advance are chosen to enter and participate in the Palace Examination. They are then called scholars of the realm. Yet do scholars of the realm come from outside the ranks of provincial scholars? Thus a scholar must possess aspirations and learning that embrace the whole realm, with virtue to guide them and ability to bring them to fruition. He must keep his capabilities in reserve, accumulate strength, and wait through the years; only then can he accomplish deeds benefiting the realm and fulfill the hopes placed in him. Such a man is what is meant by a scholar of the realm. Examination essays give expression to these qualities; examinations select men for these qualities; examination records are intended to attest to these qualities. If a man fails to pursue them and falls below this standard, he is indeed merely a provincial scholar. If he falls still lower, becoming narrow and uncultivated, he usurps the name of scholar and brings disgrace upon his province. Those whom the authorities…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
取者將為天下用而乃如此
豈士之自期者哉今夫耕且
蠶者其樹藝同其桑繅同其
所獲粟帛或衣食天下或僅
給其一方或不足自給而年
之豐歉世之休咎事事者之
勤與情皆係焉取士之得否
===
何以異是秩嘗聞諸君子志
以伊尹學以顏淵此蓋天下
之論至要其成必如皐陶之
所謂有常而後可以言德必
如周公之所謂攸濟而後可
以言才必如吉甫之所謂克
舉而後可以言器可以言力
punctuated:
取者，將為天下用，而乃如此，豈士之自期者哉？今夫耕且蠶者，其樹藝同，其桑繅同，其所獲粟帛，或衣食天下，或僅給其一方，或不足自給，而年之豐歉、世之休咎、事事者之勤與情，皆係焉。取士之得否，何以異是？
秩嘗聞諸君子：志以伊尹，學以顏淵，此蓋天下之論。至要其成，必如皐陶之所謂有常，而後可以言德；必如周公之所謂攸濟，而後可以言才；必如吉甫之所謂克舉，而後可以言器，可以言力。
translation_en:
…those selected are to serve all under Heaven. If they are instead like this, can this be what a scholar aspires to? Consider those who cultivate the fields and raise silkworms: their planting is alike, and their tending of mulberry trees and reeling of silk are alike. Yet the grain and silk they obtain may clothe and feed all under Heaven, may merely supply their own locality, or may prove insufficient even for themselves. The abundance or scarcity of the harvest, the good or ill fortune of the age, and the diligence and disposition [?] of those engaged in these tasks all bear upon the outcome. How is success or failure in selecting scholars any different?
I, Zhi, have heard from learned gentlemen: take Yi Yin as your model in aspiration, and Yan Yuan as your model in learning. This, surely, is a judgment shared by all under Heaven. As for bringing these aims to fulfillment, only with what Gao Yao called “constancy” can one speak of virtue; only with what the Duke of Zhou called “accomplishment” can one speak of talent; only with what Jifu called “being capable of carrying out one’s duties” can one speak of capacity and strength…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
由是勵修惇裕以興禮樂以
堯舜其君民而後可以言天
下之功其文之傳亦庶幾乎
敷納明揚而得與於所謂不
朽者然則士欲不局於鄉而
稱于天下求免夫鄙且野者
可不知所務哉今諸士表表
===
産茲土得於山川若是其秀
游歌
聖化若是其久且深而文獻在耳
目者又若是其足徵也其閒
豈無以天下士自期者若期
而未自信者若自限若自放
若自盈修謂不必期者盖亦
punctuated: 由是勵修惇裕，以興禮樂，以堯舜其君民，而後可以言天下之功。其文之傳，亦庶幾乎敷納明揚，而得與於所謂不朽者。然則士欲不局於鄉而稱于天下，求免夫鄙且野者，可不知所務哉？今諸士表表，産茲土，得於山川若是其秀，游歌聖化若是其久且深，而文獻在耳目者又若是其足徵也。其閒豈無以天下士自期者？若期而未自信者，若自限，若自放，若自盈修謂不必期者，盖亦
translation_en:
…From this foundation, they must strive in self-cultivation, deepen their virtue and broaden their capacities, thereby reviving rites and music and making their ruler and people like those of Yao and Shun. Only then can one speak of achievements benefiting all under Heaven. The transmission of their writings might also approach the ideal of receiving worthy men and publicly advancing the distinguished, allowing them to share in what is called immortality. Thus, if scholars wish to gain recognition throughout the realm rather than remain confined to their locality, and seek to escape narrowness and rusticity, can they fail to understand what they must devote themselves to?

Now these outstanding scholars were born in this land and have received such fine endowments from its mountains and rivers. They have moved about and sung under the sage emperor’s transforming influence for so long and so deeply, while the writings and worthies known to their eyes and ears provide such ample testimony. Among them, surely there are those who aspire to become scholars of the whole realm? As for those who aspire but lack confidence, those who limit themselves, those who abandon themselves, and those who are complacent about their cultivation and say such aspirations are unnecessary [?], there are presumably also…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
有之繼自今定則力疑則決
或改而圖焉則吾所錄者將
不皆天下士乎一方耕之而
天下食之一方蠶之而天下
衣之是錄也吾固曰一鄉之
書而天下觀者乃將曰是所
錄者皆天下士而其文與在
===
焉謂天下之書可也獨鄉云
乎哉雖然終是錄者題有名
碑注有選籍稽有功載覈有
臺評書有史筆而復定之以
君子之論夫然後天下之士
可得而稱矣秩不佞敬書于
末簡用為諸士子告
punctuated: 有之。繼自今，定則力，疑則決，或改而圖焉，則吾所錄者將不皆天下士乎？一方耕之，而天下食之；一方蠶之，而天下衣之。是錄也，吾固曰一鄉之書，而天下觀者乃將曰：「是所錄者皆天下士，而其文與在焉，謂天下之書可也，獨鄉云乎哉！」雖然，終是錄者，題有名碑，注有選籍，稽有功載，覈有臺評，書有史筆，而復定之以君子之論。夫然後，天下之士可得而稱矣。秩不佞，敬書于末簡，用為諸士子告。
translation_en:
…there are such men. From now onward, let those whose purpose is settled exert themselves, those in doubt resolve their doubts, and others amend their course and pursue this aim. Will not all those whom I record then become men of worth for all under Heaven? One region tills the fields, and all under Heaven eat its produce; one region raises silkworms, and all under Heaven wear its silk. I have indeed called this record the book of a single province, but readers throughout the realm will say: “Those recorded here are all men of worth for all under Heaven, and their writings are included alongside them. It may properly be called a book for all under Heaven. Why speak only of a province?”

Nevertheless, what brings this record to fulfillment remains to come: their names inscribed on steles, their appointments entered in selection registers, their achievements examined in records of merit, their conduct scrutinized in censorial assessments, and their deeds set down by historians’ brushes, with the judgment of gentlemen finally determining their standing. Only then may they be acclaimed as men of worth for all under Heaven. I, Zhi, unworthy though I am, respectfully write these words at the end of this volume as an admonition to all these scholars.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
山東東昌府高唐州夏津縣
儒學教諭黃秩謹序
punctuated: 山東東昌府高唐州夏津縣儒學教諭黃秩謹序。
translation_en: Huang Zhi, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xiajin County, Gaotang Department, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, respectfully composed this preface.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
紀者紊矣其為知也不亦小乎宋儒朱子
進說於君欲其嚴朝廷之綱紀而申之以
人主當務聰明之實此蓋吾之所謂大知
者也知大知之說斯可與論聰明之實矣
且聰明者耳目之德也而心實主之人君
之心天下之主也而假其用於耳目耳一
也而欲周天下之聽目一也而欲周天下
之視其將能乎必也不自用而假諸人故
曰明四目達四聰舜之所以為大知者政
===
惟有得乎此爾世之人君孰不欲聰明先
物而稱大知哉耳目之德雖同於天下而
其心或出於公或出於私故同一任人而
所任者異則其為聰明也亦異焉今夫天
下之事夥矣節之有禮和之有樂道之有
政齊之有刑弛張損益舉置推移其在物
也有則其在民也有情其在人才也有品
有類可者否者是者非者常叢沓於人君
之前人君雖以制命為職然必謀之大臣
punctuated:
紀者紊矣，其為知也不亦小乎？宋儒朱子進說於君，欲其嚴朝廷之綱紀，而申之以人主當務聰明之實。此蓋吾之所謂大知者也。知大知之說，斯可與論聰明之實矣。
且聰明者，耳目之德也，而心實主之。人君之心，天下之主也，而假其用於耳目。耳一也，而欲周天下之聽；目一也，而欲周天下之視，其將能乎？必也不自用而假諸人，故曰：「明四目，達四聰。」舜之所以為大知者，政惟有得乎此爾。世之人君，孰不欲聰明先物而稱大知哉？耳目之德雖同於天下，而其心或出於公，或出於私，故同一任人，而所任者異，則其為聰明也亦異焉。
今夫天下之事夥矣，節之有禮，和之有樂，道之有政，齊之有刑。弛張損益，舉置推移，其在物也有則，其在民也有情，其在人才也有品有類。可者否者，是者非者，常叢沓於人君之前。人君雖以制命為職，然必謀之大臣
translation_en:
…order has fallen into confusion. Is such wisdom not petty? The Song Confucian Master Zhu offered counsel to his ruler, urging him to uphold strictly the guiding principles and order of the court, and further explaining that the ruler must strive for genuine perceptiveness. This, surely, is what I mean by great wisdom. Only with someone who understands the meaning of great wisdom can one discuss genuine perceptiveness.
Now, acuity of hearing and clarity of sight are the virtues of the ears and eyes, but it is the mind that truly governs them. The ruler’s mind is the master of all under Heaven, and it exercises its functions through the ears and eyes. With only his own hearing, he wishes to hear everything throughout the realm; with only his own sight, he wishes to see everything throughout the realm. Can he possibly do so? He must refrain from relying solely on himself and instead draw upon others. Thus it is said: “He made clear the sight of the four quarters and opened the hearing of the four quarters.” The reason Shun possessed great wisdom was precisely that he grasped this principle. What ruler does not wish to perceive things before they emerge and be acclaimed as greatly wise? Although rulers share the faculties of hearing and sight with everyone under Heaven, their minds may proceed either from public concern or from private interests. Thus, although all alike employ others, the people they employ differ, and so does their perceptiveness.
Now, the affairs of the realm are numerous. Ritual regulates them; music harmonizes them; government directs them; punishments bring them into order. Relaxing and tightening, reducing and increasing, taking up and setting aside, adjusting and shifting—in things there are governing principles; among the people there are feelings and circumstances; among men of talent there are grades and categories. What is acceptable and unacceptable, right and wrong, constantly crowds before the ruler. Although the ruler’s duty is to issue commands, he must consult his high ministers…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
焉而後應之蓋自人君下至百執事皆有
職業不可相侵此固朝廷之綱紀也是故
三公論道六卿分職諮之詢之稽之質之
博之侍從參之給舍使之反覆熟議以求
是非可否之所在吾之所主果得其當而
行且嚴之固吾之聰吾之明也如其不然
則舍已從人人皆曰是必誠是也吾從而
是之人皆曰非必誠非也吾從而非之人
皆曰可必誠可也人皆曰否必誠否也吾
===
從而可否之然後揚于王庭明出命令是
而可者行之非而否者嚴之雖其計慮規
為不出於我而我能用之綱紀由是而振
肅朝廷由是而尊嚴即其事而觀之耳不
必聽而能極天下之聰目不必視而能極
天下之明豈非天下之大聰明者哉何也
聽者無所不聞之謂也有所不聞斯謂之
不聰矣明者無所不見之謂也有所不見
斯謂之不明矣今也以天下之人圖天下
punctuated: 焉而後應之。蓋自人君下至百執事，皆有職業，不可相侵，此固朝廷之綱紀也。是故三公論道，六卿分職，諮之詢之，稽之質之，博之侍從，參之給舍，使之反覆熟議，以求是非可否之所在。吾之所主果得其當，而行且嚴之，固吾之聰、吾之明也。如其不然，則舍已從人。人皆曰是，必誠是也，吾從而是之；人皆曰非，必誠非也，吾從而非之；人皆曰可，必誠可也；人皆曰否，必誠否也，吾從而可否之。然後揚于王庭，明出命令，是而可者行之，非而否者嚴之。雖其計慮規為不出於我，而我能用之，綱紀由是而振肅，朝廷由是而尊嚴。即其事而觀之，耳不必聽而能極天下之聰，目不必視而能極天下之明，豈非天下之大聰明者哉？何也？聽者，無所不聞之謂也；有所不聞，斯謂之不聰矣。明者，無所不見之謂也；有所不見，斯謂之不明矣。今也，以天下之人圖天下
translation_en: …and only then respond to the matter. From the ruler down to the many officials, all have their assigned duties and must not encroach upon one another. This is indeed the governing order of the court. Thus the Three Dukes deliberate on the Way, and the Six Ministers divide their responsibilities. Consult and question them, examine and verify their judgments, broaden deliberations to include the attendant officials, and seek further opinions from the supervising secretaries and Secretariat drafters. Have them discuss matters repeatedly and thoroughly, seeking to establish what is right or wrong, acceptable or unacceptable. If what I favor is indeed appropriate, I implement it and enforce it strictly [?]: this is assuredly my own acuity of hearing and clarity of sight. If it is not, I set aside my own view and follow others. When all say something is right, it must truly be right, and I accordingly affirm it; when all say it is wrong, it must truly be wrong, and I accordingly reject it. When all say it is acceptable, it must truly be acceptable; when all say it is unacceptable, it must truly be unacceptable, and I accordingly approve or disapprove it. Only then is it proclaimed in the royal court and clearly issued as a command. What is right and acceptable is carried out; what is wrong and unacceptable is strictly prohibited [?]. Although the deliberation and planning do not originate with me, I can put them to use. The governing order is thereby invigorated and disciplined, and the court thereby gains dignity and authority. Viewed through these actions, the ears need not themselves listen to attain the utmost acuity of hearing in the realm, and the eyes need not themselves look to attain the utmost clarity of sight in the realm. Is this not the greatest perceptiveness in the world? Why is this so? Listening means that there is nothing one does not hear; if there is something one does not hear, this is called a lack of acuity. Clarity of sight means that there is nothing one does not see; if there is something one does not see, this is called a lack of clarity. Now, employing the people of the realm to plan for the realm…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之事吾任大臣而大臣者又合天下之耳
目以爲吾一人聰明之助謂吾弗聽而吾
行無不當也有弗聞者能之乎故曰耳不
必聽而能極天下之聽謂吾弗明而吾行
無不中也有弗見者能之乎故曰目不必
視而能極天下之明曰哲曰聖頌聲流焉
書曰視遠惟明聽德惟聰又曰亶聰明作
元后其道如此此則所謂聰明之實者以
公心而任其公人也易曰知臨大君之宜
===
豈不信哉乃若好名者亦知任人矣然或
任非所任而偏聽輕信得其一言行則行
罷則罷自彼觀之可以發奸可以擿伏可
以破幽入隱可以致摠攬之名可以救獨
斷之譽而譸張熒蠱顛倒易置卒不出其
術數之内遠之愈繆久之愈暗自以爲聰
而實有未聞自以爲明而實有未見名爲
獨斷而主威不免於下移名爲摠攬而國
政不免於參出由是綱紀紊而庶事以隳
punctuated: 之事，吾任大臣，而大臣者又合天下之耳目，以爲吾一人聰明之助。謂吾弗聽，而吾行無不當也，有弗聞者能之乎？故曰：「耳不必聽，而能極天下之聽。」謂吾弗明，而吾行無不中也，有弗見者能之乎？故曰：「目不必視，而能極天下之明。」曰哲曰聖，頌聲流焉。《書》曰：「視遠惟明，聽德惟聰。」又曰：「亶聰明作元后。」其道如此。此則所謂聰明之實者，以公心而任其公人也。《易》曰：「知臨，大君之宜。」豈不信哉！乃若好名者，亦知任人矣。然或任非所任，而偏聽輕信，得其一言，行則行，罷則罷。自彼觀之，可以發奸，可以擿伏，可以破幽入隱，可以致摠攬之名，可以救獨斷之譽。而譸張熒蠱，顛倒易置，卒不出其術數之内。遠之愈繆，久之愈暗。自以爲聰，而實有未聞；自以爲明，而實有未見。名爲獨斷，而主威不免於下移；名爲摠攬，而國政不免於參出。由是綱紀紊，而庶事以隳。
translation_en:
…the affairs of the realm. I entrust great ministers with responsibility, and they in turn bring together the ears and eyes of all under Heaven to assist my own hearing and sight. You may say that I do not listen, yet none of my actions is inappropriate: could someone who leaves things unheard accomplish this? Thus it is said: “The ears need not themselves listen to encompass all that is heard under Heaven.” You may say that I lack clear sight, yet none of my actions misses the mark: could someone who leaves things unseen accomplish this? Thus it is said: “The eyes need not themselves look to encompass all that is seen under Heaven.” Acclamations of “wise” and “sage” spread abroad. The Book of Documents says: “To see far is clarity of sight; to heed virtue is acuity of hearing.” It also says: “One truly keen of hearing and clear of sight becomes the sovereign.” Such is the way. This is what is meant by the substance of perceptiveness: employing public-spirited men with a public-spirited heart. The Book of Changes says: “Approaching with wisdom is fitting for a great ruler.” Is this not indeed true?

Those who covet a reputation also know to employ others. Yet they may entrust responsibility to the wrong people, listen to one side alone, and believe too readily. On receiving a single word from such men, they proceed when told to proceed and stop when told to stop. From their own perspective, they can expose wrongdoing, uncover concealed misdeeds, penetrate obscurity and hidden matters, gain a reputation for comprehensive control, and salvage [?] their reputation for deciding independently. Yet amid deception and beguilement, inversions and substitutions, they ultimately never escape these men’s manipulations. The further they go, the more mistaken they become; the longer this continues, the more benighted they grow. They consider their hearing acute, yet there are things they have not heard; they consider their sight clear, yet there are things they have not seen. In name they decide independently, yet the ruler’s authority inevitably shifts to those below; in name they exercise comprehensive control, yet the government’s decisions inevitably issue from multiple sources. Thus the guiding principles and order of government fall into confusion, and its manifold affairs fall into ruin …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
蓋以私心而任私人其極必至於是所謂
自哲自聖而昏愚係之此之謂也夫求聰
明之名而乃爲昏愚之歸其視圖任大臣
不求爲聰明而大知歸焉者眞所謂毫釐
千里矣人君不欲天下之治則已如欲求
治二者將孰務哉知之大小聰明之名實
不可不審也雖然亦在乎學而已矣舜之
告禹曰人心惟危道心惟微惟精惟一允
執厥中此萬世聖學之源也人君務聰明
之實以成大知者其必由聖學乎故朱子
他日告君又曰心正則視明聽聰由是觀
之不由聖學以正其心而求聰明則公私
交雜吾見求實而近僅止於名其知終不
足以有臨也此朱子此疏未及之意也故
併論之
表
擬宋以歐陽脩知制誥謝表〔慶曆三年〕
劉禔
punctuated:
蓋以私心而任私人，其極必至於是。所謂「自哲自聖，而昏愚係之」，此之謂也。夫求聰明之名，而乃爲昏愚之歸，其視圖任大臣、不求爲聰明而大知歸焉者，眞所謂毫釐千里矣。人君不欲天下之治則已，如欲求治，二者將孰務哉？知之大小、聰明之名實，不可不審也。雖然，亦在乎學而已矣。舜之告禹曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。」此萬世聖學之源也。人君務聰明之實以成大知者，其必由聖學乎！故朱子他日告君又曰：「心正則視明聽聰。」由是觀之，不由聖學以正其心而求聰明，則公私交雜，吾見求實而近僅止於名，其知終不足以有臨也。此朱子此疏未及之意也，故併論之。

表

擬宋以歐陽脩知制誥謝表〔慶曆三年〕
劉禔
translation_en:
For when a ruler appoints private favorites out of selfish motives, matters must ultimately reach this point. This is what is meant by the saying, “He considers himself wise and sagely, yet darkness and folly follow.” To seek a reputation for perceptiveness, only to end in darkness and folly—compared with seeking out and entrusting great ministers, thereby attaining great wisdom without seeking to appear perceptive—is truly a case of a hair’s-breadth difference leading a thousand miles apart. If the ruler does not desire good order throughout the realm, there is nothing more to say; but if he seeks it, which of these two courses should he pursue? The difference between lesser and greater wisdom, and between the reputation and reality of perceptiveness, must be carefully examined.

Nevertheless, this depends simply upon learning. Shun told Yu: “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning and single-minded; faithfully hold fast to the mean.” This is the source of sagely learning for all ages. Surely a ruler who seeks genuine perceptiveness so as to attain great wisdom must proceed through sagely learning! Thus Master Zhu, on another occasion, also told his sovereign: “When the mind is rectified, sight becomes clear and hearing keen.” Viewed in this light, if one seeks perceptiveness without rectifying one’s mind through sagely learning, public and private motives become intermingled. I see that, though one seeks the reality, one ends up merely with the reputation [?]; one’s wisdom ultimately remains insufficient to govern. This is an implication that Master Zhu did not address in this memorial, and so I discuss it here as well.

Memorial

A simulated memorial of thanks on Ouyang Xiu’s appointment as Drafter of Imperial Proclamations under the Song〔Third year of Qingli (1043)〕
By Liu Ti 劉禔.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭張　批〔著述有式摸倣得真方是〕
〔制作法歐文典雅渥純意趣高遠人鮮能之諸作〕
〔遲辭浮靡殊失本相又體貼職掌不類事實或〕
〔遺令人厭觀此篇古淡春容宛然六一家風致噫〕
〔大羹玄酒咀之而有餘味義曷能舍乎〕
考試官教諭黄　批〔寫出歐陽公謦咳中真〕
〔意趣佳作也〕
考試官學正韓　批〔得駢儷體可嘉〕
臣某言伏奉
===
制命蒙恩特授臣右正言知制誥者伏以人
文藻潤聿昭
雲漢之章道化鋪揚叵測
乾坤之大惟典謨渾灝誥誓渙泓迨相如諭
蜀之文敬輿奉天之詔皆能言為世式動
中事宜肆在
本朝特難是選豈期末學亦濫玆除擂溢美
於
制詞沐
punctuated:
同考試官教諭張　批〔著述有式，摸倣得真，方是〕〔制作法。歐文典雅渥純，意趣高遠，人鮮能之。諸作〕〔遲辭浮靡，殊失本相；又體貼職掌不類事實，或〕〔遺，令人厭觀。此篇古淡春容，宛然六一家風致。噫！〕〔大羹玄酒，咀之而有餘味，義曷能舍乎？〕
考試官教諭黄　批〔寫出歐陽公謦咳中真〕〔意趣，佳作也。〕
考試官學正韓　批〔得駢儷體，可嘉。〕
臣某言：伏奉制命，蒙恩特授臣右正言知制誥者。伏以人文藻潤，聿昭雲漢之章；道化鋪揚，叵測乾坤之大。惟典謨渾灝，誥誓渙泓，迨相如諭蜀之文、敬輿奉天之詔，皆能言為世式，動中事宜。肆在本朝，特難是選。豈期末學，亦濫玆除？擂溢美於制詞，沐
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Writing has its established models; only by capturing their true character in imitation does one attain the proper method of composition. Ouyang’s prose is classically elegant, rich and pure, with lofty and far-reaching purport—a level few can attain. The other compositions are halting in expression [?], superficial and ornate, quite losing the original character. Moreover, their treatment of the duties of the office does not accord with the facts, or leaves things out, making them tiresome to read. This piece is antique and unadorned, with a springlike ease [?], vividly displaying the distinctive manner of Liuyi [Ouyang Xiu]. Ah! Like unseasoned broth and ‘dark wine’ [plain water used in ritual], it leaves a lingering savor when tasted. How could one put it aside [?]?”

Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “It conveys the true purport of Lord Ouyang’s own utterances. An excellent composition.”

Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: “It achieves the parallel-prose form: commendable.”

Your servant, so-and-so, states: I have reverently received the imperial command, graciously granting me special appointment as Right Rectifier of Omissions and Drafter of Proclamations. I humbly reflect that literary refinement lends embellishment and luster, brilliantly displaying the patterns of the Milky Way; the transforming influence of the Way spreads abroad, as unfathomably vast as Heaven and Earth. The Canons and Counsels are full and expansive; the Announcements and Oaths, flowing and profound. Later, Xiangru’s proclamation to Shu and Jingyu’s edict at Fengtian alike offered language that served as a model for the age, invariably fitting the needs of affairs. Thus, in our present dynasty, choosing a man for this office is especially difficult. How could I, a scholar of meager attainments, have expected to receive this appointment undeservedly? Laden with excessive praise in the words of the appointment decree [?], bathed in …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
誕恩於
宸注感先愧集責與憂幷恭惟
〇〇〇〇道同天地
孝達神明仁恕根於心恭儉出其性禮隆
會慶履端先晉於
慈宮宅起睦親飽德每聯於
皇族恐戕物命思結人心正風俗則詔禁邪巫
勤政理則屏書無逸兵以不用爲武刑以
不殺爲威求言渙發乎
===
玉音問俗隱憂乎菜色剛惟獨斷職不下侵謂
鉛槧須責文儒而綸綍實關著述丁寧
天語誕告多方顯允
聖謨式昭
來裔緬惟内批之勤綣允資良史以發揮經
緯古作樞機今付竊念臣少罹孤疢閱歷
險艱長乏技能夜讎文字救趨時之弊力
去雕華守學古之勤徒成鄙樸頃備員於
管記竟落職於言階幸軫淹沉荐蒙甄敘
punctuated:
誕恩於宸注，感先愧集，責與憂幷。恭惟〇〇〇〇，道同天地，孝達神明，仁恕根於心，恭儉出其性。禮隆會慶，履端先晉於慈宮；宅起睦親，飽德每聯於皇族。恐戕物命，思結人心。正風俗則詔禁邪巫，勤政理則屏書《無逸》。兵以不用爲武，刑以不殺爲威。求言渙發乎玉音，問俗隱憂乎菜色。剛惟獨斷，職不下侵。謂鉛槧須責文儒，而綸綍實關著述。丁寧天語，誕告多方。顯允聖謨，式昭來裔。緬惟内批之勤綣，允資良史以發揮。經緯古作，樞機今付。
竊念臣少罹孤疢，閱歷險艱；長乏技能，夜讎文字。救趨時之弊，力去雕華；守學古之勤，徒成鄙樸。頃備員於管記，竟落職於言階。幸軫淹沉，荐蒙甄敘。
translation_en:
…the abundant grace bestowed through Your Majesty’s attention. Gratitude comes first, followed by shame; responsibility and anxiety arrive together. I respectfully consider that [four circle placeholders] accords in the Way with Heaven and Earth. Your filial devotion reaches the spirits; benevolence and forbearance are rooted in your heart, and reverence and frugality spring from your nature. You solemnize the rites of assembled celebration, first paying respects at the palace of the Empress Dowager at the opening of the year. In fostering harmony among your kin [?], you frequently join the imperial clan in feasts of gracious fellowship. Fearing harm to living creatures, you seek to bind the people’s hearts to you. To rectify customs, you decree prohibitions against heterodox shamans; to apply yourself diligently to government, you have Against Idleness inscribed on a screen. You make the nonuse of arms your martial achievement and the avoidance of killing your penal authority. Your august voice issues far-reaching calls for counsel; in inquiring into popular conditions, you harbor deep concern for those whose faces bear the pallor of hunger. Resolute in your sole authority to decide, you do not encroach upon the duties of those below. You hold that work with writing tools must be entrusted to learned scholars, and that imperial pronouncements truly depend upon literary composition. Your earnest imperial words proclaim your intentions throughout the realm. Your illustrious and trustworthy sagely counsels will thus shine upon generations to come. Considering the diligence and solicitude expressed in your personal written directives, these surely require a worthy historian to elucidate them. The ordering of ancient writings and the pivotal responsibility are now entrusted to me.
I humbly reflect that, as a child, your servant suffered bereavement and illness and passed through dangers and hardships. Grown to adulthood, I lacked abilities and skills, collating texts by night. To remedy the faults of following contemporary fashions, I strove to remove ornate embellishment; persevering in the study of antiquity, I achieved only a rustic plainness. Recently I served among those responsible for records, but ultimately lost my post on account of words [?]. Fortunately, you took pity on my prolonged obscurity, and I repeatedly received consideration and reappointment.

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
通班冊府待罪諫垣謬忝四禁之嚴超置
七人之列辭章懇乞
聖意重回忽遣使以臨門俾措躬而無地臣敢
不勉圖来效仰荅
皇慈景服前脩翼成信史話言必記舉動特書
事深假于折衷意默存乎儆戒首復渾厚
之體特申懇至之詞俾
德意旁宣偕日月而普照
仁恩下浹等雨露以弘敷雖稽古未盡典謨而
===
紀實可知堯舜尚期補過助大塊於一塵
更勵匪躬頻尚方之一劒無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
策
punctuated:
通班冊府，待罪諫垣，謬忝四禁之嚴，超置七人之列。辭章懇乞，聖意重回，忽遣使以臨門，俾措躬而無地。臣敢不勉圖来效，仰荅皇慈？景服前脩，翼成信史。話言必記，舉動特書，事深假于折衷，意默存乎儆戒。首復渾厚之體，特申懇至之詞，俾德意旁宣，偕日月而普照；仁恩下浹，等雨露以弘敷。雖稽古未盡典謨，而紀實可知堯舜。尚期補過，助大塊於一塵；更勵匪躬，頻尚方之一劒。無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叄場
策
translation_en:
…admitted to the ranks of the imperial library and holding office, subject to punishment for my failings, among the remonstrance officials. Undeservedly I have entered the august precincts of the four forbidden enclosures [?] and been raised to the company of the seven. In a written petition I earnestly begged to decline, but Your Majesty reconsidered and suddenly dispatched an envoy to my gate, leaving me nowhere to place myself in my embarrassment. How dare your servant fail to strive for future service in grateful response to Your imperial kindness?

I shall reverently emulate the worthy men of earlier times and assist in compiling a trustworthy history. Every utterance must be recorded and every action expressly set down. The treatment of events depends profoundly upon balanced judgment, while admonition is silently embedded in the underlying intent. I shall first restore a substantial and unadorned style and give particular expression to words of earnest concern, so that Your virtuous intentions may be proclaimed everywhere, shining universally like the sun and moon, and Your benevolent favor may permeate the realm below, spreading abundantly like rain and dew. Although inquiry into antiquity may not encompass all the Canons and Counsels, a faithful record of events will make known a Yao and a Shun.

I still hope to remedy faults, contributing a single speck of dust to the great earth; I shall further spur myself to selfless service, repeatedly invoking the sword of the Imperial Manufactories [?]. Overwhelmed as I gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sageliness, with the utmost fervor, awe, and trembling, I respectfully submit this memorial to convey my thanks for Your hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
第一問
葉釗
同考試官訓導劉　批　〔我〕
聖祖制作之善正在有德以為之本場中答者類能知之但於制作詳
備處漫不究心此篇條荅如指諸掌非平日服膺
聖製而有志於當世務者不能讀之令人生忠愛意風簷寸晷之下
得士有此亦可為
明時慶矣
同考試官教諭潘　批　詞氣浩然如長江大河華
===
國之文貴如此
同考試官教諭傅　批
皇祖一統天下之盛煥乎文章蕩蕩乎如天之難名此士歷陳而又能
知其所本可謂善鋪張
洪休揚厲偉績者矣
考試官教諭黃　批　鋪張
聖制之懿光昭萬世無踰於此者
考試官學正韓　批　書生能熟究
聖製而頃刻成文以對其英英用世之志久矣可敬可敬
punctuated:
第一問
葉釗

同考試官訓導劉批：〔我〕聖祖制作之善，正在有德以為之本。場中答者類能知之，但於制作詳備處，漫不究心。此篇條荅，如指諸掌，非平日服膺聖製而有志於當世務者不能。讀之令人生忠愛意。風簷寸晷之下，得士有此，亦可為明時慶矣。

同考試官教諭潘批：詞氣浩然，如長江大河。華國之文，貴如此。

同考試官教諭傅批：皇祖一統天下之盛，煥乎文章，蕩蕩乎如天之難名。此士歷陳，而又能知其所本，可謂善鋪張洪休、揚厲偉績者矣。

考試官教諭黃批：鋪張聖制之懿，光昭萬世，無踰於此者。

考試官學正韓批：書生能熟究聖製，而頃刻成文以對，其英英用世之志久矣。可敬！可敬！
translation_en:
First Policy Question
Ye Zhao

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor: The excellence of 〔our〕 sagely founding emperor’s institutions lies precisely in the virtue that served as their foundation. Most candidates answering this question understood this, but gave little thought to the thoroughness and completeness of those institutions. This essay answers point by point, making everything as clear as pointing to one’s own palm. Only someone who habitually takes the sagely emperor’s institutions to heart and aspires to address the affairs of the age could accomplish this. Reading it awakens feelings of loyalty and devotion. To find such a scholar under the wind-swept eaves of the examination hall, within so brief an allotted time, is indeed cause for rejoicing in this enlightened age.

Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor: The force of his language is vast, like the Yangzi and the Yellow River. Writing that lends glory to the state is prized for just such qualities.

Comment by Associate Examiner Fu, Instructor: The magnificence of the imperial ancestor’s unification of All under Heaven was resplendent in its cultural accomplishments and so boundless that, like Heaven, it defies description. This scholar recounts these achievements in detail and also understands their foundation. He may indeed be called adept at setting forth the emperor’s great beneficence and extolling his mighty accomplishments.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: In setting forth the excellence of the sagely emperor’s institutions, whose brilliance illuminates ten thousand generations, nothing surpasses this.

Comment by Examiner Han, Instructor: This scholar has thoroughly studied the sagely emperor’s institutions and can compose an essay in response within moments. His outstanding ambition to serve the world must be of long standing. Admirable! Admirable!

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
對立法通天下萬世之大利者
聖人之業垂法汝天下萬世之大功者
聖人之德蓋法制之立
聖人大業而為天下萬世利者也然其良法美
意垂之天下萬世其功莫大焉自非
聖人備聰明聖知之天德其孰能與於此哉執
事首舉
皇祖制作下詢承學愚也幸生茲
聖明之世仰佩
===
聖謨久矣庸不能悉謹條其一二以對夫春秋
大一統者乃漢儒董仲舒之言本子思子
中庸之意也子思子曰王天下有三重焉
其寡過矣乎又曰非天子不議禮不制度
不考文言必聖人在天子之位而後行此
三重之道也非春秋大一統為天地之常
經古今之通義邪洪惟我
太祖高皇帝承
天膺曆變夷為華以
punctuated:
對：立法通天下萬世之大利者，聖人之業；垂法汝天下萬世之大功者，聖人之德。蓋法制之立，聖人大業而為天下萬世利者也。然其良法美意垂之天下萬世，其功莫大焉。自非聖人備聰明聖知之天德，其孰能與於此哉？執事首舉皇祖制作，下詢承學。愚也幸生茲聖明之世，仰佩聖謨久矣。庸不能悉，謹條其一二以對。
夫《春秋》大一統者，乃漢儒董仲舒之言，本子思子《中庸》之意也。子思子曰：「王天下有三重焉，其寡過矣乎！」又曰：「非天子不議禮，不制度，不考文。」言必聖人在天子之位，而後行此三重之道也。非《春秋》大一統為天地之常經、古今之通義邪？洪惟我太祖高皇帝承天膺曆，變夷為華，以
translation_en:
In reply: To establish laws that extend great benefits throughout the realm for all generations is the undertaking of a sage; to bequeath laws of great enduring service to the realm [?] is the virtue of a sage. Establishing laws and institutions is indeed the sage’s great undertaking, benefiting the realm for all generations. Yet no achievement is greater than transmitting those excellent laws and fine intentions to the realm for all generations. Unless a sage possessed the Heaven-endowed virtues of perceptiveness and sagely wisdom, who could accomplish this? You, honored officials, first cited the imperial ancestor’s institutional creations and condescended to question us students. Fortunate to have been born in this age of sagely enlightenment, I have long looked up to and revered his sagely plans. Though I cannot set them out exhaustively, I respectfully enumerate one or two in reply.
As for the Spring and Autumn Annals’ emphasis on the grand unity of rule, this is a formulation of the Han scholar Dong Zhongshu, grounded in the meaning of Master Zisi’s Doctrine of the Mean. Master Zisi said: “In ruling all under Heaven, there are three weighty matters. With these attended to, surely errors will be few!” He also said: “One who is not the Son of Heaven does not deliberate on ritual, establish standards, or examine written forms.” This means that only when a sage occupies the position of Son of Heaven can he carry out the Way of these three weighty matters. Is not the grand unity of rule emphasized in the Spring and Autumn Annals the constant principle of Heaven and Earth and the universally valid norm of antiquity and the present? We reverently consider how our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s mandate and assumed the imperial succession, transforming barbarian rule into Chinese civilization, and, as …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
天下之大聖行天下之大事制禮作樂為百
王之法立教垂訓宏一代之規演諸
宸翰出自
淵衷
神功莫罄
聖德難言而其所仰見者則有所謂三重之
道焉夫自元俗亂華有
禮儀定式以議禮自夷教變夏有
稽古定制以制度自胡言混中土有
===
洪武正韻以考文此皆制作之大端所以新
天下之耳目一天下之心志萬世臣民所
當遵守而不敢違者也請述其旨自天尊
地卑之位定而禮于是乎形在人則親踈
之分貴賤之等截然而不可犯者皆是禮
也禮以議之上下辨矣若
定式所載為條三十有七始之以朝叅筵宴
之節終之以器皿床榻之類至於其間最
切而要者則
punctuated:
天下之大聖，行天下之大事，制禮作樂，為百王之法；立教垂訓，宏一代之規。演諸宸翰，出自淵衷。神功莫罄，聖德難言，而其所仰見者，則有所謂三重之道焉。夫自元俗亂華，有《禮儀定式》以議禮；自夷教變夏，有《稽古定制》以制度；自胡言混中土，有《洪武正韻》以考文。此皆制作之大端，所以新天下之耳目，一天下之心志，萬世臣民所當遵守而不敢違者也。請述其旨。
自天尊地卑之位定，而禮于是乎形。在人，則親踈之分、貴賤之等，截然而不可犯者，皆是禮也。禮以議之，上下辨矣。若《定式》所載，為條三十有七，始之以朝叅筵宴之節，終之以器皿床榻之類。至於其間最切而要者，則
translation_en:
…as the greatest sage in all under Heaven, he undertook the greatest affairs of all under Heaven. He established rites and created music, providing a model for all kings; he established teachings and handed down instructions, giving broad scope to the norms of a dynasty. These were expounded through his imperial writings and issued from the depths of his heart. His divine achievements cannot be fully recounted, and his sagely virtue is difficult to express. Yet what we can perceive as we look up to him includes the Way of the so-called Three Weighty Matters. Since Yuan customs had thrown Chinese civilization into disorder, there was the Established Forms of Ritual and Ceremony (Liyi dingshi) to deliberate upon rites. Since barbarian teachings had transformed Chinese civilization, there was the Established Institutions Based on Investigation of Antiquity (Jigu dingzhi) to establish institutions and standards. Since foreign speech had muddled the Central Land, there was the Correct Rhymes of the Hongwu Era (Hongwu zhengyun) to examine and standardize writing. These were all major acts of institutional creation, serving to renew what all under Heaven heard and saw and to unite their hearts and purposes. They are what subjects and people throughout the ages must observe and dare not contravene. Allow me to explain their import.
Once the positions of Heaven above and Earth below were fixed, ritual took shape therein. Among human beings, the distinctions between close and distant kin and the ranks of noble and base, sharply defined and inviolable, are all manifestations of ritual. Through deliberation upon ritual, superior and inferior are distinguished. Thus the Established Forms contains thirty-seven articles, beginning with the observances for court audiences and banquets and ending with such categories as vessels and beds. As for what is most immediately relevant and essential among them, it is…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖諭所謂毋放肆怠聽思爲省身克已之道是
已自天圓地方之體設而度于是乎寓在
人則室廬之限輿皁之制秩然而不可踰
者皆是度也度以制之等威殊矣若
定制所編類皆經常之法斟酌夫李唐趙宋
之制兼舉夫藝祖英宗之言至於其間語
及財利者則
聖意以爲食祿之家不當與民爭利故爾自天
玄地黄之色著而文于是乎顯在人則形
===
之點畫播之聲音皆是文也文以考之形
聲正矣若
正韻一書去沈約之謬而成經緯之交其雅
音則取於中原其註釋則依於毛晃他如
東冬清青之二韻併而爲一虞模麻遮之
一韻析而爲二孰非
宸慮之所在乎爰自
聖祖以來迄今百三十餘年政不異政俗不殊
俗誠一統文明之治足以比隆唐虞三代
punctuated: 聖諭所謂「毋放肆怠聽，思爲省身克已之道」，是已。自天圓地方之體設，而度于是乎寓。在人則室廬之限、輿皁之制，秩然而不可踰者，皆是度也。度以制之，等威殊矣。若《定制》所編，類皆經常之法，斟酌夫李唐趙宋之制，兼舉夫藝祖英宗之言。至於其間語及財利者，則聖意以爲食祿之家不當與民爭利，故爾。自天玄地黄之色著，而文于是乎顯。在人則形之點畫，播之聲音，皆是文也。文以考之，形聲正矣。若《正韻》一書，去沈約之謬，而成經緯之交。其雅音則取於中原，其註釋則依於毛晃。他如東冬、清青之二韻併而爲一，虞模、麻遮之一韻析而爲二，孰非宸慮之所在乎？爰自聖祖以來，迄今百三十餘年，政不異政，俗不殊俗，誠一統文明之治，足以比隆唐虞三代。
translation_en:
…precisely what the sacred injunction means by: “Do not behave wantonly or be negligent in listening [?]; consider how to examine yourself and master your own desires.” Once the forms of round Heaven and square Earth were established, standards were embodied therein. Among human beings, the restrictions on dwellings and the regulations governing carriages and servants, orderly and admitting no transgression, are all such standards. By regulating people through these standards, distinctions of rank and dignity are maintained. The provisions compiled in the Established Institutions (Dingzhi) are all enduring rules. They weigh the institutions of the Li house of Tang and the Zhao house of Song and also cite the words of Yizu and Yingzong. Where they discuss wealth and profit, this is because the imperial intention holds that households receiving official stipends should not compete with the people for profit.

Once the dark hue of Heaven and the yellow hue of Earth became manifest, patterned expression appeared therein. Among human beings, what takes shape in the dots and strokes of writing and is disseminated through sound is all such patterned expression. By examining it, written forms and sounds are rectified. The book Correct Rhymes (Zhengyun) eliminates Shen Yue’s errors and establishes an interlocking system like warp and weft. Its standard pronunciations are taken from the Central Plain, and its annotations follow Mao Huang. Other examples include merging the two rhyme categories dong 東 and dong 冬, and likewise qing 清 and qing 青, into one each, while dividing the single categories yu–mo 虞模 and ma–zhe 麻遮 into two each. Which of these was not an object of imperial deliberation?

From the time of the sagely founding emperor until now, more than 130 years have passed. Government has remained uniform, and customs have not diverged. Truly, this is a unified and culturally enlightened order, worthy of comparison with the flourishing rule of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之盛所謂建諸天地而不悖質諸鬼神而
無疑百世以俟聖人而不惑者也至求其
制作之本則存乎
聖祖本諸身而有中庸之德焉耳夫自昔聖人
三重之制不過因前代之舊而損益其間
故功業在天下或十世百世而止我
聖祖恢復帝王自有之疆土𢌿摯今古所無之
戎狄因元人斁敗禮樂典章彞倫之後禮
以制行度以為法文以合俗其利則天下
===
萬世之利者也
聖人之業何如其大邪其功則天下萬世之功
者也
聖人之德何如其盛邪惟
聖祖道德之高制作之善功業之成如此而欲
鋪張揚厲猶摸天地而繪日月也然吾夫
子有曰大哉堯之為君也巍巍乎唯天為
大唯堯則之蕩蕩乎民無能名焉巍巍乎
其有成功也煥乎其有文章愚生殆忘
punctuated: 之盛，所謂「建諸天地而不悖，質諸鬼神而無疑，百世以俟聖人而不惑」者也。至求其制作之本，則存乎聖祖本諸身而有中庸之德焉耳。夫自昔聖人三重之制，不過因前代之舊而損益其間，故功業在天下，或十世百世而止。我聖祖恢復帝王自有之疆土，𢌿摯今古所無之戎狄，因元人斁敗禮樂典章彞倫之後，禮以制行，度以為法，文以合俗，其利則天下萬世之利者也。聖人之業，何如其大邪！其功則天下萬世之功者也。聖人之德，何如其盛邪！惟聖祖道德之高、制作之善、功業之成如此，而欲鋪張揚厲，猶摸天地而繪日月也。然吾夫子有曰：「大哉，堯之為君也！巍巍乎！唯天為大，唯堯則之。蕩蕩乎！民無能名焉。巍巍乎，其有成功也！煥乎，其有文章！」愚生殆忘
translation_en:
…in their flourishing glory. This is what is meant by: “Established before Heaven and Earth, it does not conflict with them; tested before the spirits, it admits of no doubt; awaiting a sage a hundred generations hence, it gives no cause for perplexity.” If we seek the foundation of these institutions, it lies simply in the sagely founder’s grounding them in his own person and possessing the virtue of the Mean.

From antiquity, the sages’ institutions concerning the three weighty matters merely followed the precedents of earlier dynasties, making reductions and additions along the way. Thus their achievements in the world endured perhaps ten or a hundred generations, and no longer. Our sagely founder restored the territories that rightfully belonged to the emperors and kings, and subdued [?] Rong and Di such as had never been seen in ancient or modern times. After the men of the Yuan had corrupted rites, music, statutes, institutions, and the constant principles of human relations, he used rites to regulate conduct, standards to establish rules, and writing to unify customs. The benefits of these measures extend to all under Heaven for ten thousand generations. How great is the sage’s undertaking! His achievements likewise benefit all under Heaven for ten thousand generations. How abundant is the sage’s virtue!

Such are the loftiness of the sagely founder’s Way and virtue, the excellence of his institutions, and the fulfillment of his achievements that attempting to expound and extol them would be like depicting Heaven and Earth or painting the sun and moon. Yet our Master said: “Great indeed was Yao as a ruler! How majestic! Heaven alone is great, and Yao alone modeled himself upon it. How boundless! The people could find no name for it. How majestic were his accomplishments! How brilliant were his cultural forms!” This ignorant student has perhaps forgotten …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
堯天之下平日之所誦習者唯此而已更復何
言謹對
第二問
張鉞
同考試官教諭徐批考究精密深悉儒先道統
淵源有養之士也可嘉
同考試官教諭季批敷演出正學一本意匪素有
抱負者鮮能
同考試官學正楊批荅有根據足見博洽之學
===
考試官教諭黃批此子所荅殆如親立門墻而
摳趨考亭者乎
考試官學正韓批一部道學淵源盡在此子
腹中方能隨叩隨鳴
道係於天有不可終絶之統道屬於人有
不可苟得之傳惟其不可終絶也故或異
地而同心惟其不可苟得也故或同時而
異學然則道之係於天而屬於人者豈可
以輕論哉請畧陳之道統之傳始於羲皇
alt_text:
言謹對
第二問
張鉞
同考試官教諭徐 批 考究精審深悉儒先道統
淵源有養之士也可嘉
同考試官教諭李 批 敷演出正學一本意匪素有
抱負者鮮能
同考試官學正楊 批 荅有根據足見博洽之學
===
考試官教諭黃 批 此子□荅殆如親立門墻而
摳趨考亭者乎
考試官學正韓 批 一部道學淵源盡在此子
腹中方能隨叩隨鳴
道係於天有不可終絕之統道屬於人有
不可苟得之傳惟其不可終絕也故或異
地而同心惟其不可苟得也故或同時而
異學然則道之係於天而屬於人者豈可
以輕論哉請畧陳之道統之傳始於羲皇
punctuated:
堯天之下，平日之所誦習者唯此而已，更復何言？謹對。

第二問
張鉞

同考試官教諭徐批：考究精密，深悉儒先道統淵源，有養之士也，可嘉。
同考試官教諭季批：敷演出正學一本意，匪素有抱負者鮮能。
同考試官學正楊批：荅有根據，足見博洽之學。
考試官教諭黃批：此子所荅，殆如親立門墻而摳趨考亭者乎！
考試官學正韓批：一部道學淵源，盡在此子腹中，方能隨叩隨鳴。

道係於天，有不可終絶之統；道屬於人，有不可苟得之傳。惟其不可終絶也，故或異地而同心；惟其不可苟得也，故或同時而異學。然則道之係於天而屬於人者，豈可以輕論哉？請畧陳之。道統之傳，始於羲皇。
translation_en:
…beneath the heaven of Yao, this alone is what I regularly recite and study. What more could I say? Respectfully submitted in reply.

Second Question
Zhang Yue 張鉞

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: His investigation is meticulous and precise. He thoroughly understands the origins and development of the transmission of the Way among earlier Confucian masters. A scholar of cultivated character, worthy of praise.

Comment by Associate Examiner Ji, Instructor: He expounds the meaning of orthodox learning as having a single root. Few could accomplish this without long-standing aspirations.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Schoolmaster: His answer is well grounded, amply demonstrating broad and comprehensive learning.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: From this candidate’s answer, one might almost think he had personally stood within the master’s gates and, lifting his robe respectfully, hastened to attend upon Zhu Xi at Kaoting!

Comment by Examiner Han, Schoolmaster: The entire history of the origins and development of the Learning of the Way is within this candidate’s breast; only thus can he respond whenever questioned, like a bell sounding whenever struck.

The Way is bound to Heaven, possessing a succession that cannot be severed forever; the Way is entrusted to human beings, possessing a transmission that cannot be acquired casually. Because that succession cannot be severed forever, people in different places may share the same mind. Because that transmission cannot be acquired casually, people living at the same time may differ in their learning. How, then, could one speak lightly of the Way as bound to Heaven and entrusted to human beings? Allow me to set this out briefly. The transmission of the succession of the Way began with the sovereign Fuxi…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
盛於堯舜大成於孔子至孟子而中絕焉
有宋周程朱子起而承之周子生于舂陵
南方之人也而程子受學於南安故吾與
點也之意遂得於心領之餘程子生於河
洛北方之人也而楊中立從學於潁昌故
吾道南矣之歎遂發於目送之際楊之再
傳復得朱子以集諸儒之大成焉周范造
詣固殊程張契悟亦異此朱子眷眷於人之
問也盖范文正之極高明而道中庸不過
===
庶幾焉耳其視周之默契道體固爲不同
張因范公勸讀中庸歸而求之久乃有得
與程之一見即悟者抑亦異矣然朱子承
命帝齋稟學延平以上泝濂洛之淵源則
周程之道朱實承之故朱子記周之祠有
上接洙泗下啓河洛之語其於學庸孟子
止言程子則以周之圖書專明易學而註
述未及於三書故耳豈謂周之學有異於
程哉周子之寓江西當時若歐陽脩曾鞏
punctuated: 盛於堯舜，大成於孔子，至孟子而中絕焉。有宋周程朱子起而承之。周子生于舂陵，南方之人也，而程子受學於南安，故「吾與點也」之意，遂得於心領之餘。程子生於河洛，北方之人也，而楊中立從學於潁昌，故「吾道南矣」之歎，遂發於目送之際。楊之再傳，復得朱子以集諸儒之大成焉。周范造詣固殊，程張契悟亦異，此朱子眷眷於人之問也。盖范文正之極高明而道中庸，不過庶幾焉耳，其視周之默契道體，固爲不同。張因范公勸讀《中庸》，歸而求之，久乃有得，與程之一見即悟者，抑亦異矣。然朱子承命帝齋，稟學延平，以上泝濂洛之淵源，則周程之道，朱實承之。故朱子記周之祠，有「上接洙泗，下啓河洛」之語。其於《學》《庸》《孟子》，止言程子，則以周之圖書專明《易》學，而註述未及於三書故耳，豈謂周之學有異於程哉？周子之寓江西，當時若歐陽脩、曾鞏
translation_en:
…flourished under Yao and Shun, reached its full realization in Confucius, and was interrupted after Mencius. Under the Song, Masters Zhou, Cheng, and Zhu arose to carry it on. Master Zhou was born in Chongling and was a southerner, while Master Cheng received instruction in Nan’an. Thus, through inward comprehension, Cheng came to grasp the meaning of “I am with Dian.” Master Cheng was born in the He-Luo region and was a northerner, while Yang Zhongli studied under him in Yingchang. Thus, as Cheng watched him depart, he exclaimed, “My Way is going south!” Two generations of transmission after Yang, Master Zhu emerged to bring the achievements of the various scholars to full realization.

Zhou and Fan certainly differed in their attainments, and Cheng and Zhang likewise differed in their intuitive understanding. This was a matter on which Master Zhu dwelt earnestly when responding to questions. Fan Wenzheng’s attainment of “reaching the utmost height and brilliance while following the Mean” was no more than an approximation; it certainly differed from Zhou’s tacit apprehension of the substance of the Way. At Lord Fan’s urging, Zhang read the Doctrine of the Mean, returned home to investigate it, and only after a long time gained an understanding. This, too, differed from Cheng’s immediate awakening upon first encountering it. Yet Master Zhu “received a command at the imperial study” [?], received instruction from Yanping, and thereby traced the intellectual sources back to Lian and Luo. Zhu thus truly inherited the Way of Zhou and Cheng.

Hence, in his record of Zhou’s shrine, Master Zhu wrote that Zhou “linked back to the Zhu and Si rivers above and opened the way for the He and Luo rivers below”—that is, he continued the tradition of Confucius and prepared the way for the Cheng masters. That Zhu spoke only of Master Cheng in connection with the Great Learning, the Doctrine of the Mean, and the Mencius was simply because Zhou’s diagram and writings specifically elucidated the study of the Book of Changes, and his commentaries had not extended to those three books. How could this imply that Zhou’s learning differed from Cheng’s? When Master Zhou resided in Jiangxi, such contemporaries as Ouyang Xiu and Zeng Gong…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
黄庭堅李覯各以文學鳴而於性命之説
未肯降心以從其始從終背又有若王安
石者此無他所志異也朱子宦遊南康往
来饒信諸郡士游其門者甚衆嘗與象山
陸氏胥會鵝湖屢相問辨而卒未能會其
説于一者此無他所見異也雖然庭堅游
于蘇門而光風霽月之賛乃善形容周子
之氣象吴澄主於陸學而元亨利貞之論
乃獨係屬朱子之統緒斯道之中正公論
在人不可誣也彼所見所志之異者烏能
與於斯哉嗟夫道統之傳絶於千載而續
於一時或自南而北或自北而南遠近見
聞不啻符契此皆係於天焉非人之所能
為也若夫所志所見之異而不能以强同
者雖由乎人而亦豈非天哉愚也有志於
道方欲上師古人而未知所從敢因明問
而請質焉惟進而教之幸甚
第三問
punctuated:
黄庭堅、李覯各以文學鳴，而於性命之説未肯降心以從。其始從終背，又有若王安石者。此無他，所志異也。朱子宦遊南康，往来饒信諸郡，士游其門者甚衆。嘗與象山陸氏胥會鵝湖，屢相問辨，而卒未能會其説于一者，此無他，所見異也。雖然，庭堅游于蘇門，而光風霽月之賛，乃善形容周子之氣象；吴澄主於陸學，而元亨利貞之論，乃獨係屬朱子之統緒。斯道之中正，公論在人，不可誣也。彼所見所志之異者，烏能與於斯哉！嗟夫！道統之傳絶於千載，而續於一時，或自南而北，或自北而南，遠近見聞，不啻符契。此皆係於天焉，非人之所能為也。若夫所志所見之異，而不能以强同者，雖由乎人，而亦豈非天哉？愚也有志於道，方欲上師古人，而未知所從。敢因明問而請質焉，惟進而教之，幸甚！

第三問
translation_en:
…Huang Tingjian and Li Gou each won renown for literary learning, yet were unwilling to humble themselves and accept his teachings on human nature and the heavenly mandate. There were also men such as Wang Anshi, who followed him at first but ultimately turned away. The reason was simply that their aspirations differed. Master Zhu served in Nankang and traveled among the prefectures of Raozhou, Xinzhou, and elsewhere; very many scholars studied under him. He once met with Lu Xiangshan at Ehu. They repeatedly questioned and debated one another, yet ultimately could not reconcile their teachings. The reason was simply that their views differed.

Nevertheless, although Huang Tingjian studied in Su Shi’s circle, his praise of Master Zhou as a “clear breeze and a moon after rain” aptly described Zhou’s bearing. Although Wu Cheng upheld Lu’s learning, his discussion of “the originating, the flourishing, the beneficial, and the steadfast” (yuan, heng, li, zhen) attached the succession of the Way to Master Zhu alone. The centrality and correctness of this Way are matters of public judgment residing in people’s minds and cannot be misrepresented. How could those differences of views and aspirations have any bearing on this?

Alas! The transmission of the succession of the Way was interrupted for a thousand years, only to resume within a single age. Whether proceeding from south to north or from north to south, what was seen and heard, far and near, matched like the halves of a tally. All this depended upon Heaven; it was beyond human power to accomplish. As for differences of aspiration and understanding that cannot be forced into agreement, although these arise from human beings, are they not also attributable to Heaven?

Unworthy though I am, I aspire to the Way. I now wish to take the ancients as my teachers, yet do not know whom to follow. I venture, therefore, to take your illuminating question as an occasion to seek your judgment. If you would lead me forward and instruct me, I would be most fortunate!

Third Question

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
李文潔
同考試官教諭林　批〔能言之士踈而陋大而誇亦習弊也此篇詞氣渾厚於鄉邦人物感慨抑揚而意〕
思含蓄不暴末復以神明之機存乎人乃根本之論
况餘策皆偉譬之人入海探珠徑寸先得奇寳有
所歸矣
同考試官學正章　批〔道德風俗卓有定見而士夫人物歷舉不遺豈嘗誦其書而追慕其人者歟〕
考試官教諭黃　批〔考據詳悉鋪敘整嚴策〕
學辭有其儷
考試官學正韓　批〔議論風俗由道德又推原其本在〕
朝廷其機在士夫誠爲有見
===
道有升降政由俗華風化之本在朝廷其
儀不忒正是四國風化之機在士夫盖上
有所好下必有甚焉者矣况朝廷者四方
之根本士夫者鄉國之領袖轉移感動豈
非影響之必然哉粤自先王之時以民之
punctuated:
李文潔

同考試官教諭林批〔能言之士，踈而陋，大而誇，亦習弊也。此篇詞氣渾厚，於鄉邦人物感慨抑揚，而意〕思含蓄不暴，末復以神明之機存乎人，乃根本之論。况餘策皆偉，譬之人入海探珠，徑寸先得，奇寳有所歸矣。

同考試官學正章批〔道德風俗，卓有定見，而士夫人物歷舉不遺，豈嘗誦其書而追慕其人者歟？〕

考試官教諭黃批〔考據詳悉，鋪敘整嚴，策〕學辭有其儷。

考試官學正韓批〔議論風俗由道德，又推原其本在〕朝廷，其機在士夫，誠爲有見。

道有升降，政由俗華。風化之本在朝廷，「其儀不忒，正是四國」。風化之機在士夫，盖上有所好，下必有甚焉者矣。况朝廷者，四方之根本；士夫者，鄉國之領袖。轉移感動，豈非影響之必然哉？粤自先王之時，以民之
translation_en:
Li Wenjie

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Among men skilled in expression, some are careless and shallow, others grandiose and boastful; these too are entrenched faults. This essay’s language and spirit are substantial and mellow. In discussing figures from his native region, the author expresses deep feeling, with measured praise and criticism, while keeping his meaning restrained rather than overt. At the end, he returns to the point that the power of spiritual illumination resides in people—a discussion that reaches the fundamentals. Moreover, his other policy essays are all outstanding. He is like someone who enters the sea seeking pearls and immediately obtains one an inch across: the rare treasure has found its recipient.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “On moral virtue and customs, he has remarkably firm judgments; he also enumerates the scholar-officials and other notable figures without omission. Could he be someone who has read their writings and admires the men of the past?”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “His examination of the evidence is detailed and thorough, and his exposition orderly and rigorous. In policy-essay learning and expression, he has his peers [?].”

Comment by Examiner Han, Instructor: “He argues that customs derive from moral virtue, and further traces their foundation to the imperial court and their motive force to the scholar-officials. This is truly insightful.”

The Way rises and declines; government depends on the refinement of customs [?]. The foundation of moral transformation lies in the imperial court: ‘His deportment is without fault; he sets right these states in all four quarters.’ The motive force of moral transformation lies in the scholar-officials, for whatever those above favor, those below will inevitably favor still more. Moreover, the imperial court is the foundation of all regions, and scholar-officials are the leaders of their local communities. Must not their power to change and move others operate as inevitably as a shadow follows a form or an echo follows a sound? From the time of the former kings, because the people’s …

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
視聽不可不一上之好惡不可不示也於
是教民以五禮六樂無異教也道王之德
意志慮無異政也通其貨財同其度量無
異尚也除其所怨同其所好無異情也道
四方之政和上下之志無異心也齊道德
一風俗者如此自秦以來始皇變詐峻刻
而民俗薄漢高改制易俗而民俗厚孝武
好大喜功而民俗壞孝宣綜核名實而民
俗實魏晉賤守節樂清曠而民俗浮唐太
===
宗約己治人崇儒重道而民俗醇宋承五
代之弊深仁厚澤涵養天下其俗之仁厚
又自不言可知矣升降因革循環無端固
皆上之化也若夫縣無復盜實感太丘二
絹之遺路不拾遺又激彥方一布之惠陽
城行古道居晉鄙薰德而善良者幾千人
李善存孤兒隱山陽感行而脩義者遍閭
里此又士大夫之立身行義風範乎鄉者
也江右控引荆越襟帶江湖山川特秀人
punctuated: 視聽不可不一，上之好惡不可不示也。於是教民以五禮六樂，無異教也；道王之德意志慮，無異政也；通其貨財，同其度量，無異尚也；除其所怨，同其所好，無異情也；道四方之政，和上下之志，無異心也。齊道德、一風俗者如此。自秦以來，始皇變詐峻刻，而民俗薄；漢高改制易俗，而民俗厚；孝武好大喜功，而民俗壞；孝宣綜核名實，而民俗實；魏晉賤守節、樂清曠，而民俗浮；唐太宗約己治人、崇儒重道，而民俗醇；宋承五代之弊，深仁厚澤涵養天下，其俗之仁厚，又自不言可知矣。升降因革，循環無端，固皆上之化也。若夫縣無復盜，實感太丘二絹之遺；路不拾遺，又激彥方一布之惠。陽城行古道，居晉鄙，薰德而善良者幾千人；李善存孤兒，隱山陽，感行而脩義者遍閭里。此又士大夫之立身行義，風範乎鄉者也。江右控引荆越，襟帶江湖，山川特秀，人
translation_en:
…what the people saw and heard had to be unified, and the likes and dislikes of those above had to be made manifest. Thus the people were taught through the five rites and six forms of music, with no divergent teachings; the king’s virtuous intentions and purposes were conveyed, with no divergent policies; goods and wealth were circulated and measures standardized, with no divergent practices; what the people resented was removed and what they valued brought into accord, with no divergent sentiments; governance throughout the realm was guided and the aspirations of those above and below harmonized, with no divergent aims. Such was the way moral principles were brought into accord and customs unified.

From the Qin onward, the First Emperor was deceitful and harsh, and popular customs became base. Gaozu of Han reformed institutions and changed customs, and popular customs became generous. Emperor Xiaowu pursued grandeur and delighted in achievements, and popular customs deteriorated. Emperor Xiaoxuan comprehensively examined names against realities, and popular customs became substantial. Under the Wei and Jin, steadfast integrity was scorned and carefree detachment prized, and popular customs became frivolous. Taizong of Tang restrained himself in governing others, honored Confucian learning, and esteemed the Way, and popular customs became pure. The Song inherited the abuses of the Five Dynasties and nurtured all under Heaven with profound benevolence and abundant beneficence; the humanity and generosity of its customs are self-evident. Their rise and decline, continuity and change, revolved without end: all were assuredly the transforming influence of those above.

As for theft ceasing in a county, this was indeed because people were moved by the Magistrate of Taiqiu’s gift of two pieces of silk; that no one picked up lost property from the road was likewise inspired by Yanfang’s kindness in giving a piece of cloth. Yang Cheng practiced the ancient Way while living in a remote part of Jin; nearly a thousand people became good through the influence of his virtue. Li Shan preserved an orphan’s life and lived in seclusion in Shanyang; people throughout the neighborhoods were moved by his conduct to cultivate righteousness. These, too, were examples of scholar-officials establishing their character and acting righteously, becoming models for their communities.

Jiangyou commands the approaches to Jing and Yue and is girded by rivers and lakes. Its mountains and waterways are exceptionally beautiful, and its people…

title: 弘治十四年江西鄉試錄
text:
物萃止服徳當時思賢異世南州高士徐
孺子也完節先朝血食後代宋室忠臣文
信公也彭龜年當僞學之禁不以流俗而
變劉安世傷羨餘之諷遂以設擻而歸數
君子之文學道徳所以端鄉國之習者固
已久矣久則難變也何者人情安於所習
而駭於所未見商君廢井田民怨固也王
莽復井田而民亦怨武靈王變華效胡民
怨固也魏孝文變胡效華而民亦怨習素
===
善驅之惡不能入猶習素惡驅之善不能
變也然則江右道風文物諸先正之功不
誣而鼓鑄鑪冶則
聖朝之化斯頼生斯世居斯鄉作者不無人焉
然未敢為執事道也
第四問
徐盈
同考試官訓導孟　批　策場浩如望洋輙難窮究
此作考證古今沿革之異評訂功用次第之詳古稱
punctuated:
物萃止。服徳當時，思賢異世，南州高士徐孺子也；完節先朝，血食後代，宋室忠臣文信公也。彭龜年當僞學之禁，不以流俗而變；劉安世傷羨餘之諷，遂以設擻而歸。數君子之文學道徳，所以端鄉國之習者，固已久矣。久則難變也。何者？人情安於所習，而駭於所未見。商君廢井田，民怨固也；王莽復井田，而民亦怨。武靈王變華效胡，民怨固也；魏孝文變胡效華，而民亦怨。習素善，驅之惡不能入；猶習素惡，驅之善不能變也。然則江右道風文物，諸先正之功不誣，而鼓鑄鑪冶，則聖朝之化斯頼。生斯世，居斯鄉，作者不無人焉，然未敢為執事道也。

第四問
徐盈

同考試官訓導孟批：策場浩如望洋，輙難窮究。此作考證古今沿革之異，評訂功用次第之詳。古稱
translation_en:
… men of distinction gather here. His virtue commanded respect in his own time, and later generations longed for his worthiness: such was Xu Ruzi, the eminent scholar of the southern region. He preserved his integrity under the former dynasty and received blood sacrifices from later generations: such was Lord Wen, Duke of Xin, a loyal minister of the Song. Peng Guinian, during the prohibition of “spurious learning,” did not change with prevailing fashions. Liu Anshi was wounded by a satirical remark about surplus revenues and consequently returned home [the wording 設擻 is unclear [?]]. The literary learning and moral virtue of these gentlemen have long served to rectify the customs of their native region. What has endured long is difficult to change. Why? People feel at ease with what they habitually know and are alarmed by what they have never seen. When Lord Shang abolished the well-field system, popular resentment was natural; yet when Wang Mang restored it, the people also resented him. When King Wuling abandoned Chinese ways to imitate the Hu, popular resentment was natural; yet when Emperor Xiaowen of Wei abandoned Hu ways to imitate the Chinese, the people also resented him. When established habits are good, driving people toward evil cannot make evil take hold, just as, when established habits are evil, driving them toward goodness cannot transform them. Thus, as regards Jiangyou’s moral traditions and cultural achievements, the contributions of its former worthies cannot be denied; yet their continued shaping and refining depend upon the transforming influence of our sagely dynasty. Among those born in this age and dwelling in this region, there are indeed people who rise to such achievement, but I have not ventured to speak of them to you, honored examiner.

Xu Ying

This composition examines the differences between ancient and modern institutions, their continuities and changes, and assesses in detail their effectiveness and the order in which they should be applied.
